The crowd had already swelled by that time, and by five in the morning there was no milk left," she said.

Heading: Cash-at-judge door: CBI raids house of Bansal’s munshi - Indian Express
Content:
Flooded with complaints, the Prime Minister's Office has stepped in to ensure that the 50,000 odd foreign students and researchers currently pursing higher education in India go back with a pleasant memory of the country.

Prime Minister Manmohan Singh had set up an inter-ministerial committee headed by Director General, Indian Council of Cultural Research (ICCR), Pavan Varma to recommend measures for the welfare of foreign students and to help introduce a "better regimen" which is "standardised, transparent and easy".

After rounds of marathon meetings and discussions with stakeholders across six cities identified as major educational hubs, the committee is expected to submit its final report in another two weeks.

The Indian Express has learnt that the report will suggest a series of measures starting from the visa application process to issues like scholarships, possibility of a uniform fee structure for Indian and foreign students, making it easier to open bank accounts, assisting with bettering English language skills, and making universities nodal authorities for foreign students.

"The committee is mandated to introduce a better regimen for the welfare of the foreign student in India. Assessments show that nearly 50,000 foreign students and researchers are studying in India and most of them come from South Asia, South East Asia, Africa and the Middle East and study on a self-financed basis. As of now there is no coordinated assessment of exactly what kind of framework should be there for foreign students in India and with their numbers having risen six times in the last five years, it is felt by the Prime Minister that there is an urgent need to address these issues, so the committee," Varma said.

The Indian Express had highlighted how foreign researchers applying in India were kept for waiting for months together owing to the red tapism in the HRD Ministry. Varma said a whole gamut of issues related to foreign students had been assessed and the recommendations will be far reaching.

"India is perceived as an emerging educational hub, particularly for technological and management education. The lower price of quality education here is also an incentive for foreign students and the numbers of those applying are increasing every year. But then there are problems like differential fee structures, student from various countries facing language barriers due to lack of proficiency in English and problems like opening of bank accounts etc. Having got all concerned agencies on board we have now a good understanding of the problems they face and we are now devising ways to ensure a better academic and administrative environment for them, commensurate with the very valid security concerns as well," added Varma.

The committee's recommendations are expected to lead to considerable changes in internal regulations to facilitate the whole process of foreign students seeking admission in Indian educational institutes.

The six educational hubs that attract the maximum number of foreign students are Delhi, Pune, Hyderabad, Banaglore, Mysore and Chennai and the committee has already visited all. Officials from the HRD Ministry, Home Ministry, Department of Science & Technology and the Finance Ministries are part of the committee. They have been meeting vice-chancellors, international students and their representative bodies, local authorities like the state's Home Department, police commissioners, banking sector representatives and Foreigners' Regional Registration Office office.

Heading: Encephalitis: US experts come to Gorakhpur - Indian Express
Content:
A team of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) from Delhi, which is investigating the allegations of an attempt made to bribe a High Court judge, conducted raids past Saturday midnight at the residence of Parkash Ram, junior assistant of former Haryana Additional Advocate General Sanjeev Bansal.

Raids were also conducted at the shop-cum-office of Rajiv Gupta, a property dealer in Panchkula and Bansal's friend. The CBI has reportedly recovered Rs 2 lakh in cash and some important documents from the residence of Parkash Ram in Nada village.

Some important property documents have also been recovered from the shop-cum-office of Rajiv Gupta in Panchkula. The four accused, Bansal, Gupta, Nirmal Singh and Jai Parkash, senior assistant of Bansal, are in the custody of CBI. The statements of the four have been recorded.

According to sources, the CBI has also questioned Bansal's wife, Renu. According to the statements of the accused to the Chandigarh Police, it was Renu Bansal who had packed 15 lakh in cash in a bag that was "wrongly" delivered at the residence of Justice Nirmaljit Kaur.

The CBI also questioned the stenographer and a domestic help of Bansal. "Since some forged property documents were prepared at the residence of Bansal, his steno was questioned about them," said an officer.

It is learnt that the CBI is trying to collect circumstantial evidence in order to prove the motive behind sending the money to the judge. The agency will produce Bansal and the three other accused in the court of Special CBI Judge on Monday, seeking further police remand of them.

Heading: We will watch what action BMC takes, says Raj - Indian Express
Content:
After the state Government's failure to isolate the viruses responsible for Acute Encephalitis Syndrome  cases in Gorakhpur, the Centre has sought USA's help.

On the invitation of the Government, a team of two virology experts from Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, Atlanta, are camping in Gorakhpur from August 28 and collecting blood samples for testing in their own laboratory.

Scientists at Pune-based National Institute of Virology found that unlike Japanese Encephalitis, which is a vector-borne disease — spreads through mosquitoes — the AES cases were caused by enteroviruses, which spreads through the oral-fecal route.

There are thousands of enteroviruses, and those responsible for the problem in Gorakhpur could not be identified. Experts from the US are expected to help in the identification of the viruses and check whether the present line of symptomatic treatment given to the patients is correct.

The experts are supposed to compile their report in America and give it to the Centre along with their recommendations.

"The Indian Council for Medical Research (ICMR) has a long time understanding with CDC and they have been assisting us in various projects. Thus, we thought to take their help in this case as well," said Dr M M Gore, a senior scientist from National Institute of Virology, Pune.

On Sunday, the experts visited the houses of some of the patients to see the environment in which most of the patients were living. They also visited the BRD Medical College, Gorakhpur, to check the treatment given to the patients registered under AES. 

"We have high hopes from these experts. Year after year, we have been watching large number of children being affected with the virus and we have no other option but to provide them with symptomatic treatment," said Dr Lalit Mohan, principal of BRD Medical College. "We hope that they will help us in identifying the clinical spectrum of the disease and suggest if there can be any better line of treatment," added Mohan.

AES: situation this year

People affected: 962

Related deaths: 170

Worst affected districts:

•Gorakhpur: 319 patients, 54 deaths

• Kushinagar: 226 patients, 42 deaths

•Devaria: 136 patients, 30 deaths

•Mehrajganj: 92 patients, 17 deaths

Heading: Russian Consul General moves sessions court over property row - Indian Express
Content:
Denying that his party had extended the deadline for shops and establishments to put up Marathi signboards, MNS president Raj Thackeray said his party would first peruse action taken by the state Government and municipal corporations on defaulting establishments before announcing their plan of action.

After the BMC issued a deadline of August 28 for shops to ensure that their signages included their names in Devnagari script, the MNS chief backed off from his aggressive stance on dealing with non-compliance after the Bombay High Court came down heavily on him and the state government on the issue.

Raj, who had sought to enforce the BMC deadline, had backed off by pointing out that a number of shop keepers had made the change and had asked his cadre to refrain from violence against defaulting businesses.

"After the MNS raised the issue of Marathi name boards in Maharashtra and pursued it relentlessly to its logical conclusion, everyone from the state government to the traders were shaken up, and boards in Marathi were put up in cities across Maharashtra. Most of the locations saw the Marathi name boards being put up, while many people are in the process of preparing these boards. After this change which was seen in Maharashtra for the first time, we asked our associates to lie low for the moment," said Raj, in a signed statement issued on Sunday.

Raj added that a delegation of traders had met him and asked for the deadline to be extended by another three to four months and said that the media had not reported his reply to the request. A delegation of members of the Federation of Maharashtra Stationary Manufacturers and Traders Association met Raj at his Dadar residence on Friday.

"These people have not been given nor will be given any (extended) time," said the statement, adding that the party was watching how the state Government and municipal corporations in Mumbai and the rest of the state were acting on the establishments that were yet to put up the signboards.

Heading: Bhandarkar to donate award money to farmers’ widows - Indian Express
Content:
The Russian Consulate General in Mumbai moved the Session's court against the state Government and five others who were discharged in a cheating case after the Mumbai Police gave them a 'clean chit'. The case revolves around a plot of land at Malabar Hill, which was sold to a Dubai-based businessman for $10 million in 2006. The Consulate claims the plot was leased to it.

According to a criminal revision application filed by Alexander V Mantytsky, Russian Consul General in Mumbai, the Russian Government had taken on lease a 15,000 sq ft plot of land near the chief minister's bungalow at Malabar Hill in 1996.

Heading: Maoists claim they killed Swami, say Sangh lying - Indian Express
Content:
He is known for his grip on urban themes and has won three National Awards for his films Chandni Bar, Page 3 and Traffic Signal. But before he goes to New Delhi to receive his third National Award on September 2, he has made a commitment that brings out his sensitivity towards rural issues too.

Madhur Bhandarkar has decided to donate his award money of Rs 2.5 lakh to Kamla Kashinath Waghmare, Sangita Prakash Darne and Sugandha Shyamrao Kannake, widows of Vidarbha farmers who committed suicide due to agrarian distress. Contributing Rs 50,000 from his own pocket, he would be handing over cheques for Rs 1 lakh each to them at a simple ceremony here on August 6.

"I have been hearing and reading a lot about the farm crisis. As one involved in making films over social themes, I thought it would be good if I could provide some of them with the financial leverage they so badly need in the face of the kind of grave crisis they are in. So, when the national award was declared, I decided to take the call for the noble cause," Bhandarkar told The Indian Express in an interview.

Asked how a typically urban filmmaker like him thought of addressing the rural distress, he said, "I may have made films based on urban themes, but I do keep track of everything happening around me, including issues of rural India as well."

But how about making a film on rural crises like the farm distress? "If I get a good theme, I would certainly like to work on it," he said.

Bhandarkar admits that Indian films have been somewhat lost on rural realities, but says even people from rural areas want to see what's happening in cities.

"The last film to have been made on rural background was Lagaan. But I feel Hindi cinema could again be turning towards rural themes that would be strong enough to attract all kinds of audiences like what used to be up to 80s," he said.

Even as philanthrophists and politicians are vying with each other to help Kalavati and Shashikala after Rahul Gandhi's reference to them in his speech in Parliament, hundreds of Kalavatis and Shashikalas continue to fight poverty and indebtedness in the absence of any help. Those to benefit from Bhandarkar's help are amongst the genuinely needy ones.

Sangita and Sugandha belong to Yelabara and Kumri villages in Yavatmal district while Kamla belongs to Moundhala village in Buldana district.

Sangita's husband Prakash had committed suicide on June 28, 2007 — he carried a loan burden of Rs 56,000. Sangita has two daughters, one of them visually-impaired, and a son to look after.

Sugandha faced a unique tragedy. Her husband and father-in-law committed suicide on a single day, February 17, 2007 due to poverty. She has two sons, who can't go to school due to extreme poverty.

Kashinath Waghmare's was the first suicide after announcement of loan waiver, on March 1. "In all these cases, the help would be really going to the genuinely deserving families," said Yavatmal Collector Sanjay Deshmukh.

Bhandarkar admits that attempt should be do enable and empower the farmers to help themselves, but says financial help helps one to stand in good stead till empowerment happens.

Heading: Naveen visits Kandhamal, Koraput, says situation under control - Indian Express
Content:
Amid continuing anti-Christian violence in Orissa, Maoists have claimed responsibility for the killing of VHP leader Swami Lakshmanananda Saraswati in Orissa and warned more attacks on VHP and Bajrang Dal leaders. The radical Left outfit came out with the statement amidst a blame game on who killed the VHP leader with the saffron brigade having already accused Christian missionaries of plotting and executing the murder.

The Central Committee of Communist Party of India (Maoist) said that, "The Sangh Parivar leaders like Praveen Togadia have been trying to divert the people by uttering lies that it is not the Maoists but Christian organisations that had carried out the attack on the VHP leader."

The Maoists alleged that Saraswati was a "rabid anti-Christian ideologue and persecutor of innocent Christians who was responsible for the burning down of over 400 churches in Kandhamal district alone". The Maoists appealed to secular and democratic forces to condemn the Sangh Parivar. "It is not SIMI that is to be outlawed but Hindu fanatical gangs like the VHP, Bajrang Dal, Shiv Sena, BJP, and Hindu Munnani and so on," the Central Committee said.

Equating Prime Minister Manmohan and Congress chief Sonia Gandhi with BJP leaders L K Advani and Narendra Modi, the Maoists said the Congress leadership does not see any threat to the country from "overtly communal, criminal acts of the VHP and Sangh Parivar".

"But they order the arrest, torture and harassment of ordinary Muslims and outlaw cultural organisations like SIMI. Thousands of Muslims languish in jails whether it is under the reign of Advanis, Modis or under Manmohan Singhs and Y S Rajesekhara Reddys," the Maoists alleged.

Heading: LJP favours citizenship for Bangladeshis - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik on Sunday claimed that the communal tension in Kandhamal and Koraput was under control saying more central forces were on the way to restore normalcy in the riot-hit areas.

Naveen said he had spoken to Union Home Minister Shivraj Patil for 10 more companies of forces. The state Government had sought 23 companies of additional forces and three choppers for movement of the forces to deal with the situation arising out of Swami Laxmanananda Saraswati's killing. But it had got only 16 companies.

Patnaik who visited Kandhamal on Saturday and Sunday said those perpetrating violence would be punished and promised quick relief and rehabilitation for the victims in the communally sensitive district.

The Chief Minister said people in relief camps in Kandhamal district had been provided with essential commodities, including medicines. During his visit, Patnaik spoke to inmates of the Jalespeta ashram and paid a floral tribute at the portrait of the slain Swami.

Though the Chief Minister evaded the demand for a CBI probe into the incident saying that the state police were enough, the Vishwa Hindu Parishad demanded a special task force to hunt the killers of Laxmanananda Saraswati. VHP's state general secretary Gouri Prasad Rath said it was unfortunate that the murderers were yet to be arrested though Swamiji was killed on August 23. "A special task force should be formed forthwith to nab the culprits without further delay," he told reporters accusing the state Government of ignoring the cold-blooded killing of Saraswati.

Meanwhile, two companies of CRPF and three companies of the Orissa State Armed Police (OSAP) were deployed at Jeypore where 11 persons, including officials, were injured in a clash between two communities over some objectionable graffiti in a college on Saturday.

Heading: People defy Jammu curfew to celebrate - Indian Express
Content:
With an eye on elections, the Lok Janshakti Party, a ruling UPA constituent, on Sunday favoured giving citizenship to Bangladeshis staying in the country and advocated reservation for the economically weak and minorities in Government and private sectors.

"Those Bangladeshis who are already staying in India should be provided citizenship. Further infiltration should be checked. There should be strict vigil on the border," a resolution passed by the party headed by Union Minister Ram Vilas Paswan said here. The party supported reservation for the "socially and economically" backward groups.

"The party feels that in view of their social and economic conditions, the SC and ST people should get reservation in private sector. Every community should have equal representation in all sectors," the resolution said. The party is in favour of giving 10 per cent reservation in Central Government jobs for the economically weaker sections among the upper castes.

Heading: Schools reopen, to hold extra classes - Indian Express
Content:
Defying curfew restrictions, people came out for participating in the "Victory rally" in Jammu city after the Government agreed to set aside 800 kanals of land at Baltal in South Kashmir Himalayas for the exclusive use of the Amarnath Shrine Board, forcing the police to fire teargas shells and lathicharge the jubilant crowd. More than 36 people were injured in the clashes.

After the news broke out at around 4.30 am, celebrations began across Jammu, with people coming out of their houses, congratulating and hugging each other. People were seen dancing to the tune of drumbeats and firing crackers to express joy over the decision. Some people splashed Holi colours on each other, saying that the Sunday morning had brought in new colours to the lives of Jammuites.

Given the sensitive situation, authorities had imposed curfew in Jammu, and called in the Army to prevent people from participating in the "victory rally", which was scheduled to be held at MAM Stadium at around 11 am.

Addressing the media after reaching the agreement, Samiti convenor Leela Karan Sharma said that the day's Sangarsh Rally would be celebrated as victory rally. He made the announcement, even as Dr S S Bloeria, head of the Governor's panel, requested the Samiti to cancel the rally. Following this, the authorities clamped curfew in Jammu and put barbed wires across the city at the main entry and exit points, to restrict people from marching towards the MAM Stadium, the venue of the rally.

Thousands of people, including women and children, assembled in front of the GGM Science College in Jammu and started moving towards MAM Stadium. As the cops resisted their move, the supporters of the agitation pelted stones on the cops, forcing them to retaliate with lathicharge and the firing of teargas shells. People clashed with the cops at various places such as Jewel Chowk, Janipur, Talab Tilloo, Shakti Nagar, Purani Mandi, Parade, Residency Road, Canal Road and Gangyal.

According to the police, curfew was imposed this morning, in view of credible intelligence about the presence of terrorists in Jammu. Curfew was lifted from 6 PM, after combing/search operations were completed in the vicinity of Jammu city, police added.

Heading: Curfew clamped again after fresh protests in Valley - Indian Express
Content:
With Shri Amarnath Yatra Sangarsh Samiti (SAYSS) calling off its stir and schools in the state expected to reopen on Monday, the Jammu and Kashmir Government has decided to hold additional classes in all schools to complete syllabus on time. With the state already having a high number of dropouts, the ongoing agitation has further resulted in the loss of working days.

Jammu and Kashmir Education Secretary, G A Peer, said, "To compensate the loss of the students during curfew we will be taking supplementary classes. One hour extra tuition to the students everyday can help complete the syllabus." Peer said in case the syllabus still remains incomplete, students will be given concession and wider choice in the examinations. "We will hold meeting with State Board of School Education (SBOSE) officials for giving wider choice to the students." he added.

Chief Education Officer (CEO), Jammu, Suresh Kumar, said, "Students from primary level upto the middle class will be examined only for that part of the syllabus which has been completed. Teachers would have to put in extra classes to complete the syllabus on time."

" Students have suffered a lot in terms of number of working days. Primary schools and Class XI classes could not start after summer vacations because of the Amarnath land transfer row," added Kumar.

Meanwhile, the Government on Sunday also issued an order that colleges across Jammu will begin their classes from Monday. Director Colleges, N D Wani, said, "We are holding meetings with principals of all the colleges to find measures for completion of the syllabus."

Heading: Advani satisfied with Samiti, J-K pact - Indian Express
Content:
On day eight of the curfew in the Kashmir valley, the J-K Government on Sunday announced simultaneous relaxation in curfew across the Valley but had to immediately re-impose curfew at several places after hundreds of people took to the streets raising pro-freedom and anti-India slogans. Four persons were injured when the J-K Police and Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) fired rubber bullets on the protestors in the old city.

In Srinagar, as the announcement of relaxation in curfew was made, hundreds of people took to the streets in downtown city. The people were raising pro-freedom and anti-India slogans and demanded release of the separatist leaders arrested by the J-K Police after their crackdown against the separatists in the Valley. Hundreds of people took to the streets at Rajouri Kadal, Nowhatta, Bohri Kadal, Nawab Bazar and other parts of the old city. At Rajouri Kadal, the police and CRPF tried to stop the peaceful protest march and resorted to baton charge. Then they fired rubber bullets to disperse the protestors resulting in injuries to the four persons.

The people soon turned violent and engaged in pitched battles with the J-K Police and CRPF. Soon after the protests, the J-K Police re-imposed the curfew in the old city.

However, in the Civil Lines city, the relaxation time passed off peacefully and the police extended curfew first for three hours and then by another four hours till 7 p.m.

Curfew had to be imposed again in Sopore, Baramulla and Shopian towns. In Sopore town, as the curfew was relaxed for two hours in the morning, hundreds of people took to streets and raised pro-freedom slogans. The people engaged in clashes with J-K Police and CRPF. The police re-imposed the curfew in the town soon after the relaxation was announced.

The Baramulla town too witnessed re-imposition of curfew after the people took to streets raising pro-freedom slogans. This is for the third consecutive day that the curfew had to be re-imposed in the town as a result of massive protests.

Pro-freedom processions were also taken out at several places across the valley including Shopian and Kupwara. Hundreds of people took to streets raising pro-freedom and anti-India slogans and demanding release of the separatist leaders. At several places, the protestors entered into clashes with police and CRPF. More than a dozen protestors were injured in these clashes.

Heading: ‘A shining symbol of communal harmony’ - Indian Express
Content:
BJP leader and Leader of the Opposition L K Advani has said he was satisfied with the agreement reached between the Shri Amarnath Sangharsh Samiti and the Jammu and Kashmir Governor regarding the diversion of forest land to the Sri Amarnath Shrine Board (SASB) for the duration of the yatra.

Advani had maintained that the controversy was due to the divide between the "nationalists" and "separatists".

Saying that the issue should be recognised in "its true form" the BJP leader said: "This is not a Hindu versus Muslim issue; this is not Jammu versus Valley issue. It is a surrender to the pressure of the separatists. Therefore, the problem has arisen. And therefore, when he (Singh) replied to me (in response to my letter) that 'I agree with this analysis' and also stated firmly that under no circumstances will the Government take a decision under pressure from separatists, I felt satisfied that now we will be reaching a solution," Advani told reporters after a rally organised by the BJP in New Delhi.

Advani said that from the initial reports, it appeared that the agreement reached was broadly satisfactory to the Sri Amarnath Yatra Sangharsh Samiti. "If now the decision has been reached, I'm happy," he added.

Heading: Relocating ancillary units will solve problem: Mamata - Indian Express
Content:
Details of agreement reached between the state Government and Shri Amarnath Sangharsh Samiti, bringing an end to the two-month-long agitation in Jammu.

Details of agreement reached between the state Government and Shri Amarnath Sangharsh Samiti, bringing an end to the two-month-long agitation in Jammu

•The state government shall set aside for the use by Shri Amarnathji Shrine Board, exclusively, the land in Baltal and Domail (Compartment No. 63/S, Sindh Forest Division) comprising an area of 800 kanals, traditionally under use for the annual yatra purposes.

•The proprietary status/ownership/title of the land shall not undergo any change.

• The Board shall use the aforesaid land for the duration of the yatra (including the period of making the required arrangements and winding up of the same) for the purpose of user by various service providers according to its needs and priorities.

• The aforesaid land shall be used according to the Board's requirements, from time to time, including for the following:-

i. Raising of temporary pre-fabricated accommodation and toilet facilities by the Board;

ii. Establishment of tented accommodation by private camping agencies (locals, permanent residents of the state);

iii. Setting up of the shops by shopkeepers (locals, permanent residents of the state);

iv. Facilities for ponywallahs and pithuwallahs;

v. Provision of healthcare and medical facilities;

vi. Setting yup of free langers by private persons and groups which are licenced by the Board;

vii. Facilties for helicopter operations/parking of vehicles;

viii. Arrangements of security by local police/para military forces and other security agencies as per the arrangements in place here-to-fore; and

ix. Undertaking measures relating to soil conservation, land protection and preservation of ecology.

• It has further been agreed that Board shall continue to remain responsible for the overall arrangements of the yatra on both the routes during the yatra period, including all arrangements as mandated under the provisions of the Shri Amarnathji Shrine Act, 2000 A.D.

• The state government agreed to examine in an appropriate manner on time bound basis all the demands contained in a 14-point "Charter of Demands" submitted by Samiti for consideration by state government. The main demands related to withdrawal of criminal cases against various persons during the agitation period, provision of compensation to the families of the deceased and to the injured and working out of appropriate packages of financial assistance to compensate losses of transport sector, trade and industry, horticulture, hoteliers and tourist operators. In particular, as regards the registration of criminal cases against various persons during the period of agitation, it is agreed that all cases of non-serious nature which shall mean bailable and compoundable will be withdrawn. The remaining cases will be reviewed, on the merit of each case, by a committee headed by Anil Goswami, Principal Secretary (Home) within 60 days, Till the completion of this process, no action will be taken in such cases. Also, specific allegations of atrocities on agitators, based on prima facie evidence, could also be looked into by this committee.

• Ex-gratia relief will be extended in favour of the next of the kin of deceased and in favour of permanently disabled and the injured in all cases covered under the exiting rules of the state government.

• Further, a working group, under the chairmanship of Chief Secretary will address all compensation issues relating to both Jammu and Kashmir divisions and the Central government will be approached for extending enabling financial support to the state government for this purpose within a period of two months. To make the exercise meaningful, one representative from each of the affected sectors will be associated with the deliberations of the working group.

• The Shri Amarnathji Shrine Board will be reconstituted keeping in view the provisions of the Act and the past precedents.

• It is agreed that the state government's Law Department will examine the issue of disposal of LPA in terms of the understanding made hereinabove within one month.

Heading: Singur will unleash fear, uncertainty in investors: Murthy - Indian Express
Content:
Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee on Sunday said members of agitating group would meet the Governor to press for shifting of Tata Motors' ancillary units close to the Nano project site to end the deadlock in

Singur even as, while sharing the anxiety of the Tatas, the West Bengal Government said it was "legally" not possible to return the land acquired under the acquisition law. It hoped that the corporate giant would not withdraw the small-car project from Singur.

"There is a one line solution. Everything will be settled if the ancillary units are relocated to the land on the opposite side of the small car unit," Banerjee said from her dharna platform, a day after Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi sent her a letter asking her to call off the eight-day long stir.

Sticking to her demand that 400 acres of the land acquired for the small car project be returned to the "unwilling farmers", she said the plant could come up on 600 acres site. "In that case both industry and agriculture will smile," she said.

But West Bengal Industry Minister Nirupam Sen said, while quoting a ruling from the Supreme Court, "The way Mamata Banerjee is demanding, it is impossible for the state Government to meet her demand. Legally, it is not possible to return the land acquired under the Land Acquisition Act."

"The issue was also taken to the Calcutta High Court and it said land acquisition was as per law," he said, adding that there were no legal provisions to return the land once acquired by the Government under the acquisition law.

Meanwhile, describing the Singur issue as a 'deep-rooted' problem, External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee on Sunday said the Centre was not in a position to take any initiative to end the deadlock as it was a matter related to the West Bengal Government.

"It is a deep-rooted problem. Who will invest in which state is a matter between the state Government and the investor. Since it is a matter concerning the state, it is not possible for the Centre to take any initiative on this issue," Mukherjee told reporters here when asked if the Centre had any role here to end the Singur stalemate.

In an obvious reference to the Tatas' small car, Mukherjee said, "The Centre is always in favour of new technology."

"We want industrialisation. At the same time we have to protect the interests of the farmers. We have to raise food production. We have to strike a balance," he said.

Mukherjee said state Congress president P R Dasmunsi had on Saturday made the party line clear on the Singur issue. Dasmunsi had stated that the Tatas should not withdraw their small car project from Singur and the state Government provide alternate land to 'unwilling' farmers.

"We are opposed to the shift of investment made in Singur and industry to other states," Dasmunsi said and reiterated that the Centre would not take any responsibility in bailing out West Bengal on the issue.

Heading: national news, india updates, india latest news, news updates, states news - Indian Express
Content:
Software icon N R Narayana Murthy on Sunday warned that the deadlock in Singur over Tata's Nano plant following agitations will "unleash fear and uncertainty" in the minds of all investors and is likely to be a stumbling block in the excellent GDP growth India has demonstrated in the last decade.

"What has happened in Singur is unfortunate for West Bengal, for India and for all progressive Indians," the non-executive chairman and chief mentor of the NASDAQ-listed Infosys Technologies Ltd said. Murthy also added that it is a setback for the job opportunities for youngsters in West Bengal.

"It is time that all well-intentioned Indians stand up and demand a peaceful, logical and constructive way of settling the issue of farmland in Singur and elsewhere in India," he said.

Heading: Modi asks NRGs to write email to PM - Indian Express
Content:
With the Gujarat High Court telling the Centre early last week that it can't sit on the Gujarat Control of Organised Crime (GUJCOC) Bill, 2003 indefinitely without referring it to the President for her assent, the Union Ministry of Home Affairs is in a fix. It is weighing its options whether to refer it to the President or send it back to the state Government for reconsideration by the Assembly.

A few days ago, during the hearing of a petition filed by Justice on Trial (JoT), an Ahmedabad-based NGO that is seeking directions to the Centre to obtain President's assent on the GUJCOC Act, a Division Bench headed by Acting Chief Justice M S Shah had come down heavily on the MHA for not doing anything with the Bill. The Bill was sent to the Central Government after the state legislature passed the GUJCOC Bill on March 26, 2003.

The Bench has given the MHA a last opportunity to decide on its course of action. The next date of hearing is September 10.

"We will meet early next week to take a decision with regard to our response. In view of the strong verbal observations of the High Court, we will certainly have to do something. We are studying all our options. We will also consult the Ministry of Law and Justice to seek legal opinion," said a senior MHA functionary who did not wish to be quoted.

It is learnt that a Director-level officer of the MHA had been specially deputed to Ahmedabad to be present during the hearing.

Incidentally, on the day Mufti Abu Bashir, the mastermind behind the July 26 blasts, was arrested by the Gujarat Police, Chief Minister Narendra Modi spoke to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh on phone to give him an update on the arrests and the breakthrough achieved by the state police.

He is also learnt to have asked the Prime Minister to clear the GUJCOC Bill, 2003, which has been stuck in the Ministry of Home Affairs and have been awaiting the President's assent since 2003.

Last week, Modi also met the Prime Minister seeking his intervention.

He is learnt to have reiterated that apart from the fact that the GUJCOC Bill was prepared and introduced in the Gujarat Assembly after the Government of India directed it to do so, the law is a carbon copy of the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA), which has been in force since 1999. Incidentally, MCOCA has also been extended to Delhi, a Congress-ruled state.

It was only after the Centre gave it the go-ahead on February 17, 2003 that the Bill was introduced in the Gujarat Assembly, which passed it a month later.

Thereafter, the Bill was sent to the President through the nodal ministry — Union Ministry of Home Affairs — for securing the assent of the President. However, the Bill was returned with the request to delete clauses 14-16, which dealt with interception of communication network to check organised crimes and appointment of a competent authority for authorising a police official below the rank of SP for the interception. This was done as the Bombay High Court had ruled similar provisions in MCOCA unconstitutional.

Accordingly, the Gujarat Assembly on June 2, 2004 passed the revised Act and sent it again for the President's approval on June 19, 2004.

Since then, the state has sent over one dozen requests, including personal letters from Modi to the Prime Minister, and reminders for speedy approval of the proposed law but to no avail.

Heading: CBI: single-officer probe out, teams to do the job - Indian Express
Content:
Gujarat Chief Minister Narendra Modi has requested all Non-Resident Gujaratis (NRGs) to send emails to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh asking him to approve the GUJCOC Bill. Addressing the World Gujarati Conference 2008 in New Jersey, US, via video conferencing early on Sunday, Modi said to fight terrorism and safeguard the security of the people of the state special laws like GUJCOC were needed.

Modi asked all the NRGs in the US and other countries to send an email to Prime Minister Manmohan Singh and request him to give sanction to the GUJCOC Bill which has been approved twice by the elected representatives in the Gujarat Assembly.

The Chief Minister also told the conference that he had already made a representation regarding GUJCOC to the Prime Minister and was hopeful of some positive response from the Central Government.

Heading: In the times of reality TV, an unreal story: a 7/11 victim who wasn’t - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has evolved a new system wherein 'Investigative Teams' in place instead of 'Investigative Officers' will look into cases handed over to the agency. The initiative has been taken by new CBI Director Ashwani Kumar, who said, "Team work is always better as it increases the efficiency and improves the quality of work."

Earlier, one investigative officer was given the charge of a case, but from now, for every case, there would be at least two officers forming a team and holding the probe. The maximum number of officers in a team would depend on the need of the case. "Like in the Aarushi murder case, we had a large team of 25 officers investigating the case," added Kumar.

Also, the CBI would decide on a timeframe in which investigations should be completed, but without compromising on the quality. "It is necessary to decide the duration of the investigation in a case. This would be a part of the team effort," said Kumar. The other sleuths in a particular team would report to the senior officers forming the Investigative Team.

Subsequently, a new programme is being started to boost the morale of CBI officials by providing them good medical facilities. "Officers can do good work only if they are in good health. So we are going to conduct medical examination of all CBI officials as well as their family members and would try to ensure that they are provided with proper medical facilities," added Kumar. The CBI has several residential colonies in Goa, Calcutta, Chandigarh, Nagpur and other places where medical check-ups would be conducted.

Heading: In present scenario, Advani can’t become PM: Govindacharya - Indian Express
Content:
This was one reality TV show that seems to have been rather unreal. Earlier this month, Bollywood actor Urmila Matondkar introduced a widow on an episode of the musical show War-Parivaar she hosts on Sony TV, which has been fighting terrorism as its theme. Shubhda Santosh Niwate, Matondkar said, had lost her husband in the July 11, 2006, Mumbai train blasts. 

"Between raising our voices against terrorism, we want to introduce you to a family which has seen the ghastly face of terror from very close quarters," Matondkar said, as the camera panned on Niwate and her two young daughters, Sayali, 7, and Granthali, 8. "My husband worked at the Nagpada police hospital. He died in the Dadar blast on July 11, 2006," the widow said, speaking in Marathi.  

Matondkar joined in on the episode which was shown on August 11. "Her husband was working with the railway police. So I appeal to the railways to do their best for her and her daughters," the Rangeela star said in an emotional plea and then went on to hug Niwate and her daughters and also gave them some gifts. 

While it is rather commonly known that Dadar was not among the seven locations hit by serial bomb blasts, investigations by Newsline also found that Niwate's husband, Santosh Rajaram Niwate, was not one of the 188 people killed in the attacks. 

Santosh, 35, it was found, worked as a helper in the mortuary at JJ Hospital and died only in February this year. "He had a drinking problem and took ill. He went to his hometown in Ratnagiri district and died there," said a senior mortuary official, who did not want to be identified. 

Shubhda, who lives in the Nagpada police hospital quarters and works as a maid, said she was going by the script. She said she had been approached by Pradeep Waghmare, who works for Saibaba Telefilms, the production house which makes War-Parivaar. "He said he was making some TV programme on which I had to appear and say my husband was killed in the bomb blast in Dadar and that I would be paid Rs 50,000 for it," she alleged. 

"One month ago, we were taken to RK Studios in a car and I was told what to say. After the show, we were given only Rs 1,000 and dropped in Sion instead of being dropped home. Urmila gave us three gifts. In one packet there were two coffee mugs while the other two had dolls made of jute," she added. "I don't know why they chose me for this." 

Saibaba Telefilms is headed by well-known producer-director Gajendra Singh, who has been associated with popular TV shows for over a decade. Repeated attempts to seek his comments failed as his phones were not answered. Waghmare said the entire incident was a "mistake". "From our entire unit, I apologise for everything," is all he would say. 

A representative of Sony Entertainment Television said the channel was not aware of the incident and the official spokesperson was out of town and could not be reached. "It is a licenced programme and not an in-house programme. Therefore the channel is not aware of this because at the end of the day all we get is the tape," said the representative.

(With inputs from Shashank Shekhar)

Heading: Evacuation continues; toll 70 - Indian Express
Content:
Former BJP general secretary K N Govindacharya said here on Sunday that despite managing contradictions and getting the approval of RSS and NDA leaders for the Prime Minister's post, Leader of the Opposition L K Advani himself knows that in the present scenario it is not possible for him to get the coveted post.

"Despite the Jinnah controversy, Advani was backed by the RSS and NDA for the Prime Minister's post. But even he knows that it is not possible for him to be PM in the present scenario," Govindachrya told reporters.

He further said that Advani would not be able to use the Ram Sethu and Amarnath land row issues to his advantage since the Ram Sethu Project was approved when the NDA Government was in power. And the moment he tries to encash it, the Congress will turn tables on him.

The Amarnath land row too, after Sunday's agreement had become a national achievement and political parties would not be able to encash it politically. Coordinator of the Rashtriya Swabhiman Andolan said that the Andolan had started gaining ground in the country, and at present, its creative works were on in 124 districts of the country — including Rewa, Sagar and Jhabua districts of MP.

At present, he said, he too was involved in purification of the Ganges and cow conservation. A two-day seminar on cow-conservation will be organised by the Andolan on November 6 and 7 in New Delhi.

Heading: Sunny side up: ‘cross-connection’ keeps mobiles of victims going - Indian Express
Content:
Even as Union Railway Minister Lalu Prasad visited Madhepura on Sunday to distribute relief materials through a special train, the exodus from Madhepura and its adjoining villages continued. The Bihar government claimed to have evacuated over 5 lakh people from marooned areas of Supaul, Madhepura and Araria.

Madhepura has two to four feet water. Boats have been pressed into service in the town. The official death toll is at 70 but there are apprehensions of thousands of deaths.

Operation points have been set up at worst hit Chhatapur, Triveniganj, Murlignaj, Uda Kishanganj, Bihariganj and Gwalpada of Supaul and Madhepura.

"Fifteen navy boats and 14 columns of Army have already arrived for rescue operation. We are expecting six more Army columns by tomorrow," said Disaster management additional commissioner Pratyay Amrit. He said an Army jawan, who was feared to have been drowned in boat tragedy at Mirganj, has returned safely. "He had sat atop a tree and was located by an Army boat," said Amrit.

Though water discharge from the breach had come down to 1.4 lakh cusecs on Sunday as against 1.6 lakh on Saturday, relief operation has been hit with the Madhepura-Singhewar Road getting shut because of three feet water on the road.

Saharsa and Madhepura stations remained crowded with displaced people gathering in large numbers to take special trains to safety. Over 27 lakh people have been affected so far. Some areas in Purnea and Katihar have also been affected.

Relief at camps remains unsatisfactory, as food items are not adequate. Government officials are yet to inspect new areas where dislodged people have stayed put. Meanwhile, several private groups and NGOs have joined the relief operation.

Heading: Wary of theft, victims camp close to flooded homes - Indian Express
Content:
The entire family of Shiv Kumar Suman, who works in Bihar's Health Department, is stranded on the roof of his house in Jorgama village of Purnea district for the last 11 days now. Without enough food and with no drinking water, they are in a pitiable condition, along with more than 100 others, desperately waiting for a rescue boat to evacuate them.

The only consolation is that Suman is able to hear their voice and talk regularly over a mobile phone, thanks, surprisingly, to one of the solar street lamps that the Government had provided to his village panchayat a few months back. The people of his village are now using the solar panel of the streetlight to charge their mobile phones and remain in touch with the people outside.

"I am regularly talking to my family. Sometimes the network is weak but otherwise I get to know what is happening. Thankfully, they all are safe as of now, but they have to be evacuated urgently. There is hardly any food left and little children need milk and clean drinking water," he said.

Suman said every village panchayat in the area had been given five solar street lamps by the Government. The solar panels are placed just above the lamps, which function as stand-alone lighting equipment.

After the Kosi waters rushed in, one of the people taking refuge at the roof of his house swam across to the nearest lamp, dislodged the panel and brought it back. This is now being used to charge mobile phones.

Asked whether people in other villages had also resorted to the same method, he said: "How else do you think people here are getting news about their families stuck inside? There is no electricity in these villages ever since water entered on August 21. They must be using something to charge their mobile phones."

Many of the marooned people have even exhausted their balance but they are at least able to receive calls. Mobile communication is also being used to guide rescue teams to places which need the most urgent attention.

Ask him if it's another case of adversity bringing to the fore Indian ingenuity, and Suman shrugs: "When you are dying you resort to all sorts of things to keep yourself alive. This is a desperate situation and people are making desperate responses."

Heading: Under siege: Bihari migrants caught in flood of worries - Indian Express
Content:
While thousands of poor people - with cattle as their sole property - have left their inundated homes in Madhepura and Supaul villages, the better-off people are still unwilling to move far away from their houses.

Over 4,000 people from Madhepura and Saharsa, along with those at Madhepura-Bihariganj Road, are staying put at the Jorba canal embankment, two-three kilometres away from their marooned villages. And many of them take boats, at least once a day, to visit their homes and confirm that their belongings kept in rooms on the first floor are not stolen. Several villagers swim all the way back to their villages to place locks on the gates of their houses.

Their fears are not unfounded. People from areas not affected by the flood strike at deserted houses in these villages and steal whatever is worth carrying through the waist-deep water.

"I found my cot missing when I visited my flooded house to get more belongings. Calamity has come as a god-sent opportunity for thieves and hoodlums," said Mahadev Mukhiya of Reshma village. Another villager, Sitaram Yadav from Sadhua, said he had found two sacks of wheat stolen from his house. He said the occasional distribution of 2 kg chura wouldn't sustain them for long.

The local administrations of Saharsa, Madhepura and Supaul have been receiving several complaints of thefts at deserted houses. Officials at relief camps said that though they were aware of such incidents, there was very little they could do. Additional Secretary (disaster management) Pratyay Amrit said their prime concerns were to supply relief to victims and rescue as many of them as possible.

Several con groups are collecting money under the cover of relief operations. Some collect money in the name of funeral expenses for those who drowned. A group of 20 people stopped this correspondent on Wednesday on Saharasa-Madhepura route and asked for "some money" for a boy's funeral. But there was no body nearby. After learning our identity, they moved on to stop another vehicle.

Sanjay Soni, a Saharsa resident, said: "All of a sudden, the town has 10-15 groups collecting funds for flood relief. Most of them do not look genuine as they have no idea of exact locations of camps where they are supposed to go for relief."

Heading: Assam: Army called out, NH-31 cut off, 80 pc of Majuli under water - Indian Express
Content:
Two months ago, Kananji Tiwari, a migrant labourer from Bihar, had come to Ahmedabad in search of work. But due to the floods in Bihar, he has to go back to his native village in Madhepura district for saving his family.

Tiwari told The India Express, "My brother is in Patna. Two days ago, he told me over the phone that the weather is getting worse each day. My parents and wife are stuck in Madhepura district, which is among the worst affected area. I am worried about them, as they have no food and no one to help them."

Kundan Tiwari belongs to Bihar and is an alumnus of the Indian Rural Management Anand (IRMA). He said: "I have been speaking to several NGOs and corporates for setting up an aid system and a relief fund for the flood-affected people of Bihar."

He added: "I am in constant touch with a doctor from Forbesganj in Bihar, who is providing relief with some of his friends. He says people at the grassroots level are badly hit and are without any help."

Heading: China surprises by issuing prompt visa to Arunachal MP - Indian Express
Content:
The flood situation in Assam has turned from bad to worse with the lone National Highway linking the Northeast to the rest of the country being cut off at two places, while the Army was deployed in Kamrup and Nalbari district on Sunday to rescue the marooned people. Army helicopters were also pressed into service to rescue people and drop food packets.

While the National Highway 31 was already cut off near Srirampur on the Assam-West Bengal on Friday night, the same highway was also overtopped by flood waters from the Puthimari between Rangiya and Kamalpur in Kamrup district on Sunday morning, cutting off road link between Guwahati and Lower Assam.

Army columns from the 21 Red Horns Division at Rangiya were sent out early on Sunday after the Puthimari breached its embankments at three places north of the highway and submerged at least 40 villages in the vicinity, Army PRO Col Rajesh Kalia said.

Incessant rains in Bhutan have caused every river coming down to Assam to swell with the Saralbhanga and Sonkosh affecting over 10,000 people in Kokrajhar. The Pagladiya and Mora-Pagladiya on the other hand have inundated at least 50 villages in Baska and Nalbari district. In Darrang district, the Nonoi river breached embankments at six spots and has affected over 25 villages, while the Beki and Manas have rendered homeless at least 5000 people in Barpeta district.

But the worst has been in Majuli, the world's largest inhabited river island in Upper Assam, where 1.40 lakh out of its total population of 1.65 lakh have been seriously affected. "As many as 140 of the island's 160 villages are under water, and at least 74 families have lost their homestead as the Brahmaputra has caused severe erosion in addition to inundation," Arindam Barua, extra assistant commissioner, Majuli, told The Indian Express over the phone.

Majuli is experiencing its third wave of floods since Friday, with the Brahmaputra's water that entered through breaches that were already caused in the first wave that began on July 25, cutting off the vital Pahumara-Jengrai-Garamur-Haldibari road at several points. "Flood waters that had entered the island during the first two waves were yet to drain out when the third wave came," Barua said, adding that the island was witnessing the worst floods in five years.

Heading: CPI urges EC to assess situation in South Bastar - Indian Express
Content:
A prompt issuance of visa by China has left BJP MP from Arunachal Pradesh Kiren Rijiju "surprised" who said it indicated a "positive" change in Beijing's attitude and could pave the way for resolving the border dispute, particularly over Tawang.

Rijiju, who represents Tawang constituency in Arunachal Pradesh in the Lok Sabha, has been till now critical of China for "denying" visas to chief ministers, ministers and MPs from the state who are diplomatic passport holders.

"But I was surprised when they granted me visa without any hitch and I went to Beijing without any problem as part of a delegation comprising five MPs to watch Olympic Games from August 15," Rijiju said on phone after returning from Xian, the ancient city which once used to be the capital of China, on Saturday night.

The delegation also included MP Sachin Pilot and Indian Olympic Association head Suresh Kalmandi.

"This is the first time China granted visa to a Arunachalee diplomatic passport holder and I feel with my visit a historical breakthrough has been achieved," Rijiju said.

The MP said with China "issuing visa to me is a big step forward in restoring normal relations between the two nations".

Referring to recent statement of National Security Advisor M K Narayanan that dispute over Tawang, an important Buddhist enclave on Sino-India border and birth place of the sixth Dalai Lama, is preventing efforts by two countries to cross the rubicon, Rijiju said the Government should make public what the Chinese want.

The dispute over Tawang could be settled if any minor adjustment was required in the spirit of give and take with the people consent, Rijiju said. Tawang is an area with substantial population and both Rijiju and Chief Minister Dorjee Khandu hail from there.

Recently four Chinese engineers hired by a private company came to Arunachal with visas to work in an oilfield in Changlang but they had to return following a protest by Rijiju, who contended that till China issues visas to Arunachalees, no Chinese could work in the state.

Heading: ‘Urban Cowboy’ lived too long on wild side - Indian Express
Content:
Ahead of the coming assembly polls, the Communist Party of India (CPI) has urged the Election Commission to depute its own team to make an assessment about the present situation in 'Salwa Judum' camps in Naxalite-infested areas of South Bastar, alleging that the inmates were being forcibly enrolled as voters of the polling centres to be set up at the relief camps.

"A large number of people, who were staying in the relief camp for the last three years, have already returned to their respective villages. Their names have been deleted from the electoral rolls of their native villages and have been added in the voters' list of the relief camp area", CPI leader and All India Adivasi Mahasabha President Manish Kunjam said in his letter to the Election Commission.

"Its not proper to deprive the people, who have returned to their respective villages, an opportunity to exercise their franchise in the polling stations close to their native villages", he said and claimed that CPI had raised this issue with Dantewara and Bijapur district collectors, who have expressed their 'inability' to do anything to enlist them as voters in their villages.

Pointing out that those who became eligible to cast their votes for the first time have been enlisted as voters of relief camp areas,

Kunjam said in such a situation free and fair polls were not possible both in Dantewara and Bijapur districts, particularly in the relief camps, which are "controlled" 'Salwa Judum' activists.

Kunjam, a former CPI legislator, told The Indian Express that the Commission should depute its own team to look into the matter as such 'manipulations' in the preparations of electoral rolls clearly indicated towards the possibility of bogus voting and even rigging in the assembly polls.

Kunjam said he had also written a letter to the Election Commission, pointing out that the staff, engaged in the revision of electoral rolls, did not visit more than 50 out of the total 187 polling station areas falling in the Konta (ST) Assembly segment in South Bastar.

However, the state's Joint Electoral Officer Gaurav Dwivedi told The Indian Express that the list of relief camp inmates, eligible to cast votes, were being prepared and tallied with the electoral rolls of their respective villages.

Heading: Adoption racket: rights body seeks govt intervention - Indian Express
Content:
When time magazine hit the stands on January 6, 2005, it was of particular interest to a policeman in Mumbai. The coveted cover photograph of the magazine showed a burly man with a deadeye stare on his face holding up an AK-47 assault rifle, and the caption read: 'Killer Instinct: Inspector Sharma stands armed and ready'. The cover story was titled 'Urban Cowboys' and featured Police Inspector Pradeep Sharma. With a larger than life persona and one-liners dripping of machismo such as 'Criminals are filth; and I'm the cleaner', Sharma (49) rose to fame and notoriety as the Mumbai Police's top 'encounter specialist', having gunned down 112 gangsters and criminals in a career spanning over two decades.

Early on Sunday, Sharma was dismissed from the force after Mumbai Police Commissioner Hasan Gafoor served him dismissal orders under Article 311 of the Constitution for his 'unsatisfactory prior record'. His dismissal followed a probe into his alleged links with the underworld. He joined the police force in 1983, and his batchmates included other famous encounter specialists such as Vijay Salaskar, Praful Bhonsle, Arun Borude and Ravindra Angre. Like them, Sharma has always courted controversies with allegations of Dawood Ibrahim links being levelled against him.

During the initial stages of his career, Sharma's posting at the Anti Narcotics Cell enabled him to build a strong network of contacts in the city's murky underworld. In the late 1990's, when gangland shootouts were at their peak and telephones were ringing off the hook with extortion threats to builders and Bollywood personalities, 'special squads' were formed to deal with the problem 'bullet for bullet'. Sharma was one of the officers chosen for the job on account of their strong networks. He was posted as the head of the Crime Branch's elite Crime Intelligence Unit (CIU), leading a squad of encounter specialists that included his one time protige Daya Nayak.

Some notorious criminals slain in operations supervised by Sharma include Dawood Ibrahim's close aide Sadiq Kalya at Dadar in 1999, Rafiq Dabbawala of the Subhash Thakur gang in 2001, Vinod Matkar of the Chhota Rajan gang, as well as three alleged LeT terrorists in 2003. He led a team responsible for the seizure of a huge cache of arms and ammunition sent by Chhota Rajan at Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust on May 21, 2005 that was hailed as a major victory in the fight against the underworld.

For a while, he was also heading the Crime Branch's Anti Extortion Cell. His later postings included

Kandivali and D N Nagar police stations.

In October 2006, Sharma along with five other policemen was transferred out of Mumbai to Amravati, when they were being probed for the alleged custody death of 2002 Ghatkopar bomb blast accused Khwaja Yunus. Sharma was then exonerated by the state CID in July 2007, and was posted at the main control room at the Mumbai Police headquarters and then at Dharavi police station.

On April 9 this year, Deputy Chief Minister R R Patil announced that an official probe would be initiated into allegations levelled against Sharma in the House by Leader of the Opposition (Shiv Sena) Ramdas Kadam, who alleged that Sharma was hand in glove with Dawood Ibrahim and had amassed property to the tune of Rs 5,000 crore. He also alleged that the policeman was involved in slum rehabilitation authority (SRA) schemes. Kadam also linked Sharma to 'matka-boss' Pappu Sawla and builders.

Heading: Infiltration along International Border underscores BSF vulnerability - Indian Express
Content:
The National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) has written to the Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary seeking the state government's intervention in the case of illegal adoption of Indian children in Australia.

According to a report, a gang of criminals active in South India recently kidnapped at least 30 children and sold them to "adoption" agencies who, in turn, shifted them to countries like Australia for "adoption" by affluent childless families. Some children are believed to have been taken from the streets by gangs who sold them for as little as Rs 10,000 to an adoption agency "Malaysian Social Services" based in Tiruverkadu in Chennai.

"We want to know what action has been taken against the agencies involved in illegal adoption," said Sandhya Bajaj, member, NCPCR. The Commission will also get in touch with the Australian Embassy to see how these children can be repatriated to India. "The priority is to get back those children," added another official.

A case in point is a nine-year-old girl who was abducted by a gang in Chennai a few years ago and is currently living in Queensland under a new name. Though the girl was adopted through the Queensland Department of Families, Youth and Community Care, the adoptive family has now been apprised of the situation and is keen on finding out the truth. The Central Bureau of Intelligence (CBI) has also intervened in the case and had sent an Interpol request to Australia to interview the Queensland authorities and the foster parents.

According to estimates, at least 30 of the almost 400 Indian children brought into Australia in the past 15 years were victims of trafficking. "While, adoption in India is a lengthy process, it is to be investigated how this agency was doing it and that too in a country like Australia," an official said.

Heading: Baba at bar: Exit dancers and music, enter Ramdev - Indian Express
Content:
Life on the International Border is never easy but the last few days have been especially harrowing for Ram Krishna Sharma. Sharma has a farm just inside the border fence, metres from the spot where three militants sneaked in on Monday night as Pakistani gunmen provided covering fire.

As the Jammu region hobbles to normal after the violent and crippling Amarnath protests, Sharma has got a chance to sell his produce of brinjals. But the infiltration has probably put paid to any chances he had of persuading daily-wage labourers to work on his field.

The situation reminds him of the days before the 2003 ceasefire agreement was signed with Pakistan, he says. When frequent firing from across the border had put a complete stop to all farming, and put a bullet in his thigh.

India believes that the spate of ceasefire violations over the past few months ''over 30 instances at last count'' does not mean the agreement has become irrelevant. But at ground zero, both troops and farmers have reasons to differ.

On Monday, more than 30 heavily armed Pakistanis, suspected to be Rangers, crossed the International Border near Lalyan in Kanachak and took up positions along the electrified barbed wire fence erected to keep out infiltrators.

From behind a mud 'bund' originally constructed to protect workers building the fence, they opened heavy machine-gun fire on two Border Security Force (BSF) posts. "The firing was so heavy that we could not even stand in the post, bullets were hissing past our ears," says a BSF jawan who faced the barrage.

When the Pakistanis finally withdrew after two hours of heavy firing, at least three militants had sneaked in. And Pakistan had —- with the first-ever incident of cross-border firing in this stretch of the border —- managed to open another route for infiltrators who have traditionally entered by crossing the Line of Control.

Yet, it was Pakistan that claimed to have been wronged. At the flag meeting on Tuesday, the Pakistani side, led by Wing Commander Tariq Ahmed Abbasi of the Pakistan Rangers, accused India of violating the ceasefire agreement. "Aapne puri raat firing kari. Maine to itni bardasht Kargil mein bhi nahin ki thi. Bahut muskhil se sambhala apne jawano ko," he told the Indian side led by a BSF Company Commander.

A somewhat befuddled BSF is now hastily digging new bunkers and setting up four new observation posts in Kanachak. The knee-high grass is being cut; sentries have been posted strategically along the fields. Concentrated firing from across the border can, however, still put the arrangement into disarray.

Heading: Govt schools to go hi-tech with gensets, projectors, webcams - Indian Express
Content:
Mumbai was taken by surprise when it was announced that the once popular watering hole, Deepa Bar, would undergo an unusual makeover. It will turn into yoga guru Baba Ramdev's Mumbai headquarters, where he will hold classes whenever he is in the city. The bar was shut down six years ago. Its owner, Sudhakar Shetty, has been a follower of Baba Ramdev for the past seven years.

"Fifteen years ago, my father used to run Santosh Lunch Home, a family restaurant, here. Then we leased it out and one Ashok Rai converted the place into a bar," said Shetty. After his father's death, Shetty decided not to sell the property. He set up a trust dedicated to his parents, the Varija Mallappa Charitable Trust, which will transfer the property to Baba Ramdev's Patanjali Yog Peeth.

Shetty, who is a builder and the chairman of Sahana Group of companies, said the ashram — on the 8,000 sq ft property — would offer free treatment to the poor. Twice a week, free food will be distributed to the needy. Lessons will be imparted on pranayam and doctors would also stay inside the ashram.

"When I informed Baba Ramdev that the place was earlier a bar, he did not raise any objection. Instead, he asked me to hurry up so that he could come and stay here as soon as the ashram was ready," said Shetty, adding that it would take at least five months before the makeover is complete.

When asked about the response he has received so far regarding his intention of converting one of Mumbai's most popular bars into an ashram, Shetty said most people had good things to say. He added that the staff of Deepa Bar must have found alternative jobs by now and he was willing to employ those who hadn't as yet found a job.

Deepa Bar had been at the centre of controversy more than once. In September 2005, the bar figured in a match-fixing controversy that later led police to question Sri Lankan cricketer Muttiah Muralitharan about his alleged liaisons with bar dancer Tarannum Khan, who herself was in the news after IT officials raided her house and found inordinate amount of money. The bar was in the news in early 2005 after seven people opened fire inside the bar. It was once a favourite hotspot for bureaucrats, politicians, businessmen and Bollywood stars. However, Shetty claimed he had no clue regarding the bar's controversies, as all that happened at a time when the management was not in his hands.

On Saturday, the foundation stone for the ashram was laid in the presence of Baba Ramdev and Shetty claimed that nearly 5,000 people witnessed the programme, despite rains. Commenting on the makeover, Baba Ramdev was all praise for Shetty.

Heading: Access to health info cuts maternal mortality rate - Indian Express
Content:
Camcorders, LCD projectors, web cameras,more computers in the lab, gensets in power supply affected areas and over lakh new teachers who come with a set of Information Technology (IT) skills, will soon be a reality in all secondary and higher secondary government schools. The Human Resource Development (HRD) ministry is bringing Rs 6,000 crore plan for Expenditure Finance Committee's (EFC) approval shortly.

The ministry is also open to the idea of a public-private partnership (PPP) on a five year Build-Operate-Own-Transfer (BOOT) model as is done by some state governments to help implement the ambitious scheme.

For government schools struggling with power supply, limited computers and lack of teachers, the decision to bring in new age ancillaries like web cameras, camcorders and projectors was needed as part of a larger programme to ensure children are not left behind when the Information & Communication Technology (ICT) revolution is transforming the world.

Scaling up the computer aided teaching employed in elementary schools under the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), the ministry is putting together a revamped ICT scheme for all 1.8 lakh secondary and higher secondary schools. The scheme to be rolled out later this year will equip school children with skills required to perform word processing, power point, spreadsheets, use internet for academics amongst other things.

To be spread out over the 11th plan period, the scheme will effectively roll out with an allocation of Rs 5,500 crores as Rs 500 crore has already been used to bring in labs and hardware to some 20,000 schools in the past two years of the plan period. The ministry having a large amount for the purpose has decided to invest not only in providing hardware to schools but in plugging the gaping vacuum of qualified teachers.

There will be two funding formulae for implementation of the scheme — one on 75:25 Centre-state sharing basis and the other 90:10 sharing basis for special category states in the North-East, J&K and Uttarakhand. Each school will approximately get Rs 7.65 lakh each per annum under the scheme.

"While the scheme will help schools get more computers, LCD projectors, camcorders and gensets besides the very critical qualified faculty factor, the focus will be on recruiting over a lakh teachers trained in ICT skills so that they can function not only as highly trained faculty but also double up as IT administrators, troubleshooters and e-content developers. The private sector, being the drivers of IT revolution will be of immense help in putting the scheme in place. Many big firms like Intel and Microsoft besides a host of others have already been doing a lot of work in this direction as part of their Corporate Social Responsibility initiative", said an official from the ministry.

"Getting dedicated teachers is a major thrust area as at present most schools have teachers with only basic computer skills. Still further, they are paid meagerly for this. Under the new scheme, teachers will be recruited at a salary of Rs 10,000 per month at least for classes 9th to 12th," the official said.

Schools will also get camcorders and projectors intended at helping students harness their creativity, make films and even run them for the school .

Heading: Lucknow boy headed for Arctic voyage - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the latest UNICEF report has found that the present maternal mortality rate in India leaves the country lagging in meeting the United Nations' proposed Millennium Development Goals, a pilot study by the Directorate of Health Services indicates that access to health information and services made available to married adolescents have helped in reducing the maternal mortality rate in Maharashtra. If these surveys are replicated in other states, the health authorities believe, much progress can be made.

According to state health statistics, in Maharashtra, 49 per cent rural women and 29 per cent urban women are married by the age of 18 years. Even the fertility rate is higher in Maharashtra between 15 to 19 years - compared to the national rates. While in the rest of India, the percentage of women getting married before 18 years is 44 per cent, in Maharashtra it is 48.8 per cent. "These were some of the reasons why we decided to choose married adolescents. At present there is no exclusive policy for adolescents and the focus on married adolescent girls is limited," said Dr Prakash Doke, Director of Health Services, Maharashtra.

The pilot study undertaken along with the Institute of Health Management, Pachod (IHMP) indicates that marriageable age among adolescent girls had gone up from 16 to 17 years, thereby delaying the first conception by a year. The intervention programme began in 2003 and 10 most backward districts, having a high proportion of married girls, were selected for randomised control trial. "The area had accounted for 3-5 per cent or more of neo-natal deaths and even more abortions. 65 per cent had severe complications with many of them ending in infertility all their life," added another official. A Dayalchand, director, IHMP, pointed out that the increase in marriageable age had in turn reduced the percentage of low-weight babies from 35 per cent to 25 per cent in rural areas and from 27 per cent to 18 per cent in urban areas.

The interventions made by the agencies through workshops, door-to-door surveillance and disseminating information made such an impact that use of contraceptives also saw a rise from 10.9 per cent to 23 per cent in rural areas and from 8 to 30 per cent in urban areas. The age groups surveyed by the health agencies range from 13-35 years.

Heading: Pact reached over Amarnath land, Jammu agitation finally suspended - Indian Express
Content:
Jawahar Nagar is a posh locality in uptown Srinagar where plush homes hide behind freshly built shopping arcades, cyber cafes and beauty parlours. Today, it is empty and desolate. There are only soldiers sitting on the pavements holding guns and batons. The lanes are stinky. For the last several days municipal workers have not emptied the road-side garbage dumps. At the end of the lane, a three storey house stands stark.

The door is open; it is quiet inside. Rehana (27) is cradling her child. Her husband Tariq Ahmad Sofi (30) is busy making a paste of cooked rice. Their first child Annan is 14-month-old but they cannot feed him solid food. Five weeks ago, Annan went through a surgery to seal his congenital cleft palate. The doctors advised that the child be fed only 'semi solid diet' — Cerelac, Ferni, churned bananas or milk.  But there is nothing at home, not even milk.

"The curfew was imposed suddenly and nobody anticipated that it would be so strict. They (CRPF men) don't even let us step out of the front door," says Annan's grandfather, Abdul Rashid Sofi. Tariq says he tried to get some baby food and milk. "It is impossible. They come chasing. A few elders had come out in the morning and they beat them up," he says.

Tariq tries to feed his starving son with the rice paste. But Annan cannot swallow it and vomits.Annan's grandmother Saleema Begum, meanwhile, has slipped out, risking her life to find milk for him. Everyone is anxious but nobody dares to move. After an hour of anxiety, Saleema Begum returns with the milk. For the first time in the day, Annan is fed. "There is a family in a neighbouring locality where a woman rears a cow. So I went there and begged her for some milk," Saleema Begum says. She had, in fact, walked almost a mile to Padshahi Bagh through narrow lanes and people's courtyards, avoiding the security men.

 Milk and baby food shortage is not the only worry for Rehana. Annan needs a regular examination by the doctor after the surgery. "How can we take him to the doctor? There is no way to call for help and it is dangerous to go out. We don't even know whether the doctor is able to leave his home or not," she says.

The family has other worries too. The food stocks in the house are depleting. Their menu has been restricted to rice, pulses and dried vegetables.  "We haven't had a cup of tea for days. We are used to noon chai (salt tea) and there is no milk," says Saleema Begum.

She says that she used to dry vegetables in the summer and store them for the harsh winter days when vegetables are scarce in Kashmir. "It is for the first time, we had to eat dry vegetables in summer," she says. The family does not even have a kitchen garden because there is hardly any land around the house.

The family has one thing to cheer about. They have bartered a LPG gas cylinder for vegetables for dinner. "Our neighbours have a small garden in their courtyard where they grow vegetables. They were short of cooking gas. So they gave us some fresh vegetables and we gave them our spare gas cylinder," she says.

Heading: In Valley, NC and Cong welcome pact, PDP and separatists reject ‘unilateral’ deal - Indian Express
Content:
The two-month old agitation in Jammu over the Amarnath land transfer issue was suspended today after the J&K government and the group spearheading the agitation signed an accord to allow the shrine board to make temporary use of 40 hectares of land in Kashmir during the Amarnath Yatra period.
