The panchayat elections, which the previous Government had not held for reasons best known to it, brought a new meaning to people's participation at the grassroots level, and with it society also got its first taste of women's empowerment.

Tackling unemployment too was a tough job, especially in a state where industrial activity and big investments have by and large remained absent. But a self-help group (SHG) movement that we triggered off within a few months of assuming office brought about an unbelievable silent revolution, and today we not only have over 1.50 lakh SHGs but also an atmosphere where the unemployed no longer looks just at the Government as an employment-provider. With panchayats in place, Central funds too started flowing in, and today Assam's rural economy is at such a level that per capita income has shot up from Rs 10,718 in 2001-02 to an amazing Rs 22,081 in 2007-08.

The GDP, which stood at a dismal 2.1 per cent in 2001, has gone up to 8 per cent. And, thanks to the people's positive mindset that we could bring about, Assam is today considered the fastest mover in overall rankings among all states of the country as revealed by an in-depth survey conducted by a leading magazine of the country.

Rural and overall economy also received a massive boost with our focus on road communication, and, while most roads have been repaired, we also added over 8,550 kms of road-length apart from 887 concrete bridges in the past seven years. It was only last week that Prime Minister Manmohan Singh agreed to our proposal of constructing four more bridges across the Brahmaputra, which will take up the total number of bridges on the river to nine by 2013. Sanctioning four bridges on the Brahmaputra at one go by a Prime Minister is not just a never-before decision, it is also a gesture of the UPA Government's genuine interest and commitment towards balanced development of the country with special emphasis on Assam and the Northeast. Work on the East-West Corridor is going on in full swing while more trains and flights are coming into Assam from different regions of the country today.

It is true that we had to take loans from the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to tide over our power shortage and financial problems. Without these loans, it would not have been possible to pull the state out of the morass that it was in when we took over. It was a tripartite agreement with the Centre and the ADB in 2004 that got us Rs 543.47 crore to bring about fiscal discipline in the state. An internal report of the ADB has already praised Assam for having overtaken states like Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Kerala in the field of economic and fiscal reforms.

It was my Government that completed the 100-MW Karbi Langpi hydel project where 27 years were wasted in the name of construction. We also recently handed over the Bongaigaon Thermal Power Station to NTPC which will soon add 750 MW of power to our system. Similarly, construction of the Bogibeel bridge on the Brahmaputra was speeded up only after I took over.

One area where we are paying maximum attention is the younger generation. And my particular focus has been on education and knowledge. Assam is the first state in the country to provide computers to every high school, and also the first in providing a computer to every student who secured first division in high school final examinations. Thousands of school students have been sent on educational excursion to various parts of the state under the 'Gyanjyoti' programme, and one lakh girl students from BPL families have been given bicycles. Investing in education is definitely the best one can do, and we have not only rebuilt almost every primary school in the state, but now we are also waiting for a world-class university to take off. We will soon have a Knowledge City and a Science City near Guwahati, so that our young people may acquire maximum knowledge and equip themselves with skills that make them employable. Engineering colleges, technical schools and polytechnics have already received a new lease of life due to fresh investments while the pass percentage of students in various examinations has more than doubled in the past few years.

Health care too has undergone revolutionary changes, and a steady flow of funds, coupled with a better atmosphere has helped the Government health machinery win back the people's confidence. We have opened evening OPDs in all government hospitals while IMR and MMR have come down significantly in recent years. We are also the first to have introduced health and accident insurance for the people, and today pacemakers and chemotherapy too have become free for most categories of people.

Yes, we have several major problems too, two most important being floods and infiltration. We are happy that the UPA Government has taken keen interest in solving the flood and erosion problem, and it was only last week that the Prime Minister said funds would not be a problem. Unlike our predecessors, we have taken a practical two-pronged approach to tackle influx from Bangladesh. One is to immediately put a full stop to fresh influx; and two, to speed up the process of detection and deportation under the prevalent laws and the Assam Accord. We are also updating the National Register of Citizens (NRC) so that every post-1971 infiltrator could be detected, for which the UPA Government has given us its full backing.

But the biggest achievements that I would claim are: (a) changing the mindset of the people from a state of depression to optimism, and (b) changing the perception and image of Assam outside. Assam is no longer a land of 'lahe lahe' (laid-back attitude) and frequent bandhs. The younger generation is dreaming big, beginning to work hard, is willing to take risks and become successful in life. People outside too are changing their opinion about Assam. Insurgency is beginning to become a thing of the past, and big (industrial) houses are eyeing Assam as their next destination for investment. But I am clear about one thing: I am not for uprooting farmers to set up big industries. We welcome eco-friendly industries and units based on natural resources which do not disturb the environment. Assam, after all, is still one of the greenest states in the country.

Heading: Samiti to continue Jammu struggle - Indian Express
Content:
A day after the state Government reached an agreement with the Shri Amarnath Sangarsh Samiti (SASS), ending the two-month-long agitation, three top separatist leaders — Syed Ali Shah Geelani, Mirwaiz Umar Farooq and Yasin Malik — were released on Monday. However, another separatist leader, Shabir Shah, is still booked under Public Safety Act (PSA). "We have released three leaders today," Inspector General of J-K Police, Kashmir range, S M Sahai told The Indian Express.

Sources in the Government said the decision to release the separatist leaders was taken to calm tempers in Kashmir soon after the agitation was called off in Jammu. The release was, sources said, also due to the fact that Tuesday marks the beginning of the holy month of Ramazan.

With the release of these separatist leaders, the Government has sent a message that it wants to restart a dialogue with the moderate separatists. However, it would be extremely difficult for the moderates, especially the Hurriyat faction, to publicly engage in a dialogue with New Delhi.

Since the Amarnath land row, Syed Ali Shah Geelani-led Hurriyat has substantially strengthened, especially when the two factions were united after almost six years of division. In fact, Mirwaiz Umar Farooq visited Geelani's home and after a seven-hour-long closed door meeting decided to put up a joint forum. Shabir Shah, sources said, was pivotal in bringing Geelani and Mirwaiz together. As a result, the Government would now re-open an old case against him in New Delhi, sources said.

The Valley, meanwhile, is still simmering even as the Government on Monday relaxed curfew across Kashmir, except in 13 police stations in old Srinagar. Three persons were wounded as J-K police and CRPF fired rubber bullets to disperse the mob. Following the protests, the police decided against relaxing curfew in 10 police stations of the downtown city. At Hyderpora, where Hurriyat hardliner Syed Ali Geelani stays, curfew was re-imposed at 3.30 in the afternoon, apprehending a procession at the time of Geelani's release. Geelani was taken to a hospital after he complained of sickness in police custody.

Heading: Mamata’s peace talk: Nano work should resume - Indian Express
Content:
Even as Jammu returned to normal routine on Monday after two months of agitation, the Shri Amarnath Sangharsh Samiti (SASS) planned to launch another front to tackle the "discrimination meted out to Jammu during the last 60 years by the Kashmir-centric leadership".

Sources close to the SASS revealed that a new committee would be formed after the core committee of the Samiti meets and discusses this issue. After 62 days of sustaining the agitation for land, the Samiti's latest slogan hints that the struggle is far from over: "Yeh to bus angdai hai, agey aur ladai hai (It is just the beginning, there are more agitations to come)." This particular slogan was raised even as Samiti leaders emerged from the government guest house where the fourth round of talks were held and the agreement between the two sides was signed.

Talking about the perceived "discriminatory" treatment meted out to Jammu, SASS leader Brig (retd) Suchet Singh said: "Our core committee will meet soon and this issue will be discussed so that the new committee could be given a proper shape. We will choose people who have shown exemplary resilience during this agitation."

The city, meanwhile, seemed relieved to see the end of the current agitation. After a spell of curfews, Monday saw a large number of people thronging vegetable markets, milk shops, provision stores. Jammu also experienced a traffic jam after almost two months with people rushing to their respective workplaces and children going to schools. A special prayer was organised at the Raghunath temple and other shrines across the region.

Deputy Commissioner of Jammu, Mandeep K Bhandari, said, "Jammu is normal now. All government offices have resumed work." He added that the Army deployment has been withdrawn.

All commercial establishments, banks, warehouses, institutions, cinema halls and restaurants were thrown open, bringing life back on track in the city. Inspector General of Police (Jammu zone) K Rajendra Kumar said the curfew was lifted in all districts, excluding Poonch.

Heading: Cong, SP agree to joint campaign in UP, candidate list major hurdle - Indian Express
Content:
For the first time since work was suspended at the Tata's small car factory at Singur due to a dharna by Mamata Banerjee, the Trinamool leader has urged the Tatas to start work in the factory.

She has hinted that there would not be any more blockades or attempts to stop work at the factory. Monday was the fourth consecutive day that work was suspended at the factory.

"We want immediate solution to the crisis. We are not against the Tatas," said Mamata. She urged the state Government not to resort to petty politics by influencing the closure of the factory. "The Government should immediately take steps to begin work at the factory," Mamata said. She, however, did not forget to toe her old line about the co-existence of farmers and industry.

"We are not against industrialisation. What we want is that there should be a peaceful co-existence between farmers and industries," she said. She blamed the state Government for creating a situation where both farming and factory work had to be stopped.

Mamata again reiterated her stand on holding talks and deliberations. "We are always open to talks. But the state Government's attitude to the Singur issue has been negative. Otherwise, the problem would have not lasted for two years."

The National Highway remained closed at the dharna site for the ninth consecutive day on Monday. Several intellectuals like Saoli Mitra and Aparna Sen appeared on the dharna manch. Mother and brother of Rizwanur Rehman also delivered speeches from the manch. Kabir Suman and Saoli Mitra enthralled the audience.

Heading: Gowda supports Maya as head of Third Front - Indian Express
Content:
While the Congress and Samajwadi Party agreed to "joint campaigning" in Uttar Pradesh for the next Lok Sabha elections at their first meeting to discuss seat-sharing on Monday, the news from the talks is likely to give many heavyweights in the two parties sleepless nights.

Among the Congress candidates the SP said no to were UPCC chief Salman Khursheed for the Farrukhabad Lok Sabha seat, Raj Babbar for Fatehpur Sikri, Beni Prasad Verma for Gonda, Begum Noor Bano for Moradabad or Rampur, P L Punia (former principal secretary to the UP Chief Minister) for Barabanki, Ratna Singh for Pratapgarh, and R P N Singh for Kushinagar.

SP leaders Amar Singh and Ram Gopal Yadav, who represented the party at the talks, would have nothing to do with former party colleagues Raj Babbar and Beni Prasad Verma. The party also wants to field its own candidates on other contentious seats, for instance Jaya Prada from Rampur, Baleshwar Yadav from Kushinagar, and Chandra Bhoosan Singh from Farrukhabad.

"Among the two we may agree on Raj Babbar because he is a winnable candidate, but we don't see any chance for Verma," confided a senior SP leader.

Not to be outdone by the SP, which did not hesitate to flaunt its "big brotherly status" in UP, Congress interlocutors including Digvijay Singh, Rahul Gandhi and Rita Bahuguna Joshi emphasised on "clean image of the candidates" apart from "winnability" to be the determinant factors for selection, according to sources. This may have been directed at Raja Bhaiyya's confidant Akshay Pratap Singh, who is eyeing Pratapgarh.

Also figuring on the Congress list of candidates submitted on Monday were PCC chief Rita Bahuguna Joshi from Allahabad, Union Minister Jitin Prasada from Dhaurara, and Jagdambika Pal from Domariaganj.

Amar Singh was learnt to have asked the Congress about its reported plans of an alliance with the RLD. The latter clarified that while they considered the RLD a secular party, Ajit Singh had to make it clear "whether he is with Mayawati or with us".

SP leaders reportedly also sought to expand the pre-poll alliance with the Congress beyond UP to Maharashtra, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh and Bihar. Rahul Gandhi is said to have assured them that he would convey this to Congress president Sonia Gandhi.

The Congress might have only nine seats from Uttar Pradesh in the present Lok Sabha, but it is eyeing "at least 25 to 30" out of the 80 seats. Its logic is simple: nine seats that were won last time, seven seats on which it came second, and three on which it came third but polled more than the SP. Apart from these 19, the Congress claims to have made inroads into many other seats, especially in the Bundelkhand region.

The argument put up by the Congress interlocutors on Monday was that delimitation of constituencies had changed caste equations drastically and the SP could, therefore, not start its count from the 2004 general election.

At Monday's meeting, while the Congress proposed candidates on "about two-third of the seats", the SP named its candidates on all 80 seats. Further talks will take place on September 8.

Heading: Cops deny foul play in Saraswati post-mortem - Indian Express
Content:
While saying that he has no ambition to the Third Front's throne, JD(S) chief H D Deve Gowda has said he will extend full support to BSP supremo Mayawati for the Front's top post.

He said on Monday a committee formed by representatives of all member parties would make the decision as other key members of the Front — the Left and TDP — were yet to make their stance clear.

"I will stand by Mayawati if she becomes the leader of the Third Front. I have no reservations and I also do not dream of becoming the Prime Minister once again," Deve Gowda told mediapersons here.

The Third Front comprising 11 parties, which was formed before the trust vote, lost momentum after the UPA Government won the vote. Projecting the Third Front as an 'alternative force' at the state party convention organised in the city, he said the party would hold rallies across the country to expose the UPA Government on issues such as price rise, neglect of the agriculture sector and farmer suicides.

Observing that his primary concern was ensuring that the JD(S) played an important role in national politics, he said he would hold conventions in states where the party did not have a strong presence like Rajasthan, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, UP and Maharashtra. Recently, the regional convention held in Tamil Nadu was well received, he said.

Heading: Karan Singh appeals to make up for losses - Indian Express
Content:
The Orissa Police on Monday said post-mortem was conducted on Swami Laxmanananda Saraswati and four others gunned down by unidentified attackers on August 23. The statement was issued following allegations by Congress leader Narasingha Mishra that post-mortem was not conducted on the victims. Director General of Police Gopal Chandra Nanda said post-mortem had been conducted as per guidelines followed in any murder case.

Apart from Saraswati, 84, three of his associates — Kishore Baba (45), Amritananda Baba (62) and Mata Bhaktimayee (40) — and Puranjan Ganthi (28), brother of a girl inmate of the Shankaracharya Kanyashram at Jalespeta, were killed by the attackers.

Mishra had said that in any murder case post-mortem report is of crucial importance at the trial stage. Since it was not done, the accused could never be brought to book.

A senior police official in Kandhamal refuted Mishra's allegations, saying he was present during the post-mortem on August 24. "Since the situation was sensitive, the post-mortem on Saraswati was done by doctors at Tumudibandha Government Hospital under tight security," the official said.

Chief Secretary Ajit Tripathy said the situation in Kandhamal and elsewhere in Orissa was under control. In the entire state, 558 houses and 17 places of worship were damaged or burnt in the riots following the VHP leader's killing. In Kandhamal, 185 people were arrested on charge of rioting, arson and other offences. A total of 35 people were injured in the riot in Kandhamal while 16 people have died in the riots.

Meanwhile, with law and order situation improving in riot-hit Kandhamal, day curfew was lifted on Monday. However, it remained in force at Jeypore of Koraput district, where 11 people were injured in clashes between Hindus and Christians on August 30.

Heading: Dhoot urges Tatas to talk directly to farmers - Indian Express
Content:
MP and former Governor of J-K Karan Singh has welcomed the agreement reached between the J-K Government and Shri Amarnath Sangharsh Samiti and called for all sections of society to accept it.

In a press statement issued on Monday, the MP said the need of the hour was a reconstitution of the Amarnath Shrine Board and making up for the losses incurred in terms of trade, commerce and tourism. For this the Centre, the state Government and the civil society should work together, he said.

"The autumn tourism season is still ahead of us, and it is imperative that normalcy be restored in the state so that the season is not disrupted," he said.

Heading: Abhaya: CBI says CD tampered with - Indian Express
Content:
Videocon chairman and former president of ASSOCHAM Venugopal N Dhoot has said the association is ready to talk to Ratan Tata to break the Singur deadlock. Dhoot was speaking to the media on Monday after a meeting with Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee at Writers' Buildings.

"Tatas should directly talk to the farmers. Their earnings are nearly Rs 100 crore a day and resolving this issue should not be a problem for them... I am ready to talk to the Tatas and I have already sought an appointment from him," Dhoot said.

The Videocon chairman, who plans to invest Rs 15,000 crore in steel and power projects in the state, said: "For all my projects, we are ready to offer three alternatives — cash, jobs or shares. We do not want to exploit farmers."

Heading: ‘Harassed’ nun quits order - Indian Express
Content:
The CBI which is probing the murder of Catholic nun Abhaya on Monday told the Kerala High Court that Central Forensic Laboratory in Bangalore had tampered with the CD of narco-analysis tests conducted on two priests and a nun.

CBI counsel A V S Namboothiri told judge V Ramkumar that the agency was ready for another round of narco tests at any other forensic lab and action should be taken against Bangalore lab assistant director Dr Malini, who, according to the CBI, had tampered with the CD.

Though the tests were held on October 17, 18, and 22, the CDs were handed over to the CBI on October 24. Namboothiri said that CBI official had visited the lab on October 23, asking for the CD. But the lab authorities were not ready to give it on that day.

He said the properties of the CD showed that it had been processed not during the working hours of the lab, indicating that the manipulation was done outside the lab.

The content and number of the CDs of the tests had been a bone of contention after the court had suspected that the CBI had manipulated the CDs to help the culprits. However, the CBI stuck to its stand.

Heading: Nun suicide: police say no arrest plans - Indian Express
Content:
A seniro Roman Catholic nun, who has been serving as the principal of St Mary's College, has quit her order, allegedly unable to withstand the harassment from Congregation of Mother Carmelite (CMC).

Sister Jesmy's decision to leave the Congregation and continue a nun's life is likely to emerge as a debate in the Catholic Church. Though several priests and nuns had abandoned the God's path, this is the first time that a nun had come forward to give vent to the pent-up.

Sister Jesmy (51), who had served as an English faculty in colleges under the Congregation before becoming St Mary's principal, has opted for VRS.

However, Sister Jesmy's family in Thrissur has so far not welcomed back its daughter who had left the home around 30 years back to become a bride of the Church. Jesmy told The Indian Express that she has no plans for a family life and would stay with her friends until she finds a new assignment. "No progressive nun can continue with CMC. I cannot be a naïve woman, who stands flummoxed at the murky affairs in the convent. Though I have left the Congregation, my faith in God is intact," said the PhD holder. She said CMC authorities are trying to project her as a deranged woman. A nun for 27 years, Jesmy said she was asked to attend a retreat at the controversial Divine Retreat Centre near Thrissur. "Had I gone there, the retreat authorities... would have subjected me to unnecessary medical treatment."

She said she was being targeted for protesting against the college's move to levy a hefty fee for self-financing courses. "It was also not a healthy trend to parade college girls for all rallies being organised by the Church for various issues," she said. "Convents have become torture houses. Many nuns silently suffer harassment. If you remain silent, you would be in the good books of the authorities. As an educated nun, if I do not react, who else would stand up against the torture?" she said.

"They did not even permit me to stay at home on the day my father expired. As per the present guidelines, a nun can get only a day's leave annually to spend with her family. I had taken up all the issues with Archbishop Andrews Thazathu who did not respond. Superior generals have become mere puppets in the hands of Bishops," she said.

Congregation spokesperson Sr Chrisline said that the allegations were baseless. "If the Congregation had any grudge towards Sr Jesmy, we would not have made her the principal of this prestigious college," Sr Chrisline said, adding, "She has the freedom to leave the convent and the Congregation respects her decision."

Heading: Govt revives madrasa plan - Indian Express
Content: The Crime Branch probing the suicide of nun Anupa Mary of Kollam told the Kerala HC on Monday that evidence suggested that the nun took the extreme step due to mental and sexual harassment at the convent. The police said that they have evidence against a senior nun, Superior Albina, but they don't plan to arrest her at this stage.

Heading: Fear of thugs adds to sorrow of marooned Kosi victims - Indian Express
Content:
Even as the Government is sitting over the proposal to set up a Central Madrasa Board, the HRD Ministry is coming out with a less controversial madrasa modernisation scheme which would include provisions to introduce "modern" subjects like computer science and mathematics.

The proposed scheme being voluntary in nature, the ministry hopes most madarsas would opt for it as the scheme includes a hiked pay package for madrasa teachers at par with government teachers.

The scheme would be worth Rs 625 crore and is learnt to have got the clearance of the Finance Ministry. The fully centrally funded scheme will be implemented through the National Institute of Open Schooling (NIOS).

The Government also proposes to make those madrasas, with a Minority Status Certificate, on par with NIOS study centres.It moots to train madrasa teachers under the District Institute of Education and Training.

The NCMEI proposal had insisted on eradicating gender- based educational disparity and discussed adopting a "non-polemical" approach to other religions. Many Muslim organisations had protested on the ground that it would harm the very spirit of the religious character of madrasas.

Heading: Tackling FLOOD FURY - Indian Express
Content:
Brothers Arun and Ashok Sah are desperately waiting for a boat to rescue them from Tikulia village in Madhepura district. But people in some of their neighbouring houses are not very keen. Sah's neighbours do not want to leave their village even though it is completely marooned, leaving them stranded on the roof for the past 14 days. They fear that their house would be looted by thugs, who are rumoured to be roaming the flooded villages on country-made boats.

Very few such incidents have been reported, but it's still enough to create a panic among the people who want to desperately cling on to their belongings, even at the cost of risking their lives.

"We have heard about houses being looted after they were abandoned by the owners. As a result, many people here don't want to leave the village," Arun Sah told The Indian Express over a mobile phone.

"But my brother and I are on the roof for the past 14 days. We have not eaten for the last two days. Please send a boat for us," he pleaded.

Arun's neighbours are well off and are well-stocked with food. But members of the National Disaster Rescue Force (NDRF), who are carrying out the evacuation exercise, say that there are a number of people who are refusing to leave their home and belongings.

"There are about 40-50 people in Dighi village in Purnea district who have been refusing to come out. Most of these belong to well-to-do families staying in double storey houses, who are not faced with shortage of food," said a NDRF jawan. He added that at one rescue mission, people in one such house gave him fresh drinking water. Another of his colleague said that he had come across extremely poor people who too were refusing to be evacuated.

"They asked us to bring food for them, but were not ready to come with us," he said.

Meanwhile, rescue operations were accelerated on Monday with the arrival of a number of additional boats. The Indian Express team saw 40 boats being pressed into service on Monday.

Heading: Brahmaputra flows over red mark, N-E road link cut off - Indian Express
Content:
Three people, including a child, were killed on Monday and at least 10 went missing when an Army boat rescuing flood victims capsized near Murliganj.

Here's how Bihar is coping with the situation:

w Water level has reduced from 1.90 lakh cusecs to 1.25 lakh cusecs

• 5 lakh people have been evacuated

• 200 camps are operational

• 1,300 boats have been deployed

• 86 medical centres have been opened

• Petroleum Ministry will provide 10,000 kl of kerosene and LPG cylinders

• Three more helicopters were being deployed

• Centre has provided 14 satellite phones to establish contact with marooned areas

• 5,767 tents have been dispatched and additional 1,922 tents are being organised

Heading: For penniless flood victims, relief cheques too costly - Indian Express
Content:
Floods continue to wreak havoc in Assam with the only road link to the entire Northeast, National Highway 31, getting snapped at two spots — one near Srirampur and the other between Rangiya and Guwahati — due to heavy floods that have already affected over 10 lakh people in the state. While road link remained cut off for the second day on Monday, railway services fortunately remained unaffected.

With rains continuing incessantly in Bhutan and Arunachal Pradesh, most of Brahmaputra's tributaries have been overflowing, breaching embankments and submerging human habitations and fields in several districts of the state. Road links to Nagaland and Manipur have remained cut off due to the sinking of a major portion of NH 39.

Heavy rain and thundershowers have been forecast for Assam and Arunachal Pradesh for the next two days.

Heading: The Encounter Endgame - Indian Express
Content:
The villagers of flood-affected Itaunja village on the outskirts of Lucknow have received relief cheques worth Rs 1,500 from the local administration but they were not able to encash them because the banks have asked them to open an account by making an initial deposit of Rs 500. And most villagers don't have the money.

Flood waters have washed away most of the houses of the eight villages in Itaunja and nearly 15,000 villagers have been rendered homeless. The administration started distributing the cheques about a week ago. But when the villagers went to encash their cheques in the bank they were asked to open accounts in the local branch. "I heard that banks offer a facility of having a zero-balance account but the bank have asked us to make an initial deposit of Rs 500," said Daulatram, the Gram Pradhan of Sultanpur village.

UCO Bank branch manager R K Gupta denied the allegations. However, when he was asked how many zero-balance accounts were opened with them in recent days, he failed to come up with the figure.

SDM Pawan Kumar Gangwar said, "The cheques deposited in UCO Bank were not cleared for some technical reason. Now, we are asking people to open an account with a deposit of Rs 500 or Rs 100."

Heading: Post-retirement, babus grab plum posts - Indian Express
Content:
Vijay Salaskar

Rank: Police Inspector

Profile: The son of a professor and a 1983 batch police officer like Pradeep Sharma, Salaskar is credited with having broken the backbone of the Arun Gawli and Amar Naik gangs. He shot to fame in 1997 when he killed Naik in an encounter. Some of his other well-known victims are Gawli aides Sada Pawle and Vijay Tandel, Sadhu Shetty, Jaggu Shetty, Kundan Singh Rawat and Zahoor Makhanda. Salaskar was posted as head of the Anti-Robbery Squad of the Crime Branch, and was shifted to the Anti-Terrorist Squad in the wake of the 7/11 serial blasts. Over the years, a marked rift appeared between batchmates Salaskar and Sharma. Salaskar has gunned down over 75 criminals to date.

status: He is the only famed encounter specialist who has not fallen from grace, with no criminal cases or probe against him. Currently, he is posted as head of the Anti-Extortion Cell of the Mumbai Police.

Daya Nayak

Rank: Police Sub-Inspector

Profile: Hailing from Yennehole village in the Udipi district of Karnataka, Nayak moved to Mumbai to earn a living in 1979. He worked for some time at an Udipi restaurant, and was encouraged to complete his education by its owner. Nayak joined the police force in 1995 at Juhu police station. While he was posted at the Crime Intelligence Unit, he soon shot to fame as a crackshot. Nayak, known for his intelligence network, was popular in Bollywood circles. The film Ab Tak Chhappan is based on his life. Actor Amitabh Bachchan was present during the inauguration of a school set up by Nayak at his native village. Nayak has killed 84 criminals.

status: In 2003, former journalist Ketan Tirodkar submitted a private complaint at the special MCOCA court alleging that he, along with Nayak, had acted at the behest of the mafia. However, while the police later filed a chargesheet against Tirodkar under MCOCA, Nayak was cleared for lack of evidence.

In January 2006, the Anti-Corruption Bureau raided Nayak's residence and booked him for having assets disproportionate to his known sources of income. After a non-bailable warrant was issued against him, Nayak surrendered and was taken into custody. He was immediately suspended from his post at Charkop police station. Nayak is still under suspension, but the ACB is yet to file a chargesheet against him.

Praful Bhonsle

Rank: Police Inspector

Profile: A 1983 officer, Bhonsle is credited with having slain Chhota Shakeel aides Arif Kalia and Anwar Badshah as well as Chhota Rajan sharpshooter Arun Mahajan. In 1987, he killed three alleged Khalistani militants in an operation at Vikhroli, for which he was awarded the police gallantry medal. In 2000, he was awarded the best investigating officer award. He has 75 encounter victims to his name.

status: Bhonsle is currently under a cloud of suspicion in the Khwaja Yunus custodial death case after he was named by the state CID in its probe. He was posted as head of the Ghatkopar unit of the Crime Branch, in whose custody Yunus died. He is currently under suspension.

Ravindra Angre

Rank: Police Inspector

Profile: Also a 1983 batch officer, Angre's most famous scalp is gangster Suresh Manckekar, who had over 30 cases of murder and extortion against him. Angre killed Manchekar in an encounter in Thane in 2003. Angre was posted at the Thane Anti-Extortion Cell at the time. While in the Mumbai Police Crime Branch, he eliminated some members of the Ashwin Naik gang, and was involved in a major seizure of assault rifles and grenades. He has slain over 60 criminals.

status: Angre was arrested in February this year, in a case of extortion and assault filed against him by Ganesh Wagh, a Thane-based builder. In his complaint, Wagh alleged Angre, along with three others, barged into his office and assaulted him. Angre allegedly wanted Wagh to make his wife a partner in his business, and also allegedly forced Wagh to sign a blank paper, besides taking away a Scorpio and Santro belonging to the builder. Angre, who was posted at Pune at the time, is presently in jail and under suspension.

Aslam Momin

Rank: Police Inspector

Profile: Yet another encounter specialist from the 1983 batch of policemen, Momin was posted at the Crime Intelligence Unit of the Crime Branch along with the likes of Sharma and Daya Nayak, though he maintained a low profile. While posted in charge of Unit 3 of the Crime Branch, Momin was handling sensitive cases like the probe into bookie Shobhan Mehta's connections with cricket players.

status: On July 22, 2005, then Mumbai Police Commissioner A N Roy dismissed Momin, using Article 311 of the Constitution, after evidence of telephonic conversations between Momin and Iqbal Kaskar were unearthed by the Crime Branch. Momin approached the Maharashtra Administrative Tribunal, which held that his dismissal was issued by the wrong authority. He is currently moving the authorities for his reinstatement.

Sachin Vaze

Rank: Assistant Police Inspector

Profile: Vaze was posted at the Crime Intelligence Unit of the Crime Branch in Andheri, and was Pradeep Sharma's right hand man. He took part in several encounters.

status: On March 3, 2004, Vaze was arrested by the state CID for murder and fabricating evidence in the Khwaja Yunus custodial death case. It was Vaze who had floated the theory that Yunus had fled after the jeep in which he was being taken to Aurangabad met with an accident on the Ahmednagar Highway.

Vaze was released on bail, following which he resigned from service.

Heading: CBI says proof shows accused-judiciary links - Indian Express
Content:
If you want lessons in post-retirement planning, turn to Chhattisgarh's bureaucrats who have found ways and means to rehabilitate themselves by taking up plum posts after their formal innings.

Since the state was formed eight years ago, all those who retired as Chief Secretary, except for one, have managed to secure important positions such as advisor to Chief Minister, chairman of some statutory body or of some commission.

Take the case of Shivraj Singh, who retired as Chief Secretary last month. Within two days after his retirement, the BJP Government appointed the 1972 batch IAS officer as Chief Minister's advisor, a post equivalent to that of Chief Secretary with same emoluments. He has also been made director of the Chhattisgarh State Mining Corporation. Now, there are whispers in the corridors of state secretariat about his continued clout over the administration.

His predecessor R P Bagai was tipped to be accommodated in the Cooperative Tribunal but it did not materialise.

Another former Chief Secretary A K Vijayvargiya became the state's first Chief Information Commissioner while his predecessor S K Mishra is chairman of the Electricity Regulatory Commission.

Arun Kumar, who became the first Chief Secretary following the creation of Chhattisgarh in November 2000, later took up his post-retirement job as chairman of State Administrative Reforms Commission, which was set up by the previous Ajit Jogi Government.

When IAS officers have their way, can their Indian Police Service (IPS) and Indian Forest Service (IFS) brethren lag behind?

Immediately after the creation of Public Service Commission (PSC) in the state, the then Director General of Police S M Shukla, who had two years to go for retirement, was appointed PSC chairman while his successor R L S Yadav, after his retirement, became an advisor to the then Chief Minister Ajit Jogi, mainly to look after political matters. Yadav faced criticism from various quarters, including from within the Congress, for organising conventions of other backward classes (OBC) across the state.

While another retired DGP V K Das could not get any suitable post, his successor Ashok Darbari, on his retirement, took up the post of PSC chairman. During his tenure, scandals and irregularities rocked the PSC, leading to his suspension from the post and the matter subsequently went up to the Supreme Court.

As for the IFS officers, R C Sharma who retired as Principal Chief Conservator of Forests (PCCF) was appointed CEO of state Herbal and Medicinal Plants Promotion Board.

Sources said hectic lobbying was now on by an IAS officer and an IPS officer, who were due to retire this month, to grab the post of PSC chairman, which is now lying vacant. Similarly, an Additional Chief Secretary is being tipped for a post in the State Human Rights Commission while a retired Additional Director General of Police is all set to get re-employment to head the police training wing.

The official explanation for re-employment of retired persons on contract basis is that since formation of the state, there has been a shortage of IAS and other officials. "There is no specific policy as such. Every such service extension and re-appointment on contract is being made on a case-to-case basis, depending on the requirement," said a senior minister in the Raman Singh Government. "As far as other appointments are concerned, it is the prerogative of the Government of the day. After all, experience has no other substitute."

Heading: Chorwad dumps plans to release stray dogs in Gir - Indian Express
Content:
The CBI on Monday told the court that crucial evidence has emerged in the cash-at-judge's door case and sought seven-day police custody for the four accused — Sanjeev Bansal, Rajiv Gupta, Nirmal Singh and Prakash Ram.

"During interrogation, some crucial facts have emerged suggesting a nexus between the accused and the higher judiciary, which needs to be investigated during their interrogation in police custody for effecting recovery," the remand application read.

Despite a verbal attack on the CBI by the defence counsel, the Court of Special CBI Judge Jagdeep Jain remanded Bansal and Gupta in police custody till September 3. The other two accused were remanded in judicial custody.

The court also issued non-bailable warrants against Ravinder Singh, the hotelier, who is absconding.

Notices were issued to the CBI on an application filed by Singh's counsel seeking directions to the investigating agency to open the locks of his two houses in New Delhi, that were sealed by the investigators.

Following the defence counsel's argument that Bansal had been in police custody for 13 days and the law permits a maximum of 15 days in police remand, special CBI Judge, Jagdeep Jain rejected the investigating agency's demand remarked that "Old habits die hard". The defence counsel alleged that despite court orders they were not allowed to meet the accused during interrogation, but the CBI refuted the charges.

Defence counsel S K Vohra said there was no proof to establish a nexus between the judiciary and the accused. It reiterated that the CBI had never examined a High Court Judge.

In response, the public prosecutor said the CBI had certain limitations and was exploring possibilities of examining the High Court judge as well. Jain told the defence counsel that prior permission of the Chief Justice of India had to be sought before examining a High Court judge.

The defence counsel also accused the CBI of defaming the judiciary and making 'confidential' reports available to the media.

Heading: Wi-Fi cities to help MP fight terror - Indian Express
Content:
The Chorwad Municipality authorities have rolled back their decision to invite tenders for a contract to catch stray pigs and dogs in the town and release them in the neighbouring Gir forest.

Following a news report in The Indian Express, about advertisements in local dailies inviting stray animal catchers, the District Collector ordered the municipality to reverse the order. Now a fresh ad has been put in local dailies cancelling tender invites. However, the municipality continues to be plagued by dogbites and paucity of anti-rabies vaccine in government hospitals.

According to Hirabhai Chudasama, municipality president, more than half-a-dozen cases of dog and pig bite are reported every day in Chorwad. Besides, there are no stocks of anti-rabies vaccine in government hospitals.

Heading: CVC steps in to end monopoly of  Nanda’s firm in Govt procurement - Indian Express
Content:
Madhya Pradesh on Monday joined the group of states planning to build wireless cities, but for a different reason. It plans to turn Bhopal and Indore into Wi-Fi cities within three months, to make video surveillance easy by installing cameras in public places.

"Wireless fidelity will allow us to keep an eye on the activities of organizations like the SIMI," IT minister Kailash Vijayvargiya said. The government is said to sign an MoU with Sarthak Communication Pvt Ltd, which will invest anything between Rs 200 and Rs 300 crore to offer high-speed wireless broadband connectivity in these two towns.

The minister said wireless cameras would be installed at suspect locations and busy market places, bus stands, railway stations and airports and officials in control rooms would monitor the images.

Low IT penetration has not prevented the government from boasting that it will do what Bangalore and Pune could not do despite having a head start. These two cities were the first to announce plans to become Wi Fi-enabled but are still struggling to take them to fruition.

The facility will allow laptop users to access Internet from anywhere in these towns. However, a top BSNL official told The Indian Express that Bhopal has only 1400 Wi-Fi users.

The IT minister said the state's capital and the commercial capital will be the first cities in the country to get the status ahead of any other city.

IT secretary Anurag Srivastava said the government would allow the private company all the facilities it needed. The company will be allowed to install towers on government buildings and will find it easy to lay wires to connect its towers. He claimed Bangalore and Pune are still struggling to get the status because of procedural complications.

Heading: Novak’s midnight marathon - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Vigilance Commission has initiated steps to end the monopoly of Commerce 1 (C1 India), a firm floated by arms dealer Suresh Nanda, in the Government's fast-expanding e-procurement business.

As first reported by The Indian Express, CI India benefited by an "authorization" issued by the Directorate General of Supplies and Disposals (DGS&D) for all Government organizations to use it as the e-tendering platform. This when Nanda and his firms are under the CBI scanner in connection with defence deals and the alleged bribery of an Income Tax officer.

Central Vigilance Commissioner Pratush Sinha told The Indian Express he has asked the CVC's Chief Technical Examiner (CTE) to examine allegations of irregularities in the e-procurement business. E-procurement is now mandatory.

Sinha said early warnings have been sent to Government Departments. "At all our zonal meetings, PSUs and vigilance officers are being told that DGS&D is not in a position to authorize any Government organization to use a particular e-tendering platform. All tendering has to be on the basis of competitive bidding and this holds good for e-tendering also...No private company should be allowed to move in the direction of creating a monopoly."

Significantly, some departments have switched. Ordnance Factory Board Chairman Sudipta Ghosh said his firm had withdrawn from the platform following advice from the Defence Ministry. Said Ghosh, "We forwarded the investigation done by The Indian Express to the Ministry of Defence and received a formal advice from them not to use C1 India's e-procurement any more. We are looking for other options."

But one wing of the MoD, clearly, does not know what the other is doing. A recent announcement by the Ministry's Material Organisation introduced C1 India as the exclusive "service provider" for the Navy's e-procurement.

Heading: No Clarke as Faldo sticks with Brits - Indian Express
Content:
Novak Djokovic illuminated New York's midnight hour with an electrifying performance on Sunday, surviving a 234-minute battle to reach the fourth round of the US Open.

The Serbian third seed soaked up the full force of Marin Cilic's armoury to stay in the hunt for the title with an absorbing 6-7, 7-5, 6-4, 7-6 victory. The 21-year-old squandered two match points in the 10th game of the fourth set but roared through the last 11 points of the match to seal the win when Cilic dragged a service return wide.

Asked how he was feeling, the Australian Open champion replied: "You're asking me how I'm doing after a four-hour match, not fresh, for sure. Thanks everybody for staying so late for us. I had a very very difficult match and even if I lost today, he would have deserved it. He played great."

Djokovic discovered he was in for a long night when, set point up in the opening set, he was made to scamper around like a demented bunny, only to lose a 31-shot rally. Cilic, 19, kept up the intensity throughout but was undone by his lack of experience, cracking 12 double faults.

Olympic champion Elena Dementieva won 6-4, 6-1 over China's Li Na. As temperatures soared, an ailing Marion Bartoli said it was a miracle she could battle for more than three hours, losing 7-6, 0-6, 6-4 to Austrian Sybille Bammer.

Fighting the conditions

"I had very low blood pressure and very weak pulse and the trainer advised me not to continue, especially because it was so hot," said the 12th seed. "I was sick since yesterday morning because I caught a stomach virus. Since then I had not eaten anything except one glass of orange juice."

Dinara Safina's pursuit of a maiden Grand Slam title gathered momentum when she beat German qualifier Anna-Lena Groenefeld 7-5, 6-0 to reach the quarter-finals.

Master's class

After a week of lukewarm performances, Federer turned on the heat with a masterful 6-3, 6-3, 6-2 destruction of Czech 28th seed Radek Stepanek. In his first two matches, Federer had fallen short of proving his credentials, piling up 66 unforced errors and converted only 11 of 28 break points. On Sunday, he dazzled Stepanek and 23,000 fans at Arthur Ashe Stadium when his game clicked into overdrive.

At one point, the Swiss even managed to surprise himself. With his back pinned to the rear wall, Federer leapt high into the air and his slam-dunk mis-hit bounced off a startled Stepanek's racket frame for a winner. he finally threaded a forehand down the line to seal victory and celebrated by punching the air and holding aloft his index finger, as if to remind people, "I'm still number one in New York."

"At the end of the day, what counts is winning the tournament. You forget all the unforced errors you made," said Federer. "If I were to win one of those Slams right away, I have the invincibility factor again. I don't try to impress anybody in the early rounds," said the 27-year-old.

Qualifier Gilles Muller put Luxembourg on the tennis map when he squeezed past Spanish 18th seed Nicolas Almagro 6-7, 3-6, 7-6, 7-6, 7-5 to become the first player from the nation to reach the fourth round of a Grand Slam. Eighth seed Andy Roddick beat Italian Andreas Seppi 6-2, 7-5, 7-6.

American Mardy Fish, meanwhile, became the first man to reach the quarter-finals when he breezed past French youngster Gael Monfils 7-5, 7-2, 6-2. (Reuters)

Bhupathi-Knowles ousted

Mahesh Bhupathi and Mark Knowles paid the price for their errors, losing in three sets to Argentine pair of Maximo Gonzalez & Juan Monaco after taking one-set lead. The Indo-Bahamian pair lost 6-2, 4-6, 4-6. Earlier, seventh seeds Leander Paes and his Czech partner Lukas Dlouhy advanced to the quarter-finals with a comfortable straight-set 6-3, 6-3 victory over South African Rik De Voest and Australia's Ashley Fisher. Among the juniors, Yuki Bhambri beat American Denis Kudla 6-2, 5-7, 6-3 and will next play Serb Filip Krajinovic.

Heading: Easy wins for Advani, Sethi on Day One - Indian Express
Content:
Ian Poulter and Paul Casey were chosen on Sunday as wild card picks for Europe's Ryder Cup team. Europe captain Nick Faldo made his announcement shortly after the end of the Johnnie Walker Championship.

"I've been watching these guys through the summer," Faldo said. "Ian is a very determined guy. I love his attitude and what he did at The Open — that back nine he played with the intention to win and had that emotional feeling."

Poulter could have finished in the top 10 and earned an automatic berth by finishing third in the Johnnie Walker Championship, but he skipped the event. "Maybe I should have gone to play Gleneagles, but I stuck by my word," Poulter said. "Looking back at the time, I made the right decision for me, but it was so difficult to choose the right thing to do and it's obviously been a very difficult decision to try to get across."

Faldo said he had been keeping an eye on Casey and waiting for his putting to improve. "I've been watching Paul play and he has been playing absolutely the best through the summer," Faldo said. "He has an extremely good record in the Ryder Cup and, going back, the Walker Cup." Oliver Wilson clinched the 10th and final automatic spot by finishing in a tie for 10th place at Gleneagles on Sunday, while Justin Rose and Soren Hansen also qualified to make their debuts at the competition.

Padraig Harrington, Sergio Garcia, Lee Westwood, Henrik Stenson, Robert Karlsson, Miguel Angel Jimenez & Graeme McDowell have already made the team.

Heading: From Forest Hills to Roger Federer: 40 years of US Open - Indian Express
Content:
Indian players, including Pankaj Advani, Rupesh Shah and Geet Sethi scored easy wins on the opening day of the IBSF World Billiards Championship here today.

In league matches of the points format, defending champion Shah defeated SM Shaharwardi of Sri Lanka 151-53, 151-35, 150-21 while Advani beat Calum Hossack of Scotland 151-5, 150-0, 151-17.

Sethi, meanwhile, was too good for Teik Chong Alan Puan of Singapore, winning 150-66, 151-93, 153-0.

Heading: Flying low, Air India make goalless exit - Indian Express
Content:
1968The ITF votes to allow professionals to compete and announces the first US Open from Aug 29-Sept 8 at the West Side Tennis Club (WSTC) in Forest Hills. Arthur Ashe and Virginia Wade were crowned champions.

1970First Grand Slam to introduce tiebreaker — a 9-point playoff, with the first to reach five points winning. Three years later, introduces equal prize money for men (John Newcombe) and women (Margaret Court).

1978The tournament moves to the hardcourts at Flushing Meadows after three years on clay in between. Bjorn Borg loses the final to Jimmy Connors, who remains the only player to win the Open on all three surfaces.

1985Ivan Lendl, after losing three consecutive finals, wins the first of his three titles here. He again lost in the final in 1988 and 1989, becoming the only open era player to play eight straight finals.

1994Home favourite Andre Agassi becomes the first unseeded men's singles champion of the open era. In 1997, the Arthur Ashe Stadium was opened, with Venus Williams making her Open debut.

2002Witnesses the last of the great American rivalry between Pete Sampras and Agassi. Sampras wins the battle in the final for his last Grand Slam title before announcing retirement from the game.

2006The first Grand Slam to use Hawkeye for instant replay; Agassi, Navratilova retire. Roger Federer wins his third title, retaining it the next year to become the first man to win four consecutive US Opens.

Heading: Oz coach plans life without Symonds - Indian Express
Content:
To 'Do or die' was not on the minds of either JCT or Air India on Monday. The Punjab giants were the first to make the last four of the Durand Cup, and the Mumbai team were out of the reckoning with only one point from two matches. With nothing to lose, Air India would have wanted to end their goalless run in their run-up to the I-League, but instead, made their exit from this year's competition without a single strike to their name.

The numerous analysts and the 50-odd spectators present at the Ambedkar Stadium, though, couldn't blame Air India's defence for JCT's lead. Midfielder Baldeep Singh never bothered to trouble them. Pouncing on Gurwinder Singh's pass from about 20 yards off the box, he just gave it everything, and the ball, for a moment looking like a mishit, swirled into the net in the 26th minute of the second half. If goalkeeper Sharat was left clueless, the defending line of Syed Farid, H Thomte, Uttam Singh, Amritpal Singh and Bijoy Basfore could've done nothing. The long-range strike, for a few present, washed off the hype of Thoudan Singh's hat-trick for Sporting Clube de Goa in the previous match against Tata Football Academy. It would make fond remembrances for being a first in this year's Durand Cup and leading the Goa team into the semis, but Baldeep's strike would certainly be rated among the best of the tournament so far.

While JCT's goal came as a result of frustration in failing to breach AI's defence, the latter began to rework a few strategic notes. Surojit Roy and Samson Singh kept overlapping from the left flank, creating numerous chances for Soccor Velho.

Missed chances

But AI's No 10 failed to convert any, with the worst miss coming in the 82nd minute — hardly 10 metres away from goal with only Karanjit Singh to beat, he heaved it over the bar. Getting into the shot too early was a problem then and eight minutes later, he was comprehensively outnumbered while trying to fetch Samson's corner kick.

With their I-League warm-up turning on its head, AI coach Bimal Ghosh was left speculating a few changes in his strike force. "We need to work on our combination. Bashiru didn't perform at all, and we are looking to replace him. A few more replacements are on the cards, specially in the forward line, for the upcoming I-League," Ghosh said.

With JCT resting their mainstays Eduardo da Silva, Jaspreet Singh, Julius Trabor Akpele, and still managing to keep their all-win record, coach Sukhwinder Singh was ecstatic. "We didn't miss any of the rested players. We didn't dominate throughout, but managed to win. Carrying on the all-win record was more important."

The concluding scenes at the close on Monday, though, weren't pleasing as Baldeep was helped out of the field by team mates after sustaining an ankle injury. Even as the coach discarded all speculations of Baldeep missing the semi-final, the midfielder looked in pain and said he wasn't sure of making the playing XI. "It's not a bone injury, but right now I can't walk properly. I'm not sure about playing on Thursday," he said.

Heading: No ‘private’ events, says AITA - Indian Express
Content:
Unsure of Andrew Symonds' return to the side, Australia coach Tim Nielsen is working on a plan to deal with the feisty all-rounder's absence in the side for the forthcoming India tour. After Symonds was sent home for missing a compulsory team meeting, preferring a fishing trip instead, Nielsen said he could not assume that the all-rounder would be part of the squad in India.

"I don't think we can (assume) at the moment (that Symonds will be touring India), I don't think we can bank on much at all at the moment," Nielsen was quoted as saying by AAP.

"The only thing we can bank on is providing as much support as we possibly can for him (Symonds) to make the right decision for him and for us, to come back into the group 100 per cent committed,' he said adding "how long is a piece of string?". "I don't know if Roy (Symonds) would understand or know how long it's going to take. I certainly don't," Nielsen added.

Mulling retirement

Symonds is mulling quitting international cricket and the 33-year-old player's decision would mean that he would lose his $500,000 CA contract. But the Australian can still earn handsomely in the Indian sub-continent by playing in the Indian Premier League. It is not the first time Symonds has thought of quitting cricket. He had contacted Brisbane Broncos coach Wayne Bennett and talked about reinventing himself as a rugby league player in 2002.

Australia will announce its touring squad as soon as they play the Border-Gavaskar Trophy in India in October and Nielsen said Symonds's absence would have ramifications on the team's planning for the four-match series. "Oh yeah, we've lost out No 6 batsman and our all-rounder in the Test team for the short-term, so for sure," he said.

Cricket Australia, Queensland and Australian Cricketers' Association are planning to provide Symonds with counsellors to help him deal with the demands of being an international star.

Nielsen said Symonds was sent home in everyone's best interests. But he conceded there could be a long-term risk if Symonds did not return for some time."It could have long-term implications. He could decide that he needs a bit more time than we thought," Nielsen said, adding "We just don't know, that's the hard part."

Preparing for India tour

Australia are trying to organise another warm-up match before the first Test. Nielsen said he wanted the players to reach India well ahead so that they could acclimatise to the conditions. "Everyone keeps talking about being ready for that first Test match, but I'm really conscious of the fact also that we've got to be going strongly and well by days four and five of the second Test," he said.

Australia's players have used their stay in Darwin working on strength and conditioning to prepare them for India.

Heading: Did Greeks try to outsmart IOC with rare drug? - Indian Express
Content:
The Indian tennis calendar has lost a major tournament each on the ATP and WTA tours, and the cancellations have prompted the All India Tennis Association (AITA) to undertake a major policy decision. The Indian tennis body will not be allowing any private parties to organise events on the men's or women's professional tour, and if they do, it will only be in partnership with the AITA.

"I wasn't aware of the Sunfeast Open's cancellation till I read it in the newspaper. On August 26, Globosport sent us a letter informing us of the cancellation since they had decided to sell the sanction to another party. It was too late for us to do anything," said AITA secretary general Anil Khanna. When contacted, Globosport said only the WTA would comment on the issue and not them.

"In the case of Bangalore, Vijay Amritraj told us one Arjun Rao from Reliance ADG will meet the AITA to finalise the ATP event. But despite repeated reminders, we didn't get any communication. In early August, Vijay told me that Reliance ADG was having trouble finding sponsors. When the promoters finally got in touch, they gave a ridiculous report of an investigation company proving Bangalore was not safe. But then why hold cricket matches in the city, or even the world billiards meet? Keeping all this in mind, we'll now be organising all such events on our own," he said.

Heading: We have objections, put pay hike on hold: 3 service chiefs again - Indian Express
Content:
Over a dozen Greek athletes who failed doping tests prior to and during last month's Beijing Olympics thought a rare anabolic steroid would help them elude tests, a leading anti-doping expert said on Monday. But the International Olympic Committee (IOC) had been on the lookout for cheats from Greece ever since the drug, methyltrienolone, turned up in the results of 11 Greek weightlifters in April, Don Catlin, a member of the World Anti-Doping Agency's committee for science and medicine, told Ta Nea daily.

"The Greek case...involved the use of a particularly rare and dangerous anabolic whose use had not been officially recorded before," Catlin said. "Whoever marketed it in Greece undoubtedly argued that it is not harmful and could not be traced, as only small quantities are needed for it to act."

In all, fifteen Greek athletes in three disciplines — weightlifting, swimming and athletics — have tested positive for methyltrienolone, severely embarrassing Greek authorities which on today tabled tougher anti-doping legislation in parliament.

"The (Greek) state wants clean athletes," Michalis Liapis, the Greek culture minister responsible for sport, told reporters.

The new regulations cut rewards for successful athletes to discourage drug cheating and toughen sanctions against providers of banned substances, corrupt anti-doping officials and sports officials. The doping outbreak has already sparked a preliminary judicial probe here.

Among those caught is Fani Halkia, the women's 400m hurdles at the Athens Olympics gold medalist, whose coach George Panagiotopoulos has now been sued by the IOC for causing damage to its reputation.

Catlin is a senior US chemist whose research led to the uncovering of the BALCO steroid scandal and the first test for THG, the once-undetectable drug that dope cheats had used with great success.

Heading: WB Governor Gandhi may hold keys to Tata deadlock - Indian Express
Content:
Raising fresh objections to the Sixth Pay panel notification after the Cabinet cleared it on August 14, the three chiefs of the Armed Forces, in an unprecedented move, have written to Defence Minister A K Antony that implementation for officer ranks be "held in abeyance" until their objections are addressed.

Earlier, they had raised two broad objections: higher salary for Personnel Below Officer Ranks (PBORs) and parity with civil servants for officer ranks. While thanking the government for hiking salaries of PBORs, they claim the disparity has only increased between service officers and their civil service counterparts.

Their objections:

•Disparity in Pay Bands: The chiefs claim the Committee of Secretaries (CoS) moved the Director rank into Pay Band 4 but retained Lt. Col and its equivalent in other services in Pay Band 3. Earlier, they claim, a Lt. Col got the same pay as an IAS Director and Rs 800 more than a non-IAS Director. Now he gets Rs 14000 less than an IAS director and Rs 11000 less than a non-IAS director.

•Disparity in Grade Pay: The CoS agreed to their demand to an increase in grade pay across middle-rank officers but also increased the grade pay of civil servants, thereby retaining disparity, the chiefs say. For example, he Pay Commission recommended Rs 6600 for a civil servant equivalent to a Major who was to get Rs 6100. After review, a Major will now get Rs 6600 but his equivalent in the civil service will get Rs 7600.

•Restricting elite list: The new category of HAG-plus (Higher Administrative Grade) includes all DGs and DGPs but only Army Commanders and their equivalents in other services, the chiefs complain. Their demand: all Lt. Gen officers be included in this category. The Defence Ministry is said to have conveyed that the objections are being looked into and a response will be given soon.

Heading: Days before NSG meets, China’s state mouthpiece slams India-US nuclear deal - Indian Express
Content:
West Bengal Governor Gopalkrishna Gandhi, the ruling CPM's public enemy No. 1 after his blunt comments on the Nandigram police firing, is now emerging as the "mediator" in the stand-off between Trinamool chief Mamata Banerjee and the state government over the Tata Nano project. Both sides have welcomed his role.

Gandhi called up Chief Minister Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee today to follow up on a letter he had written to Mamata Banerjee, copied to the CM, on Saturday. In that, he suggested a mediator who is neither from politics nor business.

"You take the initiative," Mamata said. "Our representatives will attend the meeting." She said she wanted the Tata Motors plant to open and function. "My feelings about the Governor's letter are very positive," said the CM. "His initiative is welcome and I thanked him."

Heading: Phone-taps legal evidence under MCOCA, says SC; boost for 7/11 cases - Indian Express
Content:
Raising pressure ahead of the next round of talks at the Nuclear Suppliers Group, China's top newspaper has called the India-US nuclear agreement a major blow to non-proliferation. The commentary today in People's Daily, the Chinese Communist Party's official paper, was a rare public response from Beijing on the deal.

Diplomats in Vienna said that a revised US proposal to lift the ban did not sufficiently ease fears the move could compromise efforts to stop the spread of nuclear weapons. India needs an unprecedented NSG exemption to seal the deal. Chinese officials have given no sign they would outright block the deal but People's Daily was unusually forthright: "Whether it is motivated by geopolitical considerations or commercial interests, the US-India nuclear agreement has constituted a major blow to the international non-proliferation regime," said the commentary by a researcher from the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, a state think tank.

Experts say China is unlikely to stymie the deal and risk pushing New Delhi closer to Washington when Beijing is seeking to avoid confrontation with India. China was not among those that raised objections in the NSG but the commentary's a reminder that Beijing is irked by the agreement. The US proposal to the NSG was vague, the paper said.

Heading: Economist-bureaucrat Subbarao new Governor, Reddy regime at RBI ends - Indian Express
Content:
The Supreme Court has ruled that intercepted communications - oral, written or telephonic- are admissible as evidence under the Maharashtra Control of Organized Crime Act (MCOCA). The ruling is likely to hasten trials in several cases being tried under MCOCA, including those related to the 7/11 Mumbai train bombings.

A bench comprising Chief Justice K G Balakrishnan and Justices R V Raveendran and M K Sharma upheld a Maharashtra government appeal against a Bombay High Court order of 2003, quashing Sections 13, 14, 15 and 16 of MCOCA, all relating to intercepted communications. The High Court had ruled that the government of Maharashtra had no right to enact a law on a subject (Communications) in the Central List.

In January 2001, diamond merchant and film financier Bharat Shah was arrested under MCOCA, and charged with using gangster Chhota Shakeel to force actors to work in his film Chori Chori Chupke Chupke. He was also accused of passing money to the Mumbai underworld through hawala.

Shah challenged the constitutional validity of MCOCA. The High Court's decision led to his acquittal under that law because there was no evidence against him except tapped telephone conversations. Shah got a light sentence under a provision of the IPC that was far less stringent than MCOCA.

In 2004, the Maharashtra government went to the Supreme Court in appeal, seeking powers for the police to tap phones of suspects.

Monday's ruling came exactly six months after the apex court stayed trials in cases relating to the 7/11 and Malegaon bombings (September 8, 2006), and the Aurangabad arms seizure of May 9, 2006.

All these cases are now likely to be examined in a new light.

MCOCA, promulgated on February 24, 1999, is a tough law that stipulates stringent punishment to any person or a gang operating as a syndicate. Any offence resulting in death attracts either a life term or the death penalty.

THE MCOCA FILE

•In 2001, diamond merchant and film financier was accused of having underworld links, and charged under MCOCA.

•In 2003, Bombay High Court declared phone-taps illegal under MCOCA. Shah escaped because the only evidence against him was based on phone-taps.

•In 2004, the Maharashtra government appealed to the Supreme Court.

•On Monday, the court ruled that phone-taps were legal under MCOCA.

Heading: Attacks on churches made Christians insecure, tarnished Orissa’s image: CM Naveen Patnaik - Indian Express
Content:
The Government took a bold call today announcing its decision to appoint Finance Secretary Duvvuri Subbarao, the IAS topper of 1972 batch, as the next Reserve Bank of India Governor. He will assume charge September 5 when incumbent Yaga Venugopal Reddy's five-year tenure ends. Reddy is expected to be in New Delhi on September 3 to meet the Prime Minister and the Finance Minister before demitting office the day after.

Subbarao takes the top job at Mint Street at a time of double-digit inflation, slowing growth, an impending election year and a slew of pending reforms in the financial sector, including in the RBI itself.

Strong lobbies were actively pushing the case of Rakesh Mohan, RBI Deputy Governor, but the Prime Minister and the Finance Minister opted for Subbarao, a bureaucrat and an economist.

An IIT Kanpur physics graduate, Subbarao did his MS in economics from Ohio State University and his doctorate in economics from Andhra University. He has worked with the World Bank as a lead economist for about five years and was in the Finance Ministry during the first phase of reforms in the 1990s under Manmohan Singh as Finance Minister.

"An overhaul of the monetary management in a phased manner can be expected with a change in guard," said a banker who did not wish to be named. To start with, there is a strong case for the RBI to stop managing the exchange rate, added another.

The current dispensation at RBI, comprising Reddy and his deputy Mohan, was also perceived to be stonewalling central banking reforms. The RBI is seen as banning almost anything it cannot manage. Many blame it for moribund corporate bond markets, a clampdown on external commercial borrowings, and resisting a real appreciation in domestic currency which has its own adverse impact on inflation.

What irked the government most was RBI's reluctance to get moving the Budget proposal to set up a debt management office (DMO). Wary it would have to cede a part of its turf, the RBI did not lend officers for creating a "middle office" in the finance ministry, the first step before a DMO to manage government debt — independent of the RBI — could be set up.

A blueprint of what needs to be done in the financial sector space is already available in the Percy Mistry report on making Mumbai an international finance centre and Raghuram Rajan's draft report submitted to the Planning Commission.

Subbarao believes that RBI has to be at the forefront in inflation management. Speaking to The Indian Express mid-July, he said, "Inevitably, we have to compromise on growth as we tighten the monetary stance. But, the long-term growth story is still credible and will not be hurt."

Subbarao, who has been given three years at RBI instead of the permissible five, is expected to be more appreciative of the government's concerns and yet be objective in his conduct of monetary policy. Although he acknowledges that healthy differences of opinion result in better public policy, he may opt for an institutional mechanism to sort these out between the RBI and the Finance Ministry.

It was last Thursday when both Subbarao and Rakesh Mohan were scheduled to represent India at the Group of 20 meeting in Rio de Janeiro. Rakesh Mohan was in the US on Wednesday and was to join Subbarao at Rio the next day. But he cut short his visit and rushed to New Delhi to meet the Finance Minister in what emerges was an interview for the post of RBI Governor. Subbarao moved ahead, both in Rio and in the race to the Governorship.

Heading: Armed Forces chiefs raise fresh objections to pay disparity - Indian Express
Content:
Orissa Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik says recurring communal violence has tarnished the image of his state, and bred insecurity in its Christian population. In an interview to The Indian Express,Patnaik deplored the "savage acts" carried out in the name of religion.

A total 558 homes and 17 churches have been set on fire since the murder of Vishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) leader Swami Laxmanananda Saraswati on August 23, state Chief Secretary Ajit Kumar Tripathy said today. At least 16 people are believed to have been killed in rioting.

"The attack on the ashram, as well as what happed thereafter, I repeat what happened after that, both are deplorable. Those who indulged in these savage acts, and I mean both in the ashram and after that in the district, stern action will be certainly taken against them," Patnaik said.

Asked if communal violence was tarnishing Orissa's reputation and encouraging afeeling that the state was intolerant towards Christians, he said, "Yes, it is. There has been a sense of insecurity among the Christians after the recent incidents. There has been recurrence of violence and tragedies. We will try our best to remove all such violence and tragedies or any disharmony among sections

of people.

"Last December there was violence in Kandhamal district; the administration brought in under control. Now again there has been violence after the killings of the Swami and his followers. The killing at the ashram was tragic as was the violence that followed. I saw the damaged houses, schools and I also visited the ashram."

The Chief Minister, however, ruled out a CBI probe into Laxmanananda's murder as proposed recently by

Union Home Minister Shivraj Patil. No one knows for sure who killed the swami, though the Maoists have claimed responsibility.

"I do not think that a CBI probe in necessary. After the incidents, a judicial enquiry has been initiated, our crime branch and police are also investigating into it. Some persons have been detained and soon the truth will come out. I am sure they are working hard to nab the culprits," Patnaik said.

The state could, however, "certainly do with more Central forces", Patnaik said. "I have been speaking regularly with Home Minister Patil. I expect 10 companies to reach here today."

He denied the Biju Janata Dal's alliance with the BJP was hampering his peace initiatives in Kandhamal. "There is no interference of any kind. I don't think the secular credentials of this government can be doubted. They (the BJP) are not pressurising us in any way."

Is it true that Christian missionaries have been on an aggressive evangelical mission in Kandhamal, as the VHP claims?

"They (the missionaries) have been there for decades. NGOs and missionaries are there in certain belts of Orissa. We will leave it at that.

"There are laws regarding conversions and every person in any country should follow the law of the land."

Patnaik highlighted efforts made by the state government to return normalcy to affected areas. "I was in the district. Relief has reached there in the way of food and other items. Senior secretaries of the departments which are providing relief will soon visit the district. Very shortly assessment of the losses will be made. Funds are being made available. Security forces are there in Kandhamal and Koraput districts.

"Touch wood, now the situation is under control."

Heading: Maya demands Rs 2,200 cr flood relief package from Centre - Indian Express
Content:
Raising fresh objections to the Sixth Pay panel notification after the Cabinet cleared it on August 14, the three chiefs of the Armed Forces, in an unprecedented move, have written to Defence Minister A K Antony that implementation for officer ranks be "held in abeyance" until their objections are addressed.

Earlier, they had raised two broad objections: higher salary for Personnel Below Officer Ranks (PBORs) and parity with civil servants for officer ranks. While thanking the government for hiking salaries of PBORs, they claim the disparity has only increased between service officers and their civil service counterparts.

Their objections:

•Disparity in Pay Bands: The chiefs claim the Committee of Secretaries (CoS) moved the Director rank into Pay Band 4 but retained Lt. Col and its equivalent in other services in Pay Band 3. Earlier, they claim, a Lt. Col got the same pay as an IAS Director and Rs 800 more than a non-IAS Director. Now he gets Rs 14000 less than an IAS director and Rs 11000 less than a non-IAS director.

•Disparity in Grade Pay: The CoS agreed to their demand to an increase in grade pay across middle-rank officers but also increased the grade pay of civil servants, thereby retaining disparity, the chiefs say. For example, he Pay Commission recommended Rs 6600 for a civil servant equivalent to a Major who was to get Rs 6100. After review, a Major will now get Rs 6600 but his equivalent in the civil service will get Rs 7600.

•Restricting elite list: The new category of HAG-plus (Higher Administrative Grade) includes all DGs and DGPs but only Army Commanders and their equivalents in other services, the chiefs complain. Their demand: all Lt. Gen officers be included in this category. The Defence Ministry is said to have conveyed that the objections are being looked into and a response will be given soon.

Heading: Tata Motors shutdown continues as dharna enters 10th day - Indian Express
Content:
The UP Chief Minister Mayawati on Monday demanded a flood relief package of Rs 2,200 crore from the Centre.

Talking to media after an aerial survey of the flood affected districts in Azamgarh, Gorakhpur, Faizabad and Basti divisions, she said, a proposal to this effect would soon be sent to the Centre.
