As a nervous nation watched to see if Gustav would deliver another Katrina-style hit on the partially rebuilt city, officials steadfastly insisted three years of planning and infrastructure upgrades had prepared them for whatever was to come.

"We don't expect the loss of life, certainly, that we saw in Katrina," Federal Emergency Management Agency Deputy Director Harvey E Johnson said. "But we are expecting a lot of homes to be damaged, a lot of infrastructure to be flooded, and damaged severely."

On the high ground in the French Quarter, nasty winds whipped signs and the purple, green and gold Mardi Gras flags hanging from cast-iron balconies. Like the rest of the city, the Quarter's normally boisterous streets were deserted save for a police officer standing watch every few blocks and a few early-morning drinkers in the city's famous bars.

"We wanted to be part of a historic event," said Benton Love, 30, stood outside Johnny White's Sports Bar with a whiskey and Diet Coke. "We knew Johnny White's would be the place to be. We'll probably switch to water about 10 O'clock, sober up, and see if we can help out."

FEMA estimated there were only about 10,000 people left in the city, and the state said about 1,00,000 remained on the coast. Nearly 2 million people answered the call to leave south Louisiana in the days before Gustav's arrival, a massive evacuation effort designed to avoid the nearly 1,600 deaths suffered when Katrina struck an unprepared Gulf Coast in 2005.

New Orleans police superintendent Warren Riley said there had been no reports of looting or calls for rescue. The Superdome was locked up and city officials stuck to their pledge not to open a shelter of last resort. Public officials sternly warned in the days leading up to the storm that anyone leaving their homes after a dawn-to-dusk curfew was imposed would be swiftly thrown behind bars. Evacuees watched television coverage from shelters and hotel rooms hundreds of miles away, praying the powerful Category 2 storm and its 115-mph winds would pass without the exacting Katrina's toll.

Gustav weakened on Monday to a Category 2 storm as its eyewall rolled onto land. Katrina made landfall as a strong Category 3, which has sustained winds of between 111 mph and 130 mph. At 8 AM, the storm's centre was located about 85 miles south of New Orleans and was moving northwest at 16 mph. It had top sustained winds of 110 mph.

The city of Franklin, about 100 miles west of New Orleans, was bracing for a direct hit if Gustav stays on its current track. Dozens of sheriff's deputies, along with state troopers and guardsmen, waited at an emergency operations centre inside the courthouse.

Three years after Katrina

•Hurricane Gustav is a tropical storm which made landfall in western Cuba on August 30, 2008, causing major damage and displacing 250,000. It also killed at least 80 people in the Caribbean on August 30.

• Headed to the Gulf Coast of Mexico, the federal government declared a state of emergency in Louisiana on August 29, while New Orleans ordered the evacuations of its residents on August 30. Millions in the predicted path of the hurricane, in Louisiana and Texas, have left their homes.

• Hurricane Gustav comes almost three years to the day after Hurricane Katrina ripped through New Orleans, the Gulf Coast in Louisiana and Mississippi. About 1,830 people died in the hurricane and 705 went missing. Among recorded hurricanes, it was the sixth strongest overall and the third strongest to make a landfall in the United States. The storm is estimated to have been responsible for $81.2 billion in damage, making it the costliest natural disaster in US history.

Heading: Gustav spoils McCain party - Indian Express
Content:
The American military handed over responsibility for the security of the western province of Anbar, once a stronghold of the Sunni insurgency and one of the most violent regions in Iraq, to the Iraqi Government on Monday, a long-delayed milestone.

The transfer was made possible, Iraqi and American officials said, by an increase in Iraqi security forces and a reduction of violence largely attributed to the local forces known as Awakening Councils. It is the first handover of a province bordering Baghdad, where there has been intense sectarian conflict. Other provinces that have been shifted to Iraqi control have been in the less troublesome south and in the northern Kurdish region.

The transfer ceremony took place in the center of this city, which two years ago had been destroyed by almost daily battles between the American military and insurgents. Now, Ramadi has been rebuilt, and the number of deaths of American soldiers has fallen virtually to zero.

"You have lost a lot of blood and life to reach this day," said Mowaffak al-Rubaie, Iraq's national security advisor. "This would have been a dream tow or three years ago. This was the cradle of the al-Qaeda."

President Bush hailed the handover. In a statement released by the White House, he credited "the courage of our troops, the Iraqi Security Forces, and the brave tribes and other civilians from Anbar who worked alongside them".

The US military has been reducing the number of American troops in Anbar, to 25,000 from 37,000 in February, and the Iraqi police force has grown to 28,000, up from 5,000 three years ago, according to the Marine Corps.

American forces were originally scheduled to transfer control in late June, but the transfer was postponed. At the time, American military officials said that a dust storm had made it impossible to fly dignitaries in for a ceremony and that the postponement was unrelated to a suicide bombing near Falluja a day earlier that killed 20 people.

In July, the Anbar Provincial Council asked the American military to delay turning over security for at least a year, saying that Iraqi forces were not prepared to keep tight control of the province's borders. The appeal was widely perceived as stemming from a bitter dispute between the Iraqi Islamic Party, which has long been politically dominant in Anbar, and the increasingly powerful Awakening Council forces backed by the Americans.

The Awakening Councils were drawn to large extent from the ranks of Sunni Arab insurgents who had fallen out with leaders of al-Qaeda in Mesopotamia, a homegrown Sunni Arab extremist group that American intelligence agencies have concluded is foreign-led. The Awakening forces took issue with the other group's violent tactics and religious extremism, and were paid by the American military to provide security.

The councils are credited with reducing crime and violence in Anbar, but have recently come under attack by the Iraqi Army, which is controlled by the Shiite government in Baghdad.

The Government's campaign has been particularly pronounced lately in the area west of Baghdad, where the Iraqi Army has arrested scores of Awakening members. Former insurgent leaders have contended that the Iraqi military is pursuing 650 Awakening leaders, many of whom have fled.

Heading: Zardari’s control over n-arsenal worries US - Indian Express
Content:
Republicans open their convention on Monday to nominate presidential candidate John McCain with no pomp and little politics, shelving the usual celebration out of deference to the approaching threat of Hurricane Gustav.

Fearing televised images of Republican festivities would be inappropriate as a killer storm slammed the Gulf Coast, McCain and his party will hold a curtailed business-only session for about two hours on the convention's opening day.

McCain visited a hurricane command centre on Sunday. He does not want to risk comparisons to President George W Bush, who was seen as out of touch and was heavily criticized for his failure to respond to the devastation of Hurricane Katrina three years ago.

"I have every expectation that we will not see the mistakes of Katrina repeated," McCain said by satellite from St. Louis after being briefed on storm preparations in the region.

The four-day Republican convention will nominate McCain and his vice presidential running mate, Alaska Gov. Sarah Palin, to face Democratic rival Barack Obama and his No. 2, Delaware Sen. Joe Biden, in the November 4 presidential election.

The convention opens four days after Obama concluded the Democratic convention with an acceptance speech before 75,000 flag-waving supporters in Denver's open-air football stadium.

Republican officials would not predict when or even if the remainder of the convention would proceed, and McCain told NBC News he might deliver his acceptance speech on Thursday via satellite from the Gulf Coast.

Bush and Vice President Dick Cheney had cancelled their appearances at the convention even before the schedule was reduced. The White House said Bush might address the convention later in the week.

McCain's campaign chartered an airplane to ferry delegates from Gulf Coast states back home to prepare for the storm.

Both camps struggled with the political implications of the storm, trying to appear responsive without appearing to be political opportunists. Most polls show Obama and McCain in a close race. A CNN/Opinion Research Corp poll released on Sunday night showed Obama leading McCain by 49 percent to 48 percent, a statistical dead heat after last week's Democratic convention and McCain's surprise selection of Palin.

Heading: Pakistan to suspend military strikes for Ramzan - Indian Express
Content:
If Pakistan's upcoming election goes as expected, Asif Ali Zardari, widower of assassinated leader Benazir Bhutto, will succeed Pervez Musharraf as the country's next President, giving Zardari at least partial sway over the Muslim country's nuclear arsenal. Concerns spiked last week with the disclosure of medical records indicating that as recently as last year, doctors hired by Zardari had diagnosed him with mental problems including dementia, depression and posttraumatic stress disorder. While Zardari's spokespersons say he has been cured, many US officials, among them Rep Pete Hoekstra, the ranking Republican on the House Intelligence Committee, told Newsweek that word of Zardari's mental-health history took them by surprise. "Typically," said Hoekstra, "(The US) wouldn't want that kind of person" involved in a nuclear chain of command.

Lawyers for Zardari argued in London's high court that he was too ill to testify in corruption-related cases, and they submitted recent mental-health evaluations as evidence. In March 2007, the Financial Times reported, New York psychologist Stephen Reich concluded that Zardari was "chronically anxious and apprehensive" and had thoughts of suicide, though he had not acted on them.

The newspaper wrote that a New York psychiatrist, Philip Saltiel, found that Zardari's long imprisonment in Pakistan while facing corruption probes had left him with "emotional instability" as well as memory and concentration problems. Dr. Reich declined to comment; Dr. Saltiel could not be reached.

Two American officials, who asked for anonymity when discussing a sensitive issue, said that Washington regarded Zardari's medical diagnoses as a legal ploy designed to stall corruption cases against him. Pakistani officials and Zardari supporters said all the allegations against him were trumped up by his enemies. (Last week, days after Newsweek.com reported that Zardari might use his new political clout to try to shut down a Swiss corruption probe, Geneva's prosecutor announced that he had ended his inquiry—a development that Jacques Python, a Geneva lawyer who formerly represented Pakistan, called "extremely shocking.") Zardari's supporters added that the prison stresses were real.

Heading: Italy to compensate Libya $5 billion for colonial rule - Indian Express
Content:
Pakistan will suspend a major military operation against insurgents during the Muslim holy month of Ramzan, a top official said, adding that the country is not taking orders from the United States in its fight against militancy.

The comments by Interior Ministry chief Rehman Malik indicated Pakistan's main ruling party is eager to avoid being seen as too pro-American as it tries to put together a new governing coalition in the face of escalating militant violence.

"We are fighting this war. This is our war. There is no question of America's dictation," Malik said. He said security forces would still retaliate against any militant attacks staged in the Bajur tribal region after the operation there is suspended early Monday.

The US has pushed Pakistan to crack down on militants in its northwest tribal regions, fearing Taliban and al-Qaida-linked fighters involved in attacks on American and NATO forces in Afghanistan.

Pakistan's five-month-old Government at first tried peace talks, but those efforts bore little fruit. It has turned to force in recent weeks, including using air power to strike insurgent hide-outs. The People's Party is considered generally in line with US goals in the war on terror, but because of deep anti-American sentiment in Pakistan, it has to tread carefully when it approaches the subject.

Heading: Georgia fallout: Oz rethinks Russia n-deal - Indian Express
Content:
Italy agreed on Saturday to pay Libya $5 billion as compensation for its thirty-year occupation of the country, which ended in 1943.

Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi and Libyan leader Moammar Gadhafi signed a memorandum pledging a US$5 billion compensation package involving construction projects, student grants and pensions for Libyan soldiers who served with the Italians during World War II. "It is a material and emotional recognition of the mistakes that our country has done to yours during the colonial era," Berlusconi told reporters at the airport on his arrival. "This agreement opens the path to further cooperation."

In return, Italy wants Libya to crack down on the thousands of illegal migrants smuggled across the Mediterranean to Italian shores. Libya largely hasn't delivered on pledges over the last few years to eliminate the problem. Italy will fund $500 million worth of electronic monitoring devices on the Libyan coastline. With the agreement, there should be "fewer clandestine migrants leaving Libyan shores for Italian" coastlines, Berlusconi told reporters in Libya in comments carried on Italian state TV.

Heading: Buckingham guards may soon lose bearskin hats - Indian Express
Content:
Australia is reconsidering a pact to sell uranium to Russia following its military push into Georgia, Foreign Minister Stephen Smith warned on Monday. Speaking as the head of a parliamentary committee examining the deal that would allow sales of uranium for use in Russia's civil nuclear power industry, expanding on them terms of a 1990 agreement, raised fears the yellowcake could be diverted for nuclear weapons use.

Smith told parliament that Australia would take into account Russia's actions in Georgia and the current state of Moscow's ties with Canberra when deciding whether to ratify the pact signed by the two countries last year. "When considering ratification, the government will take into account not just the merits of the agreement but recent and ongoing events in Georgia and the state of Australia's bilateral relationship with the Russian Federation," Smith said.

Smith said he made Australia's views clear to Russia's ambassador when he summoned the envoy last week to call on Moscow to pull its troops in Georgia back to the positions they held before the conflict began on August 8.

He also criticised Russia's decision to recognise the independence of the Georgian rebel regions of South Ossetia and Abkhazia as unhelpful.

"I think that we could supply uranium to him and if he changed his mind about the uses to which he was going to put it, I don't think we'd have any effective comeback at all," Kelvin Thompson, who chairs the parliamentary treaties committee, said.

Heading: Drought threatens Argentine farms economy - Indian Express
Content:
The stunning sight of the change of guard at Buckingham Palace with the lofty splendour of the iconic and glossy crest of black worn by the Queen's soldiers may soon be a thing of the past.

Britain is mulling replacing the 200-year-old traditional bearskin helmets, worn by the guards on ceremonial duty at the Royal residence in London, with a designer, humane alternative preferably made from synthetical materials.

Baroness Taylor, the Minister for Defence Procurement, is to meet activists from the People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA) this week to discuss the idea of phasing out the 18-inch bearskin headgear.

According to sources, the Ministry of Defence is very much open to the idea, provided any alternative can be worn in all weathers.

"The MoD is not opposed to use of synthetic materials as an alternative to bearskins, provided such materials meet the requirement for a very high quality product that performs adequately in all weather conditions.

"Regrettably a suitable alternative continues to prove elusive," an unnamed MoD spokesperson was quoted by The Daily Telegraph as saying.

Meanwhile, PETA has asked British designer Vivienne Westwood to produce an "innovative" new design, while Stella McCartney and US designer Mar Bouwer have also been asked for help if commissioned by the MoD.

In fact, the bearskins have long been a target of animal rights groups, as a highly visible garment made from the fur of Canadian black bears, whose numbers are falling in the wild.

They have been worn by the Foot Guards in the British Army's Household Division since the Battle of Waterloo, where the hats were taken as badge of honour by the Grenadier Guards when they defeated French Emperor Napoleon's bearskin-wearing Imperial Guard.

"This meeting is hugely significant for our campaign to save North American bears. If she (Baroness Taylor) has a heart and can see the PR nightmare of the MoD continuing to support the Canadian bear slaughter, she can push the MoD to scrap the bearskin caps sooner rather than later," PETA's Director Robbie LeBlanc said.

Heading: EU ‘vigilant’ on Russia ties - Indian Express
Content: The worst drought in 20 years is wracking Argentina, stalling the country's conflict-ridden farm economy just as the government needs agricultural export income to protect its budget surplus at a politically troubled time. The National Meteorological Service says nearly every part of Argentina is experiencing drought conditions - ranked as "extreme" or "absolute" in most areas - that already have killed thousands of cattle and withered crops. The damage is worst in the country's northern farm belt, which for decades has produced the bulk of Argentine agriculture, fueling the nation's growth.

Heading: 20-yr-old held for stealing music systems from cars - Indian Express
Content:
Prosecutors in an Italian court Thursday asked the key middleman in the IAF's VVIP chopper deal whether the initials 'AP' in an alleged "budget sheet" for bribes to politicians referred to Ahmed Patel, the political secretary of UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi.

The middleman, Guido Haschke, who has consistently denied bribing Indian officials or politicians, replied that he did not know who or what 'AP' stood for.

As first reported by The Indian Express, Italian prosecutors had last month produced a handwritten document they alleged was a "budget" drawn up by two middlemen — Haschke and Christian Michel — which purportedly lists initials of Indian politicians and designations of bureaucrats and IAF officers who allegedly had to be "handled" to fix the Rs 3,546 crore deal.

The alleged "budget sheet" detailed how kickbacks of 51 million euros would be divided and under the heading "POL" — Haschke has claimed this referred to Indian politicians — there is a reference to "AP" against which "3 million euro" has been listed.

Another amount of 15/16 million euros was listed against "FAM" which is said to be "Family". Haschke has claimed the note was dictated to him by British consultant Michel during one of their meetings in 2008.

On Thursday, Italian prosecutor Eugenio Fusco asked Haschke during a court hearing in Busto Arsizio near Milan whether "AP" in the note was a reference to Ahmed Patel.

In his reply, the middlemen said he did not know what AP meant when he wrote it down. Haschke also denied any bribes were paid for the contract and said that the "budget sheet" was just an imaginary note drawn up and was never acted upon.

He also said the budget sheet was merely bragging by Michel about his Indian contacts and that Haschke tried to disassociate himself from the Briton.

Strongly denying any wrongdoing in the deal, Haschke also claimed to Indian interrogators in the court that no bribes were paid for the contract and that the money he received from AgustaWestland - in excess of 24 million euros - is justified as fees for engineering consultations.

Italian prosecutors also produced another note in court Thursday - a March 2008 fax by Michel to Peter Hulett, said to be the then head of region, govt sales at AgustaWestland's India office. The fax said that among the politicians who would use the choppers once acquired by India would be UPA chairperson Sonia Gandhi and her senior advisors, including Ahmed Patel.

However, Sonia is not entitled to use government helicopters. She can use VIP aircraft only when she flies with the PM, President or ministers who are officially entitled to the aircraft. This fax by the British middleman has also been shared by the Italian side with the CBI team that is in Busto Arsizio for the hearing.

Michel has been elusive and no investigative agency has been able to reach him.

Haschke, who is facing a case in Italy for being part of a conspiracy to bribe Indian officials to ensure the AW 101 chopper was picked by the IAF, faced several questions from the Indian side and denied any irregularity.

But the Indian side did not ask Haschke to explain what AP, FAM or any of the other acronyms in the note - "DS", "JS AIR", "AFA", "DG Acquisition", CVC" etc - referred to, source said.

The middleman, who was quizzed about his association with former Air Chief S P Tyagi - named as an accused in the CBI case in the deal - denied that any money had been paid to the retired Indian officer. Haschke, sources said, admitted that he was in regular touch with three cousins of Tyagi who have also been named in the case.

In response to a question from the Indian side, Haschke said he was not aware if any money was paid to S P Tyagi.

The UPA government had come under pressure in connection with the alleged kickbacks last month after The Indian Express report on the budget sheet of the middlemen. The opposition BJP had demanded the government reveal what or who "AP" and "FAM" stand for. The party also said that it wants a detailed discussion in Parliament on "alleged payments to persons close to the ruling establishment" in connection with the controversial chopper deal and has accused the government of "running away from discussions".

The discussion did not take place as the Parliament session was abruptly called off midway.

Heading: Now, an apolitical party to look after traders’ needs - Indian Express
Content:
A 20-year-old was arrested by Kandivli police for allegedly stealing CD and DVD players worth Rs 69,000 from four cars. According to the police, the accused Prakash Ashok Pawar, a resident of Ambujwadi slum in Malwani, has confessed to his crime and told the police that he had stolen music systems from four parked cars in S V Road, Dahanukarwadi and Poisar Gymkhana areas.

A team of police officials led by Senior Police Inspector Surendra Kumar Jaiswal was carrying out combing operations in Kandivli when they received a tip off about Pawar's whereabouts. They suspected him of being involved in some unlawful activity and therefore arrested him. During the interrogation, he confessed to having stolen music system.

Police records revealed that Pawar had carried out the thefts last year after which four car owners had lodged complaints at the Kandivli police station. Four music systems were recovered from him. Jaiswal said that Pawar is presently in magisterial custody. He added that the accused had no previous criminal records.

Chitroda gets Rajiv Gandhi Award
The 'Rajiv Gandhi Shiromani Award was conferred by the National Integration and Economic Council (NIE) on Mumbai-based Sonal Chitroda, the founder and chairman-managing director of ALL Services, a facility management firm.

The NIE Council endeavors to recognise individuals who have made outstanding contributions in the fields of industry, business, public life, administrative, social, educational and cultural services. Chitroda's pioneering work in the field of facility management merited not only the Shiromani award but also a gold medal for excellence. ENS

Heading: Now, BMC wants to know when a plane is registered - Indian Express
Content:
Nearly a week after the Federation of Retail Traders' Welfare Association (FRTWA) protested against the Maharashtra Navnirman Sena's (MNS) diktat regarding Marathi signboards, FRTWA joint secretary and owner of Roopam chain of stores Viren Shah on Tuesday announced the formation of an apolitical organisation to look after issues concerning traders in the city.

"There are around 5 lakh traders in the city, several of them do not have a common platform to address their issues and problems. Keeping this in mind, we have decided to form a governing body wherein traders from across the city can openly talk about issues bothering them," Shah said. The name of the organisation is yet to be decided.

Lawyer Majeed Memon and film director Mahesh Bhatt have also extended their support to the organisation. "We will whole heartedly support this body. Such a body is the need of the hour. It will prevent people from taking law in their hands," said Memon. Stressing that this body will be devoid of any political aspirations, Shah said though the body will be looking after the traders' cause, even civilians are welcome to share their grievances with the organisation. "Apart from traders, if anybody has any problems concerning law and order, they too are welcome to come and speak up," he said.

Clearing his stand on the Marathi signboard issue, Shah stated that he has the highest respect for Marathi culture and does not think that any language is inferior to other. "We are not against Marathi culture or the language. Like all Mumbaikars, we too respect the language. We have adhered to the shop and establishment law of 1961, but we would like to carry on our business without any political pressure," he added. Requesting MNS not to create law and order problems in the city Memon said, "Supremacy of law is of primary importance. There cannot be any extra constitutional body dictating terms to us; much less in violent ways. As a party, MNS should respect every community in the city."

Heading: Fake blasts victim: WR seeks apology from channel, producer - Indian Express
Content:
Octroi evasion: Will write to DGCA to have a system in place

After sending notices to two firms, one owned by Anil Ambani and the other by Mukesh Ambani, for alleged evasion of octroi on two planes and one helicopter located in Mumbai, the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) now wants to prevent possible evasion by city-based importers of aircraft and helicopters. The civic administration will soon write a letter to the Union Ministry of Civil Aviation seeking to establish a system through which it will be provided information on aircraft being registered in Mumbai.

"We want a system, as existing in RTOs, where the BMC is kept informed about all the planes and helicopters whose business location is registered as Mumbai," said a senior official from the octroi department. "The letter will be sent to the Director General of Civil Aviation in the next few days."

When a vehicle is registered with the RTO, the BMC is given the information after which it verifies whether octroi is paid or not. "It becomes difficult for the BMC to track down importers who have evaded octroi duty on airplanes as they are registered with the Director General of Civil Aviation in Delhi. It is only through news reports or tip-offs that the vigilance department can get information on octroi evasion," said an official.

Civic officials have already communicated with the DGCA and the ministry is said to have reacted positively to the BMC's demand. "If we receive the intimation on the registration of airplane in Mumbai, we can immediately know whether the octroi is paid or not and follow the issue with importers," the official said. DGCA officials in Delhi were unavailable for comment.

The octroi evasion has been calculated at Rs 16 lakh for Mukesh Ambani's Falcon plane and Rs 18 lakh for Anil Ambani's Bombardier plane and a helicopter, officials told Newsline.

In July, the customs department had issued notices to 50 industrial houses, including Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Commercial Developers Private Limited and Anil Ambani's Reliance Transport and Travel Private limited, for alleged evasion of customs duty.

Heading: Mantralaya area set for Rs 1,000-cr makeover - Indian Express
Content:
Unwilling to take a false charge lying down, the Western Railway on Tuesday issued two letters, one to Sony Television and the other to Gajendra Singh of Saibaba Telefilms, which produces the reality TV show that presented a woman, whose husband died this year, as the widow of a July 2006 serial blasts victim.

Asking them to explain the circumstances in which the show War Parivar hosted by Urmila Matondkar featured an episode on August 11 where Shubhda Santosh Niwate claimed she had not been given compensation despite being a widow of a 7/11 blast victim, the letter signed by Chief Public Relations Officer Shyam Sundar Gupta says: "It is extremely shocking to read the unreal story mentioned in the news report of The Indian Express. It is very sad that a production house, Saibaba Telefilms, which has such a great reputation in the TV industry, has made such a programme which not only delivered the wrong story but also played with the emotions of TV viewers. It also projected the Railways in bad light."

It continues: "You are strongly advised to arrange to publish an unconditional apology in prominent newspapers and in electronic media for damaging the image of Western Railway." It says failing this, the railway administration would be "forced to contemplate" legal action.

The letter to Sony Television also says the channel and the production house have tried to gain TRP ratings by "playing with the emotions" of millions of television viewers.

Niwate had said on the show that her husband worked at the Nagpada police hospital. "He died in the Dadar blast on July 11, 2006," the widow said, speaking in Marathi.

While it is rather commonly known that Dadar was not among the seven locations hit by serial bomb blasts, investigations by The Indian Express also found that Niwate's husband, Santosh Rajaram Niwate, was not one of the 188 people killed in the attacks. Niwate later said she had been roped in with a promise of Rs 50,000.

Despite repeated efforts, Gajendra Singh was unavailable for comment. His spokesperson Puja Nautiyal said she was not aware of such a letter had reached him.

Heading: Olive Ridley turtle rescued from Juhu dies - Indian Express
Content:
Proposal: Three twin towers, underground parking, tunnel

Over 1 lakh sq metres of prime land currently housing the state government's seat of power in Mumbai's most expensive pocket of Nariman Point-Churchgate is all set to be redeveloped to the maximum potential.

The Cabinet Committee on Infrastructure recently approved the proposal submitted by private architect Raja Aederi Consultants for the makeover of the Mantralaya premises. The plan, announced two years ago, was primarily conceived for the complete renovation of the Mantralaya building, the new administrative building and Vidhan Bhavan. It also has provides for an underground car parking and a tunnel connecting Mantralaya building to Vidhan Bhavan.

VK Agarwal, additional chief secretary (planning), confirmed that the committee has given its in-principle approval for the proposal this month along with suggesting minor changes. "The committee has asked for an auditorium to be included for holding meetings, an impressive entrance for Mantralaya and an extra room for guests in each of residential apartments," said Agarwal.

The 20-odd ministers' cottages in the green enclave opposite Mantralaya will be demolished to make way for three multi-storeyed twin towers for ministers, judges and senior officers. While the first two would house 30 sprawling duplexes for ministers and judges, the third would have 60 flats for secretaries. Officials working on the project state that the reservation of a 16,000 sq mt garden and part of the 24 metre wide proposed road would be deleted for the purpose of the twin towers.

"We will still have more open space once the cottages are razed. The public works department will now work out the details and invite bids from developers for the project," Agarwal added.

Pegged at over Rs 1,000 crore, the project includes construction of a 90-suite MLA hostel and a 54-suite guesthouse. There would also be a building for political party offices behind Sarang at Churchgate. The private developers appointed for the project would be allowed to commercially exploit a 17,000 sq mt plot in the vicinity on Build Operate Transfer (BOT) basis.

Heading: ‘If crude prices fall below $100, passengers can expect reduction in air fares next year’ - Indian Express
Content:
A stray Olive Ridley turtle rescued from the Juhu beach in June and which was being treated at the Bombay Society for Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (BSPCA) hospital, died recently, the hospital officials said. The endangered animal, found by civic workers on June 29, had one of its limbs missing and showed signs of chronic illness since the day it was admitted to the hospital, they said.

"The turtle was in a very bad condition when rescued. One of its front limbs was missing, possibly because of an accident. A gangrene had formed around its broken limb and its bones were exposed. We couldn't perform an operation on the amphibian because of its weak health," Dr Yuvraj Kagnikar, BSPCA hospital manager, said. He said the turtle died in the mid week of August.

At the start of the monsoon this year, three full-grown turtles were rescued — one from the Juhu beach and two from Cuffe Parade — and sent to the BSPCA. Olive Ridley turtles, known for their group nesting activity on the shores of Orissa every winter, are listed as endangered in the International Union for the Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources (IUCN) Red list.

According to S B Kadam, assistant secretary of the animal hospital, the dead turtle's carcass has been handed over to the forest department, while the two others have been sent to a rehabilitation centre in Goa after obtaining required permissions. "The health of the limbless turtle was deteriorating and it collapsed while we were planning to shift the turtles. The two healthy ones have now been sent to The Green Cross Animal Rehabilitation Centre in Goa," Kadam said. He added, "It was the first time we shifted the animals by air."

Meanwhile, the forest department has handed over the 10-kg carcass to taxidermist Dr Santosh Gaikwad for preservation. Gaikwad said, "I have started working on preservation of the turtle and it will be complete in about two months."

Heading: 15 years on, 4 convicted in kidnap case - Indian Express
Content:
With oil corporations cutting down on aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices by 16% this Sunday, there was partial relief for domestic carriers. However as far as relief for passengers is concerned, there seem to be none in the offering in the near future.

Despite this fact, there is a possibility of a potential drop in passenger fares if international crude oil prices stabilise at current levels and stay the same for at least the next six months. A senior official from the country's largest private carrier who did not wish to be named said, "If oil prices stay the same and airlines are not treated to the shock and awe of rising crude prices, we can expect a drop in passenger fares in about six months time period."

With ATF prices having dipped after a long time, there is definitely talk among passengers and travel agents whether airlines' stand in not passing the benefit to the passengers is justified. While speaking to Newsline, Sharukh Kapadia, managing committee member, Travel Association of India (TAAI), said, "Prices had hit rock bottom because of competition and only now have airlines got some breathing space. As far as prices are concerned, how can you expect it to come down in such a scenario."

R Sreesankar, head of research at IL&FS Investmart said, "You should realise that airlines were not able to pass on the increase in crude prices because of competition and even when they did pass it on partly, there was a decrease in their load factor. So at present there cannot be an increase but in future it all depends on how domestic fuel prices behave vis-à-vis international crude oil prices."

However Gaurang Shah, Chief Financial Manager at Geojit Financial Services believes that only if crude prices fall below the $100 mark should anybody expect a drop in airline prices. "I don't think that there will be another drop in oil prices till coming December-January but we can only expect a drop in passenger fares, provided oil prices stabalise at current levels, by June-July next year or if crude falls below $100." Shah added, "Airlines did not just have to cope up with rising fuel costs but also rising infrastructure costs. All of it should be taken into account."

Milan Zatakia, representative, Air Passengers Association of India, told Newsline that at least for now, a drop in fare is not being anticipated,"The writing is on the wall and with airlines having lost so much money in past, we should allow them some breathing space," said Zatakia adding, "Or else we'll all have to travel on trains and spend three days on travel for a days work in other cities."

Heading: High Court grants 4-yr-old’s custody to mother - Indian Express
Content:
After 15 years, the Sewree fast track court has convicted four people in a kidnap case. In 1993, jeweller Hasmukhlal Zagda (47) was abducted by associates of his distant relative, Bhartiben Zagda. They wanted to extract Rs 22 lakh from the victim. Ad-hoc assistant sessions judge P M Chouhan sentenced the accused—Mansoor Masudi and Jagannath Surv— to five years of rigorous imprisonment on charges of extortion and wrongful confinement on Tuesday.

Zagda, who ran a family business dealing with gold, was first threatened by unknown persons on February 13, 1993. Six people had landed up at his factory in Borivali and told his brother, Bharat, that Zagda would be killed if he didn't return Rs 22 lakh he owed to one Bharatiben. In his deposition before the court, Zagda claimed that he did not know any Bharatiben but later learnt from his mother that she was his maternal uncle's sister-in-law and had misappropriated some money.

According to Zagda's deposition, on February 17 when he was going to one of his factories, Mansoor Masudi and Krishna Shetty (both accused in the case) dragged him to a waiting rickshaw at gunpoint. Zagda was then taken to a hut near a construction site in Kandivli. The others accused, Manoj Pujari and Jagannath Surve were waiting for him in the hut. They started assaulting Zagda and asked him to pay Rs 22 lakh that he allegedly owed Bharatiben. After torturing Zagda throughout the day, they released him the next day, after telling him that he would have to sell his factory and flat to repay the amount.

Zagda went to the Borivali police station the next day and filed a complaint. The police arrested Pujari soonafter. They seized the spoon, metal plate, revolver, gunny bag, and other tools that were used to torture Zagda. However, the accused were soon released on bail. Pujari was later killed in an encounter while Shetty jumped bail and has been absconding ever since. Bharatiben, who is now a paralytic patient and uses a wheelchair to move, was sentenced to one year imprisonment.

Heading: 16-year-old commits suicide - Indian Express
Content:
The Bombay High Court on Tuesday handed over the custody of a four-year-old child as an interim relief to his mother Deepti Nandlal (34), an Indian citizen, who is entangled in a custody battle with her husband Rishi Nandlal (46), a South African national.

Before passing the order, the Division Bench of Justice B H Marlapalle and Justice D B Bhosale spoke to the couple as well as the child in their chamber. "Both of them seem to have convinced themselves that the marriage is beyond repair," Justice Marlapalle said.

The judges felt that the father should be given the freedom to choose the school for the child's education but also maintained that he should bear the expenditure for schooling.

The court also said that the father should have access to his son whenever he is in India. The court then allowed Rishi to spend time with his son till September 6, when the matter will come up for next hearing.

The judges observed that the child clearly wanted to be with his mother. They also suggested that the couple sit along with their lawyers and discuss terms and conditions for divorce by mutual consent before the family court, independent of the custody matter. The lawyers have sought two days' time for this. As of now, the father may not get the custody of the child but he can visit the child, the court further held.

The judges, however, asked Rishi to deposit his passport in the court till Friday while allowing him to take his son out for the next three days, before he leaves for South Africa on Saturday. Advocate M M Vashi, who appeared for Deepti, had expressed apprehension that Rishi might run away with the child if his passport was not deposited. The court also suggested that the couple make arrangements regarding maintenance for Deepti, their child and his education here while discussing the terms for the divorce.

The boy, who was born on July 16, 2004 in Durban, South Africa, had been living there till December 2006 before he came to Mumbai with his mother. Within eight days of their arrival, Deepti filed a petition for his legal custody and divorce from Rishi. Alleging ill-treatment, she had left Rishi's house in Durban and come to Mumbai to reside with her family. In her petition, Deepti has said that she can take care of her child as she was in a better position to look after him with the support of her family.

Heading: Three arrested for robbing, killing 70-yr-old - Indian Express
Content:
Depressed after having failed her SSC examination, a 16-year-old committed suicide on Tuesday. Pallavi Rajesh Kadam lived in Navjala Chawl on the Dhayabhai Patel Road with her widowed mother Sunita Kadam (35), her maternal uncle Laxman Mahadik (37) and her grandmother. A case of suicide has been registered at the Dindoshi police station.

On Tuesday, she returned home at 2 pm after her classes for the next examination and informed her grandmother that she was going to the fourth floor to sleep. At around 3 pm, her uncle Mahadik found her body hanging from the ceiling. She was immediately rushed to Mava Desai Hospital but was declared brought dead.

"We believe that Pallavi may have been mentally disturbed after failing the examination," said Senior Police Inspector Utam Khairmode of the Dindoshi police station.

Body found on Marine Drive
An unidentified body floated on to the tetra pods on Marine Drive opposite Marine Plaza hotel on Tuesday evening, said police. A pedestrian alerted the police who along with the fire brigade rushed to the spot. With the help of the lifeguards of the fire brigade, the body was recovered and handed over to the police. "The body is of a 25-year-old man and it must have come from other parts of the coast. He seems to be suffering from polio. So far, the only identification mark on his body is an 'Om tattoo' on his right arm," said Police Sub-Inspector S Garud of the Marine Drive police station.

Heading: Indian Craft & Textile Exhibition brings together craftsmen from across the country - Indian Express
Content:
The Mumbai Police Crime Branch on Tuesday arrested three robbers who allegedly murdered and robbed a 70-year-old man in Nehru Nagar on July 31. According to the police, one of the arrested used to work at the victim's jewellery shop. Police said he took the step to take revenge from his employer's son who sacked him, after turning down his leave request.

The arrested have been identified as Navalsingh Dhasana (22), Gangasingh Rajput alias Doctor (20) and Laxmansingh Dhasana (20). While Navalsingh was arrested from Mira Road by Unit 6 of the Crime Branch, the other two accused were picked up from Nallasopara. Two of the four others who are still at large, have been identified as Fatehsingh Rathod (30) and Sumersingh Sadana (25). The police so far has recovered jewellery worth approximately Rs 22,000.

The victim, Moolchand Kothari (70), was the proprietor of Chandresh Jewellers located outside Kurla railway station on Shiv Shrusti Road. Moolchand was also a pawnbroker, and used to keep the jewellery pawned with him at a flat in Naik Nagar Society located near his shop. As part of his daily routine, Kothari used to visit this flat at 12.30 pm everyday to make a list of the pawned jewellery.

On July 31, Kothari went to the flat to check on the jewellery. When he failed to return to the shop, his son sent a servant, identified as Sohanlal Umawat (25), to check on him. Sohanlal returned in a while and informed that Kothari was lying motionless in the shop with his limbs bound and his mouth gagged. When his son rushed to the flat, he found Kothari dead and some of the jewellery robbed. Crime Branch Unit 6 worked on the case, and arrested three involved on Tuesday afternoon.

Joint Commissioner of Police, (Crime), Rakesh Maria said, "This is a dangerous gang, that might be involved in several serious cases. These accused do not leave any witnesses behind." He added, "All the accused involved hail from Rajsamand district in Rajasthan. Navalsing worked in Kothari's shop for eight years. Around two and a half years ago, Kothari lost a hand in an accident and was in hospital. Navalsing asked Kothari's son for leave in order to visit his native place at the time, and was slapped by him for his request. This is when he decided to take revenge on his employers. He knew Kothari's routine, and was aware of the pawned jewellery kept in the flat near the shop. A month prior to the offence, he conducted a recce of the place by turning up on the pretext of looking for a job."

According to the police Navalsing passed on the tip to Gagansingh, who in turn informed Fatehsingh. The latter then roped in the other accused. The police are now on the lookout for four others involved in the case. The police believe that the arrests have caused a major set back to a gang of criminals allegedly involved in several crimes in the city.

Heading: Ramabai Nagar firing: Witness says injured did not attack police - Indian Express
Content:
Leather lampshades from Andhra Pradesh, lacquered and terracotta wood from Gujarat, palm leaf etchings from Orissa, and Warli paintings from Maharashtra have been displayed in all their glory at the Indian Craft and Textile Exhibition, held by the non-profit organisation, Paramparik Karigar.

The exhibition, was inaugurated on Tuesday by Nana Chudasama, the founder of Giants International, at the Coomaraswamy Hall in Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya. The exhibition will showcase traditional art and craft exhibits from all over the country.

Paramparik Karigar, the organisation which holds the exhibition annually, allows craftsmen from different corners of the country to exhibit their art, and gives them a platform to market their wares in cities across the country. The craftsmen who are invited to the exhibitions held by the NGO, are allowed to sell their craft directly to consumers, thus eliminating any middlemen from entering the picture.

Venkat Raman Singh Shyam, a craftsman from Madhya Pradesh, who paints in the Gond Tribal style, using both acrylic and natural paints says, "I began painting when I was seven years old. Most of what I do is based on traditional mythology and nature." The gifted artist adds, 'There are no middlemen involved here, and the artist himself interacts with the buyer. We are also given awards, fellowships and other encouragement." He also points at the fact that the art and crafts exhibited during Paramparik Karigar exhibitions are separate from the textile exhibits, making it a better experience for many buyers.

Hanif Galwani, who comes from a family of potters says, "I've been associated with Paramparik Karigar for eight years now. It's an art that runs in my family. This is an excellent place to market our goods. Otherwise, nobody would know us, since we work out of Dharavi." Maharana Dilipkumar, whose father had been associated with Paramparik Karigar, something that he plans to continue says, "Most of our paintings are made from natural colours and have mythological depictions. The fine drawings are made from rat hair."

Anu Sorabjee, a volunteer with Paramparik Karigar, while acknowledging the talent of the artists who exhibit their work says, "The craftsman is the most important person here. When they do well, the difference can be seen among their families and their villages. We also send them abroad for exhibitions and to showcase their work there."

Heading: Property scam: Police say directors of shipping company cheated Russian embassy - Indian Express
Content:
The Sewri fast track court examined two more witnesses in the Ramabai firing case on Tuesday.

Dr Ketan Vaghulkar from Rajawadi Hospital who had attended four injured persons after the incident, told the court that the condition of all the four victims was critical. Producing the medical reports prepared after the accident, Dr Ketan Vaghulkar on Tuesday informed the court that all four victims were fired at from long distance and none would have reached the policemen. Injured persons—Heeraman Gaikwad, Vijay Gaikwad, Ramchandra Kadam and Bapu Kolekar—were attended by Vaghulkar. Police's version states that the firing was carried out only after the mob converged and attempted to attack the police.

Another witness, Tai Bai Kamble, sister of injured Dattu Kamble, also said that none of the injured persons had traveled towards the west of the location. According to the police a tanker parked near the chawl had been set on fire by the furious mob which had led to the firing.

On July 11, 1997, state reserve police officer Manohar Kadam had ordered his platoon to open fire on a mob of dalits for allegedly rioting at Mata Ramabai Ambedkar Nagar following desecration of Dr B R Ambedkar's statue. The incident claimed 10 lives and injured 26.

A commission was appointed under justice S D Gundewar in November 1997, which completed its inquiry in August 1998.

The report indicted Kadam for firing indiscriminately at the mob.

The state sanctioned Kadam's prosecution in August 2001 and an FIR was lodged against him with the Pantnagar police station on August 30 that year.

Heading: Christian organisations call for end to Orissa violence - Indian Express
Content:
No evidence against the accused in the case and they are not part of the conspiracy to cheat the Russian Government , say police

The Mumbai police while defending its decision to give a clean chit to five persons, accused of cheating the Consulate of Russia by allegedly forging papers and selling property at Malabar Hill, have named two Russian nationals as prime accused in the case. The property had been leased to the Russian embassy by the state government.

While replying to the criminal revision application filed by Russian Consul General Alexander V Mantytsky challenging the acquittal of Dawood Moinuddin (62), Anand Vora (35), Dina Shah (52), Lohit Kankadi (47) and Pravin Kumar Shukla (25), the police said there was no evidence against the accused in the case and they were not part of the conspiracy to cheat the Russian Government.

In the reply filed by Assistant Commissioner of Police (Azad Maidan Division) Isaaq Bhagwan, the police said that the two prime accused were two directors — Andrew Stechenko and Valentin Lysyi— of the Soprat shipping company, a Russian company to which the Marine House (the disputed property) was given for lodging its employees. The two directors had allegedly forged the documents and sold it to Moinuddin for $ 10 million. The police also issued a Red Corner notice against the wanted accused.

The Russian Consulate had moved the sessions court after these five persons who were accused of cheating the Consulate walked free without any trial, after the police gave them a clean chit.

Bhagwan in his reply further said the sale deal took place in Dubai where Moinuddin, a Non Resident Indian (NRI), lives. The two wanted accused Stechenko and Lysyi forged the ownership papers of the 15,000 sq ft property and sold it to Dawood in 2006. Soon after the sale, they fled to Moscow, the reply said. The money was also transferred to the bank accounts of the accused in Moscow.

According to a complaint lodged by Russian consul general Alexander V Mantytsky at the Malabar Hill police station on July 20, 2006, private security guards posted at the entrance prevented him from entering the premises when he paid a visit to the building in April 2006. He was told the property had been bought by Dubai's Dawood Moinuddin for $10 million.

The police then filed a report in the 40th magistrate's court at Girgaum stating that the five accused had not committed any offence of cheating and forgery. In an order passed on March 21, 2007, Magistrate V S Dixit acquitted them. Following this, Mantysky moved the sessions court praying that the magistrate's order is bad in law and should be set aside.

Heading: Aneesa Mirza, who turned city’s mega dream into a reality, passes away - Indian Express
Content:
Christian organisations in the city along with film director Mahesh Bhatt and social activist Teesta Setalvad said at a press conference on Friday that 'attrocities' against the Christians in Orissa must end soon. They said they would call for a ban on Hindu organisations which worked as outfits to generate terror. The meet was planned by the Catholic Secular Forum along with the All India Christian Council and the Indian Christian Voice. Two priests who had fled from one of the villages in Orissa also attended the meet. They described the situation in the state and displayed photographs of churches and homes which were destroyed by mobs.

Speaking on the occassion, filmmaker Mahesh Bhatt said, "We have spoken to the President and we pointed out that India is heading for elections and that it is always possible for political parties to intervene for profit and to enlarge their power base."

R B Sreekumar, former DGP of the Gujarat police, who was also present at the meeting, said, "The happenings in Orissa are a clear subversion of the criminal justice system." He added, "Even in December 2007, it was clear that the Hindu mobs targeted the areas where the Christians shopped, but no officers were punished, and nothing was done. This is why the violence this time is completely related to the incidents of December 2007."

While appealing to people of Mumbai to extend support to the victims of the carnage in Orissa, Teesta Setalvad said, "Over 40 people have been killed so far and 13,000 people have been living in six relief camps. Orissa is one of the poorest states and these are some of the poorest people whose homes have been destroyed." Setalvad also said that apart from providing immediate relief to the victims, they were also awaiting the reports of the fact-finding commission, which would be out in 15-20 days and would shed more light on the December 2007 happenings.

General secretary of the Catholic Secular Forum, Joseph Dias said that they would try and build moral pressure to get various parties like the BJP and the VHP to issue a formal apology for the events in Orissa. "Their silence speaks for itself," he said.

Heading: ‘Terror manual’ recovered by DCB from mosque well - Indian Express
Content:
Former mayor worked tirelessly to earn the mega city tag for Ahmedabad

Aneesa Begum Yusuf Ali Mirza, during whose mayoral tenure Ahmedabad was declared a mega-city, died on Tuesday. She was 56 and is survived by three sons.

When she took charge of the mayor's office in April 2003, she had expressed confidence about getting the cooperation and support of the members of the Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) while pursuing her dream of converting Ahmedabad into a mega city. Two years later, her dream finally came true.

Mirza had also upheld the tradition of putting development above party politics, when she became the mayor.

She took to active politics in 1969 when she joined the Congress. In 1987, she was given the party ticket to contest from the Raikhad ward, from where she emerged victorious. She went on a winning spree since then and earned the nickname of aapa (elder sister). Though she maintained the impression of having a stiff upper lip, she was very much concerned about the downtrodden, especially the slum dwellers.

She fought many a pitched battle for their rights, despite her failing health. Perhaps her fighting skills came from her love of chess. She was a great patron of the game in the city.

A double post-graduate, Mirza did her MA in History from St John's College, Agra and MA in English from University of Udaipur where she also did her LLB before coming to Ahmedabad in 1968.

The daughter of a former judge of the Rajasthan High Court, Mirza had done social work under the guidance of Mridula Sarabhai and Hemlata Hegishte, well-known social workers of their time.

Mirza was known for her erudition and subtle political sarcasm while speaking in the AMC general board meetings. She was also known for her penchant for quoting Urdu couplets and Hindi dohas during her speeches.

Her spotless white dress had become her trademark identity on the AMC premises. She was also a great fan of famous Urdu poets and authors and had maintained family relations with many of them.

Watching her argue over delicate literary topics at select gatherings – be it poetry or prose – used to be a sheer delight. At the same time, she tirelessly championed the cause of the homeless and did not shy away from taking up the cudgels for their rights.

Heading: State govt tutors citizens to tackle terror - Indian Express
Content:
Register fished out by cops has details of Mumbai blast probe, police interrogation techniques and way to circumvent them

Acting on a tip-off, the Ahmedabad City Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) recovered several incriminating documents from a well in the Sidi Saiyed Mosque compound near Lal Darwaja on Monday.

The documents include a register in Gujarati language containing details of police investigations in the 2007 Mumbai train blasts, a training manual for the terror camps across the country and police interrogation techniques including the Narco Analysis Test and the ways to circumvent them.

Assistant Superintendent of Police Himanshu Shukla announced this at a press briefing on Tuesday.

He said most of the documents recovered are either in Urdu or in Hindi, with the exception of the register. He said some of the documents are also inflammatory in nature and instigate the people to die in the name of religion.

He said the DCB also recovered some magazines in Urdu and Hindi. One of them, titled Nishan-e-Raah, has been edited by Mufti Abu Bashir, the mastermind of the Ahmedabad blasts.

Shukla said the documents were wrapped in a plastic bag and were thrown inside the well by one of the accused in the Ahmedabad serial blasts. He said the accused had abandoned the materials so that the police could not lay their hands on it, in case his house was raided. The bag was recovered with the help of the officials of the Ahmedabad Fire and Emergency Services.

Shukla refused to name the accused who had disposed off the documents in the well.

Heading: Schools strike back, observe total strike - Indian Express
Content:
Comes out with full-page ad in local dailies suggesting ways to combat terror

The Information Department of the Gujarat government released a full page advertisement in the local dailies on Tuesday on means to combat terror. The ad issued in Gujarati urged all citizens to come together to wipe out terrorism.

It also listed the precautions the people should take in their various day-to-day activities.

The ad comes with some 'interesting' observations and provides a checklist of signs to identify a terrorist.

It says: A terrorist could be a person loitering around in a coat or jacket in summer, or without one in winter. A terrorist will walk uninvited into community programmes and try to strike polite conversation with the people. Also, if a person's clothes bulge at all the wrong places, it may be because he is hiding a bomb or a weapon inside, the advertisement says.

Bhagyesh Jha, Director, Information Department, said all suggestions listed in the advertisement were formulated carefully based on intelligence reports. "We went through everything in the advertisement before it was released. All the suggestions made are based on intelligence inputs," he said.

P P Pandey, Additional Director General of Police (Intelligence) said: "The tips in the advertisement are based on inputs provided by us."

The ad also asks people to spot differences in the front and rear number plates of vehicles. The police should be informed if a car is found tilting suspiciously due to a heavy boot, the ad says.

Car dealers in the state have also been advised to carry out a thorough check on customers from other parts of the country interested in buying or selling vehicles. The locals have, however, been exempted from this. But the advisory does insist on verifying the documents of the customers , including retaining a photograph of the customer for record.

The ad further narrows down the search by telling people that the terrorists may be found in places like hospitals, railway and bus stations, religious places and malls.

There are also pointers in the advertisement that highlight the steps be taken in case of a terrorist attack. It says that people should look for safer places away from high-rise buildings or parking lots and contact the police.

The advertisement ends with a call to 'come together and identify them.'

A Modi confidant said: "Certainly, the advertisement has political implications. While there has been a significant restraint in the party's reaction after the blast, with most of the suspected masterminds arrested from all over the country, Modi has already proved his mettle as a tough fighter against terrorism. These advertisements will only project him as an effective leader ahead of the Lok Sabha polls."

valuable Suggestions

In case of a terrorist attack:

* Run to a safe place, avoid high-rises and parking lots. Inform the police.

After the attack:

* Call 100, follow police instructions. Leave the site immediately and make way for security vehicles.

In property dealings: Get the details of the person in question, including documents establishing his/her identity. In case of suspicion, call the police.

How can you help

* Remember the faces of people who look suspicious.

* Unclaimed objects at bus stations, railway stations and airports must be reported to the police. In case of an emergency, call 100 immediately.

* Co-operate with the security agencies in case of any investigation or inquiry.

Impractical suggestions

* Ways to spot a terrorist: Anyone who wears clothes that aren't suitable for that season. Any uninvited person who tries to mingle in community gatherings. Clothes that bulge out may be hiding bombs and weapons. Be cautious of car buyers and seller from outside Gujarat.

Heading: ‘Politics never weakened our bond’ - Indian Express
Content:
All private schools in Rajkot remain closed in protest against assault on school staff by parents

More than 510 primary and 205 secondary and higher secondary self-financed schools in Rajkot city and 74 other self-financed schools in major centres of Rajkot district like Morbi, Wankaner and Gondal remained closed on Tuesday in protest against the assault on school staff by parents.

The strike call has been given by the Rajkot district Self Finance School Administrative Association (RSFSAA).

On Monday, owners, staff and students of the schools took out a silent protest rally from Chaudhary High School playground and went to the District Education Office, District Collector Office and Police Commissioner's Office. They submitted a memorandum to all the authorities regarding the assault by the parents on school staff and gave a strike call for Tuesday. However, some self-finance cum granted schools of the city avoided to take part in the strike

The agitation was triggered after some parents assaulted and abused the owner and teachers of P.V.Modi Schools, after a student went missing from the school a few days ago. It was later found that the boy had escaped from the school to attend the Janmashtami fair.

Bharat Gajipara, president of RSFSAA, said they are not protesting against any one in particular. The aim of their protest is to create discipline in society. "We just want a proper atmosphere to provide best the education to children. Teachers will stop taking personal interest in a student's career if parents create a big ruckus over every small issue and attack the school staff. It will ultimately cost the students only. We just want to create awareness in society. We want to request parents to co-operate with the schools and teachers."'

He added: "In order to compensate for the students' academic loss because of the strike, the self-financed schools will remain open on the coming Sunday, September 7," he said.

The National Students Union of India (NSUI), however, has opposed the ongoing agitation by the city schools. In protest against the strike, NSUI supporters submitted a memorandum to the District Education Officer, demanding strict action against these schools. In a press release, the NSUI said that after taking a huge fee from the students, the self-financed schools cannot observe strikes and play with the future of the children.

District Education Officer, K.D.Bagda said he was not happy with the action taken by either the parents or the school authorities.

"Neither should the parents assault the teachers in front of students nor should the schools observe a strike and close down over a single issue. However, these schools will compensate for the loss of students' academic day by holding classes on Sunday. But this is against the rule that except vacations, no schools can keep classes on Sundays. NSUI members have come to me with the demand to take action against these schools. We are not giving any kind of grants to these schools. They are just affiliated to us. At the end of the day, the students will suffer if we take any hard steps like cancellation of the affiliation," he said.

Heading: Union Agriculture Secretary appointed GERC Chairman - Indian Express
Content:
Gujarat Assembly Speaker Ashok Bhatt pays homage to his 'rakhi sister'

In a way, it's a personal loss to me. For, Aneesaben always considered me her 'rakhi brother' and had been tying a rakhi on my wrist every year on Rakshabandhan over the last three decades. I don't remember her ever having skipped a visit to my residence at Khadia on Rakshabandhan.

It was a proud moment for me when she went on to become the Mayor of this historic city while representing the Raikhad ward as a councillor. Although she belonged to a different political party, politics never intruded into our 'brother-sister' relationship, and we continued to share this bond for ages. I made it a point to visit her house on Id every year.

She was one of the most successful and efficient mayors of the city. During her mayoral stint, she took a series of measures for the all-round development of Ahmedabad.

She represented the Raikhad ward and would take special care of the poor and the middle class, who comprise a major chunk of the voters here. I was also impressed by her oratory skills, which was often punctuated by Urdu couplets.

Aneesaben was the first Muslim woman to become a mayor in the country and was in the truest sense of the term an 'iron lady' with a brave heart.

I still remember how 10 years ago she fearlessly entered the operation theatre to undergo a by-pass surgery. I had accompanied her to the hospital then. Just two days before she left this world, I visited her at the V S Hospital to inquire about her health. I was a bit shaken as she was in coma. May her soul rest in peace.

As told to Bashir Pathan

Heading: Junagadh Agriculture College wins first prize in cultural event at international expo - Indian Express
Content:
Gujarat cadre IAS officer P K Mishra was earlier Chief Minister Narendra Modi's Principal Secretary

Gujarat cadre IAS officer Dr P K Mishra has been appointed as Chairman of the Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission (GERC). Mishra is known to be close to Chief Minister Narendra Modi and was his Principal Secretary before he went to New Delhi on a Central deputation in 2004. He retired as a Secretary in the Union Agriculture Ministry on August 31.

On Tuesday, Modi administered him the oath of office. State Chief Secretary Manjula Subramaniam, Additional Chief Secretary (GAD) George Joseph, Principal Secretary (Energy) M M Srivastav and senior GERC officials were present on the occasion,

Mishra had earlier told Newsline over the phone from Delhi that he was informed of his new appointment by the State Energy Department .

He had said his topmost priority as GERC Chairman would be to encourage and facilitate competition among the public and the private players in the power sector in Gujarat.

"It will be easy for me to handle the new task, for during my previous tenure here, I had spent about six years in the Gujarat State Electricity Corporation (GSEC) as its MD, and three years in the Gujarat Electricity Board (now GUVNL) as a member secretary (Finance)," he said.

Mishra said he was also offered the post of a Country Director of the Food and Agriculture Organization of the UN. "But I did not accept the offer as I did not want to move outside the country," he added.

The post of GERC chairman had been lying vacant since January this year, when the term of senior retired bureaucrat G Subbarao came to an end. The government decided to appoint Mishra after the Gujarat High Court recently directed it to fill the slot in response to a petition filed by a local consumer body.

Incidentally, Mishra's appointment was a foregone conclusion as his name had been shortlisted in July this year by a search committee headed by Justice A M Kapadia of the High Court.

Mishra's immediate task as GERC chief would be to tackle two identical petitions filed by the GUVNL and Torrent - proposing to hike the multi- year power tariff.

While the hearing of the Torrent petition is over, the hearing of the GUVNL's petition is yet to be taken up.

Heading: Pious pledge: Girl students of 226 schools to launch postcard campaign to save the ‘girl child’ - Indian Express
Content:
A students' team from the Junagadh Agriculture College (JAC) has won the first prize in a cultural event organised at the International livestock and dairy expo (ILDEX) -2008 in New Delhi.

A total of 136 private sector run agriculture based companies and 10 agriculture universities took part in the international event. From Gujarat, only the Junagadh Agriculture College was invited for the expo.

Ridhdhi Jadeja, a team member said: "We performed the Garba and received accolades for our performance, which was adjudged the best at the venue."

The team was headed by Dr Virendra Singh, Assistant Professor, Department of Horticulture, JAC, and was awarded with a trophy and certificate. Other members of the team include Dhirajsinh Rathod, Rajani Mayur, Maliwad Shivam, Gholiya Mayur, Hadiya Bharat, Priyana Gupta and Ila Pithiya.

Dr B K Kikani, Vice-Chancellor, Junagadh Agriculture University has congratulated the JAC students on their success .

Heading: Flood of sympathy: Citizens, NGOs come forward to help Bihar victims - Indian Express
Content:
As part of its mission to save the girl child, the Saurashtra Jaldhara Trust (SJT) of Surat distributed 2 lakh post cards to the representatives of 226 schools of the city, on Tuesday. The girl students of these schools, aged 13 to 17 will write messages on the postcards and send them to different schools in other talukas.

At a meeting held at the Saurashtra Samaj Hall at Varachha today, Surat Municipal Commissioner S. Aparna, Veer Narmad South Gujarat University Vice-Chancellor Babubhai Prajapati, South Gujarat Chamber of Commerce President Chetan Shah, Surat District Education Officer K R Zanzhrukiya and other well-known personalities participated along with the representatives of the schools.

Mathurbhai Savani of SJT said two years ago, the people of Saurashtra staying in the Varachha area had organised a programme against female foeticide. Lakhs of people from different parts of state had participated in the programme, she said.

The SJT also has plans to organise a Jal Yatra on theBeti Bachao Abhiyan from Surat to the Somnath Temple in the near future. The rally will begin on October 31 at Surat and end on November 5 at Somnath, covering 226 talukas between the two centres. Water will be collected from the different talukas, which will then be handed over to the priest of the Somanth Temple. A bottle containing this water will be gifted to President Pratibha Patil. The rally will pass through Ankleshwar, Vadodara, Ahmedabad, Unja, Surendranagar, Rajkot and Junagadh.

"We expect a huge participation in the six-day rally. Over 300 cars will be used in this rally flashing banners of Beti Bachao Abhiyan. We have planned the rally in such a way that the participants will come in contact with people of all the 226 talukas, who will take an oath over water from their village. The water will be then handed over to the rally participants," said Savani.

Heading: Govt nod to 100-seat medical college at Patan - Indian Express
Content:
City-based DAPA launches a massive drive for collecting 1 lakh sarees

After the Gujarat government announced a financial assistance package of Rs 5 crore to the flood-affected in Bihar, its now the turn of the citizens and NGOs to come forward and support the displaced people.

Goonj, a Bihar based NGO, contacted Darpana Academy of Performing Arts (DAPA) on Tuesday to request for 1 lakh sarees for women.

Mallika Sarabhai, co-director of DAPA told Newsline: "The NGO contacted us on Tuesday morning. They asked us to collect around 1 lakh sarees. The flood victims are getting basic necessities like chiwra, biscuits, packed eatables, water purifier tablets, medicines, children clothing, bed sheets, stoves, utensils and buckets from all over the

country."

She added: "The clothes that have reached the affected areas are primarily western, which the rural women are not accustomed to wearing. We have set up five collection centres and are appealing the public to donate sarees for the flood-affected."

Anshu Gupta, founder director of Goonj, said: "We contacted people in Gujarat and Maharasthra for sarees. We hope to get more support from Gujarat, especially Surat, as it is the textile centre of the country."

Meanwhile, Janpath, a network of voluntary action groups in Gujarat has started a Bihar Calamity Response Initiative (BCRI) in Ahmedabad.

Harinesh Pandya, Ahmedabad Secretary, Janpath, said: "With active support from 'Punjabi Seva Samaj', a relief collection centre has been set up at the Punjabi Seva Samaj in Navrangpura."

He added: "This initiative has got an overwhelming response from the society and received contributions in the form of clothing, tarpaulin, jaggery etc."

Heading: Two blast accused were frequent visitors to Paldi cyber café - Indian Express
Content:
Proposals for establishing medical colleges at Mehsana and Palanpur also under consideration

It's raining medical colleges in Gujarat. The government has decided to set up a 100-seat medical college at Dharpur village near Patan in north Gujarat, for which it has already allotted 60 acres of land.

In addition, proposals for establishing medical colleges, one each at Mehsana and Palanpur are also under consideration.

State Health Minister Jay Narayan Vyas said on Tuesday that the government had sent an application and other necessary documents, including an essentiality certificate and financial statement, to the Medical Council of India (MCI) in Delhi for setting up a medical college near Patan.

Vyas also said the government was open to the idea of setting up a medical college near Patan on a public private partnership (PPP) model.

If any individual or group of donors can come forward to bear at least 50 per cent of the total cost (of medical college), we are not averse to the idea of attaching their names to the proposed institute," he said.

The government was also actively considering two separate proposals -- one received from an educational group to establish a medical college at Mehsana and the other from a renowned public trust to set up a similar institute at Palanpur, Vyas said, adding, "My department will also positively consider setting up a medical college in Sabarkantha, if a concrete proposal for this comes from the district".

Heading: As Dalit activists cry hoarse, state fares poorly on implementation of SC/ST Act - Indian Express
Content:
Qayamuddin and Tauqeer made seven rounds between April and July

Qayamuddin and Abdul Subhan alias Tauqeer, two of the main accused in the Ahmedabad serial blasts, had visited a cyber café in the Paldi area of Ahmedabad at least seven times between April and July in 2008, the Ahmedabad Detection of Crime Branch (DCB) said.

On Monday night, the DCB conducted a raid on the Inet Cyber Café at the Lal Bahadur Shastri Complex near NID in the Paldi area and seized the hard disks of seven computers.

These were sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) for investigation.

The café is owned by one Adil Malik, a resident of Juhapura area, the police said.

Ashish Bhatia, Joint Commissioner of Police, DCB, said: "During the investigation, we found that Tauqeer and Qayamuddin had been visiting the cyber café for four months prior to the blasts."

DCB officers said investigations into the presence of the accused at the café could provide some vital evidence in connection with the threatening email, which was sent just before the Ahmedabad blasts.

They added that details about the kind of activities the two indulged in at the cyber café would only be known after proper investigation of the seized hard disks by the FSL.

Hemant Karkare, Joint Commissioner of Police, Mumbai ATS, said: "In view of the fresh evidence, we will send our team to look into the developments to get a clear idea."

Heading: Figure it out: Cases of atrocities against Dalits on decline, says Govt - Indian Express
Content:
Panel to monitor atrocity meets for fourth time but has no outcome to show
