Even as the state committee for monitoring the Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe Atrocities (Prevention) Act met for the fourth time on Tuesday, the Dalit activists are crying hoarse over the lackadaisical implementation of the Act in Gujarat.

Dalit activists have now submitted a memorandum to the Chief Minister, who also happens to be the Chairman of the committee, in this regard.

"We have been collecting evidence of non-implementation of this Act across Gujarat for a long time through various means including the Right to Information (RTI) Act," said Kirit Rathod, Secretary, Gujarat Nagrik Adhikar Suraksha Samiti.

"In our memorandum, we have listed such lapses and examples the committee could take up for consideration. For example, Section 16 of the Act has provisions for mass penal actions. But in the absence of any such steps, atrocities like social boycott and mass exodus from villages are growing across the state," he added.

He said there is also a provision whereby at least one member of a victim family is to be provided subsistence assistance.

But till date, such a step has not been taken anywhere in the state.

Even the monitoring committee has met only four times compared to the 14 meetings it ought to have held till now since its inception in 1995, Rathod said.

The three previous meetings were held on January 27, 1999, August 25, 2004 and May 31, 2006.

"The committee has met as a routine process and the issues included in the agenda were discussed," said a member of the committee.

While the activists did meet the government representatives with their memorandum, the grievances raised by them will be addressed separately, the member said.

"What they brought along was not a part of our agenda and the government will address those concerns separately," the member added.

Heading: City cops on their toes as season of festivities begins - Indian Express
Content:
While activists raised the issue of effective implementation of laws to fight crimes against the Scheduled Castes and Tribes, the official figures say there is now a decline of 44.03 per cent of registered crime among the SCs in the state. For the STs the corresponding figure has gone down to 48.26 per cent.

A statement issued by the Gujarat government has said that the decline is a result of the effective measures taken by the state. It has said that the registered crime against Dalits has come down from 1844 in 1997 to 654 in 2007. The corresponding figure for STs has gone down from 400 in 1997 to 108 in 2007.

The fourth meeting of the State Monitoring Committee for the implementation of SC/ST Atrocities (Prevention) Act was convened under the chairmanship of Chief Minister Narendra Modi at Gandhinagar on Tuesday.

Modi has sanctioned six new courts for dealing with atrocities against the SC/STs. At present, there are 10 such courts in the state.

Heading: Municipality chief officer arrested, granted bail - Indian Express
Content:
Security stepped up to ensure peaceful Ramzan and Ganesh Utsav

The City police are taking no chances with security this time with Ramzan and Ganesh Utsav happening side-by-side. Sensitive areas have been brought under CCTV surveillance, while the installation of metal detectors at puja pandals and appointment of women guards there have also been mooted.

Vadodara Police Commissioner Rakesh Asthana said: "Along with routine vigilance and cooperating with the public, we will be installing about 20-25 CCTV systems on an experimental basis on almost all the communally sensitive locations of the city. Normally, during a riot, a case is registered against a faceless mob while the real culprits go scot-free. These CCTV cameras will help us bring the real perpetrators to the book. Still photographs and videos will be shot. These measures will be in place during the whole period of Ganeshotsav, but we will be extra careful during the visharjan period, which is more prone to communal violence."

Asthana further said that the various Mandal Samitis organising the Ganeshotsav have been asked to tell their volunteers to be extra cautious this time and report any suspicious activity or person (s) to the police. "Though it is not compulsory, but we have also advised them to install metal detectors at the pandals and even employ women security guards to frisk the women entering them," he added.

Meanwhile, the Deputy Collector (Civil Defence Force) Ranjan Waja also called a meeting of the civil defence committee. Ravindra Brahmashatriya, a staff officer of the Civil Defence Committee, said: "We have been asked to educate the normal public to be more vigilant this time round. As people in huge numbers crowd the public places during this time, the civil defence people will work with the police round-the-clock to ensure the festival passes off peacefully in the city."

Heading: NSUI’s Gaekwad elected commerce faculty gen sec - Indian Express
Content:
A Minor tiff between the wives of Rajpipla municipality chief officer Nitin Bodat and Dakshin Gujarat Vij Company Limited (DGVL) engineer, Sandeep Bhagat, led to the arrest of the former on Tuesday. According to Rajpipla police, Bodat was arrested when the engineer's wife, Dipti Bhagat, accused him of slapping her five times on August 26. He was granted bail on Tuesday evening.

Inspector T K Patel of Rajpipla police station said, "Bodat and Bhagat are neighbours at the Karjan Colony in Rajpipla area of Nanod taluka in Narmada district. Their wives quarreled over a minor issue when their children were playing outside. It was then that Bodat allegedly barged into Bhagat's residence and slapped Dipti."

Bodat has been arrested under Sections 452, 504, 506 (2) and 323 of the IPC for trespassing, assaulting and thereby causing breach of peace. He was recently appointed as the municipality chief officer.

Heading: Rush for Russian: MSU students strike rich - Indian Express
Content:
National Students Union of India (NSUI) candidate Raviraj Gaekwad won the M S University (MSU) Commerce Faculty elections to the post of General Secretary on Tuesday. Gaekwad defeated Independent candidate Pratik Rajput by 510 votes and Akhil Bharatiya Vidhyarthi Parishad (ABVP) candidate Nilesh Kahar by 693 votes.

Jyoti Achanta, MSU Commerce faculty Presiding Officer said: "Gaekwad polled 973 votes, but Rajput and Kahar could manage only 463 and 280 votes respectively."

A total of 1996 votes were cast for the five candidates in fray, of which 45 were found to be invalid. The voting per cent this year was around 11. 5, much less in comparison to last year's figures, said faculty officials.

Heading: MiG-29 wreckage found near bird sanctuary - Indian Express
Content:
As MNCs explore new markets in Russia, varsity students cash in on dearth of language experts

Globalisation is registering a welcome effect on the foreign languages department of the M S University (MSU). Prospective employers are now making a beeline to the Department of Russian Language, as the market is now looking towards Russia.

While a multinational company (MNC) has employed two students this month to collate and analyse the expertise of companies in Russia, 10 others have been absorbed in the Navratna public sector undertakings such as Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) and Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC), to survey the Russian market.

Even as teachers of the said department refused to name the MNCs offering jobs, Julie Thomas, a final year Russian Language student said, "I have recently appeared in a test where an MNC asked us to analyse and compare the cost and mode of payment in three Russian companies. Our reports have been sent to Paris for further analysis."

Along with Julie, another student named Dhruti Trivedi is likely to be employed by the company.

There is a dearth of expertise in the Russian language in India. Therefore, companies doing business with this country find it difficult to deal with them, said Prof Debal Dasgupta of the MSU Russian Department.

He added: "Few months ago, Prime Minister Manmohan Singh had made an official announcement to develop a human resource proficient in Russian. The Russian market had witnessed a decline in the '90s, but due to a change in its market strategy in 2005, Russia is rising again. Therefore, those interested in doing business with this country need people to communicate in Russian."

While most of the fighter aircraft such as the MiG and the Sukhoi in the inventory of the Indian Air Force are Russian, yet only a fraction of the population understands the language. The PSUs and Indian MNCs need to learn a lot of strategies from the Russian market, said Prof Dasgupta.

In recent times, not only HAL and ONGC but also IT companies like Infosys and Wipro have recruited students from the Russian Language Department, he said.

"Even small-scale industries such as optical shops in Vadodara and broom-stick manufacturers in Kerala are coming to the Russian and French departments to smoothen their overseas business transactions. These companies offer jobs too," said Prof Dasgupta, who is single-handedly managing the Russian and French departments.

Heading: HC stalls MC chief polls in Punjab - Indian Express
Content:
The wreckage of the MIG-29 fighter that crashed off the Jamnagar coast on Monday has been located 3.5 miles off Narara Bet, a bird sanctuary near the Off-shore Oil Terminal (OOT) at Kandla.

Sources said the Indian Coast Guard (ICG) had sent two boats, C-132 and IC 110, from its Vadinar base to help the Navy salvage the wreckage, which was found floating on a 30-metre deep stretch in the Arabian sea.

The satellite oil terminal of the Kandla port had a miraculous escape, as the jet had crashed five nautical miles from the second Single Buoy Mooring (a small, round floating platform in mid-sea to unload crude oil) of the Indian Oil Corporation.

Two huge oil tankers were working in the Vadinar harbour when the jet crashed. While the oil tanker, Devasi, from Bombay High was unloading its cargo of 73,000 metric tonne crude oil at the second SMB, another oil tanker, Formasa, was loading oil at a newly constructed jetty of Essar Oil.

"Thank god the plane crashed 8 kms away from the jetty. I visited the crash site yesterday and found the wreckage scattered all over the place," Dr G S Rao, Chief Operations Manager and head of OOT, Vadinar, told Newsline on Tuesday.

He said they offered all possible help to the Coast Guard during the salvage operation.

Sources said a major disaster was averted on Monday. Had the fighter crashed into any of the tankers on work, it would have been a catastrophe. Marine life would have been destroyed, apart from a huge economic loss.

Heading: ‘All schools must have a panel to redress sexual harassment’ - Indian Express
Content:
A Division Bench of Punjab and Haryana High Court today stalled the elections to the office of president in all municipal councils in Punjab till further orders.

The orders were passed after a writ petition was filed by O P Gupta along with nine other members of the Mandi Gobindgarh Municipal Council challenging the validity of the rule for providing reservation to presidents of the committee in various MCs in the category of women, SCs and backward castes.

The counsels for the petitioner Satya Pal Jain, Dheeraj Jain and R K Chopra submitted that the official language of Punjab is Punjabi. As per Official Languages Act, 1967, all orders rules made by Punjab have to be in Punjabi.

However, Punjab in 1994 framed the rules in English. Jain added that since the entire election work is being done in Punjabi, there is no justification for preparing the lists of MCs in English. So the entire set for reservation should be changed. Citing a Supreme Court ruling, he said that such lists have to be prepared in every state in their official language.

The counsel for the respondents said that since the rules were framed in 1994, the validity of the same cannot be challenged in 2008. The judges adjourned the hearing of the case till September 8.

Heading: Government decision to withdraw PU’s central status irks teachers - Indian Express
Content:
One issue that is bothering me the most these days are the recent cases related to child abuse and harassment that have come to light. I believe that all schools should make special efforts to sensitise adolescents about the same.

Under the recommendations of the Raghavan Committee, all government and private schools are required to have a sexual harassment committee but there are many schools who are not complying with the same. I believe that it is a very sensitive issue and needs immediate attention. All schools should have a complaint box in place and students must be encouraged to submit complaints if they have any.

Schools should also organise awareness programmes for both students as well as their parents. Students need to be told that if any incident related to sexual harassment occurs, then it needs to be brought out in the open. Students need to be counselled so that they do not hesitate in bringing up such issues with the seniors. Also it is not only in the schools that cases related to child abuse can take place rather such issues can also come up at home where relatives might be involved. Thus, there is a need to educate the parents as well so that students do not hesitate in discussing the issue with them.

During counselling sessions with students, I have often noticed that most of the students are not even aware that someone has taken undue advantage of their innocence.

Schools can do a lot in motivating the students to fight all odds and have a major role in making the students mentally strong. Schools should also keep in mind that both boys and girls should be counselled since both of them may be affected by such issues.

Heading: Following protests, expulsion of 3 DAV students revoked - Indian Express
Content:
The withdrawal of consent on the grant of a central university status to the Panjab University has come as a surprise for the faculty and students.

The move has caused a lot of resentment among the faculty, who believe that the Punjab Government, by withdrawing its consent, has made a mockery of itself and in the meanwhile, has lost its credibility.

G K Chatrath, former advocate general of Punjab, and a PU fellow said: "The government has lost its credibility after announcing for it twice publicly. The government appointed all the former vice-chancellors and withdrawing the consent on their protest, indicates that the government has succumbed to pressure from its staff."

Professor Manjit Singh, former Panjab University Teachers Association (PUTA) general secretary said: "It is my earnest request to all the teaching, non-teaching staff and students to join the protest against the double standards being maintained by the Punjab Government. We all should now shed our inhibitions and come together for a common cause."

Sources, meanwhile, maintained that the sudden move by the Punjab Government is due to the immense political pressure.

Though all the officials of the government are tight-lipped on the issue, the PUTA has decided to start with the agitation once again.

Pawan Kumar Bansal
Union Minister of State for Finance and Congress MP

We are back to square one on the issue of central university status. It is very unfortunate that the Punjab government has reiterated from its stand. At present, the Centre is contributing 60 per cent funds for the varsity while the share of the Punjab government is only 40 per cent. However, adequate funds are not being released. With the vice-president being the chancellor of the PU and the vice-chancellor being appointed by the Centre, the control of the central government over the varsity is more. There would have been no major change in the functioning of the varsity if the central status had been accorded rather it would have ensured benefits including more financial aid and increase in the retirement age of teachers.

satya pal jain
The Centre does not need the approval of the state government for granting central university status to PU. Since Chandigarh is a Union Territory, it is ruled by the Centre. The Congress government is merely politicising the issue. It shows its unwillingness to grant central status to the university. They have now put the ball in Punjab government's court. We are in favour of central status for the university, as it would bring in a number of benefits for the teachers and the students.

Heading: St Stephen’s give PFA the blues - Indian Express
Content:
Three students of DAV College, Sector 10, were expelled yesterday because they had locked the mess of the BTC hostel owing to the poor quality of food being served there. The order was, however, revoked today.

The three students are Vicky, Vinod of BA (III) and Saurabh Malik of BA (II).

On Tuesday morning, the student bodies protested against the college authorities and also met the principal, B C Josan.

The principal constituted a committee to decide on the matter and called all the student leaders for a meeting.

The students claimed that the food is sub-standard and that they could not eat the food any more.

"We have not done anything wrong. If our demands are not genuine then we are ready to face the consequences," said Vinod, a student.

"I can't say anything right now as the matter is still pending before the committee and it will decide on the matter. I have given orders to the mess contractors to arrange for better food in the future. This is a political stunt before the upcoming elections," said Josan.

"It is our democratic right to protest in a peaceful manner and the students have genuine demands. If their demands are false then the authorities can take any action against them," said Vikas Rathee, INSO president. Prof B C Josan added, "As I had not given any written order of their expulsion, it was just a warning to the students. If they create any more nuisance in the future then we will not tolerate it."

INSO demands more hostels
PU students led by the Indian National Students Organisation (INSO) protested on Tuesday against the hostel problems and the high rates being charged at student centre shops and the PU market. PU campus chairman, Sukhdev Kundu led the student procession to press for their demands. Later, the INSO delegation also submitted a memorandum to the PU vice-chancellor. Kundu said that the problem of hostels had been discussed with the v-c many times earlier. He also said that students of some departments like diploma students of Psychology have been denied hostels. He demanded that PU make some interim arrangements like vacating hostels for students and converting more buildings into hostels. PU should plan and construct four more boys and girls hostels this year, the INSO leader said. –ENS

Heading: Waqar Younis to inaugurate T20 JCD ICL tournament - Indian Express
Content:
The thin line that made the difference for St Stephen's School Football Academy, Chandigarh was that extra combined team effort and passes that not only helped the team create number of chances but also keep the opposition Punjab Football Academy on the back-foot. Because of the superb game displayed by the whole outfit, St Stephen's Academy made a perfect start to its campaign by winning their first match in its first match in the sixth Administrator's Challenge Cup All-India Football Tournament for Under-17 being organised by the Chandigarh Sports Department at the Sector 42 Football Stadium on Tuesday.

Unlike yesterday, there were very little spectators, the only few being the teams that are participating in the championship and players who come for practice at the Sports Complex. Both the team started off brightly and it was the Punjab team who had the first shot at the goal as a swirling long shot by Jagjeet just sailed over the bar.

Missed chances
There was a superb chance to score a goal but this time the team was that of St Stephen's Academy. Rising high to a long pass, Samandram Langba tried his best to head the ball into the net but his effort was thwarted by Nishad Sindham who collected the ball easily. Two minutes later, St Stephen earned a free-kick just outside the penalty area but Punjab player Jagjeet didn't play heed to the referee's instructions to clear the line to which he was shown a green card as a sign of caution. St Stephen players slowly paced up their game and started juggling the ball to and forth. However, one of the stars of the match, Umakanta Singh's goal was disallowed in the 24th minute when his shot hit the bar and then the ball rebounded and touched the goal line but the referee disallowed the goal.

Cool finisher Antil
However, the day belonged to Kuldeep Antil as his effort in the 38th minute put his team on the advantage. The team erupted into joy while slowly frustration seemed to dawn on the Punjab players as they made rough tackle on the opposition team players.

After getting the lead in the first half, the St Stephen's Academy played a much composed game while the Punjab team put a much better performance in the second half and created a number of chances to neutralize the lead The best chance for PFA came in the 76th minute when Jagjeet failed to put the ball into the empty net and shot wide after the St Stephen goalkeeper had stumbled and fall down. In the last ten minutes, PFA got some golden opportunities to save the sagging match as Kulbir Singh volleyed the ball over the crossbar and Manjeet's shot was adeptly caught by Stephen's goalkeeper. St Stephen's Academy earned three corners to PFA's two, one of which changed the course of the match and brought smiles on the St Stephen's team.

Earlier, Chandigarh Football Academy kept a clean sheet while thumping Haryana by 7-0 in the match played in the morning. CFA has scored an astounding 16 goals in just two matches. Gagandeep scored a brilliant hat-trick for CFA while Amandeep, Sehnaj, Sumit Passi and Samuel turned the heat on the Haryana team with their strikes. Tamil Nadu failed to capitalise on a superb brace by SS Dharan as they could not overcome a spirited Rohit Academy (Orissa) side and lost the match by 3-4. The third match was played between Delhi and Chattisgarh where the Delhi side drubbed Chattisgarh by 3-0. This match also witnessed the first red card of the tournament as Arshulla Khan was sent off from the ground for using abusive language.

Over-age players tally increases to 24
ADDING to the woes, ten more players were found overage in the medical check-up that was carried out at the Government Multispeciality Hospital, Sector 16. These players were debarred from taking part in the on-going tournament. The number of overage players has risen to 24 after 14 players were found to be over the limited age for the participation in the championship. Punjab Football Association and Madhya Pradesh Football Association had three overage players each.

Heading: Drug racket: ‘DSP Sodhi has unblemished service record’ - Indian Express
Content:
Former Pakistani speedster Waqar Younis along with Haryana Chief Minister Om Parkash Chautala would inaugurate the T20 JCD International Cricket League for JCD ICL Trophy to be played from September 5 to 15 at the JCD Vidyapeeth in Sirsa.

The tournament will feature number of International and domestic cricketers playing in the T20 mode.

Addressing a press conference here today, JCDNCA president Digvijay Singh gave details about the tournament. According to him the tournament would be played on round robin league basis and all the eight teams have been divided into two groups. Group 'A' would have Lahore Lions Pakistan, Air India, Indian Air Force and JCDNCA whereas Sharjah Tigers Dubai, Sri Lanka, LIC Cricket Club and Indian Navy would be in group 'B'. The best two teams from each group would qualify for semi-finals which would be played on September 12 and 13. The final will be played on September 15.

Doordarshan Sports will telecast the inaugural match, the semi-finals and final live. A number of Indian international cricketers have already confirmed their participation.

As far as pitches are concerned, four of them have been prepared as per international standards, whereas three practice grounds have also been prepared separately. He informed that Punjab Electricity Board and JVM Club are the reserve teams.

Digvijay Singh said that the JCDICL would be an international level annual cricket event and the winners and runners-up would get Rs 5 lakh and 2.5 lakh, respectively.

Man of the Series would get Rs one lakh wheres as the Man of the Match would get Rs 21,000 each. The best batsman and the best bowler would also be honoured with the trophies, he added.

Further announcing details about the stadium Digvijay remarked that the seating capacity of the floodlit stadium is 10,000, while price of the ticket is Rs 200.

A state-of-the-art cricket stadium has been set up on the premises of the JCD Vidyapeeth, where day night matches would also be organised. The stadium has been prepared as per the specifications of the Punjab Cricket Association's Stadium in Mohali. The JCD Stadium also has VIP enclosures and press enclosures and provision of day and night matches, he added.

JCDNCA was set up in April this year. Around 700 players in the age group of 12 to 19 years from Haryana, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Delhi, Chandigarh, Rajasthan and Himachal Pradesh participated in the trials. Out of these, 40 were selected for admission to the academy, who are being trained by able coaches, Digvijay Singh added.

Though, Digvijay was not clear about Pakistan's Taufeeq Umar's participation in the tournament as he is involved with Indian Cricket League. And the fact is known to everyone that BCCI is totally against ICL and has asked BCCI contracted players to stay away from the rebel league. So, it remains to be seen whether Taufeeq Umar will feature in the tournament.

Heading: MC POLLS: Three file nominations - Indian Express
Content:
Haryana Deputy Superintendent of Police Gurdarshan Singh Sodhi had an unblemished service record of almost 40 years, following which he was re-employed after his retirement.

DSP Sodhi was arrested following the recovery of 1.23 kilogram cocaine, which is worth Rs 1.25 crore in the international market, from a Mohali-based ex-serviceman Dara Singh.

Dara had told the police that he got cocaine from DSP, who further named Head Constable Joginder Pal and Constable Manohar Singh of Rajasthan Armed Police as sources for the contraband.

At a media briefing on Tuesday, Mohali Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Jatinder Singh Aulakh said that Sodhi had an exceptional service record, which fetched him re-employment in the Telecommunication Wing at the Haryana state police headquarters in Panchkula.

He added that even Dara didn't have any previous criminal record and was arrested for the first time

Both Sodhi and Dara were sent to the Joint Interrogation Centre of Punjab Police (JIC) in Amritsar for sustained interrogation.

Both of them will be brought back to Mohali on Wednesday to be produced before a local court.

"We are hoping for another cache of narcotics in the coming days," hinted Aulakh.

Meanwhile, a local sub-divisional court denied the prosecution's request for extending the police remand of arrested Joginder Pal and Manohar Singh, whose two-day police remand expired on Tuesday.

Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate Lalit Kumar Singla has instead sent both the cops to judicial remand till September 11, said Superintendent of Police (Operations) Harinderjeet Singh Sidhu.

Heading: For your eyes only... - Indian Express
Content:
Stress is more than just a disease, which not only affects our personal being but also ruins our social life

Life throws up innumerable situations, which we greet with both negative and positive emotions such as excitement, frustration, fear, happiness, anger, sadness, joy. And when the negative reactions to life's situations become repetitively intense and frequent, we tend to develop symptoms of depression. Depression is prevalent among all age groups, in almost all walks of life. But in our modern scenario with the constant rise and development of our companies, which is setting high standards for the employees, There is something else that is stealthily developing with it, that is, stress. Stress is a psychological and physiological response to events that upset our personal balance in some way. When faced with a threat, whether to our physical safety or emotional equilibrium, the body's defences kick into high gear in a rapid, automatic process known as the "fight-or-flight'' response, says Dr Shiney Benedict. The responses could be in various forms — palpitation, tensing muscles, breathing fast, heavy perspiration, blocked thoughts. Science is constantly experimenting about the impacts that stress could have on the overall health of an individual, as it is a contributing factor and all common ailments like backaches, insomnia, cancer, chronic fatigue syndrome and so on. Stress is one of the biggest killers and cause of most chronic diseases, which makes an individual miserable. It is linked to major ailments like cancer, heart diseases, lung diseases and even suicides. It is found that 75 to 90 per cent of youngsters who visit primary care physicians complain of stress-related symptoms. This happens especially in the age group of 25 to 40 years.

To overcome these problems the most common solution that these youngsters adopt is to pop ills (sedatives) without realising that how dangerous these could be. Confirming the above facts, psychiatrists say that consumption of sedatives have increased rapidly in the last few years due to stress. Naturopathy and yoga, a system of natural health care, will help to take charge of the situation. It addresses the continuum of stress, using relaxation and detoxification techniques rather than prescription of drugs. Relaxation therapies in naturopathy include body massage with aromatic oils that destress the entire system. Hydrotherapic treatments like steam bath, sauna bath also helps to relax. Fuller mud bath is helpful to detoxify the skin. Detoxification treatments in combination with other hydrotherapy treatment and yogic sessions can have a very positive impact on an individual.

Talking about the solution, there are three basic ways an individual reacts to stress:
* You can get angry scream, shout, throw things, start a fight, or go on a rampage.
* You can withdraw - take a drink, shut up in a room, take a pill, daydream, stop talking to everyone.
* You can take charge - think out the problem; take steps to overcome the physical stress.

Heading: Supplementary demands passed - Indian Express
Content:
Prevent eye injuries & save vision, says DR RAJAN CHUGH

Eye injury is a scourge, because more often than not, it is associated with serious outcomes as far as vision is concerned. With increase in competitive sports, more and more cases of eye injuries are being seen and reported. Injury to the eye and visual outcome depends upon the magnitude of impact, damage to vital tissues of the eye and early treatment and surgical intervention helps. Various types of eye injuries sustained in different sports can be one or combination of eye-lid bleeding and laceration, sub-conjunctival haemorrhage, angle recession, rupture of sclera/globe, traumatic glaucoma, cataract, dislocation of the human lens, ciliary body injury, vitreous haemorrhage, choroidal and retinal detachment, optic nerve injury and orbital fractures etc. Awareness of the fact that the eye can be damaged, cannot be taken casually. Wherever possible, protective eye-wear, which has come of age must be used, but not ordinary glass which breaks and does more damage. These devices can be used as one-piece eye guards or be fitted with face protectors and helmets. A highly impact resistant plastic, polycarbonate which does not break into shreds or splinters or allyl resins is good for such purposes. Sportspersons who wear glasses can use contact lenses or undergo Lasik laser. The use of ultra-violet glasses by players help in cutting down harmful effects of these rays.

In case of injury, immediate treatment should be done and the patient is advised to be in touch with the eye specialist for long-term serious side-affects of such injuries. A child can have permanent loss of vision in one eye because of 'lazy eye phenomenon' due to non-use. Perforating injury to one eye can cause decrease and damage vision in the fellow normal eye, a condition called 'sympathetic ophthalmitis' even years after the injury.

The writer is an eye surgeon & laser specialist & can be contacted at chugheyeunimaginable@rediffmail.com

Heading: ‘Small traders will not be affected by big houses’ - Indian Express
Content:
VIKRAM KAPOOR shares his non-traditional lifestyle approach to fat loss

I'M going to be really blunt and honest. If you want to burn fat, discard several pounds, and get into better shape and health, I've got news for you. Looking for a nutrition and workout program that you can follow for life will not do you any good at all. In fact, I believe that the traditional lifestyle approach to fat loss is nonsense. I'll share my Non-Traditional Lifestyle Approach to fat loss in a moment, but first, here's why I believe lifestyle plans suck:

The most frequently asked question I received after I achieved a very high level of fitness and physique with single digit body fat percentage. "Can you maintain that way of eating and exercise for life?" Absolutely not! If I was to continue to train that way, I would eventually burn out. If I was to continue to eat that way chances are my body would adapt, but not until I eventually wilted away. I burned a lot of body fat during that journey and when I reached my goal and didn't want to burn any more fat, why would I continue with a program that was designed to melt the fat off my body rapidly? Not to mention, following a fat loss program for a long period of time is mentally draining as well. But here's the thing - It was absolutely necessary for me to crank up the intensity of my workouts and push my limits. It was necessary for me to buckle down on my nutrition and eat a lot more natural foods. It was absolutely crucial to boost my mental game and stir up some serious internal and external motivation.

The traditional lifestyle approach is a cop out!

When someone tells me, "I'm looking for a program that I can follow for life", I immediately think that this person is copping out. In my humble opinion, this is an excuse not to put forth your very best effort.

The lifestyle approach gives you an 'out'. If you aren't experiencing success you can always say, "I don't like strict programs. I prefer to enjoy life". But are you really enjoying life in an overweight and unhealthy body? Are you able to do every thing that you want in life? Are you full of energy and living to your fullest? The traditional lifestyle approach allows you to stay in your protective little bubble. You never have to test your limits. It's safe. There's no chance of failure. How can you possibly expect to achieve great results with this approach?

If you want to burn fat and improve your body you absolutely must step outside of your comfort zone. You must be willing to test your limits and go beyond them. You must be willing to push yourself and do the extraordinary, not the usual. Ladies and gentlemen, don't expect extraordinary bodies if you are putting in ordinary efforts. It's never going to happen.

If you want to stay where you are at keep doing what you're doing. If you want to stay in the current level of health keep your physique in the shape that it currently is at, then by all means follow a lifestyle approach. That's what it's designed for. But if you have fat to burn or muscle to put on, a lifestyle approach will not get you where you want to go. I personally allow myself to temporarily be satisfied with where I'm. I admire the success that I just experienced and give myself a nice pat on the back. But shortly after that celebration I begin looking for my next challenge. I begin to look for new ways to improve my physique and my health. To me, this is the TRUE lifestyle approach. It's an approach of constant and continuous improvement. You grow as an individual each and every day. You live to your potential. You become the best YOU that you could possibly be. That's what makes life worth living! I give my absolute best to every program that I follow. I want to see just how effective it really is. I like to see if a program can live up to it's claims. The only way to know that for sure is if I put forth 100 per cent of my effort.

So my question to you is - Are you putting your very best effort into your fat loss program? Or are you just coasting in a traditional lifestyle approach hoping that you will succeed somehow? If you want results it's time that you pick up your game and kick it into high gear. Why wait for the end of your life to achieve results? Get them now and get them quick, then move onto the next goal. How bad do you really want a lean and desirable physique? Are you willing to do what it takes to get it? Come on now! I'm demanding more from you and you should be doing the same for yourself. Show me what you are really made of!

Till then stay fit.

(The writer is a fitness consultant

with Ozone Health Club and a personal trainer. He can be contacted at

fitnessarchitects@yahoo.co.in)

Heading: Hooda assures surplus BPL families same treatment - Indian Express
Content:
The Haryana government today assured in the assembly that it would ensure that interests of the small traders in the state do not suffer due to the arrival of big industrialists in retail business.

Answering a question of Indian National Lok Dal (INLD) member, Sushil Kumar Indora, Parliamentary Affairs Minister Randeep Singh Surjewala said there are only 18 shopping malls in the state against 1.03 lakh small traders and the entry of malls would not affect them adversely. "We are well aware of the situation and would ensure that the small shopkeeper does not suffer in the wake of the arrival of malls arrival," he said.

Indora expressed his apprehension that the entry of big industrialists in the retail market would affect the business of the small-time shopkeepers. Later responding to a calling attention motion, Agriculture Minister H.S. Chatha said cotton crop over about 40,000 hectares of area has been affected by the mealy bug.

Heading: Bill passed to transfer Tribunal cases to High Court - Indian Express
Content:
Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda today made it clear that the state government would provide same kind of facilities to the surplus BPL families as the number of BPL families in the state is much higher than permitted by the Planning Commission. He said the list has been finalised and all objections would be redressed before October 15.

Talking to the media persons, Hooda said the increase in the BPL families should not be interpreted as the increase in the number of poor.

The figure of BPL families was 6.38 lakh against the figure of 12.96 lakh families this time. "There was bungling during the survey conducted during the previous Om Prakash Chautala government as many of the families were not registered. We have conducted the survey in a transparent manner and all the deserving had been included in the survey," he said.

He said the present government conducted a door-to-door survey to identify BPL families through Haryana Ex-Services League independently in rural areas. Prior to field survey, each and every household was numbered by the Gram Panchayats and the photographs of the surveyed households were also taken by the surveyors. The field work was completed during 2007.

Hooda said, "There are a total number of 47.59 lakh families in Haryana. Out of these 12.96 lakh are BPL families, out of which 8.58 lakh are rural families and 4.38 lakh urban.

Out of the total BPL families, 5.55 lakh are SC families and 4.08 lakh BC families, thus SC and BC BPL families account for 9.63 lakh in the state."

He said in Punjab there are 3.44 lakh rural BPL families as compared to 8.58 lakh in Haryana.

Separate SGPC: Report awaited

Content:
The government today introduced a Bill to transfer all cases and applications pending and disposed of by the Himachal Pradesh Administrative Tribunal to the High Court and a Bill to amend the provisions to increase the subscription fee to HP Advocates' Welfare Fund.

Himachal Pradesh Administrative Tribunal (Transfer of Decided and Pending Cases and Applications) Bill, 2008, and Himachal Pradesh Advocates' Welfare Fund (Amendment) Bill, 2008, were introduced in the Assembly by Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal.

A lifetime membership is also proposed to be increased to Rs 5,000.

Heading: Stress, the silent killer - Indian Express
Content:
Swedish study finds genetic link to men's relationship woes

Swedish researchers say they have found a link between a specific gene and the way men bond to their partners, which can explain why some men are more prone to problems in their love life. "There are, of course, many reasons why a person may have relationship problems, but this is the first time that a specific gene variant has been associated with how men bond to their partners," said Hasse Walum, a post-graduate student at the Karolinska Institute. The researchers found that men who carry one or two copies of a variant of the gene often behave differently in relationships than men who lack the gene variant. Four of 10 men in Sweden carry the gene variant, called allele 334 said Walum. The study surveyed 550 twins and their partners or spouses in Sweden. Men who had two copies of allele 334 were twice as likely to have had a marital or relationship crisis in the past year than those who lacked the gene variant, it said. "Women married to men who carry one or two copies of allele 334 were, on average, less satisfied with their relationship than women married to men who didn't carry this allele," Walum said. The gene in question controls the production of a molecule receptor for vasopressin, a hormone that is found in most mammals. The same gene has previously been linked to monogamous behaviour in male voles, a mouselike rodent.

Heading: No going back on CFL scheme: CM - Indian Express
Content:
Stress is more than just a disease, which not only affects our personal being but also ruins our social life

Life throws up innumerable situations, which we greet with both negative and positive emotions such as excitement, frustration, fear, happiness, anger, sadness, joy. And when the negative reactions to life's situations become repetitively intense and frequent, we tend to develop symptoms of depression. Depression is prevalent among all age groups, in almost all walks of life. But in our modern scenario with the constant rise and development of our companies, which is setting high standards for the employees, There is something else that is stealthily developing with it, that is, stress. Stress is a psychological and physiological response to events that upset our personal balance in some way. When faced with a threat, whether to our physical safety or emotional equilibrium, the body's defences kick into high gear in a rapid, automatic process known as the "fight-or-flight'' response, says Dr Shiney Benedict. The responses could be in various forms — palpitation, tensing muscles, breathing fast, heavy perspiration, blocked thoughts. Science is constantly experimenting about the impacts that stress could have on the overall health of an individual, as it is a contributing factor and all common ailments like backaches, insomnia, cancer, chronic fatigue syndrome and so on. Stress is one of the biggest killers and cause of most chronic diseases, which makes an individual miserable. It is linked to major ailments like cancer, heart diseases, lung diseases and even suicides. It is found that 75 to 90 per cent of youngsters who visit primary care physicians complain of stress-related symptoms. This happens especially in the age group of 25 to 40 years.

To overcome these problems the most common solution that these youngsters adopt is to pop ills (sedatives) without realising that how dangerous these could be. Confirming the above facts, psychiatrists say that consumption of sedatives have increased rapidly in the last few years due to stress. Naturopathy and yoga, a system of natural health care, will help to take charge of the situation. It addresses the continuum of stress, using relaxation and detoxification techniques rather than prescription of drugs. Relaxation therapies in naturopathy include body massage with aromatic oils that destress the entire system. Hydrotherapic treatments like steam bath, sauna bath also helps to relax. Fuller mud bath is helpful to detoxify the skin. Detoxification treatments in combination with other hydrotherapy treatment and yogic sessions can have a very positive impact on an individual.

Talking about the solution, there are three basic ways an individual reacts to stress:
* You can get angry scream, shout, throw things, start a fight, or go on a rampage.
* You can withdraw - take a drink, shut up in a room, take a pill, daydream, stop talking to everyone.
* You can take charge - think out the problem; take steps to overcome the physical stress.

Heading: Health buzz - Indian Express
Content:
Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal today said that there will be no going back on the Rs 80-crore energy saving scheme — Atal Bijli Bachat Yojana — which involved distribution of free compact fluorescent lamps (CFLs) among domestic consumers.

The scheme, launched by Dhumal on August 15, currently has been put on hold following complaints relating to supply orders given to four leading manufacturers of CFL bulbs.

Dhumal told mediapersons today that he had asked Chief Secretary Asha Swaroop to look into the complaints, sent by a rival CFL manufacturing company, and consult the experts on distribution of bulbs, which are durable, carry a long warranty and don't play havoc with the power transmission system.

The CM claimed that the controversy on the issue was a result of clash of business interests, but the government had been prompt to order an inquiry. "Just look at the government's honesty. We don't want any controversy on the issue as the scheme is linked to Atalji's name," he said.

"The issue for the inquiry is simple. Whether the government should go for the best quality bulbs of 0.85 power factor (PF) or 0.05 PF. The latter, no doubt, will save Rs 18 to 20 crore, but we will damage our system, which will cost the exchequer very heavily," Dhumal maintained.

The Chief Minister termed the scheme as highly innovative, which no other state has tried so far.

Asked about reverting the heritage US Club into "Services Club", as during the Raj days, Dhumal said members of the IAS association had met him recently and requested for restoring the Club back to the Services.

"The matter is under consideration of the government," he added.

Heading: Lovelorn... - Indian Express
Content:
Do fibroids really cause infertility? DR NIRJA CHAWLA states the facts

The association between fibroids and infertility has been controversial. With advances in infertility management like fertility drugs, ART (Assisted Reproductive Technologies like IVF, ICSI) and advanced surgical techniques like hysteroscopic and laparoscopic myomectomy (removal of the fibroid), there is considerable interest in the commonly asked questions: Do fibroids really cause infertility and which fibroids would require myomectomy?

Fibroids are bundles of smooth muscle cells in the uterus forming benign tumours. Depending on their location they affect fertility in different ways. Those which are inside the cavity of the uterus are called polypoid/submucous fibroids depending on whether they hang with a stalk or not. Intramural fibroids lie totally within the walls of the uterus. Those arising from the outer surface of the uterus are subserous fibroids. An estimated 20 to 30 per cent women have fibroids during their reproductive years, more with increasing age. The current trend of delaying childbearing increases the chances of having fibroids. Most fibroids are detected because of the symptoms they may cause: excessive menstruation, pelvic pain and sensation of weight, pressure on the urinary system or rectum. All such fibroids will require treatment irrespective of their size, number and location. More fibroids, however, are asymptomatic, with no symptoms other than infertility or repeated abortions, and are picked up on routine ultrasound. Since the most essential information is whether there is distortion of the uterine cavity and the inability of simple ultrasound to give this information, hysteroscopy is a key diagnostic tool and the gold standard.

An excellent review was published in the April 2008 issue of the American Journal of Obstetrics and Gynaecology. Briefly, the data confirms that submucous fibroids are associated with a 20 per cent decrease in pregnancy rate as compared to infertile women with no fibroids. Most infertility specialists therefore recommend removal of these fibroids to enhance pregnancy rates. Though actual scientific evidence to support this strategy is limited, hysteroscopic myomectomy is an important treatment modality to improve pregnancy rates and should be considered, especially as the safety of this procedure is well-established.

Intramural fibroids may decrease pregnancy rates slightly, but this should be viewed with caution since most journals tend to publish papers showing positive effects. Currently, routine removal of intramural fibroid for optimizing pregnancy rate is not justified unless it is larger than seven cms or there has been a previous IVF failure. And certainly removal of subserous fibroids does not enhance fertility. This is about fibroids in those women who have realized, after one year of trying to conceive, that they are infertile. The crucial question concerns those who have not attempted to conceive as yet or have tried for less than a year and have been incidentally diagnosed as fibroids. They desire a future pregnancy and wish to be 'fit' for it. This review confirms that pregnancy with fibroids is associated with increased rates of preterm delivery, caesarean section and haemorrhage. Simultaneously, most women with asymptomatic fibroids conceive easily and remain well enough throughout pregnancy and labour, very often achieving normal delivery even with large fibroids. The risks such women may be exposed to are not high enough to justify the costs of hospitalization and surgery, however easy and safe it may be.

So the bottom line is that certain fibroids will require removal in infertile women, not in those whose infertility status is not as yet known.

The author is a Chandigarh based infertility specialist and gynae hystero-laparoscopic surgeon. You can visit her website www.endoscopy.co.in for more information. She can be contacted at drnirja@gmail.com

Heading: Auction fetches GMADA Rs 63 cr - Indian Express
Content:
VIKRAM KAPOOR shares his non-traditional lifestyle approach to fat loss

I'M going to be really blunt and honest. If you want to burn fat, discard several pounds, and get into better shape and health, I've got news for you. Looking for a nutrition and workout program that you can follow for life will not do you any good at all. In fact, I believe that the traditional lifestyle approach to fat loss is nonsense. I'll share my Non-Traditional Lifestyle Approach to fat loss in a moment, but first, here's why I believe lifestyle plans suck:

The most frequently asked question I received after I achieved a very high level of fitness and physique with single digit body fat percentage. "Can you maintain that way of eating and exercise for life?" Absolutely not! If I was to continue to train that way, I would eventually burn out. If I was to continue to eat that way chances are my body would adapt, but not until I eventually wilted away. I burned a lot of body fat during that journey and when I reached my goal and didn't want to burn any more fat, why would I continue with a program that was designed to melt the fat off my body rapidly? Not to mention, following a fat loss program for a long period of time is mentally draining as well. But here's the thing - It was absolutely necessary for me to crank up the intensity of my workouts and push my limits. It was necessary for me to buckle down on my nutrition and eat a lot more natural foods. It was absolutely crucial to boost my mental game and stir up some serious internal and external motivation.

The traditional lifestyle approach is a cop out!

When someone tells me, "I'm looking for a program that I can follow for life", I immediately think that this person is copping out. In my humble opinion, this is an excuse not to put forth your very best effort.

The lifestyle approach gives you an 'out'. If you aren't experiencing success you can always say, "I don't like strict programs. I prefer to enjoy life". But are you really enjoying life in an overweight and unhealthy body? Are you able to do every thing that you want in life? Are you full of energy and living to your fullest? The traditional lifestyle approach allows you to stay in your protective little bubble. You never have to test your limits. It's safe. There's no chance of failure. How can you possibly expect to achieve great results with this approach?

If you want to burn fat and improve your body you absolutely must step outside of your comfort zone. You must be willing to test your limits and go beyond them. You must be willing to push yourself and do the extraordinary, not the usual. Ladies and gentlemen, don't expect extraordinary bodies if you are putting in ordinary efforts. It's never going to happen.

If you want to stay where you are at keep doing what you're doing. If you want to stay in the current level of health keep your physique in the shape that it currently is at, then by all means follow a lifestyle approach. That's what it's designed for. But if you have fat to burn or muscle to put on, a lifestyle approach will not get you where you want to go. I personally allow myself to temporarily be satisfied with where I'm. I admire the success that I just experienced and give myself a nice pat on the back. But shortly after that celebration I begin looking for my next challenge. I begin to look for new ways to improve my physique and my health. To me, this is the TRUE lifestyle approach. It's an approach of constant and continuous improvement. You grow as an individual each and every day. You live to your potential. You become the best YOU that you could possibly be. That's what makes life worth living! I give my absolute best to every program that I follow. I want to see just how effective it really is. I like to see if a program can live up to it's claims. The only way to know that for sure is if I put forth 100 per cent of my effort.

So my question to you is - Are you putting your very best effort into your fat loss program? Or are you just coasting in a traditional lifestyle approach hoping that you will succeed somehow? If you want results it's time that you pick up your game and kick it into high gear. Why wait for the end of your life to achieve results? Get them now and get them quick, then move onto the next goal. How bad do you really want a lean and desirable physique? Are you willing to do what it takes to get it? Come on now! I'm demanding more from you and you should be doing the same for yourself. Show me what you are really made of!

Till then stay fit.

(The writer is a fitness consultant with Ozone Health Club and a personal trainer. He can be contacted at fitnessarchitects@yahoo.co.in)

Heading: Govt depts, PSUs set for revamp - Indian Express
Content:
* Booth prices fell from Rs 1.56 cr to Rs 66.25 lakh

* An SCF fetched Rs 6.3 cr, double its earlier rate

* SSS bids reduced from Rs 2.6 cr to Rs 2.53 crore

The coffers of the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA) swelled by Rs 6304.75 lakh on Tuesday after the sale of 33 freehold commercial sites in Mohali. GMADA's earnings soared by 192.87 per cent against the reserve price of Rs 3268.97 lakh.

Six sites including two Shop-cum-Flats (SCFs) in Sector 64, two booths in Sector 56 and one booth each in Sector 59 and Sector 65 were, however, not auctioned due to inappropriate bids, said GMADA Estate Officer Sukhjeet Pal Singh.

Heading: Plots for politicians: Court raps Haryana govt, HUDA - Indian Express
Content:
Dhumal has given nod to administrative exercise for rationalisation of depts

Even as the BJP government has kept under wraps its move to re-organise the districts, fearing a political storm, a move to revamp the government departments and public sector undertakings (PSUs) is on the cards in Himachal Pradesh.

Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal is learnt to have given his go-ahead to an administrative exercise for rationalisation of major departments, including public works, irrigation and public health (IPH), police, agriculture and horticulture. Some of the field circles, posts and divisional-level offices will also be re-located.

Significant changes are also on cards in the health department, where the government has introduced a special incentive scheme for the doctors being appointed on contract basis by rogi kalayan samities (RKS), instead of the government. By the next five or 10 years, cadres like CMOs or BMOs will be non-existent.

"The need for rationalisation of the departments has been long felt. We will do rationalisation based purely on the administrative needs. Wherever necessary, local MLAs will be consulted, but the exercise will be done keeping in mind the government's administrative needs," he confirmed.

Dhumal gave an example of some field divisions and circles of the Public Works Department, which, he claimed, are intermingled and require urgent revamping. Even in the police department, he said there was no need for an ADGP (law and order) and also IGP under him stationed at Shimla. "If one of them is stationed elsewhere, that will make police operations easier," he asserted.

Similarly, departments like IPH, agriculture and horticulture need rationalisation and shifting out of certain posts to those areas where these are actually required to be. Some steps have already been taken by the government, said the Chief Minister, as he outlined the priorities to provide better services to people.

Beside the departments, most PSUs already in the red will also see the effect of the rationalisation drive. A committee headed by the Chief Secretary has been entrusted with the job to work out rationalisational and merger of those PSUs whose functions are almost identical. "The committee will also ask options of the employees before making final recommendations to the government," Dhumal said.

Inquiries from the General Administrative Department (GAD), which is held by the Chief Minister, reveals that some rationalisation of departments has already been done. These include agriculture and horticulture.

The coming days are expected to see a series of changes in the districts. But the government maintains that the rationalisational exercise will be undertaken to cut down administrative expenditure. No additional financial burden will be allowed.

Heading: Chandigarh Connected 90% of residents have cellphones - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court today issued notices to the Haryana government and Haryana Urban Development Authority (HUDA) on a petition which challenges the reservation of residential plots for sitting MLAs and MPs in High Potential Zones such as Panchkula and Gurgaon.

The Public Interest Litigation (PIL), filed by the Herald Cooperative Group Housing Society Limited, Manimajra, states that this reservation is causing "tremendous loss to the state exchequer as the allotments are not thrown open for auction".

The petition further states that MLAs and MPs are the elected representatives of the people and should not be granted "unreasonable benefits" by the government. "Rather than these politicians, it is the general public, which is in dire need of accommodation in Chandigarh and Delhi," states the petition.

Arguing for the petitioner, advocate Gunjan Mehta said the last general elections were held in Haryana in February 2005 and the next polls are expected around 2010. "Therefore, only around one year is left for the elected legislators to visit New Delhi.
