Heading: ‘State responsible for PU’s financial crunch’ - Indian Express
Content:
Nowadays, the cellphone seems to have integral part of our lives. With every rickshaw-puller, washerman, vegetable vendor, even the roadside cobbler, sporting the gadget, the number of cellphone users in the city is at an all-time high.

According to the Statistical Abstract 2007, released by the Chandigarh Administration recently, Chandigarh, with a population of around 12 lakh has around 11 lakh mobile phone subscribers (approximately 91.6 per cent).

While there were around 5.9 lakh mobile users in 2005, the figure doubled in 2007 with the number of subscribers crossing 10 lakh.

"At present, the figure stands at over 11 lakh subscribers and is increasing rapidly," said a senior official of the Chandigarh Administration's Statistical Department.

According to the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI), in July the country witnessed the highest-ever increase in the mobile subscriber base when 92.2 lakh new subscribers were added.

In June, the number of new subscribers was 89.4 lakh.

This trend is reflected across the country. According to Cellular Operators' Association of India, there were 2.33 crore mobile phone users in 2004 who have now crossed 21.89 crore.

Chief Operating Officer (Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh), Bharti Airtel, Sanjay Bahl said: "I am not at all surprised at the rapid growth of the mobile market. The people of this region are well known for their dynamism and modern outlook. They are risk-takers and eager to try out any technology that will help improve efficiency and ensure profitability."

PCOs vanishing
The ubiquitous Public Call Offices (PCOs) are a rare sight now. Of the 2,524 Public Call Offices (PCOs) in the city, over a 1,000 have already closed down, according to the figures released in the Statistical Abstract 2007. "The PCO operators at bus stands, railway stations and markets have started winding up operations, as there are hardly any customers these days," said Parveen Kumar, a shopkeeper in Sector 22 who earlier operated three PCOs.

Heading: Kurukshetra University to start course in Forensic Science - Indian Express
Content:
The Panjab University is suffering from a financial crunch, owing to less amount of money paid by the state government in its annual budget.

Under the Recognition Act, the Punjab Government is required to pay 40 per cent of its share in the PU budget, but officials at the university maintain it has not fulfilled the criterion even once.

Out of Rs 38 crore earmarked for the PU, the government has been paying Rs 16 crore.

The deficit has thus led to a major financial crunch at the university. The Centre too pays only 20 per cent of the Rs 16 crore, further increasing the crisis.

The state of higher education in the state can also be gauged from the fact that only seven new colleges have been started in the last three years. These colleges, moreover, lack permanent faculty and are run with aid from the guest faculty.

G K Chatrath, former advocate general and a PU fellow said: "The Centre should look at the letter written by the Punjab Government regarding withdrawing the consent for central university status. The fact that a progressive state like Punjab has started just seven colleges in the last three years clearly reflects upon the government's interest."

Another official at the PU said: "When the government is not ready to take any steps towards the development of the university, why can't it leave it to the Centre to decide the fate of the PU."

The grant-in-aid to the affiliated colleges is also frozen since 1980 and there are 400 vacant posts in different colleges across the state.

Heading: Cash-at-door scam: CBI seeks CJI’s permission to examine two judges - Indian Express
Content:
For all those who are keen on taking up forensic science as a profession in the near future, have a reason to smile as the Kurukshetra University is all set to start a degree course in Forensic science.

Not only would the practicals for the same be conducted at the forensic laboratory at Madhuban, the students would also be given a preference for filling up vacancies at the laboratory.

"While we have to start with the course from the coming year, the diploma for the same was started this year itself. Till now, the general science students were filling the various vacancies in the laboratory.

"But with the starting of this course, we would be able to employ specialised professionals," said Dr Manmohan Krishna Goyal, the director of the Madhuban Forensic Science Laboratory.

He also added that the course would be affiliated to the Kurukshetra University and while the theory classes would be held at the University premises, the practical classes would be conducted at Madhuban itself.

It was also added that the course has a seat capacity of 25 and admission to the course would take place through entrance tests.

Heading: CBI sleuths visit Solan to probe HP land deal case - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has decided to write to Chief Justice of India (CJI) KG Balakrishnan seeking his permission to examine at least two Punjab and Haryana High Court judges as witnesses in the "judge-bribery scam". The names of these two judges has already figured in the remand applications of the investigation bureau.

Sources said that the CBI has decided to examine the judges to get a clearer picture of the case. "It is not possible to make a headway in the case until the two judges are examined. Since there are limitations in examining a judge, we have to seek prior permission from the CJI," said a senior CBI officer.

The CBI will be examining the judges as witnesses in the case.

In a significant development, meanwhile, various contradictions have been found in the statements given to CBI by one of the accused, Rajiv Gupta.

Gupta had been claiming that he had gone to Justice Nirmal Yadav's residence on August 14, to deliver the packet of Rs 15 lakh as directed by prime accused Sanjeev Bansal.

Sources said the description of interiors and exterior of Justice Yadav's residence as given by Gupta did not match with the actual location and interiors. Moreover, the ITBP guards posted at the residence refused to identify Gupta. Gupta is learnt to have given varying statements to the CBI.

Till now, the CBI has not added any new sections in the FIR, which was re-registered by them after it took over the investigation from the Chandigarh Police.

The Chandigarh Police had also registered a case of forgery against Nirmal Singh and Gupta for forging some property documents in order to create an alibi and save them.

The CBI has not registered any case of forgery against the accused till date. "We are still investigating the case and might register a case of forgery, but the facts concerning the offence of forgery are yet to be confirmed," said a CBI officer.

The CBI will produce Bansal and Gupta in the court of Special CBI Judge Jagdeep Jain on Wednesday.

According to law, the maximum duration of police remand (15 days) — that can be granted by a court — has already lapsed. Sources said the CBI will stress on police custody of Gupta than Bansal. The CBI is also making efforts to arrest

Ravinder Singh, the "kingpin" in the case, who is still absconding. "Ravinder Singh's arrest will be of great help in solving the case. He might surrender once Bansal and Gupta are remanded in judicial custody,"said a CBI official.

Heading: Auto drivers stage protest, submit demands to STA - Indian Express
Content:
A two-member team of the Central Bureau of Investigations on Tuesday, arrived in Rihun village, Solan sub-division, to probe the case where 18 people from Haryana, including Punjab and Haryana High Court Judge Nirmal Yadav, had purchased land allegedly in violation of the Himachal Pradesh Land Reforms and Tenancy Act-1972. The team also visited the office of Tehsildar and inquired about the facts relating to the controversial land deal.

Sources in the Revenue department revealed that the team focussed on the execution of sale deeds at a price allegedly much less than the prevailing market rate .

The team also gathered some information from Naib Tehsildar N S Chauhan, who had executed the sale deeds, registration clerk and document writer concerning the land deal.

They also talked to the person who had identified the sellers and purchasers before the execution of the sale deeds.

Sources revealed that after scrutinising some documents, the team also visited Rihun village along with field officials of the Revenue department, where the members also met some of the villagers, who had sold the land in question on August 14.

Heading: PGI doctor gets ‘best paper’ award from American Urological Association - Indian Express
Content:
The Auto Rickshaw Union held a rally in Sector 17, to protest against the decision of the State Transport Authority (STA) to phase out diesel-run auto-rickshaws from the city. The date for the same has been decided to be August 31, 2009.

The union also submitted a memorandum of demands to Vandna Disodia, Secretary, STA. They said the earlier life span of the diesel-run autos was 15 years earlier, but many operators have not been able to repay their loan installments.

Jarnail Singh Chauhan, President, Auto Rickshaw Union said: "Those who had taken a loan for auto rickshaws a year or two ago, have not been able to repay the same.

No financial help or subsidy was provided in 2001, while phasing out of the petrol auto-rickshaws and the same is expected this time too. Also, as there are very less number of LPG outlets, it will create a law and order problem in the city."

The Administration has decided that no further renewal of permits will be allowed beyond August 31, 2009 and only LPG auto rickshaws will be allowed on the roads of Chandigarh.

It was also protesting against the Administration's decision to ban auto rickshaws from carrying school children.

Heading: Ravinder’s bail dismissed by special CBI Court - Indian Express
Content:
The research paper of Dr S K Singh, Professor of Urology, PGIMER, has received the 'best paper' award from the American Urological Association (AUA) in Orlando, Florida, USA. The paper, titled "Spermatozoal Immobilisation Factor from Staphylococcus Aureus: Receptor-specific Interaction", highlights upon the role of bacteria in causing infertility in couples. The research was a collaborative effort of the Department of Microbiology, Panjab University and the Department of Urology, PGIMER.

The work was done by Navchetan Kaur, a research fellow, under the supervision of Dr Vijay Prabha, Reader, Panjab University and Dr S K Singh, PGIMER.

The research reads: "A sizeable number of infertile couples have no detectable cause for their infertility and some of them, who can afford it, proceed for costly assisted reproductive techniques (ART).

The staphylococcus aureus bacteria is a dominant flora in male and female genital tract and can inhabit there without causing infection and without producing any symptoms. These bacteria can produce a substance, sperm immobilisation factor (SIF), which can decrease sperm motility."

Heading: CM lays stone of thermal plant - Indian Express
Content:
The bail application of absconding Delhi-based businessman Ravinder Singh in the 'cash-at-judge's door' scam was dismissed by Special CBI Court of Jagdeep Jain on Tuesday.

Defending the accused — former Haryana Advocate General Sanjeev Bansal — his counsel said that the fact whether the identity of Ravinder Singh in question and the one accused in the scam are the same has not been established, since no details of Ravinder have been mentioned so far.

He added that it is only Bansal who had said that the money he had was given to him by Singh. Since Bansal is himself an accused, he cannot be made a witness in the case. He said that investigation in the case has established that there was a deal for land, which was located in Himachal Pradesh and was bought by Singh along with other persons. He was liable to pay his share and even if it is assumed that there was a monetary transaction between Singh and Bansal in Delhi, it cannot be assumed that it was for the illegal gratification or influencing any public servant or use same for corrupt means.

The counsel also stated that the purpose of giving the money has not been found till date. No case pending in the court has been found out where Singh could have been benefited. Also, if a gift is accepted by a judge, the same might be considered as misconduct as per the code of conduct, but the same cannot be perceived as corruption.

The CBI prosecutor said that Singh's arrest is vital to unearth the unholy nexus existing in the legal system and therefore, the bail application was dismissed.

Heading: Gill for visa centre in Holy City, passage to Kartarpur - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Chief Minister Parkash Singh Badal today laid the foundation stone of 1,980-MW Talwandi Sabo Thermal Power Plant at Banawali in Mansa district in a function organised by the Punjab State Electricity Board here today amidst an unprecedented show of strength.

Strength at today's rally outstripped yesterday's Congress meet in Lambi. A beaming Sukhbir claimed that more than two lakh people came for the rally. However, a large number of people could not reach and were seen stranded in buses along the route.

Qualifying to be called as misnomer due to its location in Banawali village in Mansa, the Talwandi Sabo Thermal Power Plant has been named so due to the proximity with the historic town of Talwandi Sabo in Bathinda district. The project would be carried out by Sterlite Energy Limited, a Vedanta Group Company, on build own and operate (BOO) basis at a basic cost of Rs 9,000 crore.

Badal said he was grateful to the villagers who gave land for the project. He announced development funds for four villages, Raipur, Banawali, Pero and Talwandi Aklian. He said the smooth acquisition had been possible only after changing the law.

Badal hit out at Amarinder for controversy over land acquisition near Barnala for Trident Group and claimed credit for solving the issue.

Badal said the rally was the biggest he saw in his entire political life. "There were two mega rallies of the SAD (B) that were of massive magnitude. One was in Ludhiana and other in Moga to celebrate the birth anniversary of the party. But today's rally has surpassed both of them," he said.

Announcing that battle for Parliamentary elections had begun, Sukhbir called upon the gathering to repeat results of Assembly and panchayat elections. Earlier, after stepping on the stage, Sukhbir claimed that while on his way to the venue on a chopper he saw traffic jam, spanning around 35 kilometres.

He made an appeal to the audience to maintain discipline to accommodate the people, who were heading towards the rally, but were caught in the jam. During their speeches, both CM and Sukhbir Badal showered praises on Vedanta Group Chairman Anil Agarwal for undertaking the project. Earlier, Agarwal said their first priority would be to provide employment to locals.

Heading: Bank robbery: Student nabbed - Indian Express
Content:
Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports MS Gill today stressed opening the passage to Kartarpur from Dera Baba Nanak at the earliest in the interest of pilgrims and to boost relations between India and Pakistan.

However, he said such efforts would lose meaning unless a visa centre was opened in Amritsar. Gill was in Tarn Taran today to lay foundation stones of a de-addiction centre and Sri Guru Arjun Dev Senior Secondary Girls' School.

He said he had raised the matter of the passage to Kartarpur and a visa centre in Amritsar in Parliament, besides writing to the External Affairs Minister, who had also visited the area.

He urged the government to comply with its three basic duties of maintaining law and order and providing health and education facilities to the people.

Heading: Jalandhar resident held for killing mother - Indian Express
Content: The Rajasthan Police with the support of Punjab Police Monday evening raided a hostel of the pharmacy institute on the Moga-Ferozepur Road and nabbed a third-year student, who was allegedly involved in a recent bank robbery of Overseas Bank in Jaipur. Police said a Jaipur Police party, headed by DSP Ram Singh, sought assistance to arrest Yogesh Sharma, a native of Aligarh in Uttar Pradesh. Police said the Jaipur Police had arrested two persons earlier and during investigation, they confessed of the involvement of Yogesh.

Heading: A song to win - Indian Express
Content:
The police cracked a case of murder of a woman with the arrest of her son. The accused confessed to have committed the crime because his mother was not agreeing to his marriage.

Lakhi of Rehmanpur village in Jalandhar Cantonment was found murdered in her house on July 17 and her son Lal Chand, who is a peon, had told the police that when he returned home, he found the house bolted from outside. "When I opened the door, I found my mother killed and some household articles lying scattered," he had told the police.

Police found many contradictions in the statements of Lal Chand and rounded him up. During his interrogation, he admitted to have killed his mother by strangulating her, and to make it look like a murder, he scattered the household item around her body.

Heading: She’s out - Indian Express
Content:
Voice of India participant Vipul Mehta sings along with MCM DAV girls

Here's another Punjabi, who's making himself heard in the Voice of India contest. While many may look upon him to fill Ishmeet's shoes, Amritsar born Vipul Mehta has created quite a fan-following for himself. "I am a great fan of Ishmeet. It's sad that he is no more among us," says the teenager, who was in MCM DAV College, Chandigarh, for a musical interaction with the students, with some lucky ones even getting to share a melody with Mehta. So how's the journey been so far? "It feels great to be part of the show and be among such talented singers. With platforms like these, it has become easier for talented people to come to the forefront. Now we can be sure that the opportunity is there, rest depends on how far we can go with our hard work and creativity. It's a great learning experience. My training in classical music is paying me rich dividends in the show," smiles Mehta, adding that since the age of ten he has been learning classical music from Ustad Maqbool Khan. Mehta had come to Ludhiana to audition for Voice of India and was the only one to be selected from there. Now he's keeping his fingers crossed and singing in tune to win the title.

Hailing from a business family, Mehta was encouraged to pursue his interest in music. "My father in fact, is a keen music lover and wants to see me as an established singer." A fan of Rafi, the contemporary singers that he lends an ear to are Sonu Nigam, Sukhwinder Singh, Enrique and Rahat Fateh Ali Khan. Eager to make it to playback, Vipul dreams to lend his voice to Akshay Kumar and Abhishek Bachchan. While that may take some time, for now he is focussing on the show. Just the right way to go!

Heading: Health on a platter! - Indian Express
Content:
After her eviction from Bigg Boss, Rakhi Vijayan wants a production house with Rahul Mahajan

After politician Sanjay Nirupam, it was Rakhi Vijayan's turn to be evicted from the Bigg Boss house. Her stint on Bigg Boss Season 2-Aapka Faisla came to an end on Friday. Despite her ouster, Vijayan maintained a happy face and seemed full of plans.

"Initially, I came with an objective of having fun and enjoy the stay. Winning was not so important. But eventually, I wanted some time to prove something to the audience. Even though, I didn't get that opportunity, it's fine with me and I am all set to start my work with fresh enthusiasm," she says. The actor has just signed Raj Kanwar's untitled film, which stars Rishi Kapoor, Hema Malini and Rekha. She will also be seen in Rohit Shetty's Golmaal Returns, Ganesh Acharya's untitled film starring Govinda.

"I am not a person of controversy; I was very calm and good to every one. People wanted some spice in the show, which I failed to create," Vijayan gives reasons for her eviction. But what about her link up with Raja Chaudhary? Vijayan rubbishes rumours with a "Raja is like my brother".

However, she confesses having a great time with Rahul Mahajan, who along with her faced the eviction threat this week. Vijayan says, "We got along like a house on fire. While exiting, we hugged and shook hands. We plan to start a television production house. Rahul and me will announce it when the show is over."

Bollywood awaits her as well. She says: "I will be meeting Anees Bazmee today."

Heading: Caravan to Fame - Indian Express
Content:
It was a dishy affair all the way! Fortis Hospital, Mohali held a Nutritious Cooking Competition, as part of the National Nutrition Week. The theme of the competition was baking, steaming and salads, all healthy ways of cooking. Deepak Soni won the first prize for his dish of whole-wheat honey bread, while Gurpreet Singh won the second prize with his innovation of a tri-colour wheat pizza and Jitender won the third prize. Parul Thakur and Arjun Kaushal won consolation prizes for their fruit and sprout bhelpuri and whole-wheat sprouted dim-sum, respectively. Said Sonia Gandhi, Head, Clinical Nutrition, "the objective of the competition was to help people realize that they can bring in variety in their diet by using different cooking methods. As important, these methods conserve nutrients, are easy to digest and quick to cook." The National Nutrition Week is being celebrated to promote awareness among people regarding good nutrition and healthy eating for all age groups. Various stalls of health foods were set up in the Fortis lobby for patients, staff and visitors which would help them gather information and implement it in their daily diet pattern.

Eat right!
When it comes to cooking, steaming and baking are healthier options, for the food becomes easily digestible, there is conservation of nutrients and there is retention of flavour and colour of food. As steamed foods are mainly fermented, there is an increase in the availability of vitamins and minerals. Salads too should be an integral part of meals as these add fibre to the diet, add colour, are low in calories. Fruits and vegetables have good satiety value, help relieve constipation, control cholesterol and blood sugar and are an excellent source of antioxidants, vitamins and minerals.

Heading: New on the shelves - Indian Express
Content: Children's author Deepa Agarwal's Caravan to Tibet (Puffin) has been selected for the Honour List 2008 of the International Board on Books for Young People (IBBY), a biennial survey of what is best in children's literature worldwide. Set in 19th century Tibet, Agarwal's book is about a desperate journey to the Forbidden Kingdom with its mysterious lamas and ferocious robber chiefs, and a boy discovering his inner strength. "My grandfather belonged to Milam, a village on the Indo-Tibetan border, and it was customary for the men to go on a trade expedition to Tibet every year. I thought it would make an exciting adventure story," says Agarwal, who then spent a while researching on mountain expeditions and then three years of writing and rewriting. "Children sniff out false notes very fast, so situations and characters should be authentic," she says. And you thought children's writing was all about dreaming up fairy tales?

Heading: Naach Basanti! - Indian Express
Content:
Mobile mania
Small and stylish HTC Touch and HTC P3400i phones are the latest in the touch screen navigation. HTC Corporation offers a unique way of controlling touch screen-based devices by recognizing and responding to the sweep of a finger across the screen. Touch and HTC P3400i are priced at Rs 14,990 and Rs 10,990 respectively. LG Electronics India has also launched a new model in its dynamite series, the LG KP199. The handset offers a talk time of up to 11 hours and stand-by time of up to 30 days! And of course, it comes with add-ons like FM music, camera, MP3 player, anti-theft mobile tracker...Keep talking.

Richie Rich!
Ultra Merchandising and retails Ltd has acquired licence and merchandising rights for the kids' favourite, Richie Rich by Harvey Entertainment. "The company has recently produced soft toys of character 'BOO' of the film Love Story 2050 and holds license for merchandise for the Richie Rich. In addition, the company is in advanced stage of negotiation with leading international brands to produce soft toys in India," informs Sushil Agrawal, Managing Director, Ultra Merchandise and Retails.

Log On!
Bigadda.com, a youth networking site, introduces an all-new Mobile Adda, a social networking site which will be available on mobiles. So, you can now easily sign in, read and reply to E-mails and send requests to friends. Besides, one can keep a back-up and retrieve the phonebook whenever required, along with sharing photos. 'MobileAdda' also includes key features of social networking like searching for friends, inviting them from your phonebook and communicating with them through innovative options like text, voice and photo scribbles.

Hot shades
This season go in for Ray Ban's Wayfarers with your eyes closed. The classic eyewear from Ray Ban has been revived in all-new avatar. Ideal for those who love the styles and attitudes from the 80s, the Wayfarers are available in neon shades and startling chic color contrasts. Priced between Rs 5,490 and Rs 6,990, they are certainly a steal.

At all leading eyewear boutiques

Night light
Disco balls, strobes, lasers, electric-coloured neon lights and more unusual beautiful crystals are art of Swarovski's 'Passages of Night' line. Innovative shades of purple Heliotrope, Bermuda Blue, and shades of grey make it to the collection this time. Dedicated to the nocturnal spirit of a woman, the 'Passages of Night' collection is for all the lovely ladies who like to step out when it's dark.

Visual delight
For anyone with an eye for style, eyewear options from Versus seem like a good bet. Their Autumn/ Winter 08 collection has a good range to choose from. From rimless ones to those with hockey ends, this young eyewear line is hip and happy.

At all leading eyewear boutiques

Heading: Divine art - Indian Express
Content:
We are all familiar with overkill. This, people, is the overkill of overkill. Just when we thought we'd had enough of reality bites, crooning glories and jumping Jacks and Jills, SaharaOne TV whips out Saas vs Bahu: Kaun Kisse Nachayega. "Fictionalised reality", the show's all set to make hooked-to-tele homemakers thirsty for more blood, this time, on the dance floor with the 'belan queens' ready for some latka-jhatka and tez tadka. In town to promote this whole-new sindoor-saree charade, we quiz the ladies, also the participants; onscreen saas Krutika Desai and Jayati Bhatia, and bahu Manava Naik on this national 'phenomenon' which, ironically, has turned out to be a befitting answer to cricket-obsessed husbands for 8 pm to 10 pm, the remote control rests with the wives.

"It's an interesting concept for it involves elements of a dance show and the characters of saas-bahu," Manava stays on the politically correct track. We move our questioning gaze to the veterans, Krutika and Jayati. "To begin with, it's not easy to dance Bollywood style," says Jayati, who, by the way, has learnt the Odissi dance form. Calling them grilling sessions, Krutika says she's in it 'for a change'. But why only saas-bahu, why not a sasur-jawai? "Because any relationship with a woman is complicated. Get two of them, and you have your answer!" reflects Krutika, while Jayati feels that "in our country, sons-in-law are a pampered lot," she points out to a demi-godly status men enjoy. "Of course, we want to do different stories and varied characters. But the tele space right now is limiting, and unfortunately, this is what the audiences want. They are hooked to it," adds Jayati. "See, it's not that the channels don't experiment, look at Balika Vadhu or Sarabhai vs Sarabhai, but the fact is that they struggle with TRPs, and the producers have no choice but to bring in a commercially viable saas-bahu angle. Bass, the story changes tracks and derails," Krutika chips in with plausible reason.

If not anything else, it's the biggest success formula in the history of television. Sample this: there's a film round the corner, Saas-Bahu aur Sensex, Star has an online store selling saas-bahu stuff, there are kitty parties on the concept and what's more, middle-aged homemakers who couldn't copy Kareenas and Katrinas have saas-bahu as walking talking fashion divas! Seriously, if we take a closer, scientific look, then Dolly was just a teaser, Saas-Bahu is perhaps the most successful cloning experiment so far. "You know, everyday we walk in thinking our roles will be better, meatier today, but everyday we return disappointed," says Jayati, who along with Krutika and Manava carry on their theatre acts, for that's "the true art." "Once upon a time, television too was much like that. We had A-class directors giving us top-bracket programming. Television was treated as an art form, it had a seriousness, an impressive aura about it, which today films enjoy. Meanwhile, what we are doing on the tube is mere time pass masala, there's no room for a message," Krutika hands it out, let down by "how the television has been robbed of its IQ...it's mediocre in every department."

On a positive note, the actors feel this vicious circle will break, the bubble will burst. "But we need channels and producers to work towards it, as actors, we can only walk out or refuse a role." Anyone listening?

Heading: Made to Rock - Indian Express
Content:
Pendants, lights, key chains...the city is seeking Ganesha's divine blessings through art!

He is probably one of the most loved of all the Indian Gods, and after his 'debut' into the movie world, Ganesha's popularity is no less than a star's. With devotees preparing for Ganesh Chaturthi, the market for Ganesha products is quite animated. Though it's another part of the country that chants 'ganpati bappa moreya' the loudest, now even Chandigarh is embracing the festival of the elephant god with mighty fervour. From roadside to high-end stores, Ganesha is smiling at all.

Episode in Sector 9, Chandigarh, boasts of a large sale of Ganesha idols every year. "Usually it's Diwali that sees the highest demand but throughout the year people purchase the idols on different occasions. Ganesha is a symbol of good luck and prosperity so whether it is a festival or house-warming people like to gift this," tells Anu Bains, the owner. Owing to the high demand during Diwali, the store will have a huge collection in a month's time. "People usually purchase huge idols to place at the entrances of their houses and even offices," she adds. These range from Rs 14,000 onwards and can be decorated with water and petals to add more appeal. While wood is big and striking, ceramic and brass are also popular. But terracotta with special paint finish is a perennial favourite. "The paint makes it weather-proof so people can place the idol outside in the gardens as well. I haven't heard of a similar concept elsewhere in the city," claims Bains.

If it's smaller idols that you want to look for, then gift shops like Archies are just the place for you. "Ganesha stands for wisdom so it's a favourite among parents," tells Kaul of an Archies outlet, Panchkula. Tiny idols are often picked up as gifts for children. Choose from innovative water balls (Rs 425), pencil stands that can also used to hold agarbattis, key chains, Ganesha frames, car hangings (Rs 170), wooden idols (Rs 299 plus), marble ones (Rs 650) and ones in black stone and white stone. Take a pick of a pendant and a coin at

Tanishq where the gold pieces are available in weights of two grams to eight grams.

Uma Gift Mart, Sector 9, Panchkula keeps innovating the different moods of Ganesha. There is such a variety in themes that customers are always in for a surprise. Uma is a self-manufacturing unit so Capt. Sharma, Managing Director, keeps working on new ideas with his team. "The most popular Ganesha idols have been Ganesha with mridangam and Ganesha with sitar. People loved different postures of Ganesha," he tells, adding that Ganesha sitting with trunk on the right side is considered auspicious. But the most exciting one probably was the 11-member Ganesha cricket players' team! The prices range from Rs 500 to Rs 20,000, however here's the catch. "The metal rate is exorbitantly high and fluctuating, so if you are buying a six-inch statue for Rs 300 today may be in few days, you will have to shell out Rs 600 for the same!" warns Sharma. At Uma you may shop for idols in brass, poly raisin, wood carvings and bronze. "Brass has longer life so it's more in demand." There are also Ganesha paintings available in the price range of Rs 2,500 to Rs 6,000.

Letting Ganesha light up your world. Deep Glamour Lights, Sector 7, Chandigarh has various options in gate, verandah, hanging and wall lights. Amardeep Singh tells that the wall lights are made on order and glass of any colour is cut in the shape of Ganesha. While the gate lights are priced at Rs 450 the others cost Rs 275. So whether you want a 'godly' present for a friend or yourself, let Ganesha bless all!

Heading: Chautala faces Cong wrath in absentia - Indian Express
Content:
COVER STORY: Rolling Stone magazine has the star cast of Rock On on its September cover

The accolades have not stopped coming in since Abhishek Kapoor's Rock On released on Friday. The story of male bonding has not only touched a chord with the audience, but now, the eclectic cast of the movie has scored another first. This month, actors Farhan Akhtar, Arjun Rampal, Purab Kohli, Luke Kenny and the music director trio of Shankar-Ehsaan-Loy are on the cover of the legendary Rolling Stone magazine. Even though musicians might debate the validity of the selection of the actors on a hardcore music magazine, the cast along with the music directors were apparently chosen on the basis that it is the first Indian film on rock music. Considering that AR Rahman has been the only other Indian face to have ever featured on the magazine, that is indeed breaking new grounds. Pump up the volume, guys!

Heading: More flack for Chautala, INLD stages walk out - Indian Express
Content:
From fatichar to nalayak, Haryana Assembly touches another low

Once known as a Haryana strongman, former chief minister Om Prakash Chautala was today referred to as "fatichar soch ke malik" in the Vidhan Sabha, when the treasury benches entered into aggressive sparring to defend what they alleged. Ironically, this is the same House where Chautala had repeatedly declared, "Jab tak jiunga CM rahunga".

Even his absence failed to prevent his bete noire, Congress MLA Karan Singh Dalal, from attacking him on the first available opportunity as the members were winding up their questions for the day.

INLD member Sushil Kumar Indora was trying to raise a point, but before he could be heard, Dalal was on his toes on a point of order which the Speaker allowed. "Speaker sir, fatichar soch ke malik shri Om Prakash Chautala ……….," he was yet to complete his sentence that the INLD members were up on their feet, creating a ruckus. In between the slogan-raising against the government, Indora shouted, "Nalayak ko nalayaki ke siva kaya aata hai?"

This was enough to get a similar response as allegations were hurled from both the treasury and opposition benches. Ironically, Chautala always remained at the centre of the discussion of the House, as almost every important member of the treasury benches made comparisons between his and the present government.

All efforts to calm down the INLD group with persuasions and browbeating died in the din. An irate Parliamentary Affairs Minister Randeep Singh Surjewala urged the Speaker not to allow the handful of members to take the House for ransom. But there was no let up in the INLD group as they continued shouting "tanashahi nahin chalegai" and "Haryana sarkar murdabad". However, Speaker Raghuvir Singh Kadian then allowed INLD member Sita Ram to present his call attention motion, but within minutes of peace, tempers flared up again as Indora reacted sharply to some comment from the members. This time Kadian also got enraged and warned Indora, who retorted, "This is no way to warn."

This further infuriated the Speaker, who named Indora and asked the marshalls to send him out. The marshalls immediately surrounded Indora at his seat, who then left the House protesting and raising slogans. Another INLD member Balwant Singh Sadhaura, who protested naming of Indora, was also named.

Chinks in INLD come to fore
The incident also exposed chinks in the INLD. After Indora was named and he left the House, one of the INLD members tried to convince all other members to walk into the well of the House and he himself reached near the Speaker's podium. But the remaining members had their reservations in joining him. Some of them stood behind him, but only to grab their seats back immediately.

Heading: Vizag civic officials visit Chandigarh - Indian Express
Content:
Pandemonium broke out in the Haryana Vidhan Sabha during the presentation of the preliminary report of the Committee of Privileges concerning contempt of the committee by the Indian National Lok Dal leader and former chief minister Om Prakash Chautala.

Incidentally, in the preliminary report, the Privileges committee had recommended that Chautala be reprimanded in the House for his disorderly and disrespectful conduct during tendering the evidence in the meeting of the committee held on July 2 in respect of notice of breach of privilege given by Randeep Singh Surjewala, Parliamentary Affairs Minister. INLD members were up on their feet the moment Speaker Dr Raghubir Singh Kadian announced the presentation of the report.

All hell broke lose as the INLD members rushed to the well of the House shouting, "Tanashahi nahi chalegi, gundagardi nahi chalegi, Haryana sarkar murdabad." Om Prakash Chautala was not present in the House when the report was being presented. Leading the charge, Dr Sushil Indora continued to demand that the report be taken back. Indora was vociforously supported by the rest of the INLD legislators.

The bedlam continued for more than 15 minutes, despite repeated request by the Speaker to calm the INLD members. When the infuriated INLD members continued to create a scene, the Speaker named four members one by one,namely Ramphal Chirana, Iswhar Singh Palaka, Gyan Chand and Balwant Singh Sadhora.

The other four INLD members immediately staged a walkout except Sushil Indora who continued to shout slogans against the dictatorial attitude of the ruling party members.

At this point Congress MLA and Chairman of the Privilege Committee Karan Singh Dalal said it was most unfortunate that some of the members of the House had failed to respect the oath to protect the dignity and sanctity of the Constitution.

Castigating the INLD legislators, Dalal said, "Chautala has simply lost his mind. Even today he behaves as if he is some judge and we the convict. "Pahle bhi Chautala Vidhan Sabha ka tamasha banata raha hai. Aise logon ka sahi ilaj hona chahiye. Chautala ko House mein bulakar achhi tarah samjhana chahiye,'' said Dalal. Making a scathing attack on Chautala, BJP's Ram Kumar Gautam said, "Chautala ne Haryana ki arbon, kharbon ki sampatti looti hai." Gautam appealed to Haryana Chief Minister Bhupinder Singh Hooda not to be lenient towards Chautala.

Radhey Shyam Sharma of the Congress too spoke against Chautala. Later the Speaker ruled that the matter would come up for discussion again tomorrow.

Heading: Case lodged against security agency for fund embezzlement - Indian Express
Content:
A team of the Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation visited Chandigarh to take stock of the functioning and progress of the various projects undertaken by the Municipal Corporation.

After a brief presentation by Municipal Commissoner Dr Roshan Sunkaria and Mayor Pardeep Chhabra, the delegation members visited various parks and green belts developed by the civic body, the sehaj safai kendras, fire stations and dumping ground. Senior Deputy Mayor Anju Beniwala, Deputy Mayor Harphool Chander Kalyan and Additional Commissioner P K Sharma were also present at the meeting.

While briefing the delegates, Chhabra said that there is highest per capita supply of water in Chandigarh. It has the most modern automatic slaughter house in the public sector in the country. The civic body is planning for a cent per cent of sewage treatment. He said that the civic body has the latest fire fighting equipment and machinery and well maintained green belts and parks.

Explaining about the water supply, Dr Sunkaria said that the total water supply is 84 million gallons daily (MGD), which includes 64 MGD of surface water from canal at Kajauli and 20 MGD of underground water from 200 tubewells. The MC has proposed to treat 50 MGD sewage water with the augmentation of existing 15 MGD STP at Diggian as the per pollution control standards.

Earlier, leader of the delegation Barala Srinivas gave a brief introduction of the Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation. He said that under JNNURM, a plan was being prepared to develop the city at a cost of Rs 14,000 crores in seven years.

Many projects were taken up and some of them are in progress. Fifty per cent of the project cost will be borne by the Centre, 20 per cent by the state government of Andhra Pradesh and the remaining by the civic body under the JNNURM.

Heading: Milk to cost dearer as Verka hikes prices again - Indian Express
Content:
The Economic Offences Wing of the UT Police today registered a case against Aman Security and Detective agencies, for embezzlement of public money, amounting to more than Rs 17 lakh.

The MC had employed nearly 450 safai karamcharis from the agency, apart from labourers and drivers. A number of complaints, were, however, received from individual employees, complaining that the agency was not depositing Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) and Employees' State Insurance (ESI) shares paid to them by the corporation, in their accounts.

After making correspondence with the office of the Regional Provident Fund Commissioner and the Director, ESIC, the offices failed to supply information, in the absence of the account numbers, which were to be supplied by the agency. It was later found that the agency had deposited less money paid by the corporation to the agency. A case has been registered under Sections 406 of the IPC, 14A of the EPF Act and 85/86A of the ESI Act.

Heading: Ishmeet’s kin head for Maldives today - Indian Express
Content:
For the second time in the year, Verka has announced a price hike for milk, to be in effect from September 1. The 500 ml pouch will be dearer by 50 paise in Punjab while in Himachal Pradesh, the price will increase by a unit.

Balwinder Singh, general manger, Verka Milk Plant, said, "We had to announce the hike to generate a better price for our milk producers and also to offset the increase in the cost of processing and distribution."

Singh added, "We are paying nearly 78,000 milk producers almost 25 per cent more as compared to last year. The input costs for dairy farmers have increased as fodder has become more expensive. Also, the hike in diesel prices has increased transportation costs."

Singh said the salaries of the staff strength, working at the plant, has also gone up.

"With these constraints, we had no option but to increase the prices," he added.

The Verka plant at Ludhiana produces nearly 2 lakh litres of milk everyday but consumers have been facing a shortage of milk over the last two days.

Suman Arora a resident of Sarabha Nagar, said, "The Verka booth from where I buy milk every day was out of stock. The booth owner told me that the supply from the dealer was low. Now, that we have been told about the hike. I am sure the shortage must have been created just to make extra money."

General Manager Balwinder Singh, however, maintained, "Milk is an essential item and we cannot do this at our end. Some dealer must have withheld his share."

Heading: Minor raped, one held - Indian Express
Content:
State-level function held to celebrate young singer's birth anniversary; Ishmeet Singh Foundation launched

Gurpinder Singh and Dr Charan Kamal Singh, father and uncle of singer Ishmeet Singh who died in Male a couple of weeks ago, will leave for Maldives tomorrow to initiate an inquiry into the circumstances that led to the death of the young singer.

Ishmeet had died last month at a beach resort in Male while swimming in a hotel pool. The Star Voice of India 2007 winner was in the country along with a troupe in connection with the second series of the same show which was on air. Eyewitnesses claimed that Ishmeet had gone deep into the water.

Though post-mortem report of the late singer clearly states that he had died due to drowning yet his family has all along been maintaining the late singer knew how to swim. "We want to establish the circumstances that led to his death. How could he drown in a hotel pool where there are waiters and other hotel staff around," said Dr Charan Kamal Singh, Ishmeet's uncle. Apart from the family the state government had also appealed to the Government of India to press upon the Maldives government for a detailed inquiry into the incident. The post-mortem was conducted at the Civil Hospital as Maldives has no provision for conducting the examination.

Meanwhile, the family celebrated the young singer's birthday that falls today. The family announced the launching of Ishmeet Singh Foundation which is headed by his father. Dr Charan Kamal Singh said, "This foundation is an independent body that will work towards promotion of music and art in the state." The family apart from visiting the local gurdwara also cut a birthday cake in the memory of the 21-year-old singer. The state government held a musical evening in the memory of the late singer.

Heading: Encroachments galore at Akalgarh market in Chaura Bazar - Indian Express
Content:
In two different incidents across the city, a minor was raped and another escaped a gang rape attempt by three youths on Sunday. After registering both cases, the police have arrested three accused in separate cases.

Meanwhile, the Focal Point police have also registered a case in connection with the rape of a minor by two persons in the last week of August.

In first incident, a 10-year-old daughter of a migrant labourer in Sunet village was allegedly raped and sodomised by her neighbour Jamshed on Sunday. The Sarabha Nagar police have registered a rape and sodomy case against the accused, who is a resident of Muzaffarnagar in Uttar Pradesh. The victim's mother told the police that the accused took her daughter on the pretext of giving her a ride on his motorcycle and raped her on an isolated road near South City.

The Sarabha Nagar SHO Devinder Kumar told Newsline that the accused has been arrested. The SHO said that Jamshed was produced in a local court and the court sent him to two-day police custody. "We have got the medical examination of the victim done. While the rape has been confirmed, sodomy is yet to be ascertained," the SHO added.

In another incident, three youths residing in the neighbourhood of Nanaksar Mohalla made an unsuccessful bid to rape a 14-year-old on Sunday.

According to sources, these youths took the girl to a room and tried to gang rape her. When the girl raised the alarm, they left her but threatened her of dire consequences if she reported the matter to anyone. The girl narrated the episode to her family who further reported the matter to the police.

The police yesterday registered cases against the three accused Jagdev Singh, Kipa and Gurdeep Singh alias Bawa. Assistant Sub Inspector (ASI) Dalbir Singh told Newsline that of these Jagdev and Gurdeep have been arrested. They were produced in a local court and the court sent them in the police custody for a day.

The police said that efforts were on to nab the third accused.

Meanwhile, the Focal Point police also have registered a case in connection with the rape of a 14-year-old girl. According to the police sources, the girl, a resident of Giaspura, was abducted by two youths from her neighbourhood and allegedly raped her on August 25.

The Focal Point police have registered a rape case against one Vinli and Arun Kumar, both residents of Giaspura.

Heading: City’s oil trader felicitated for using eco-friendly techniques - Indian Express
Content:
Ten feet shops in the Akalgarh market have encroached encroachment around 20-feet space outside their shops. Some have either displayed goods outside their shops while others have given the space on rent to a private vendor.

The market, which has around 750 shops, does not have any space for free movement.

Fed up with this arrangement, about 15 shopkeepers of the market have filed a PIL against the encroachers for which the status report will be presented in the court on September 19. An MC team had visited the market in the past two weeks and issued warnings to the erring traders but to no avail.

The members of Akalgarh Market Bachao Sangrash Committee, who have also filed this PIL, said," Because of the encroachments at the ground floor, the shopkeepers at upper floors get no business. Moreover, goods can no longer be taken upstairs as there is no space to walk around in the market."

Kartar Singh Patna, Chairman of the committee and general secretary of Lok Jan Shakti Party, Punjab, said," We did bring the issue to the notice of the MC authorities long ago but then they were not interested. They often used to give an excuse that it is a private market. On August 29, erring shopkeepers were told to remove their goods from the site. However, nothing has been done till date."

Manpreet Singh Bunty, another member, added, "The traders who have their shops on the first floor have no business. Many of them are planning to sell their shops as they are finding it difficult to survive in the market."

Not more than 20 shopkeepers have encroached the two main entrances of the market as they get hefty rentals between Rs 2,000 and Rs 20,000.

Heading: St Stephen's give PFA the blues - Indian Express
Content:
Ecofriendly rice bran oil without using any chemicals - This is what Dhuri-based A P Solvex Group of Industries claims to be offering to its consumers. Set up in 1986, the company supplies rice bran oil to big brands including Saffola Gold and Sundrop Heart, which contain 80% refined rice bran oil.

"We refine our oil physically without using any chemicals. This way we are able to save oryzonol- the basic nutrient to reduce. However, other oil companies use alkalis to give a better colour to the oil and kill most of nutrients," said A.R Sharma, the 49-year-old chairman of the group.

Soon, Dhara's new brand Dhara Health with 80% of rice bran oil and 20% of sunflower oil will be packaged from this unit.

For following eco-friendly measures, this company got the first national award in the field of research and development in the country. Sharma said, "We bagged the award for R&D in medium enterprises category."

Sharma was conferred with the award by Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh on August 30 at Vigyan Bhawan along with a cash prize of Rs 1 lakh, besides a certificate and a trophy. And to know more about the health problems, Sharma is all set to do Ph.D in food laws from Panjab University.

The company, which also markets its oil under the brand name Ricela, has emerged as the largest rice bran oil refining group in the country with a capacity to process around 350 tonnes of rice bran daily.

"In the view of the growing awareness about health benefits of rice bran oil, the company has decided to increase the capacity by another 150 tonnes per day at Dhuri besides setting up a refining unit at Jagraon.

Sharma, who is a post-graduate in law, said that rice bran is popularly known as heart oil in Japan but was upset about the fact that India, which is second largest producer in paddy after China, lags behind and was using it mainly for non-edible purposes.

Heading: Inter-House chess competition held - Indian Express
Content:
The thin line that made the difference for St Stephen's School Football Academy, Chandigarh was that extra combined team effort and passes that not only helped the team create number of chances but also keep the opposition Punjab Football Academy on the back-foot. Because of the superb game displayed by the whole outfit, St Stephen's Academy made a perfect start to its campaign by winning their first match in its first match in the sixth Administrator's Challenge Cup All-India Football Tournament for Under-17 being organised by the Chandigarh Sports Department at the Sector 42 Football Stadium on Tuesday.

Unlike yesterday, there were very little spectators, the only few being the teams that are participating in the championship and players who come for practice at the Sports Complex. Both the team started off brightly and it was the Punjab team who had the first shot at the goal as a swirling long shot by Jagjeet just sailed over the bar.

Missed chances
There was a superb chance to score a goal but this time the team was that of St Stephen's Academy. Rising high to a long pass, Samandram Langba tried his best to head the ball into the net but his effort was thwarted by Nishad Sindham who collected the ball easily. Two minutes later, St Stephen earned a free-kick just outside the penalty area but Punjab player Jagjeet didn't play heed to the referee's instructions to clear the line to which he was shown a green card as a sign of caution. St Stephen players slowly paced up their game and started juggling the ball to and forth. However, one of the stars of the match, Umakanta Singh's goal was disallowed in the 24th minute when his shot hit the bar and then the ball rebounded and touched the goal line but the referee disallowed the goal.

Cool finisher Antil
However, the day belonged to Kuldeep Antil as his effort in the 38th minute put his team on the advantage. The team erupted into joy while slowly frustration seemed to dawn on the Punjab players as they made rough tackle on the opposition team players.

After getting the lead in the first half, the St Stephen's Academy played a much composed game while the Punjab team put a much better performance in the second half and created a number of chances to neutralize the lead The best chance for PFA came in the 76th minute when Jagjeet failed to put the ball into the empty net and shot wide after the St Stephen goalkeeper had stumbled and fall down. In the last ten minutes, PFA got some golden opportunities to save the sagging match as Kulbir Singh volleyed the ball over the crossbar and Manjeet's shot was adeptly caught by Stephen's goalkeeper. St Stephen's Academy earned three corners to PFA's two, one of which changed the course of the match and brought smiles on the St Stephen's team.

Earlier, Chandigarh Football Academy kept a clean sheet while thumping Haryana by 7-0 in the match played in the morning. CFA has scored an astounding 16 goals in just two matches. Gagandeep scored a brilliant hat-trick for CFA while Amandeep, Sehnaj, Sumit Passi and Samuel turned the heat on the Haryana team with their strikes. Tamil Nadu failed to capitalise on a superb brace by SS Dharan as they could not overcome a spirited Rohit Academy (Orissa) side and lost the match by 3-4. The third match was played between Delhi and Chattisgarh where the Delhi side drubbed Chattisgarh by 3-0. This match also witnessed the first red card of the tournament as Arshulla Khan was sent off from the ground for using abusive language.

Overage players increases to 24
ADDING to the woes, ten more players were found overage in the medical check-up that was carried out at the Government Multispeciality Hospital, Sector 16. These players were debarred from taking part in the on-going tournament. The number of overage players has risen to 24 after 14 players were found to be over the limited age for the participation in the championship. Punjab Football Association and Madhya Pradesh Football Association had three overage players each.

Heading: North India artistalent hunt is on - Indian Express
Content:
A six-day workshop on cardio-thoracic nursing organised by the College of Nursing, DMCH, began last evening at the Dumra auditorium in the institute. The workshop will conclude on September 6.

Secretary of DMCH Managing Society, Prem Kumar Gupta inaugurated the workshop. Among those present at the inaugural function were Vice-Principal of DMCH, Dr Jagdeep Whig, Chief Cardiologist, Dr G.S. Wander, Medical Suptds, Dr B.S. Shah and Dr Rajoo Singh Chinna, Principal of the College of Nursing, Dr Jasbir Kaur, and Vice-Principal of College of Nuring, Suresh Sharma.

In her address to the audience, Dr Jasbir Kaur welcomed the dignitaries present on the occasion and informed them about the various topics and sessions to be included in this week-long session. She said that advanced nursing procedures, comprehensive nursing care and other supportive nursing care had significantly improved the outcome of critically-ill patients in ICU.

The medical administrators present on the occasion lauded the efforts of College of Nursing in organising such a workshop. They stressed that nursing was a very noble profession and required elements of competence, courtesy and positive communication skills as an integral part of the curriculum of a nurse.

The main aim of DMCH is to train the best possible nurses, so that they can provide best possible care to the patients. Suresh Sharma, Vice-Principal, College of Nursing (CoN), thanked all the dignitaries for their support and guidance and said that the workshop would prove to be of immense use to the the nursing students.

The topics which were discussed during the first two days of workshop included "Review of anatomy and physiology of heart", "E.C.G eecording", "Care of patient with MI (Myocardial Infarction), "Care of patient with CABG", "Pre & post care of cardiac catheterisation", "Administration of drugs: I/M injection" and "I/V cannulation and site care".

Heading: Factor in soil test report while applying fertilizers: PAU experts - Indian Express
Content:
The process of rationalisation is back to square one. The process which was restarted yesterday under the Chairmanship of Surjit Kaur, Assistant Director Public Instructions(Secondary Schools) today witnessed the same problem which surfaced at the previous rationalisation process. On August 22 and August 23 about 30 surplus teachers from different government schools of the district were transferred at distant places. These teachers alleged discrepancies in the process. Following which Dr Jagtar Singh Khatra, Director Public Instructions(Secondary Schools), ordered to stop the process of rationalisation in between on August 24.

The process of rationalisation started again on August 31 when Surjhit Kaur ADPI(Secondary Schools) dismissed the previous transfer orders after reviewing them. All the surplus teachers of the district were again called at R S Model Senior Secondary School Shastri Nagar on September 1 and 2. As per Surjit Kaur, "We asked these teachers about the choice of the stations where there is vacancy. Now we will issue them transfer orders accordingly. But today the team, headed by Surjit Kaur witnessed the same problem. About 30 teachers who earlier alleged discrepancies in the process when they were posted at distant places again made hue and cry when they were given the option of stations. Sudesh Bajaj DEO(Secondary) Ludhiana said, "This is the same group of teachers who were also posted at distant places in previous process of rationalisation. And again these teachers are being posted at the distant places as there are no vacancies in the nearby schools. And we cannot afford to allow them for continuing their services in the present schools."

All this led to lot of confusion among the officers as well as teachers. After two days' long wait these teachers tried their best to convince the officers about their problem. But the ADPI as well as DEO(Secondary), Ludhiana, convinced them that only distant stations had the vacancies. Sudesh Bajaj said, "We will have to allot them these stations as there is no other option." However, about eight teachers were still waiting for their counselling after 7:30pm.

Meanwhile, Surinder Grewal, president of Democratic Teachers' Front alleged the policy of rationalisation was not made clear to them. He said, "Teachers were not aware of this policy." While DEO denied this saying,"We made teachers aware about it through MLAs as well as through school headmasters and principals also. These are false allegations."

Heading: Orientation programme for fresh MBA students held - Indian Express
Content:
"Application of fertilizers to different crops should be based on soil test report," stressed Dr A.S. Sidhu, Head, Department of Soils, PAU, while explaining that soil testing laboratories in the department were providing this service to the farmers.

Giving details, Dr Balwinder Singh said that a total of 3,517 soil and 1,208 water samples were analysed by the department during 2007-08. For their organic carbon content, 48.5, 45.1 and 6.4 % soil samples were reported as low, medium and high while for available phosphorus content, 29.7, 33.6 and 36.7 % samples tested low, medium and high, respectively. Dr Singh added that 11.5, 60.2 and 28.3 % samples showed low, medium and high availability of potassium. Dr Sidhu said that fertilizer application should be applied as per the advice of soil scientists so that there was no wastage.

Quality of irrigation water was also important, said these scientists. Dr Singh said quality of irrigation water samples tested by the soil testing laboratory showed 47.8, 31.2 and 21.0 % samples were found fit, marginal and unfit for irrigation, respectively. Dr Sidhu said that irrigation water in south-western districts of Punjab were brackish and therefore, farmers should get them tested to get expert advice from soil scientists. He also said that the water testing was important even in the case of deep wells, as the situation may vary from site to site.

Dr M.P.S. Khurana said that water in village ponds contained essential plant nutrients like nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium. However, it may also contain salts such as carbonates, bi-carbonates and chlorides of calcium, magnesium and sodium in undesirable amounts. He, therefore, suggested that village pond water should also be got tested from the laboratory before using it for irrigation.

Dr Sidhu said that besides the main campus at Ludhiana, facilities of soil testing were also available in different regional stations of PAU such as Regional Station, Gurdaspur and Bathinda, from where the farmers could get their field soils and irrigation water tested.

He suggested that farmers could also approach Krishi Vigyan Kendras of their areas for getting their soils and water tested. Dr Sidhu informed that charges for this service were kept nominal. For soil testing in respect of major nutrients or trace elements the charges are Rs 20 per sample while for comprehensive testing of major as well as minor elements the charges are Rs 40 per sample.

Heading: Storms swirl in Atlantic, deadly floods hit Haiti - Indian Express

Heading: Pak-born US scientist indicted on murder charges - Indian Express
Content:
Heavy rains flooded parts of Haiti with head-high water on Tuesday and sent walls of mud down the hillsides, killing at least 25 people as Tropical Storm Hanna swirled over the Bahamas and took aim at the southeastern United States.

A new tropical storm, Josephine, formed off Africa behind Tropical Storm Ike. Both were moving westward just as Hurricane Gustav dissipated after slamming into the U.S. Gulf Coast near New Orleans.

The flurry of Atlantic storms underscored predictions for a busier than normal hurricane season and was worrisome news for US oil and natural gas producers in the Gulf of Mexico, millions of people living in the Caribbean and on U.S. coasts, and farmers fearing flooded fields.

The US government has forecast 14 to 18 tropical storms will form during the six-month season that began on June 1, more than the historical average of 10. Josephine was already the 10th, forming before the statistical peak of the season on Sept. 10.

By Tuesday night, Hanna was bearing down on Great Inagua Island with 65 mph (100 kph) winds, the U.S. National Hurricane Center said.

It was expected to strengthen back into a Category 1 hurricane on the five-step Saffir-Simpson scale of intensity, with winds of at least 74 mph (119 kph) on Wednesday or Thursday.

Hanna dumped torrential rains on the southeastern Bahamas, the Turks and Caicos islands, Haiti and the Dominican Republic.

In Haiti, heavy rains caused severe flooding in the northern port city of Gonaives, where thousands of people died four years ago during a similar catastrophe.

"The city is flooded and there are parts where the water gets to 2 meters (6.5 feet)," said civil protection director Alta Jean-Baptiste. "A lot of people have been climbing onto the tops of their houses since last night to escape the flooding."

Authorities said flooding and mudslides from the storm killed at least 25 people across Haiti, including 12 in low-lying Gonaives and three in the nearby town of Gros Morne.

FLORIDA EMERGENCY

Hanna was nearly stationary but was forecast to turn northwest on a track that would take it near the Bahamian capital of Nassau and near the US East Coast on Thursday. It was likely to come ashore at the end of the week somewhere between northern Florida and the Carolinas.

Although the official forecast kept it over water as it skirted the Florida coast, state Gov Charlie Crist declared a state of emergency.

Tropical Storm Ike headed west after forming on Monday between Africa and the Caribbean and appeared likely to become a hurricane that would threaten the Caribbean islands and possibly the United States.

It was too early to say where Ike might go but the storm drew the attention of energy companies running the 4,000 offshore platforms in the Gulf of Mexico that provide the United States with a quarter of its crude oil and 15 percent of its natural gas.

Ike was about 930 miles (1,500 km) east-northeast of the Leeward Islands and moving west at 17 mph (28 kph) late on Tuesday. Its top sustained winds had strengthened to 65 mph (100 kph) and were expected to reach hurricane strength of 74 mph (119 kph) on Wednesday.

Josephine swirled over the far eastern Atlantic about 180 miles (290 km) west-southwest of the Cape Verde Islands. It was moving west at 12 mph (19 kph), with top sustained winds of near 50 mph (85 kph), and could become a hurricane on Wednesday.

Heading: Indian students may have to push harder to get Aus visa - Indian Express
Content:
A Pakistan-born US scientist Aafia Siddiqui, with suspected links to al-Qaeda, has been indicted on federal charges that she tried to kill the American interrogators after her arrest in Afghanistan.

The 36-year-old neuro-scientist was arrested in Ghazni province of Afghanistan in July this year while loitering around the Governor's compound.

Siddiqui was held for questioning by army officers and FBI agents, but she allegedly snatched an Army officer's M-4 rifle and fire it at other members of the US interview team.

She repeatedly stated her intent and desire to kill Americans, according to the indictment filed on Tuesday.

If convicted, Siddiqui could spend her life in prison.

She was indicted yesterday and scheduled to be arraigned on Thursday.

However, none of the officers were injured in the scuffle that followed.

The indictment further said that a number of items were in Siddiqui's possession when she was detained, including handwritten notes that referred to a "mass casualty attack".

US officials, who privately described her as a "treasure trove" of information on the al-Qaeda terror network, alleged that she was carrying a list of some of the city's prime locations like Plum Island, the Empire State Building and the Statue of Liberty, among others.

Siddiqui, who had been missing for five years and reappeared in Ghazni under suspicious circumstances, was arrested by Afghan police on July 17 and brought to the US the next day on the pretext that she had been planning a suicide attack.

The US educated scientist faces one count of attempting to kill US nationals abroad; one count of attempting to kill US officers and employees; one count of armed assault of US officers and employees; one count of using and carrying a firearm during and in relation to a crime of violence; and three counts of assault of US officers and employees.

A FBI statement said that if convicted, Siddiqui faces a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison on each of the attempted murder and armed assault charges; life in prison on the firearm charge; and eight years in prison on each of the remaining assault charges.

The indictment charges that Siddiqui not only had documents listing the landmarks but also various ways to attack "enemies, including by destroying reconnaissance drones, using underwater bombs, and using gliders".

A computer flash drive found from the scientist at a time of her arrest also referred to "specific 'cells' and 'attacks' by certain 'cells,'" the charges read.

However, Siddiqui's lawyers claimed that the Pakistan-born scientist had been detained secretly since 2003 after she left her parents home in Karachi for Islamabad.

Siddiqui is married to a nephew of Khalid Shekh Mohammed who, the US says, is among the people who helped plan the September 11 attacks on Washington and New York.

Heading: Three bullets fired at Pak PM's motorcade, Gilani unhurt - Indian Express
Content:
Indian students seeking admission in Australia may have to push harder to get a visa as authorities there have moved India up on the 'immigration risk' scale to check their numbers.

According to the latest official data, there were 65,000 Indian students in Australia in the year to June, mostly in vocational education. Although they constitute smaller number as compared to Chinese students but their growth rate was much higher – up to about 55 per cent as compared to China's 19 per cent.

While India was not alone in moving up the risk scale, Visa applicants from Colombia, Egypt, Ghana, Jordan, Nigeria, Sri Lanka, Romania and Zimbabwe will also have to now do extra work to show that they were bona-fide students.

"The status of these nine countries had been changed 'to combat increased levels of immigration risk'," an spokesperson from the Department of Immigration and Citizenship said.

The spokesperson, however, said "genuine applicants had nothing to fear from the changes".

"All universities were likely to have asked students to lodge their visa applications and processed before September 1 change in immigration risk levels, which affects a host of overseas markets," the pro-Vice Chancellor (international) of New South Wales University, Jennie Lang said.

We will also be encouraging (Department of Immigration and Citizenship) staff in offshore posts to ensure that university sector applicants are given priority, Lang was quoted in The Australian newspaper.

The students of the nine countries will have to give extra evidence of their capacity to support themselves financially, especially with savings histories, the report said.

The risk levels are set across various sectors, including English language courses, vocational education and higher degrees.

The higher risk assessment affects all sectors of the Indian education market, which moved up by one level. In the latest year-to-date figures from Australian Education International, there were more than 392,000 overseas students in Australia, representing almost a 20 per cent increase in enrolments.

India, China and Nepal continued to be strong growth markets, but those such as Japan, Hong Kong and Taiwan continued to decline.

Heading: NSG waiver seems an uphill task for India - Indian Express
Content:
Shots were fired at Pakistani Prime Minister Yousaf Raza Gilani's motorcade on Wednesday but he was not hurt, his spokesman said.

"Multiple shots were fired ... the Prime Minister is safe," said the spokesman, Zahid Bashir, adding at least three bullets had hit Gilani's armoured vehicle.

The attack happened on the main road to the airport in the capital, Islamabad. Earlier, Gilani had arrived back at the airport from a trip to the eastern city of Lahore.

Gilani is a senior member of former Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto's party. She was killed in a suicide gun and bomb attack on Dec 27 while campaigning for a general election.

The government said al Qaeda-linked militants killed her.

Bhutto's party went on to win the Feb 18 election and Gilani became Prime Minister of a coalition government.

Heading: Pakistani Taliban claims Gilani attack - Indian Express
Content:
An unconditional NSG waiver for India appeared to be an uphill task on the eve of the 45-nation grouping's crucial meeting with a few sceptic countries holding confabulations among themselves in Vienna on Wednesday.

The countries, which include New Zealand, Austria, Ireland and Switzerland, are understood to have discussed the strategy to be adopted at the two-day NSG meeting called to consider whether India should be allowed to resume civil nuclear trade with the international community.

These countries continue to nurse apprehensions with regard to the waiver as they feel it will compromise the global non-proliferation system.

Compounding the problems for India was the disclosure of US State Department documents which make clear Washington's emphasis on denying New Delhi the right to reprocess and snap nuclear cooperation if India conducts atomic tests.

This document could be used by the critical NSG countries to insist on incorporating such provisions in the waiver of the grouping.

The United States is trying to push these countries not to block the waiver and the effort is still on.

The US has deputed Under Secretary of State William Burns to the NSG meeting to demonstrate its keenness to ensure that the exemption is granted to India.

Foreign Secretary Shivshankar Menon, who is in the US, will come here directly. He will be joined by Prime Minister's Special Envoy Shyam Saran, R B Grover, Director, Strategic Affairs in the Department of Atomic Energy and some other officials of the Ministry of External Affairs.

Though India is not a member of the NSG, the delegation led by Menon will be camping here to meet envoys of the NSG countries, if necessary, to make further efforts to persuade them.

The NSG will consider a draft which is being presented before the grouping after amendments following demands by at least 15 countries during the August 21-22 meeting.

The sceptic countries continued to have reservations even after amendments to the original draft as they feel that the changes were only cosmetic in nature and conditions are not attached.

China, too, appeared on Monday to be joining the countries having reservations when the ruling Communist Party's mouthpiece 'People's Daily' described the Indo-US nuclear deal as a "blow" to non-proliferation.

However, the Chinese Government yesterday sought to indicate that it will not block the initiative.

India, on the other hand, has maintained that if conditions are attached to the waiver, it could walk away.

Meanwhile, New Delhi today refused to comment over the American position that it will stop fuel supplies if it conducted a nuclear test as reflected in the document made public in the US after being kept under wraps.

"I have read the statement. But I will not comment," External Affairs Minister Pranab Mukherjee said.

Asked to comment on the outcome of the NSG meeting, Mukherjee said "I will keep my fingers crossed."

Heading: Belarus' love for Bollywood and Bangalore - Indian Express
Content:
Pakistani Taliban on Wednesday claimed responsibility for the attack on Premier Yousuf Raza Gilani's car which was fired at near the garrison city of Rawalpindi and threatened to carry out more strikes against the government leaders.

Muslim Khan, the spokesman of the umbrella militant organisation which was banned by the Pakistani government last week, said the Pakistani Taliban had carried out the attack on Gilani's car.

More such attacks would be carried out on government leaders in the future, he said.

Gilani's car was fired at by unknown assailants near Rawalpindi but contradictory statements were made by officials later about his presence in the vehicle.

Heading: US to push hard for NSG waiver amid continued scepticism - Indian Express
Content:
As many of the residents of this Belarusian capital head for their dachas on weekends, a group of girls, young and not so young prefer to stay back home and head in the evenings for a special class that would help them achieve their dreams- to learn the classical Indian dances.

The teacher is not Indian but a Belarusian.

For many in this tiny country which was known as Silicon Valley of the erstwhile Soviet Union, India has always been a mystery. They avidly watched Hindi movies that were received, dubbed in Russian, from Moscow. None, however, dreamt of visiting India.

The meagre incomes just didn't permit the luxury of foreign travel. Things, however, changed after Belarus became independent in 1992. More of India can be seen- thanks to the exhibitions of Indian goods - sarees, shawls, handicrafts and apparel that are being held regularly.

An ISCON temple too has opened and aroused interest among many in the is former communist culture. New avenues have opened up.

Tiny advertisements in the city's buses featuring the Taj Mahal are enough to drive hoards of Belarusian girls to the exhibitions that he has been organising for the past few years says Navin Kohli. Settled in Minsk for over a decade, Navin has married a Belarusian girl. Business is good, he says as he directs his sales staff to look after the customers in the exhibition that has Indian consumer goods for sale.

Their natural inclination towards technology has drawn the Belorusians towards Bangalore. As many Soviet day statues and street names remain unchanged, a busy traffic junction and a huge park in the capital have been named after Bangalore which was made a sister city by Minsk.

Heading: Obama's mother may have spent 5 years in Pakistan - Indian Express
Content:
Amid continued reservations of some member countries over granting waiver to India, the Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG) will hold a crucial two-day meeting in Vienna from Thursday to consider the initiative.

The NSG will consider a draft which is being presented before the 45-nation grouping after amendments following demands by at least 15 countries during the August 21-22 meeting.

Countries like New Zealand and Austria, which are still not satisfied with the revised draft, are expected to voice their concerns over non-proliferation issues.

On studying the draft circulated to them by Germany, the current Chair of the NSG, these countries feel that the amendments in the text are only cosmetic in nature and conditions are not attached.
