Heading: Small Talk - Indian Express
Content:
Some of them deliquescing and others waiting in dark vaults of collector's closet for their turn to gradually get decayed, putting an end to a story that once touched the hearts of multitudes. Preserving these photochemical relics, which considering the fact that only one classic, till now in Bollywood, got the opportunity to get restored and colourised in true sense, appeared a far-fetched dream till the time Purab Gujar came up with his film restoration studio and technique in the year 2007.

"There are two aspects of preserving a film, one is conservation and another is restoration. Conservation is what we have been practicing in India till now to preserve films. The need now is to take a step ahead," shares Gujar .

Gujar's claim to the fact that the technology is completely aboriginal comes loud and clear as he goes about explaining the ratio of foreign support he took in developing the technology. "People and friends specially NRIs in the Silicon Valley have contributed towards the making of this technology in their specific areas of expertise. But the full time developers and technologists working on this were from India, mainly Pune. Thus Cameo is clearly indigenous technology, states Gujar "

Gujar, a graduate in engineering from VIT College came up with concept of developing an affordable film restoration software and studio when he was in college. "The requirement of film restoration was found out when we were studying imaging. We talked to people concerned, who endorsed the grave problem the industry was facing already. We went ahead built a few prototypes of what we thought could be done for the problem, and demonstrated it to various people in the film industry. And then we got down to the task of building the entire software required to put up a full fledged restoration studio, "elaborates Gujar."

The technology allows tens or hundreds of computer-servers to work together, along with human assisted computers to remove damages from films. "It took us more than a year for the research and close to a year to build the technology. Pune, being a primary IT hub allowed us to find most of the required talent locally. We had IIT graduates and experts from imaging, computer vision, Linux and computer software coming together to make this first generation of the technology. This was largely possible due to the contribution of Aditya Godbole, the CTO who has immense knowledge and network in open source groups, shares Gujar"

In the thinly populated list of film restoration studios in India, Cameo carves an altogether different section for itself because of the fact that the technology has been completely developed in India. Where Da Vinci 2k plus, an American software is used by some restoration companies others use European software to restore films. " Where Shemaroo in Mumbai imports its technology from USA, Prasad studio in Chennai uses European software to restore films. Ours is the only software that has been developed in India and that's why the service we provide our patrons with is so cheap," shares Gujar.

The current team of Cameo comprises of 40 restorers trained exclusively on the Cameo technology, are from various backgrounds including Art graduates, animation students, creative design, engineers, BSC graduates. " We have restored Chetan Anand's Haqeeqat, Jag Mohan Mundra's Kamla and right now we are working on the restoration of Jag Mohan Mundra's Surag," informs Gujar who remains hopeful about signing a contract with NFAI to restore the classics.

Heading: Spanakopta - Indian Express
Content:
Grannies making modaks for grandchildren is an unwritten tradition in most of the Maharashtrian houses

On the first day of Ganesh festival, the reason that makes the otherwise naughty and playful children stand quietly for the aarti is a delicious one! Aarti and pooja are interesting, but what is more tempting for the kids are hot, steaming modaks.

Ganesh festival is the festival of happiness and togetherness, but what modaks bring together are generations. "My grandmother makes the best modaks in the world" or "I wish you had eaten the modaks made by my granny" and sentences of similar kinds are quite common for the ones who visit Maharashtrian families during Ganesh festival. In most of the Maharashtrian families, grandmothers are known to make modaks for the grandchildren.

According to Sayali Panse, student, "Since childhood, modak and granny has been an equation. On the first day of Ganesh festival, we used to go to our grandmother. She was an amazing cook and more than the recipe it was the love that used to add the taste to the modaks. She never ever kept modaks ready for us. After the aarti, she used to cook it for us and serve it hot. Wherever I go, I will never in my life forget the modaks that my granny used to make."

Alaka Kshirsagar, teacher, says, "Making modaks for your grandchildren is a different feeling altogether. I used to make modaks for my children as well, but with grandchildren there is more affection and belonging. I make modaks and serve them with hot ghee. In fact my four-year-old grandson likes to have the modaks without the fillings and feeding him is a great satisfaction."

Nirmala Kulkarni owns a small food joint in Dahnukar colony is also a grandmother and says, "Yes we make modaks otherwise also but what is special about the modaks in Ganesh festival is that they are made with coconut, kesar, elaichi and jaggery. Other than that, there are a number of fillings like the ones from cucumber, khoya, potatoes and so on."

Pradnya Kadam, housewife adds, "Me and my mother, both make modaks, but my children, more than my modaks, like the ones prepared by my mother. And I feel that it is quite natural because as a child, I used to prefer the ones mace by my granny. So I take it in a positive spirit thinking that my grandchildren would enjoy my modaks."

While this is about granny and grandchildren, Ganesha seems to enjoy modaks made by anyone and everyone. Otherwise, eating 21 modaks is no joke!

Recipe

Ingredients coconut, jaggery, elaichi, poppy seeds, rice flour.

Method Stuffing: Grate the coconut and mix it with jaggery (750 gms of jaggery against 1 kg of coconut) and cook for sometime. Then add cardamom powder and poppy seed to the mixture.

The coating is made of rice flour. Take water and rice in equal quantity. Heat the kadai, and put some ghee, then add water. When the water starts boiling, put rice flour in it. In about 45 minutes, the mixture of water and rice flour becomes homogeneous. Now knead the rice flour mixture with your hand to prepare soft dough of the mixture. Now it is ready to be filled with the coconut stuffing. Steam the filled modak for 10 minutes and serve with hot ghee.

Heading: Meal Ticket - Indian Express
Content:
(Pronounced spa-na-koh-pay-tah)

Best eaten fresh out of the oven, Spanakopita is delicious Mediterranean pastry from Greece. It can be described thus: A traditional filling of spinach and cottage, feta or ricotta cheese wrapped in phyllo dough (pronounced fillo, these paper-thin sheets of unleavened dough are popular for making pastries in the Mediterranean) and baked till golden brown. The combination of crunchy phyllo dough with the soft stuffing of the pie that includes cheeses, herbs and onions makes Spanakopita quite nice. Small triangles cut out of the Spanakopita pie are popular breakfast snacks in Greece. It is also a popular appetiser at parties. In as much as it is tasty, Spanakopita is loaded with calories. The pastry is slathered with butter and the cheeses come loaded with fat too. It is as good or as bad as eating a fattening chicken-cheese burger. Nonetheless, it's a great idea to give diets a break and eat some Spanakopita at Frangipani, Trident.

Heading: Now, buy stamp paper at a click of the mouse - Indian Express
Content:
Already tried out in US, India launch by November

A vaccine that can stall the onset of cervical cancer, the second most common form of cancer among women in India, will be introduced in the country by November this year, experts told The Indian Express on the eve of the International Conference on Cancer. The two-day conference will get under way in Pune from Saturday.

Swati Bhave, member of the Apollo Hospital consultant committee for Human Papillomavirus Vaccine (HPV), said that the vaccine will be launched by November. It has already been in use in the US for two years.

More than 130,000 new cases, about a fourth of the global total, of cervical cancer cases are reported in India every year, with only breast cancer having a higher incidence. An estimated 74,000 Indian women die annually from the disease.

While the country's National Cancer Control Programme has emphasised the importance of early detection and treatment, there is no organised screening programme and the disease is usually detected and treated at a late stage.

A vaccine would help stop women from falling prey to the disease, said Sanjay Deshmukh, organising chairman of the cancer meet.

The HP virus, which causes 70 per cent of cervical cancer cases, is transmitted through sexual contact, especially in cases where there is poor personal hygiene. Cervical cancer is the cancer of the mouth of the uterus called cervix.

All sexually active women are at risk of contracting this disease. But it is seen mostly in woman aged between 50 and 55. If detected at a pre-cancerous stage, it is 100 per cent curable.

Ruby Hall Clinic's Kamalnayan Bajaj Cancer Centre will conduct the conference. A pre-conference live surgical workshop was held today, during which advanced surgical procedures were performed at Ruby Hall operation theatres and relayed simultaneously. Tata Memorial Center-Mumbai Director K A Dinshaw will inaugurate the conference.

Heading: Weeks before birthday, oil exec from city killed in Dubai chopper crash - Indian Express
Content:
Electronic purchase and authorised dealers part of tamper-proof system

Pune has become the first city in the state to roll out e-stamping, a process that is aimed at curbing stamp-paper scams of the kind Abdul Karim Telgi was involved in.

As Telgi showed, normal stamp paper leaves scope for fraud. Under the e-stamping system, stamp duty administration is computerised. "Purchase of stamp paper is electronic. Payments are made to the government electronically, making it a secure and techno savvy approach," said Mahesh Avhad, deputy inspector general of registration and deputy controller of stamps (computers), who is overseeing the project.

The city kicked off the process a week ago, with the Stock Holding Corporation of India Ltd (SHCIL) operating the e-stamping outlet at the Government Photo Registry building behind the Collectorate. Initially, SHCIL will be operate as the central record keeping agency. Eventually, banks will take on as agencies.

"In just a week, we have had around 200 people accessing this facility and collected Rs 12 lakh as revenue," Avhad said.

The process involves authorised dealers so that private vendors are kept out. However, the system called franking, which involves private vendors, persists. This will eventually be replaced by a centralised server base and database. The database will be made available at the click of a mouse.

A unique feature is the stamp certificate, a personalised online registration as part of a tamper-proof demat system. It marks a complete break from the stamp paper era for all types of documentation.

"The security system will comprise an optical thermal image that will display the original certificate; otherwise, if the document has been photocopied, it will say copy. While buying the certificate one has to provide details like the value of the stamp certificate, document type and particulars of the property to be registered. There will be a bar code in the certificate that can be read with a special hand-held unit; this will store information of the buyer. Once issued, these details will be locked to prevent tampering," Avhad said.

With the first counter open and some private banks having already shown interest, the process would soon be branched out, officials said. Mumbai will follow Pune before the process is rolled out across the state.

FROM TELGI TO TECHNOLOGY
Objective: Buy stamp paper electronically, avoid Telgi-like scam

Where: Stock Holding Corporation of India Ltd for now, banks to take over later

Novelty: The stamp certificate, a personalised online registration paper, as part of a tamperproof demat Coming soon: A a centralised server base to do away with the franking system

Heading: Sandalwood thief nabbed after 15-km highway chase, shootout - Indian Express
Content:
An executive from Pune was among seven persons killed in a helicopter crash in Dubai on Wednesday evening.

Julias Durant Periera, who would have turned 38 this month, was a resident of Lokmanya Nagar in Duttawadi. He was working as a materials coordinator on a ship of an oil company in Dubai for the last one year. His shell-shocked family and friends they had been preparing to celebrate his birthday on September 28.

"Julias was a simple and hardworking man. This is a big shock to all of us," said Sameer Pathan, a friend.

Julias Periera's brothers, Peter and Savio, also work abroad. All three had recently come to Pune for a family gathering. "For Julias, it was the last visit home," a relative said. The body will be sent to Pune for the last rites.

Julias had worked with the company for a year. The helicopter crashed into an oil rig off the coast of Dubai around 8.20 pm, killing all seven people on board, including Pareira, another Indian, a Briton, a Pakistani, a Filipino and a Venezuelan.

The helicopter was flying from Dubai's main international airport to the Rashid oilfield, around 70 kilometres off the coast. The aircraft crashed onto the deck of a drilling rig after which it broke up and fell into the sea. The bodies were recovered on Thursday afternoon.

The cause of the crash was not known. The civil aviation authority of UAE has set up a special team to investigate the cause.

Heading: City artist’s contribution to flood relief: 1,000 Ganesh idols in 72 hours - Indian Express
Content:
After a dramatic chase along the highway followed by a shootout in the early hours of Friday morning, the city police nabbed a sandalwood thief. He had four cronies, who got away.

The chase began around 2.15 am and ended around an hour later, after traversing 15 kilometres through the city . The suspect, Kadir Asif Pathan (29), along with four accomplices, had chopped off a sandalwood tree at the premises of Himgauri society in Erandwane. An alert resident saw them and informed the police immediately. A team of Kothrud police, led by sub-inspector R R Shelke, was on night patrol in the area and rushed to the spot.

The police team spotted the thieves in a Tata Safari jeep in front of Leelavati Apartment in Erandwane. Shelke tried to stop them, but the thieves drove off. He also fired two bullets, one of which hit the jeep window. The thieves, however, managed to flee.

Shelke and half a dozen cops, in a police jeep and on motorcycles, started chasing them. The police control room alerted all their staff already on nakabandi operation. The thieves passed Karve Road, dashed against a police vehicle on nakabandi at Warje Malwadi and reached Mumbai-Bangalore highway via Chandni Chowk. At Wakad octroi post, the police tried to block their way with the help of three trucks.

The thieves tried to steer clear of the blockade by moving along the edge. Their luck ran out when the jeep slipped on a road under construction and was stuck in a pit near old Wakad chowky. The thieves started running away but a team led by police sub inspector Jyoti Agane chased and nabbed Kadir. The other four — Safar Mane, Dada More, Ravi More and Pappu — escaped. A hunt is on.

The police have seized the jeep used by the thieves. A mobile phone and sandalwood worth Rs 50,000 were also recovered.

Heading: Festival Kicks Off - Indian Express
Content:
Anil Kamble will work non-stop from Sunday morning to Wednesday morning, then put his creations up for sale

Come Sunday and a young artist in Pune will try his hand at achieving a feat and adding a flavour to the ongoing Ganesh festival. This young man, aged 34, has set a target of creating 1,000 Ganesh idols of different types in three days without a break.

The purpose of the 72-hour task, which will begin on Sunday morning and end on Wednesday morning — to raise funds through the sale of these idols, which will be sent to the flood-affected people of Bihar. Anil S Kamble, a senior faculty member with Sumeru Academy of Digital Arts, Dhole-Patil Road, who will be carrying out this activity, is busy making preparations and collecting the necessary material.

Sumeru Academy general manager Srinivas Yerra said, "We embarked on the idea of creating 1,000 idols at one go, after watching people suffering in Bihar due to the floods. We felt that we needed to contribute in some way for them and, therefore, decided to raise money through this unique activity."

"I have set the target of making 1,000 idols of Lord Ganesh without taking my hands off work for three days. I will be using different material for creating these idols. While the main material will be chemically prepared clay, other items like stones, pieces of tiles, wood, seashells, coconuts, sand, rangoli will also be used," said Kamble.

"Not a single idol will be mould-cast and I will craft Ganesh in different forms, including the abstract. They will also be in different sizes in the range of 1 inch to 10 inches," added Kamble.

Kamble is equally adept at painting, sculptures and murals, and also has experience of creating sets for Ganesh mandals during the Ganpati celebrations for many years.

"With the target of making a thousand idols, I will have to be very brisk and make an idol with an average speed of four minutes. During this task, I will avoid sleep, as I am accustomed to working for days during special assignments. The more time I spend on creating idols, the better," the artist said.

Once the activity is over, these idols will be put for exhibition-cum-sale to raise the succour amount for the Bihar flood-affected. The exercise will be open for all to witness.

Heading: 4 held for manhandling traffic cop - Indian Express

Heading: Sugar prices to go down - Indian Express
Content:
We will now hit back with batons, say police

The Airport police have arrested four persons for allegedly manhandling a traffic police constable and then puncturing the wheels of towing van on traffic police duty near Suzuki Kothari showroom on Nagar Road on Thursday afternoon.

According to the police, the accused identified as Ramesh Adhav, Chandrakant Kadgaon, Akhil Sheikh and Nitin Balu Sheikh allegedly slapped the towing van worker Munawar Shiekh, who was lifting their two wheelers from the no-parking zone.

They allegedly manhandled police constable Bhagyawan Namdev Nikam of Yerwada traffic control branch and punctured the tyres of the towing van. The police have booked them for obstructing government work.

In another incident, Chatushrungi police arrested 21-year- old Pratikbahu Jagtap, son of a railway police officer, for allegedly engaging into a scuffle with a traffic police constable at Range Hills corner on Ganesh Khind Road around 9.30 am on Thursday. Police said that Jagtap was speeding his car in no-entry zone. Constable S K Jadhav of Chatushrungi police station stopped him and asked him to pay the fine. But Jagtap allegedly used abusive language and entered into a scuffle with the cop.

In the wake of this incident, the traffic control branch of Pune police has now decided to make a proper use of their batons issued recently for cracking down the miscreants.

"Just in last one month, 44 persons have been arrested during 12 incidents of misbehaving with the traffic police on duty. Now, that the number of such cases increasing, the traffic police would now use the batons for hitting back," said assistant commissioner of police (traffic) P A Jaffarbhai. "We have asked the traffic cops to use the batons for teaching a lesson to the miscreants. The action would be strict henceforth," he said.

"We appeal the citizens to avoid misbehaving with the traffic police. If there is any complaint, citizens should approach senior traffic police officers. We assure that proper inquiry would be conducted. If found guilty, we would take legal action against cops," he added.

Heading: IPA, IAPMO join hands to provide plumbing education - Indian Express
Content:
Sugar prices are set to go down by this month end as the millers are trying to meet the deadline set by the government to sell the buffer stock in the market.

By September 30, sugar millers across the state will have to offload a little over nine lakh tones of sugar in the market, which includes the buffer stock and the levy free stock slotted by the government for the month of September. The state millers are required to sell about10.35 lakh tones of sugar under its quota for buffer stock out of the 50 lakh tones slated for the entire country, till September end. Millers in the state have already sold around 5 lakh tones of sugar in the market. "The remaining buffer stock of around 5 lakh tones has to be sold by this month end, in addition to the levy free stock of 4.40 lakh tones meant for the month of September," said Prakash Naiknavare, managing director, Maharashtra State Co-operatives Sugar Factories Federation Limited. Naiknavare was speaking at a press conference called to dismiss speculations that the price of the Statuary Minimum Price (SMP) for sugar would be increased this year. At present, the sugar prices stand at around Rs 1,700 per tonne. "It may come down to Rs 1550 per tonne by September end," said Naiknavare. If the millers do not manage to sell the remaining buffer stock of about 5 lakh tones, then the government is eligible to confiscate it under as levy, which would be less economical as the price for levy has already been fixed at Rs 1344 per tonne, he said.

However, he added that the prices would again rise to the level of Rs 1,700 per tonne as the fundamentals are strong. Meanwhile the heads of the sugar cooperatives dismissed calls that the SMP for 2008-09 should be increased. A day before his retirement, T Haque, ex- chairman of Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices is said to have dashed off a letter to the Union Agriculture Minister Sharad Pawar that the SMP decided for this year is less. Shivaji G Patil , chairman of Indian Sugar Exim corporation Limited said that it was Haque who fixed the SMP at Rs 811.1 per tonne ( for base recovery of 9 per cent and additional Rs 90 per tonne for every rise of one percent recovery).

Heading: Darda bags Rajiv Gandhi award - Indian Express
Content:
To provide plumbing education throughout India at multiple levels, Indian Plumbing Association (IPA) have joined hands with International Association of Plumbing and Mechanical Officials (IAPMO), USA and education and training arm of IPA – Indian Institute of Plumbing (IIP).

The goal of the IPA-IAPMO plumbing education to employment program can best be met through joint ventures and collaboration with established educational institutions throughout India. The programme seeks to partner with Indian universities, colleges, and vocational institutions who can provide quality instruction that will meet the goals of the programme.

The programme serves three audience groups. Each group has a unique relationship to the uniform plumbing code -India and the national plumbing industry at large, requiring educational objectives and curriculum of varying focus. The audience groups include engineers, contractors, construction managers, supervisors, and plumbing systems installers and repairers "To speed up the process IAPMO has appointed full time director (India) Subhash Deshpande, well-known figure in the education and plumbing field," said Subhash Deshpande, director IAPMO.

Heading: Kumar Sublime gets five-star eco-housing rating - Indian Express
Content:
City-based businessman Rahul Darda has been awarded the Rajiv Gandhi Shiromani Award presented annually by the Delhi based National Integrated and Economic Council.

Darda who is the director of Bluebell Ergonomics Pvt Ltd and also Kundan Distributors city's leading pharmaceutical dealers received the award from the Haryana Governor A R Kidwai and Mizoram Governor Lt. Gen (retd) M M Lakhera in Delhi. Former Governor of Tamil Nadu and Assam Bhisma Narain Singh presided over the function.

Heading: Sonata launches Super Fibre - Indian Express
Content:
Kumar Sublime, a project by Kumar Builders at Kondhwa, received the prestigious five-star eco-housing rating certificate from Municipal Commissioner at a function held recently. Arun Nigvekar and Prashant were among those presenton the occasion.

The certification has been initiated for the first time in the city. For the 5 star eco housing rating, the minimum criteria is 800 points. This is an interim certification till the completion of the project, said a press release.

"We consider ourselves privileged to be selected for the 5 star eco-housing rating. It has always been our endeavour to be at the forefront in preserving the environment, and we leave no stone unturned to comply with the same," said Lalit Kumar Jain, CMD, Kumar Builders.

PMC engaged an expert panel from Science and Technology Park, University of Pune for monitoring, evaluating and certifying eco-housing projects in Pune. The selection for certification is based on 88 criteria – some of the criteria are site planning, environment architecture, efficient building material, energy efficient lighting, solar water heaters, water conservation and segregation of waste and other innovative technologies.

Heading: Thakur shines as Fergusson edge past Petit - Indian Express
Content:
Sonata on Friday announced the launch of Super Fibre. This new range comprises strong, stylish, youthful watches which target the large sub-Rs. 500 market in urban, semi-urban and rural India.

Designed primarily for youth in the age group of 16 to 30 years, Super Fibre watches embody style and sportiness with a rich blend of colour. Watches in this collection begin at a very affordable price of Rs. 275 and all Super Fibre watches are priced at Rs. 550 or less.

Speaking at the launch, Bhaskar Bhat, managing director, Titan Industries Limited said, "Sonata is India's largest volume brand of watches with a sale of over 5 million watches per year. These watches will appeal to young Indians across all markets, including smaller towns and villages of our country. Their superior quality, trendy designs and affordable prices make them an unbeatable combination. We are confident that with this new product thrust, Sonata is on its way towards becoming a 10 million watches per year brand in the next three years. This will also make Sonata one of the largest volume brands of watches in the world."

Sonata Super Fibre watches are made with material of superior and durable quality.

Heading: Akash Goel, Nikita Lad win carrom tournament - Indian Express
Content:
Fergusson beat JN Petit 3-1 in the tiebreaker of the inter collegiate football tournament conducted by the Zilla Parishad, held at the SSPMS grounds on Friday.

The game got off to a shaky start as both teams were unable to find their feet in the opening few minutes. The opening chance went to JN Petit when in the 7 th minute a free kick that was floated in the box found an unmarked player who failed to convert the opportunity. After that, Fergusson played some good passing football and applied pressure on the opposing goal. They came close to scoring through a free kick but the keeper saved the ball well. They were looking dangerous from the set piece position as they almost scored both the corners that they won. Then in the 18 th minute, they were rewarded with a goal through Jai Thakur. Thakur struck a hard shot from 30 yards out and beat the keeper. This turned out to be the last action of the half as the referee blew his whistle. The score was 1-0.

In the 2 nd half Fergusson were looking comfortable and were passing the ball around with relative ease. In the 22 nd minute they had a chance to extend their lead when a good cross was played in from the right wing.

However, the striker failed to convert this opportunity.

Following this JN Petit were playing some good football and even launched a few attacks on the opposition goal. Then in the 27 th minute they were awarded a penalty as the defender handled the ball in the box.

Adil Khan kept his nerve and equalized for his team. Fergusson responded well and were attacking the Petit goal with purpose. They won a couple of free kicks in dangerous positions but could not convert either. The game ended 1-1 and had to be decided by a penalty shootout.

Jai Thakur was the hero of the day for Fergusson College as he scored his penalty and made 3 crucial saves. Sudhanshu Sane and Varun Mallya scored the other two penalties for the winners and Faizan Jamadar scored for the losing team.

Heading: HRD Ministry to make one last try - Indian Express
Content:
The Vigilance Bureau (VB) a nabbed a naib tehsildar of Bholath sub-division while accepting a bribe of Rs 5,000. The VB also raided his house in Jalandhar and recovered some documents.

DSP Tarsem Singh, along with a government witness, laid a trap and caught naib tehsildar Gurdev Singh red-handed in his office today morning when complainant Charanjit Singh of Boparai village was giving him Rs 5,000 in a girdawari case.

Charanjit told the SP (Vigilance) in his complaint that the naib tehsildar was demanding Rs 10,000 for conducting girdawari of his 38 kanals, but the deal was settled at Rs 5,000.

Meanwhile, a patwari of Nawanshahr, Sarwan Kumar, was caught on the complaint of Ludhiana resident Pritam Kaur, a tiller on 27.5 acres of government land who had demanded copies of 'fard' from the accused.

She alleged that the patwari had demanded Rs 10,000 and she paid the first installment of Rs 5,000 today.

Cases against both have been registered under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

Heading: After Punjab, PUTA takes a u-turn - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab government may have backtracked on its decision to allow a central university status to Panjab University, but the Human Resource Development Ministry is not giving up.

The alma mater of Prime Minister Manmohan Singh who also taught Economics there once will get one more chance to get Central status, which will not only bring in more funds to the pre-Independence institution but also be run centrally.

Top government officials from the HRD Ministry said they would be writing soon to both the university and the Punjab government, proposing a central status for it.

"We will try once again and write to them shortly on the issue. A central status will really help the university in all ways," said a senior official.

While the HRD Ministry had earlier added a condition that the amount the Punjab government would save if the central status was accorded to PU should be re-invested in higher education, they have now withdrawn the condition. That doesn't seem to have helped, though.

While things were looking up for the university so far, the Akali government withdrew on September 1 its 'no-objection certificate' needed for the clearance and informed the PMO and the HRD Ministry about its decision. They cited objections from the 'intelligentsia' in Punjab as a reason behind the move.

With politics playing centerstage now, Vice-Chancellor R C Sobti now prefers not to comment on the issue.

Though the HRD Ministry will make one last-ditch effort to get the Punjab government on board, officials said there is little else that can be done except sending a renewed proposal.

Heading: LIC buys GLADA land near Old Courts for Rs 228 crore - Indian Express
Content:
After the state government withdrew its consent to support Panjab University's bid for central varsity status, now it seems to be the turn of the Panjab University Teachers' Association (PUTA) to perform a volte-face.

PUTA president, Ronki Ram, told Newsline: "All we want are funds for the university; we have no issues whether PU is awarded central status or not. We are completely in favour of a united Punjab."

This is a complete flip from PUTA's earlier stand of demanding central status for the varsity. In fact, PUTA was to observe Teachers' Day as a black day in protest against the government's decision today but the plan was shelved at the last minute.

Vice-Chancellor Professor R C Sobti had presented similar views during a Senate meeting in March where he said PU would welcome complete central funding. He was, however, opposed by a section of senators who had supported the demand for central varsity status.

But there are some who are still firm on the demand. Former PUTA general secretary Professor Manjit Singh said: "We were and shall always be for the central varsity status for PU. But now, if PUTA has decided that it is content with just central funds, it is their decision. I would not like to comment on that."

Heading: Ex-tehsildar booked in Vigilance case - Indian Express
Content:
Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) bought 3.6 acres of commercial land in the Old Courts area, near Lakkar Bridge, for Rs 228 crore at an auction held by the Greater Ludhiana Area Development Authority (GLADA) today. GLADA registered an increase of 31 per cent as against the reserve price of Rs 1 lakh per square yard, the bid went upto Rs 1.31 lakh.

Another 11,000 square yards, located on the road opposite the old courts, was sold at Rs 1.46 lakh per square yard as against the reserve price of Rs 75,000.

Six bidders participated in the auction including Aerens R Enterprises, Chadha Group of Companies, Malhotra Land Developers and Delhi-based Best Real Estate Company. GLADA Additional Commissioner Administrator S R Kler and Estate Officer Jeet Ram were also present at the auction.

"GLADA expected more returns from the sale, but the bidders were not much interested in the sites as they are located very close to the under-construction Lakkar bridge," said a source.

The Tehbazari Branch of the Municipal Corporation, meanwhile, took the opportunity to conduct an anti-encroachment drive today. As the auction went on, rehris and stalls near the sites were removed. But MC authorities claimed that the drive was part of a routine exercise.

Heading: Amarinder seeks court’s permission to go abroad - Indian Express
Content:
A case of disproportionate assets was registered against a former tehsildar by the Vigilance Bureau (VB) on Thursday.

Gursewak Singh, who was appointed as a tehsildar in the city about one-and-a-half years ago, is currently posted at Phillaur. Deputy Superintendent of Police (Vigilance Bureau) Gurcharan Singh said the FIR was registered after a detailed inquiry and the investigations were on.

Vigilance Bureau sources said Singh owns properties at Mohali and Malout, which are disproportionate to his known sources of income. "An inquiry was ordered against the tehsildar after some complaints were received against him. Singh was questioned as well but the officers were not satisfied with his answers. A detailed report of the inquiry was sent to senior Vigilance Bureau officers at Chandigarh after which an FIR was registered agains

Heading: ‘My father-in-law said if I sat at home, it would be a waste’ - Indian Express
Content:
Former Chief Minister Captain Amarinder Singh filed an application on Friday seeking the court's permission to go abroad. The former CM is facing trial in the infamous City Centre case at the Ludhiana court.

District and Sessions judge G K Rai fixed September 6 as the next date of hearing and directed the prosecution to file a reply on the said application.

Singh's counsel T S Sood said the former CM wanted to visit England for three weeks from September 10 as he has been invited by the Umeed Foundation as chief guest for a function scheduled for September 24. Also, Singh wants to meet the publisher of his forthcoming book —The Last Sunset — Lan Boltomley, while in the country.

The application also states that the former CM suffered a bout of low blood pressure on August 26 in Amritsar. "The team of cardiologists which examined him recommended that he consult his personal physician and cardiologist in England. Captain Amarinder Singh has sought an appointment with Dr David P Lipkin of Wellington Hospital, London, and Dr Sisar of Harley Street London," states the plea.

Heading: City schools celebrate Teachers Day with fervour - Indian Express
Content:
She is neither a teacher by chance, nor by choice. It is destiny that brought Paramjit Kaur to this profession in 1986. Twenty two years later, the principal of BCM Arya Model Senior Secondary Shastri Nagar was conferred with the prestigious 'CBSE Award-2007' by Union Minister of State, Human Resource Department, Mohammad Ali Ashraf.

"There are two kinds of people — one who grow with the institution and the other with whom the institution grows. In my case, I grew up with the school and the school grew up with me. I owe my achievement to the school and my family members who always inspired me," says Paramjit.

A graduate from Fergusson College, Pune, Paramjit wanted to be a doctor. "I could not clear PMT, but had cleared the test for Bachelor of Dental Surgery (BDS). But my father, who was in the Indian Army, did not send me for BDS," she recalls.

One of her teachers at the college had told her once that "if you are a star you can be a star in any field". The words made her realise her real potential and she passed MSc in chemistry with gold medal and then cleared her MEd.

She started her career as a science teacher in a Chandigarh school, but left the job after marrying into a Ludhiana family. It was her father-in-law, Captain Niranjan Singh (retd), who motivated her to get back to her professional life. "He had said if he made me sit at home, it would be a national wastage. His words inspired me and I joined the BCM School as a teacher in 1989," says Paramjit. She became the vice-principal exactly ten years later.

The new millennium came with another promotion and she assumed the office of principal on January 1, 2000. "There has been no looking back since then," she says.

Paramjit has a multifaceted approach to learning and has maintained high academic standards of the school that has 5,500 students. Two of her projects brought laurels for herself and also for the school. Her 'open basic education' project is for the dropouts from schools affiliated to the National Institute of Open Schools. The second one is about making villagers aware about clean drinking water. The project won her appreciation from former President Dr A P J Abdul Kalam.

A mother of two sons, Paramjit believes in not leaving anything for tomorrow. "Despite my busy schedule, I teach chemistry, my favourite subject, to senior classes and always go well prepared with my lecture. This is what I tell my teachers."

Students and teachers like to share their problems with her and so does Paramjit, who goes through all the slips on her table before she leaves for the day.A versatile personality, Paramjit is an avid reader, writes poems, makes paintings and is equally good with handicrafts. "The bright future of my school" is all she always prays and works for.

Heading: MBA students’ concerns addressed: PAU - Indian Express
Content:
Different city schools today celebrated Teachers Day with enthusiasm. At Ram Lal Bhasin Public School, the students decorated their classrooms with flowers, bells, festoons and balloons and recited poems, delivered speeches to mark the day. The students also presented an amazing dance performance and entertained everyone present at the celebrations. The school management also honoured the teachers on the occasion. The director of the school, S Verma inspired the teachers to think positive while the headmistress Tarannum Fatma asked them to be the role models in the lives of the students.

Drishti Dr. RC Jain Innovative Public School, Pakhowal Road, Narangwal, celebrated Teachers Day in a unique manner as the management management presented the teachers with inspiring books. The students wished them all the happiness and also prayed that the teachers should always be there to guide them. The teachers were flooded with good wishes, flowers and cards on the occasion. The Principal exhorted the teachers to come up to the expectations of the profession. Dr. Radhakrishanan's contribution to education and philosophy was highlighted at the function.

BCM Senior Secondary School, Chandigarh Road, celebrated the day with fervour as Satyanand Munjal presided over the function. He delivered an inspirational speech to motivate students as well as teachers. The students presented different games, songs and dance performances on the occasion. Principal D P Guleria appreciated the efforts of students while SK Mehta, Manager of the school, encouraged the teachers to do their best. The teachers were honoured with gifts on this occasion.

At Green Land Convent School, Haibowal, the students presented a cultural programme for their teachers. While Rajesh Rudhra, chairman of the school, stressed the role of teacher at the function. Principal Jyoti Pujara said that the students must respect their teachers.

Sat Paul Mittal School held a function to mark the day which started with a poem based on the teachers' day. Lt Col DB Sharma addressed the audience with thought-provoking speech and highlighted the importance of the day. Students presented rock dance, skit among other activities on the occasion while the school teachers collectively sang a song to mark the day.

Tagore Public School celebrated the Teachers' Day with zeal. All the members of the school management along with Amrita Gakhar, principal of the school, congratulated the winners and motivated them to work hard. The students of class XII took reins of the school in their hands as they took place of the teachers. A cultural programme was also presented by the students. Govind Ram Bansal, school President awarded gifts to the teachers.

Everest Model High School, Giaspura celebrated the day with enthusiasm as SK Sharma, the manager of the Everest educational Society honoured the school teachers. Dheeraj Sharma, principal of the school, spoke on the works and contribution of Dr Radhakrishnan on the occasion.

Students presented cultural programme on the occasion. Rajiv Nagalia, school principal, emphasised the tremendous efforts of teachers. About fifty meritorious students were honoured on the occasion.

Teachers Day was celebrated at New Senior Secondary School Civil Lines with great enthusiasm. Sunil Maria, school president, congratulated the school staff and principal. DR S Radhakrishnan was also remembered. A magic show was arranged for the recreation of students. Monica Sharma, the school principal, gave away prizes to the best performers.

Students of GRD Academy organsied a cultural programme to express their feelings towards the teachers to mark the teachers' day. They presented dance and song items. Aneeta Kundra the school principal along with teachers and students cut the cake on the occasion.

Students and teachers of Sanatan Vidya Mandir Sen Sec School, Deep Nagar here the students of senior classes acted as Mock teachers and handles the school activities for the day. the administrative work was also handled by the students. Sadhana Shram the principal of the school awarded the best mock teachers. Rajesh kashyap president, C L Sachdeva the school manager were also present on this occasion and congratulated the teachers.

Heading: Teachers pay tributes to Dr Radhakrishnan - Indian Express
Content:
The issue of the management students of Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), who were protesting against hike in number of seats in agri business was resolved after Dr Tejwant Singh, Dean, College of Basic Sciences and Humanities, assured the protesting students that their interests would not be compromised with.

Dr Tejwant Singh remarked, "Because of the lack of information, students had apprehensions but as the matter has been discussed, we have been able to convince them."

He added, "Interests of the students are foremost for us and the said decisions can in no way affect the students' prospects." The prime reason for the students' protest was the fact that the university had decided to add five more seats to the Agri-business Management course. And the students had apprehended that this would harm their placement prospects.

Another issue raised by the students was about changing one of the formalities regarding submission of synopsis into a project report. The Dean clarified, "We are already on to the process and as soon as the Dean, Post-graduate Studies, joins back, matter would be taken up."

"The students were convinced and they have suspended their protest," added Dr Tejwant Singh. So while the matter was resolved in the afternoon, the Department of Business Management staged a dharna outside the Thapar Hall, the main administrative centre of the university, in the morning.

The students shouted slogans and sat in front of the hall as a mark of protest. However no other student from the remaining three colleges of the university joined the protesting students. "We do not want a strike. The idea is just to get our voice heard," said a student on the condition of anonymity, countering that word, 'strike' is too harsh for what they are doing.

The students had started protest on Thursday demanding that five extra seats that were to be added in Agri-business management course should be withheld. The students claimed that it would have an impact on their placements.

"We have 15 seats already and five more would add to the in-house competition," feared a student.

Heading: Christians take out march to protest Orissa incidents - Indian Express
Content:
Students and teachers of Partap College of Education, Hambran Road, Ludhiana, celebrated the Teachers' Day as a mark of tribute to the contribution made by teachers to the society. Students presented bouquet and greetings to the teachers as a mark of appreciation for their dedication and sincere efforts. They also presented a colourful programme on on the occasion.

Dr Balwant Singh, principal of the college, in his address said that September 5 was the birthday of a great teacher Dr Sarvapalli Radhakrishnan, former President of India, who was a staunch believer of education, and was a well-known diplomat and scholar.

He also spoke about the role of teacher in one's life, and also about the changing values. He condemned the discrimination being done against the teachers. He added that apart from the fun aspect of the day, it was also a day when one could look back, admire and get inspired by Dr Radhakrishnan, a small town boy, who grew up to become one of the most respected politicians of India.

Heading: Teachers should instill moral values in students: Dr Johl - Indian Express
Content:
Protesting gainst the on-going attacks on the fellow Christians in Orissa, the churches of the Ludhiana district today organised a rally and peace march at Sarabha Nagar's holy Cross Church.

The rally began with a special service praying for fast establishment of peace, so that the people could return to their homes and could be rehabilitated. Hundreds of protestors marched silently to draw attention to the distressing developments and express their solidarity and sympathy with the brethren in Orissa who were "facing atrocities of all kinds."

The march passed through many important city points and handed over a memorandum to the Deputy Commissioner of Ludhiana for forwarding it to President and the Prime Minister. In the memorandum, they urged the Central Government to expedite measures to restore normalcy.

Heading: Meanwhile, computer teachers observe Black Day - Indian Express
Content:
"Teaching is not merely a job but an on-going process. Like kindling a lamp, a good teacher ignites the minds of his students to unveil their hidden talents". These thoughts were shared by Dr S.S. Johl, an eminent agricultural economist and former Vice-Chancellor of Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana and Punjabi University, Patiala. He was giving a special lecture on 'Role of a model teacher' to PAU faculty at a special function to celebrate the Teacher's Day today. The function was organised in the Pal Auditorium of the University by Punjab Agricultural University Teachers Association (PAUTA).

Elaborating upon the qualities in a good teacher, Dr Johl said that besides teaching his subject, a good teacher must devote some time in the classroom to instill moral values in his students. "Since the students of today are the leaders of tomorrow, they are the building blocks of good society. We can not create a good society if we fail to produce good human beings", he remarked. "Give your students love, affection, watch their activities and feel concerned for your students", advised Dr Johl.

On this occasion, 40 teachers, who retired from the university during the last one year were also felicitated.

Presiding over the function, Dr N.S. Malhi, Director of Extension Education, said a teacher should be like a ladder on which a student could step on to rise in life. Describing teaching as the noblest profession, Dr Malhi remarked that a teacher may not earn enough money but he earns a respect, which one cannot buy with all the money. Teacher's Day should be a day of self-introspection, he added.

Earlier, PAUTA president Dr. M.S.Mahal welcomed the guest and teachers.

Heading: Woman held with fake currency - Indian Express
Content:
In protest of their pending demands the Computer Teachers today observed black day. They came dressed in black colour dresses and did not participate in teacher day celebrations. The teachers demand included regularization and release of salaries on time etc

However the teachers of all government aided private schools also did not celebrate the day. All these teachers today went to Chandigarh to participate in the protest rally. And the schools remained closed today.

Heading: SIFT gets a leg up - Indian Express
Content:
Acting on a tip-off, the customs staff posted at Attari railway station, Amritsar, seized fake Indian currency amounting to Rs 10 lakhs from a lady passenger Pakeeja Khatun, coming from Pakistan in Samjhauta Express.

According to a press release issued by A.K Mehra, Commissioner of Customs, the woman was having Indian passport and had gone to Pakistan on a short visit. The fake currency consisting of five hundred rupees notes was concealed in cavities made in rubber chappals.

The custom's intelligence wing had said that the fake currency was being smuggled into India by some unscrupulous elements from Pakistan and passengers of bus and train were being used for the purpose, added Mehra. The preliminary investigation revealed that the lady was acting as a carrier.

Efforts are being made to trace other persons behind this racket and follow up action has been taken at Delhi and other places. The woman has been been arrested.

Heading: Residents rue inflated water bills - Indian Express
Content:
Sportking Institute of Technology has been recognised by EET Connection, a Geneva-based company, seeking to develop educational and cultural cooperation between Switzerland and India.

The company is organising a contest between Swiss and Indian fashion schools in the context of the 60th anniversary of the Swiss-Indian Friendship treaty. The contest has been designed to stimulate mobility and intensify students and teachers exchanges in the field of fashion.

"It is a platform for us to explore numerous professional and economic opportunities in artistic and cultural fields, both for India and Switzerland. Not only will it help in building lasting links of friendship and solidarity between the two nations but also increase public awareness of more responsible consumer choices," commented Sunil Puri, Executive Director, SIFT.

Heading: Simrat, Gambhir put Chandigarh in driver’s seat - Indian Express
Content:
Residents of MIG Colony, Phase-2 Urban Estate, Dugri, have expressed resentment that Municipal Corporation has wrongly issued exorbitant water bills ranging between Rs 12,000-14,000 to each resident of the colony.

According to the residents, their flats had been built on area less than 100 square yard while government has waived off water and sewer bills for houses having an area of 125 square yard and less than that.

Kuldeep Singh Kreer, general secretary of the society, said, "We have already moved the High Court because MC is issuing us bills since long and every time we are giving this plea which is not being accepted. Now again they have sent fresh bills along with arrears which is not justified."

"Moreover when the case is in court, no bills can be issued to us. So the MC should take these bills back," he said.

Heading: St Stephen’s show Himachal who is boss - Indian Express
Content:
After Chandigarh struggled against Zone A in its last match, formidable Chandigarh came back strongly against Jalandhar today, and cleaned up them for paltry 96 runs in 45.5 overs in the match held at Sector 16 Stadium on Saturday.

Batting first, Jalandhar was skittled out for 96 in 45.5 overs. It was Chandigarh off-spinner Gaurav Gambhir who scalped 3 wickets for 27 runs and helped his team clean up Jalandhar. India U-19 opener Taruwar Kohli again faltered as he could not open his account. Surinder Sharma scored 29 runs for Jalandhar. In reply, Chandigarh came good with the bat were 203 for 3 at the end of the day.

Openers Sarul Kanwar and skipper Vishwas Bhalla were involved in opening partnership of 69 runs of 12.5 overs. Batting two down, southpaw Smirat Bawa slaughtered the bowlers scoring blistering half-century. He is unbeaten on 62 runs along with Uday Kaul who is batting at Uday Kaul 31 not out.

In the second match played at PCA Stadium, Mohali packed Zone A for 84 in 36 overs. Medium-pacer Varun Khanna (4 for 17) and left-arm spinner Harmeet Singh (4 for 28) destroyed Zone A's batting line-up.

Batting second, Mohali scored 210 for 4 in 51 overs before they applied the closure to their innings. Opener Ishan Dogra was in a devastating mood as he plundered an unbeaten 133 runs of 154 balls. He sent all the bowlers on a leather hunt and hit 14 sizzling fours and 4 towering sixes. He was associated in an unbroken fourth wicket stand of 91 runs with Yuvraj Singh 30 not out. Left-arm spinner Bhagwan Singh took 2 for 65 for Zone-A. Zone A were 7 for one in their second innings at the end of the day's play and were trailing by 119 runs with 9 wickets in hand.

In the fourth match played at Ludhiana between Ludhiana and Zone-B, Ludhiana won the toss and elected to bat first scoring 214 runs in 93.1 overs. In reply, Zone B were 36 for 4 in 13 overs at the end of the day's play.

Brief Scores:

Jalandhar: 96 all out in 45.5 overs (Surinder Sharma 29, Gaurav Gambhir 3 for 27, Gurinder 3 for 16)

Chandigarh: 203 for 3 in 47 overs (Simrat Bawa 62 not out, Vishwas Bhalla 51, Sarul Kanwar 46, Uday Kaul 31 not out, Rahul Kumar 2 for 34)

Zone A: 84 for all in 36 overs (Pradeep Kumar 21, Varun Khanna 4 for 17, Harmeet Singh 4 for 28)

Mohali: 210 for 4 declared in 51 overs (Ishan Dogra 133 not out, Yuvraj Singh 30 not out Bhagwan Singh 2 for 65)

Ludhiana: 214 all out in 93.1 overs (Tarun Passi 40, Ankur Kakkar 32, Varun Chitkara 30, Arjun Kumar 3 for 44, Jatinder Singh 2 for 20)

Zone B: 36 for 4 in 13 overs

Patiala: 210 for all in 76.1 overs (Tanmeet Bawa 56, Kunwar Raina 45, Amitoj 24

Charanjeet 4 for 42, Sumit Sharma 3 for 51, Manish Bhatia 2 for 22

Amritsar: 51 for 1 in 16 overs (Manish Bhatia 34 not out, Sumit Sharma 15 not out Rajwinder Singh 1 for 12)

Heading: Written exams for panel umpires held - Indian Express
Content:
Himachal Pradesh Football Association players were reduced to mere visitors by the St Stephen's Football Academy unless a 82nd minute by Rajan Kapur saw them made a fight-back but it came too late as they were beaten by 10-1 by the St Stephen side who secured a semi-final berth in the ongoing Administrator's Cup.

Himachal made a disastrous start as they conceded a penalty in the third minute itself for bringing down Umakanta in the danger area. Showing no signs of nervousness, Johny Chand Singh put the ball past the Himachal goal keeper. St Stephen were on target again when Samandram Lanba made a solo effort from the centre-half and slammed a low shot into the right side of the goal. Johny's purple patch in front of the goal continued when he put a piercing cross from Umakanta into the net. The terrific due of Johny and Samandram rattled the Himachal defence and slammed goals after goal, leaving the opposition team thoughtless. However, Himachal's defence was less erratic in the second half and the forwards also had few shots at the goal, one of which resulted in a consolation goal for them.

Earlier, in the morning, Mohun Bagan began their campaign with a 13-0 win over Bihar Football Association. Chandigarh Football Association won their fourth straight game and entered into the last four following a 6-1 win over Rohit Football Academy, Orissa. Indian Football Association also ensured a semi-final berth by drubbing Chhattisgarh Football Association by a record 17-0 margin. Madhya Pradesh blanked Bihar Football Association by 6-0.

Heading: Accident claims life of 25-yr-old - Indian Express
Content:
A panel of umpire examiners, headed by S Venkatraghavan, former test umpire, conducted the BCCI Panel Umpires written examination at PCA Stadium on Friday. The other panellists were S K Bansal (North Zone), Subrata Banerjee (East Zone), V K. Ramaswamy (South Zone), B A. Jamula (West Zone), Narendra Menon (Central Zone). As many as 33 first class cricketers and 80 non-cricketers took the written examination. The result of the written examination is expected on September 6 and the candidates who pass the examination will appear for viva on September 13 and 14 at Bangalore. According to Sushil Kapoor, spoke person of PCA, 15 successful candidates will be recommended for BCCI panel umpires.

Sumeet bowls Shivalik School to victory
CHANDIGARH: A fine bowling performance by Sumeet Kumar (5 for 29) and a brilliant knock by Aditya Kumar (49 runs) powered Shivalik Public School, Sector 41 towards an emphatic 75 run win over DC Model School, Panchkula in the inaugural Molly Carver Champions League Cricket Tournament being organised by Chandigarh Cricket Association, at Government Senior Secondary School, Sector 19 on Friday.

Batting first, Shivalik Public School made 134 runs in 23 overs. Aditya and Karan were the main scorers with knocks of 49 and 37 runs respectively while Saurav and Milan bagged three wickets each for DC School.

In reply, DC Model were bowled out for 59 runs in 13 overs. Rizul top scored with 17 runs.

Saint Soldier register double victories
CHANDIGARH: Saint Soldier International School registered victories in both boys' and girls' CBSE Cluster Thirteenth Kho-Kho Championship held at St Soldier School, Sector 28 on Friday.

Saint Soldier girls' defeated VR Senior Secondary School, Baddi by seven points (12-5) while the boys' team got the better of MIA DAV Mehatpur, Himachal Pradesh by two points (10-8).

Heading: Govt to seek extension of industrial package - Indian Express
Content: A rashly driven vehicle claimed a life in Chandigarh in the early hours of Friday. While the deceased is yet to be identified, police said they were trying to trace the driver who managed to flee after the accident that occurred around 12.15 am near Industrial Area, Phase-I. According to an eyewitness, the man, aged around 25 years, was crossing the road when he was hit from behind. The police said a police control room vehicle rushed him to the GMCH-32, where he was declared dead on arrival.  "We found the body lying on one side of the road. The man must have died on the spot as he had sustained severe head injuries," said a police officer. A case on charges of rash and negligent driving has been registered.

Heading: UT fails to honour its teachers on their day - Indian Express
Content:
The BJP government has stepped up its effort to seek extension of the industrial package duration up to 2013, as was originally planned.

At Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal's initiative, the state Assembly today adopted a resolution, making a strong demand to the Centre to resist pressure by bigger states and grant fresh extension to the current tax holiday for new industries in Himachal Pradesh.

Ironically, when the resolution was tabled in the House, the opposition Congress had already walked out of the Assembly after its protest on the PTA issue.

Dhumal was earlier instrumental in getting the package sanctioned from former prime minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee in 2003, a few months before the BJP lost power in the Assembly elections. The package, proposing three-tier tax concessions, was originally proposed for 2013, but was later reduced till 2007 by the UPA government. Later, pressure from the state helped in increasing the limit till 2010.

Moving the resolution in the House, Dhumal asserted that the government has created sufficient infrastructure, has ensured additional power availability and taken measures to improve roads. More than Rs 3,360 crore investment has already been received and a large number of industrial projects have been cleared at different stages, he said.

He, however, expressed concern over "propaganda being unleashed by adjoining states" about industrial units shifting to Himachal. "The fact remains that most of the industrial units that came to Himachal are being set up by investors from Karnataka, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and other states. Not even a single industrial unit has shifted here from Punjab, Haryana or other neighbouring states," he said.

Dhumal said the government would ultimately seek extension of the package till 2020 once the Centre agrees for restoring the original plan.

During question hour, the government informed the House that serious violations have been detected in the allotment of industrial plots during the earlier Congress government.

An inquiry conducted recently has confirmed irregularities and action would be taken in the cases where violation were committed, it was stated.

Earlier, the House passed two Bills, one among them relating to regulation of admissions and fixation of fee structure for private technical and vocational educational institutions.

The Chief Minister also announced a hike in the monthly remuneration for widows and family members of soldiers of World War-II.

Heading: New cath lab inaugurated in Fortis - Indian Express
Content:
Setia says he was 'too busy' to shortlist names for the state award, 'function not before September 15'

While teachers all over the country were honoured on Friday for their contribution in the field of education, the UT Education department is yet to draw the list of teachers who were to be conferred with the state award on their day. Reason: Director Public Instructions (Schools) S K Setia was "too busy to shortlist the names".

On September 2, the UT Administration had issued a statement, saying it would honour eight teachers with state awards and another eight with commendation certificates at a state-level function. Setia had said he would finalise the names by the next day.

While the Teachers' Day is over, the Education department now says it can hold

the function only after

September 15.

The delay in shortlisting the names has not gone down well with the teachers' fraternity.

Pleading anonymity, the principal of a school said: "It has happened for the first time that the department has failed to honour teachers on their day. He (Setia) seems to be the busiest DPI the department has ever had. He has ignored the very people who form the core of his department."

The teachers alleged that Setia was trying to start his own tradition of advancing and postponing things. "The DPI is in the habit of doing things at his own pace. If Setia does not understand the importance of the award and the day, he might as well just not honour any of us. This is sheer mockery of the teaching fraternity," says a teacher who did not want to be named.

Talking to Newsline, Setia said he was "tied up" with meetings of the Planning Commission. "I am yet to go through the files that are lying in my office. I have not got time to shortlist the teachers as these meetings are taking most of my time. I will try to finalise the names for the awards by Sunday," he clarified. He said the department would hold the function only after September 15, "after I am through with my meetings".

Heading: Illegal PTA teachers to go: Dhumal - Indian Express
Content:
Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president and Member of Parliament from Faridkot, Sukhbir Badal, inaugurated a new state-of-the-art cath lab at Fortis Hospital in Mohali on Friday.

The MP exhorted the hospital authorities to set up more hospitals in Punjab. "Healthcare is a priority area for the state and the government is more than willing to facilitate the setting up of such advanced hospitals," said Badal.

Executive Director (Cardiac Surgery), Fortis Hospital, Dr T S Mahant said: "The cath lab, which has been imported from Germany, has a number of features that will benefit both the surgeon and the patient.

As it boasts of a very efficient cooling system, a large number of surgeries can be conducted continuously. It will allow surgeons to conduct procedures on obese patients with ease as well."

Speaking on the occasion, Shivinder Mohan Singh, CEO and Managing Director of Fortis Healthcare Limited, said: "Our mission is to create a world-class integrated healthcare delivery system, entailing the finest medical skills combined with compassionate patient care."

Use of a cath lab
Cardiac catheterisation is a procedure which allows the surgeon to reach the heart vessels through a small incision, either through the groin, wrist, elbow or neck. In this minimally invasive surgery, a catheter (tube) is inserted through the incision and once in place, it can be used to perform a number of procedures including angioplasty, angiography and balloon septostomy. The surgeon can also 'look' into the heart and the surrounding blood vessels.

Heading: ‘Environmental factors have deep links with acute, chronic diseases’ - Indian Express
Content:
Even as Congress leaders today went all out to support the movement of PTA teachers, Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal today said all illegal appointments will be cancelled.

Commenting on the agitation, Dhumal said the PTA teachers are not government employees. Moreover, inquiries by the government have revealed that a lot of them don't meet basic eligibility criteria such as educational qualifications and were "close relatives of Congress leaders".

"The government is all set to decide the fate of all those who were appointed illegally and also by transferring regular teachers. We will recruit regular teachers through Subordinate Services Selection Board and Public Service Commission on merit and those who don't meet eligibility criteria or have been wrongly appointed will lose their jobs," he announced.

Over 10,000 PTA teachers were appointed by the Congress government and a high-level inquiry has detected serious violations in the appointments.

Heading: Punwire scam: Retired IAS officer booked after 15 years - Indian Express
Content:
An Indo-US joint workshop, the first of its kind, on the environmental risks of the respiratory diseases started here on Friday. The workshop is focussing on preparing a list of recommendations to be followed in the two countries to combat environment-related health hazards.

Nearly 20 experts from top institutes of the USA, including the National Institute of Health (NIH), are participating in the workshop being organised by the Department of Pulmonary Medicine at PGI.

Talking to Newsline, Head of Department Prof S K Jindal said it has been globally recognised that environmental factors, especially those at the living and the workplace, have important links with infectious as well as non-infectious diseases of both acute and chronic nature.

"The who estimates that 24 per cent of global disease burden and 23 per cent of all deaths can be attributed to environmental factors. The burden is more on the developing than the developed countries."

He said: "In developing countries, an estimated 42 per cent of acute lower respiratory infections are caused by environmental factors."

The experts delved on the effects of climate change on human health. "Global warming as well as the increase in ground-level ozone, airborne allergens and other pollutants, have adverse effects on the respiratory health," summarised Jindal at the end of the first day's session.

The experts highlighted that both the indoor and the outdoor pollution have adverse effects on the health of the people.

The major burden of these hazards is borne by the lungs. Bronchial asthma and other allergies; chronic obstructive lung disease, respiratory infections including tuberculosis and occupational lung diseases are some of the common problems with a strong environmental risk which, account for a large disease burden all over the world, including in India.

"There is a need for extensive studies to gauge the effects of environmental factors on the human health."

He added: "The workshop should see a number of research project on the issue being discussed so that the concentrated research work can be carried out in the area," added Dr Jindal.

Heading: Anuradha murder: Charges framed against husband, two others - Indian Express
Content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation's Delhi based Anti-Corruption Branch today booked a retired senior IAS officer of the Punjab government, Arvind Mahajan, on charges of cheating and under the provisions of Prevention of Corruption Act, in the ongoing investigation of the multi-crore Punjab Wireless Limited (Punwire) scam.

Following the registration of FIR against Mahajan after almost 15 years, a CBI team today raided Mahajan's residence in Sector 10, in Panchkula. Sources, however, say he is out of India at present. He was booked on charges of allegedly siphoning off money belonging to various Punjab State Boards and Corporations in favour of Punwire and also in favour of a relative. While the CBI is investigating the matter, the officials claimed to have seized some vital documents from his residence.

Mahajan, who was posted as Deputy Director (Investment Cell), Ministry of Finance, Punjab, in early 90s had allegedly siphoned off around Rs 30 lakh, in violation of the rules. The CBI was probing into the multi-crore Punwire scam since the last 8 years. In 2002, it had filed chargesheets in the 24 FIRs registered in connection with the scam.

A profit-making company for over 20 years since its establishment in 1975, the company with its expertise in wireless communication technology had shot into limelight for the establishment of the prestigious communication link between Dakshin Gangotri (Antarctica) and New Delhi. The operations of the company came to a grinding halt in 1999, following the unearthing of the scam. The company was locked for liquidation in July 2000, and the final winding up orders was passed in February 2001 by the Punjab and Haryana High Court.

Heading: GMCH-32 to hold seminar on PNDT Act, female foeticide - Indian Express
Content:
A local court today framed charges of murder, criminal conspiracy and furtherance of common intention against Baljinder, Vijay Pal Singh alias Nikku and Ashok on charges of murdering Anuradha, wife of Baljinder.

The charges have been framed under Sections 302, 407, 397, 34 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code (IPC).

Anuradha's body was found with her throat slit in her bedroom on the first floor of the duplex house in Sector 38 in May. The trio had also allegedly killed Nikku, a co-accused, to impress upon the police that it was Nikku, the domestic help of the house, who had been murdered. They also had tried to mislead the police by giving bribery as motive behind the murder.

Anuradha Sandhu (35), a boutique owner, was the wife of Baljinder Singh, a leading property dealer in Mohali. A case against the three was registered by the Chandigarh police in May this year.

It was, however, later discovered that Baljinder had conspired with Nikku to eliminate Anuradha.

Her sister Rekha had later told the court that Baljinder was financially weak and was being supported by Anuradha's brother.

"After the marriage, Baljinder went to America where he did some business. He was a womaniser and would beat up my sister in front of their children," Rekha had deposed before the court.

Heading: ‘Numerous cities have developed without compromising on their heritage’ - Indian Express
Content: The Government Medical College and Hospital (GMCH) in Sector 32 is organising a seminar on the Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PNDT) Act. More than 150 delegates from different parts of the country are expected to participate in the seminar, being jointly organised by the Department of Radio Diagnosing and Imaging, GMCH, and the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. Dr Suman Kochhar, head of department, said the seminar would focus on the success and failure of the Act, especially in Punjab, Haryana, Himachal and Chandigarh, which record the country's worst sex ratio.

Heading: Last day of PGI workshop focuses on hernia - Indian Express
Content:
"The creation of Le Corbusier and the vision of Jawaharlal Nehru, Chandigarh, is slowly heading towards its ruin. It is paradoxical that the Administration which reveres Corbusier, is hell bent upon destroying his creation," said M N Sharma, the first Indian chief architect of the city. He said that the policies of the Administration are proving detrimental towards the growth of the city.

Talking to Newsline, Sharma said that though the Masterplan is unique in its concept, efforts are being made to tamper with it. "The Capitol Complex is not complete. The fourth building, the Museum of Knowledge, has not been constructed till yet. The changes made in the interiors of the Assembly building have hampered the structure. No one cares about the landscaping of the area."

He added: "The Sukhna Lake was supposed to be a quiet place and meant for meditation. It has, however, turned into a mela ground with swings, restaurants, a dummy wind mill and various such proposals that the Administration comes up with, without sparing a thought. Although no houses were supposed to come near the lake, the proposal was violated."

The IT Park is being expanded to the second and third phase without the completion of the first phase. The Chandigarh Housing Board (CHB) has turned into a private developer. While it was supposed to look after the housing needs of all income groups, it now caters to the needs of only the high income groups.

Malls are being constructed in the Industrial Area, which leads to a chaos-like situation, owing to lack of parking space. The increase in floor area ratio will further compound the problem.

Expressing his fears on the way new projects are being developed across the city, Sharma says there is a need to review the same.

"There are numerous cities around the world which have moved along the path of development without compromising on their heritage. We need to follow the same in Chandigarh. There is an urgent need to check the land mafia. The city needs a regulatory body to advice the Administration on the various issues," he says.

Heading: Now, lodge your FIR at special counters - Indian Express
Content:
New processes of surgical techniques in urogynaecology were discussed on the second day of the international live operative workshop being organised by the Department of Urology at the PGI today. The two-day workshop concluded at the institute with sessions focusing on problems including operative techniques in hernia.

Dr Rakesh Kapoor from Lucknow, demonstrated that a simple hernia mesh meant for hernia repair can be fashioned to the need for pelvic floor repair and thus, the indigenously designed mesh will cut the cost factor of the treatment of pelvic organ prolapse.

Dr Linda Cardozo from UK and Dr Pranathy Reddy from Hyderabad demonstrated other methods for the treatment of prolapse.

Earlier in the day, the sessions by experts from various institutes across the country highlighted that monofilament or polypropylene mesh adds to the strength of pelvic floor, to prevent recurrence of big prolapse.

During the workshop, the contemporary techniques of repair, both natural tissue as well as polypropylene mesh, were discussed.

"Monofilament mesh application and proper anchorage to the pelvic wall adds to the strength of the pelvic support and hence the recurrence of the organ prolapse can be minimised, especially in larger prolapse," emphasised the doctors at the end of the session.

Dr Ajay Rane said the addition of this technique has an inherent problem of erosion, which may occur in upto 12 per cent of cases.

Heading: PTA issue: Cong makes a big noise - Indian Express
Content:
The Kapurthala Police have opened specials counters for hassle-free registration of FIRs.

Counters have been opened at CPRC centres of Kapurthala and Phagwara and at the offices of Phagwara DSP and Kapurthala SSP.

Kapurthala SSP Rakesh Agrawal said residents can come to a counter and just fill in a form to get the FIR lodged. Copy of the FIR would be made available within 24 hours. FIRs can also be sent through email to sspkapurthala@yahoo.com.

Proof of identity of the complainant would be taken at the time of registration of FIR to avoid impersonation. He said to prevent this scheme from being misused, SHOs have been issued instructions, including not to arrest a person against whom FIR has been registered without collecting evidences.

Besides, written permission of SSP would be necessary for an arrest. And, in case the FIR is found to be fake, proceeding under Section 182 of the IPC would be initiated against the complainant.

Courts have also been requested to readily accept the cancellation reports of FIRs submitted by the police.

Heading: Court notice to CBI on Ravinder’s plea - Indian Express
Content:
Assembly witnesses noisy scenes, sloganeering, walkout

The Himachal Pradesh Assembly on Friday witnessed noisy scenes and sloganeering for almost an hour after the opposition members entered the well of the House to protest against the alleged lathicharge on PTA teachers yesterday and also press for an adjournment motion on the issue.

On the last day of the monsoon session, the Congress tried to score some political mileage by raking up the PTA issue. However, they also missed out on two important discussions — one of these a resolution to seek extension of the industrial package till 2013 and another on hydro-power generation.

Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal, after the Congress members left the House, accused the opposition of picking up a "wrong issue" to get public attention. He reminded former chief minister Virbhadra Singh that he himself had tried to crush the opposition during his tenure and had resorted to lathicharge on BJP MLAs twice, beside registering criminal cases against them.
