The Congress protests began immediately after the question hour, when CLP leader Vidya Stokes, backed by former CM Virbhadra Singh and PCC president Kaul Singh Thakur, asked Speaker Tulsi Ram about the fate of the adjournment motion that they had moved this morning to allow discussion on the alleged lathicharge on protesting PTA teachers.

The Speaker said the motion was under consideration and he will inform them about it later. This did not satisfy the Congress MLAs, who were on their feet immediately to press for suspension of the House proceedings and discuss the PTA teachers' protest.

Soon after, the Congress MLAs, led by Stokes and Virbhadra Singh, entered the well of the House and started shouting slogans against the government for its alleged anti-PTA stance. The members refused to pay heed to the Speaker's repeated pleas to take their seats and even tried to disrupt the House proceedings. At one stage, when BJP MLA Mohinder Singh was called to initiate a discussion on his resolution relating to hydro-power generation, the Congress MLAs trooped close to his seat and raised slogans loudly. This, however, did not stop the BJP MLA from continuing with his speech.

The BJP members also made an attempt to counter the Congress MLAs, but were advised by the Speaker to calm down.

It was during this mayhem that the House adopted two bills — one of these relating to amendments in the Panchayati Raj Act. The Congress members rejected the Speaker's requests to participate in the House proceedings and walked out.

After they left the House, the Chief Minister launched a blistering attack on the opposition, especially Virbhadra Singh, for making wrong appointments of PTA teachers in complete violation of norms and allowing backdoor entries of close relatives of Congressmen and other favourites at the cost of deserving candidates.

On the issue of decorum, Dhumal said, "It's strange that top Congress MLAs — three of them former speakers and one five-time chief minister — did not care to uphold the dignity and

prestige of the House during the protest."

Mohinder Singh questioned the Congress' moral right to talk of democratic traditions when during its rule the party had "thrown all norms to the wind".

Heading: First dengue case reported in Jalandhar - Indian Express
Content:
The Punjab and Haryana High Court issued notices to the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Friday on an anticipatory bail application filed by Delhi-based businessman Ravinder Singh, who had allegedly sent Rs 15 lakh in cash to a High Court judge's residence last month.

The CBI has been directed to file a reply by September 16.

Demanding interim protection for Ravinder, his counsel Harnam Singh Bhullar said according to the FIR registered by the CBI, no offence was made out against his client.

"As per the FIR, no evidence is available to prove that Ravinder Singh can be booked under Section 8 or 9 of the Prevention of Corruption Act," submitted Bhullar.

Defining the relevant sections under the Prevention of Corruption Act, he contended that neither was Ravinder a public servant nor had he offered any bribe.

Terming the entire issue a goof-up, Bhullar said the cash amount of Rs 15 lakh was meant for a land deal, which landed at a wrong address.

He submitted that the CBI should be directed not to arrest Ravinder.

Taking note of the contentions raised by Bhullar, the High Court questioned the defence counsel as to why Ravinder was not surrendering.

The judge observed that in case he surrendered, his medical examination could be conducted.

The court said the presence of the defence counsel would also be ensured whenever the CBI questioned him in connection with the case.

The defence counsel, however, submitted that Ravinder would surrender only if the High Court granted him protection.

Heading: City has more than 50,000 unemployed youths: report - Indian Express
Content: First case of dengue was reported in Jalandhar on Thursday. Kulwinder Singh of Bhargo Camp was admitted to Civil Hospital after his tests reported positive for dengue. However, he was kept under observation in isolation. Civil Surgeon Dr SS Walia, confirming it to be a case of dengue, appealed to the residents to wear full-sleeve clothes and avoid accumulation of water in and around their houses.

Heading: Naib tehsildar, patwari  held for taking bribe - Indian Express
Content:
Among them are doctors, engineers and teachers, besides graduates and undergraduates

The Chandigarh Administration has claimed that it will introduce 60,000 direct jobs for information technology professionals in the next two years. Going by the present employment scenario in the city, however, it seems the Administration needs to do something sooner than that. There are more than 500 graduate engineers, besides hundreds of diploma

engineers, who are jobless in Chandigarh.

The figure runs into thousands when it comes to graduates and under-graduates. More than 50,000 youths are registered with the Regional Employment Exchange, Chandigarh. The actual figure may be even more; not all unemployed people go to the exchange after all.

The figures were revealed in the Statistical Abstract-2007 released by the UT Administration

recently.

According to the data procured from the UT Regional Employment Exchange, it is not only engineers, but also doctors, agriculture specialists and teachers who are among the thousands hoping to get a job some day.

"People come to us after completing their studies and get themselves registered. We note down their details, particulars and keep photocopies of their certificates. We inform the applicants as and when any private or government organisation contacts us with specific requirements. The registration is free of cost and we are not bound to find a job for the applicants," said Regional Employment Officer M P Siwach.

According to the figures, there are nearly 10,000 matriculates who are looking for jobs. The number is almost similar in the case of under-graduates.

Many graduate and diploma engineers, hundreds of craftsmen trained at industrial training institutes and those with work experience are also registered with the exchange.

Till 2007, there were around 60 allopathic doctors and 94 ayurvedic and homoeopathic doctors who were jobless. Besides, there are hundreds of teachers with a Master's degree who have failed to find employment.

According to the employment exchange records, there are around 470 government and private sector organisations that approach it to recruit people.

"People who register with us are also given guidance, both individually and in groups. They are shown ways to choose career options. We also keep referring applicants to training institutes for apprenticeship. A few of them even get placements," said a senior officer posted at the employment exchange.

The scenario may improve for the IT professionals after the completion of the Rajiv Gandhi Chandigarh Technology Park, but for the others the future doesn't seem to be holding out much hope.

Heading: Protests mark teachers' day - Indian Express
Content:
After the state government withdrew its consent to support Panjab University's bid for central varsity status, now it seems to be the turn of the Panjab University Teachers' Association (PUTA) to perform a volte-face.

PUTA president, Ronki Ram, told Newsline: "All we want are funds for the university; we have no issues whether PU is awarded central status or not. We are completely in favour of a united Punjab."

This is a complete flip from PUTA's earlier stand of demanding central status for the varsity. In fact, PUTA was to observe Teachers' Day as a black day in protest against the government's decision today but the plan was shelved at the last minute. Instead, a token one-day strike was observed.

Vice-Chancellor Professor R C Sobti had presented similar views during a Senate meeting in March where he said PU would welcome complete central funding. He was, however, opposed by a section of senators who had supported the demand for central varsity status.But there are some who are still firm on the demand. Former PUTA general secretary Professor Manjit Singh said: "We were and shall always be for the central varsity status for PU. But now, if PUTA has decided that it is content with just central funds, it is their decision. I would not like to comment on that."

Heading: Black flags order of the (Teachers’) day in Mohali - Indian Express
Content:
Government schoolteachers give celebrations a miss

Teachers' Day celebrations remained a silent affair this year as most government schoolteachers' chose to give them a miss. This was done as a sign of protest against the Education Department for not fulfilling their long pending demands. They were also joined by teachers of the Sarv Shiksha Abhiyaan (SSA) and those serving on a contract basis.

They also held a protest at the Masjid Ground, Sector 20, today.

Talking to Newsline, Arvind Rana, president, Sarv Shiksha Abhiyaan Teachers' Union said: "The department has overlooked even the most basic demands of the teachers. Keeping in view the indifferent attitude of the department, we will not be celebrating the Teacher's Day this year."

He added: "Despite appointing SSA teachers as per the norms of the Central government, the department has not implemented the Central pay grade for us. It has also failed to provide the Provident Fund benefits since the last three years."

He said the department had also reflected its high-handedness by not giving them the salary for the summer vacations. "The department issued the order that we will not be given our salary for the summer vacations, without giving any prior notice."

Madhu Sharma, an SSA teacher said: "The department is also indifferent to the demands of the lady teachers. We get three months' maternity leave without pay. Although we had sent many requests to the department to give us leave with pay, nothing has been done so far."

The teachers on a contract basis, too, boycotted the celebrations as they feel the department has failed to protect their rights. "Even after so many years, the department has neither promoted us to the lecturer grade nor prepared any seniority list. We have not been shifted to the regular grade despite instructions by the Governor," said Rajesh Kumar, a teacher.

Heading: ‘Journalism is my chosen profession, it will do justice to my intelligence’ - Indian Express
Content:
Massive black flag demonstration by the teachers of government-aided schools across Punjab marked the Teacher's Day state-level function at Shivalik Public School in Phase VI on Friday.

Thousands of teachers, under the banner of Punjab Aided School Teachers Union, squatted on the road leading to the function venue and chanted slogans against the state government even as the ruling Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Badal and Punjab Education minister Dr Upinderjeet Kaur honoured 16 government school teachers with state awards of excellence in service.

Heavy police force had a tough time preventing the protesters from reaching the venue. They, however, managed to surpass the police barricades to reach near the school gate. After being not allowed to proceed further, they turned more vociferous to rent their ire against what they called as "apathy" of the state government towards the government-aided schoolteachers.

Sporting black turbans and dupattas with black flags in their hands, the protesters rued that they were not even paid the salaries for the past six months.

Union president Gurcharan Singh Chahal said the revival of pension scheme, which was withdrawn since May 31, 2003, lifting of ban on new recruitments in the government-aided schools, implementation of 5 per cent interim relief and adequate medical reimbursement and house rent were among the major demands of the aided teachers, which were hanging fire since long despite repeated assurances by the state government and the ruling SAD-BJP combine.

It was only after a five-member delegation of the agitators were escorted by the police to meet the Education Minister, who assured to fulfill their genuine demands and called them for a meeting on September 17, that the protest was suspended.

Sukhbir, meanwhile, announced to create a special budget for education from the next fiscal year to uplift the present state of education, which he admitted was in a shambles. He also announced that every government school has been asked to plant at least 101 new saplings in and around their campuses. He asserted that as Punjabi has been made compulsory from Class I onwards in all schools, it will be mandatory for each student to clear the exam.

Heading: Six years on, GPS and PIS projects linger on - Indian Express
Content:
"I believe in taking things in my stride. We should not fret over what has happened, but try to look at the brighter aspect of things," says 14-year-old Urvashi.

Her approach to life is positive and this finds reflection in academics, where she has always been among the top 10 students of her class. Social Science is her favourite subject and Civics interests her a lot. She says: "Civics provides an insight into the working of the country. Reading about Fundamental Rights, the framing of our Constitution, the working of the Panchayati Raj interests me a lot."

Apart from academics, she is equally good in sports and is a member of the school football team. She has also represented her school in various tournaments. "It is my favourite sport. Other than keeping me physically fit, it helps break the monotony of academics," she says.

Urvashi was trained at the Words Model United Nations Conference (MUN) last year to represent her school at the MUN Conference, which will be held in November this year. "One of my teachers suggested that I should participate in MUN as it would provide a platform to express my views. I am inclined to creative writing and hope the MUN experience will help," she says.

A member of her school's Reporter's Club, Urvashi has a flair for creative writing. "I want to take up journalism as my profession as I believe it will help my creative juices," she chips.

Her hobbies include reading and her favourite writer is Chetan Bhagat. "He writes in a simple language and this is what makes his books a breezy read," she adds.

Like teens her age, she loves going out with friends and family during spare time. She looks up to her father who she says, is her best friend. "I admire his patience. Even in the worst situations, I have not seen him losing his calm. He handles problems in a controlled manner and that is what I like best," shares Urvashi.

On her chosen profession, she says, by being a journalist, she will be able to do justice to her intelligence and creativity.

Heading: Advisor to Planning Commission discusses city projects with Rodrigues - Indian Express
Content:
The projects, worth an estimated Rs 94 lakh, like several other projects of the CTU, still hang fire and is waiting for approval by the Administration department

Six years have passed since the Chandigarh Transport Undertaking (CTU) had announced its innovative project— Global Positioning System (GPS) for 100 buses and Public Information System (PIS) for 100 buses and 50 queue shelters. The project, worth an estimated Rs 94 lakh, like several other projects of the CTU, still hangs fire.

The proposal, now with the Administration department, is waiting to see the light of day.

Even with UT Finance Department Secretary Sanjay Kumar having recently given a nod , the project is hanging fire

Director CTU Capt P S Shergill says that once the project gets a final clearance from the Administration department, it would be installed in a time period of three months.

IBuilt Technologies Ltd, a New Delhi-based company, was given the project after a successful demonstration which got the better of six other companies that had applied.

Initially the project was proposed for offline processing, which was later converted into an 'online real time' GPS and PIS in 2004. Even after starting a trial run of the GPS in a CTU bus in 2006, the officials are uncertain as to when the project will actually take off.

The project is technically managed jointly by the Centre for Technical Engineering, Punjab Engineering College. It was initially decided that three departments — Health, Police and CTU — would jointly use the GPS on a single platform.

The authorities realised later that with its feasibility being low, it would be wise to go for a separate base system along with the other applications on individual platforms.

According to plans, CTU would form a central control room to track the movement of buses. Audio-enabled information about buses running on a particular route would be displayed at 150 bus shelters. The shelters would be connected to a central control room that will provide instant updates to the shelters.

The system is expected to help commuters get information about buses along different routes. An electronic display screen will be installed inside the buses to give information about the next stop and the route. Commuters will be able to track the exact position of a bus over the phone or by sending an SMS to a toll-free number connected to the central server.

Heading: Airtel to compensate for ‘deficiency in service’ - Indian Express
Content:
Senior Advisor to the Planning Commission, Bhaskar Chatterjee, held a meeting with the Governor of Punjab and UT Administrator General S F Rodrigues (Retd) on Friday. Homes for street children and the mentally challenged children, vocational training centre and the rehabilitation of nearly 26,000 slumdwellers featured in the discussion.

Chatterjee toured various areas of the city to scrutinise and analyse the ground realities to allocate the additional budget to various departments of the UT Administration.

UT Finance-cum-Home Secretary Sanjay Kumar, Director Public Instructions (Schools) S K Setia and Director Social Welfare Amandeep Kaur accompanied the Senior Advisor in his visits.

Chatterjee visited the e-Sampark Centre, Sector 23, to comprehend its working. He also visited Chandigarh Institute of Hotel Management, Sector 42, to inspect the infrastructure of mid-day meal for children upto Class VIII.

Chattarjee also inspected education centres as the department has sought additional funds of Rs 20 crore for the construction of infrastructure and Rs 14 crore for other reasons like paying salaries to elementary teachers.

Heading: Defective tyres cost Good Year India Rs 5,000 - Indian Express
Content:
Upholding the order of the District Consumer Forum, Singrur, the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Punjab, has directed Bharti Airtel to pay Rs 10,000 for allegedly misleading a consumer and witholding information that roaming facility cannot be activated in Jammu and Kashmir.

The complainant, Munish Kumar, a resident of Longowal village, Singrur, was a prepaid subscriber of Airtel mobile. He planned a trip to Vaishno Devi in December 2006 and made all the necessary arrangements.

To confirm that roaming facility is available in Jammu and Kashmir, Munish contacted the customer care where he was advised to send a message to 121 to enquire about the roaming rates in Jammu and Kashmir. The complainant received a reply that his roaming facility has been activated.

After reaching Jammu, he found that the mobile phone was not working. Munish alleged that he and his family suffered a lot as they could not contact the hotel authorities that were to send a car for receiving them. They had to wait at the railway station for over two hours and also missed the helicopter, which forced them to go to the shrine on foot.

Alleging mental and physical harassment at the hands of the mobile company, Munish moved the district consumer forum in Singrur.

In its reply, Airtel denied the allegations and ruled out any deficiency on their part. The company said they had activated the roaming facility and as per the notification issued by the Government of India, Ministry of Telecommunication, roaming facility is unavailable in Jammu and Kashmir.

The forum ruled that it was the duty of the telecom company to inform the respondent about the non- availability of roaming facility when asked.

The forum then directed Airtel to pay a sum of Rs 10,000 as compensation for the loss suffered by him.

This order by the district forum was challenged before the State Commission, which on Friday upheld the decision.

Heading: Residents ‘overcharged’ at parking lot outside DC office - Indian Express
Content:
The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum on Friday directed Good Year India Limited to pay Rs 5,000 as compensation for deficiency in service.

The complainant, Surinder Mohan, a resident of Sector 15 had purchased one AVEO car from Dynamic Motors in Industrial Area. He alleged that he found some defects in the tyres, manufactured by Good Year India Limited. As the car was in the warranty period, he approached the dealer but his complaint failed to evoke any response. Due to the defect, the complainant was unable to drive his car as it started to wobble after touching a speed of 40 km per hour.

The forum ruled that Dynamic Motors and Good Year India were both responsible for failing to design their product and also breaching the warranty period.

The company was also directed to pay litigation costs of Rs 2,200.

Heading: Fourth cocaine seizure in Mohali in a week - Indian Express
Content:
The parking lot opposite the Deputy Commissioner's office in Phase I highlights the flouting of rules as Mohali residents are overcharged for parking, right under the nose of the District Administration.

A board affixed at the entrance of the parking lot opposite the Deputy Commissioner's office in Phase I, indicates charges of Rs 5 for a car and Rs 2 for two-wheelers, a contractor at the parking lot charges Rs 10 for a car, Rs 5 for a two-wheeler and Rs 20 for a Sports Utility Vehicle.

Even as people protest against the practice, the contractor and his "musclemen" force the vehicle owners to pay double the listed rates, which they claim are "old ".

While the district administration shrugged off its responsibility on the pretext that the parking lot was auctioned by the Greater Mohali Area Development Authority (GMADA), the Estate Officer of GMADA Sukhjeet Pal Singh expressed ignorance over the issue.

"We will check it and act accordingly," assured the GMADA Estate Officer when Newsline apprised him of the problem.

He agreed that parking rates could not be more than that in Chandigarh, where Rs 5 and Rs 2 was charged for a car and two-wheeler parking respectively.

Municipal Councillor and senior Congress leader Kuljit Singh Bedi demanded an immediate cancellation of the parking contract besides asking for penalising the contractor for "overcharging" and "misbehaving" with the public.

"The contractor should be made to pay back with penalty on all the collections made," urged Bedi while lamenting that the practice which took place outside the district administrative complex raises several apprehensions.

Bedi asked for the blacklisting of such contractors and urged for a joint role of the District Administration and the GMADA authorities to ensure that parking is provided to the public at nominal rates.

Heading: ‘Admn biased towards farmers’ - Indian Express
Content:
In its fourth catch of cocaine within a week, the Mohali district police on Friday announced the arrest of two more residents of Rajasthan and claimed to have recovered 900 gram cocaine, worth Rs 90 lakh in the international market, from their possession.

Mohali Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Jatinder Singh Aulakh said that Krishan Singh and Bhagwan Singh of Peepar Ror village in Peepar City district of Rajasthan were held with the contraband while their accomplice Yogesh Kumar of Chhattarpur village in Hathar Mahamaya Nagar district in Uttar Pradesh managed to escape.

The SSP revealed that the alleged narcotic smugglers were held on a tip-off when they were present near a hotel opposite railway station in Lalru late last night while looking for buyers.

A bag, which Krishan Singh was carrying, was searched and a red packet containing cocaine was found from inside, said Mohali Superintendent of Police (Operations) Harinderjeet Singh Sidhu, who supervised the trap laid on the alleged drug peddlers.

The Mohali district police had, earlier, made three major seizures of cocaine in the district over the past one week. A Haryana DSP, Mohali-based ex-serviceman, Haryana Head Constable and Rajasthan Constable were arrested following a recovery of maximum 1.23 kilogram cocaine last Friday. The police had also recovered a bag with Cobra 999 on it.

That was followed by a recovery of 960 gram cocaine from a Haryana farmer with alleged Pakistan connections, on Monday night. On September 3, another Rajasthan youth Lekh Raj was held with 930 gram cocaine from Kharar.

The traps took the total cocaine seizure to 4.120 kilogram, worth over Rs 4 crore in the international market.

It's Tiger 555 now
The bag, in which Krishan Singh was reportedly carrying cocaine, had imprinted on it, "Tiger 555, m. date 10.9.07, exp date 10.10.2010 and Thailand". "We are probing into the meaning of these words from the accused," said the investigating officials.

Heading: The winner takes it all - Indian Express
Content:
The Manimajra Farmers Welfare and Environment Protection Society reiterated their accusation against the Chandigarh Administration of having a biased attitude towards them.

In the executive body meeting of the society, the members said the Administration is misleading the people by suppressing and twisting the facts.

A member of the society said: "The UT Administration continues to be evasive on the legal issues regarding the exploitative and forcible land acquisition policy and non-implementation of the National Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy, 2007 (NRRP)."

They alleged the Administration had not conducted any survey on the affected families, while it is mandatory according to Chapter IV of the NRRP Act.

Heading: Rooting for Rock - Indian Express
Content:
Naresh Gulati means business
"I sold my wife's jewellery to realize my dream and began my business in an area of just 125 square feet. Yes, I've come a long way,'' Naresh Gulati, CEO of the OCA Group, walks down memory lane. Born in Chandigarh, Naresh recounts how he sold candles on the road to earn a living. "We borrowed 5,000 rupees from someone to start the business and our assets are now 400 crore today,'' Naresh has created an enterprise in Australia that is valued at A$100 million. Two of Naresh's companies, Oceanic Consultants, one of the most successful companies in the international education industry and BPO Intelligence, have bagged several Australian Business Awards. A former student of Government College, Sector 11, it's his college and teachers that he attributes musch of his success to, "Education plays a big role and I guess I was at the right place at the right time and my will to move abroad and start from scratch proved to be a blessing,'' Naresh's in town to catch up with family and friends. "It hasn't been an easy journey. I had to work hard and it was a struggle to complete my post-graduation from RMIT University, Melbourne and set up a business in an alien land. But hard work, patience and honesty always pay,'' Naresh says you have to believe in yourself to be a success.

Heading: Mark my space - Indian Express
Content:
What is it that makes this genre of music a record deal?

Headbangers stand redeemed, and their moshpits are now at par with the heavens above, right where the Gods of Rock rule. And like flies are to wanton boys, the world and its book of man-made rules is to these Gods. They walk all over them for their soul satisfaction. That's the way rock is, solid to the core. And so, it comes as no surprise when this genre survives the whiplashes of time, the ignorance of age and the cold shoulder of norms. What started out as a rebellion and was put on mute for being the 'devil's' music', today enjoys an envious godly status. Look around - from rock websites, rocking accessories, rocking attitudes to rock on films, clubs that rock and bands that jam, it's the music that's 'rocked' the world, and it's here to stay and play.

"For me, it's the true voice of the youth. It's making a statement without giving a damn," rocker and music director Vishal Dadlani calls it the language of the youth. "It's linking the mind with words, songs and music," he connects as we push the rewind button and stop on two words: Jim Morrison. It was the '60s and post-jazz era that The Doors opened and the world got the baap of rock, Jim Morrison who jammed on stage with no strict melody, no right note. But surprisingly, everybody loved it. "Rock developed as a stage, live form of music, and in the '60s, it was all about sex, drugs and rock 'n' roll," says hard-core rock fan and city-based guitarist Sherry Sekhon. It was never about the words as much as it was about how it was being played. "Janice Joplin, Joe Crocker, Queen, Led Zepplin, Lynyrd Skynyrd, Jimi Hendrix...for rock stars, it were the drums and guitar, it was more about music than singing, and hence the instrumentation," she adds. Song programming came with Deep Purple, Pink Floyd in the '70s, time of classic rock. With '80s and '90s rolled in Bon Jovi, Kiss, Aerosmith with attitude, pumping up the volume with their dirty hard rock while Nirvana, Greenday gave us the punk grunge rock. Cut to present day, and it's all about alternative rock, creating music that's innovative in melody - Cold Play, Dave Matthew, Radio head, Train, Black Eyed Peas...

Excellent marketing, websites devoted to downloads, videos and music exchange, soon the rock base grew. We now have platforms like Irock, Launchpad, The Great Indian Rock, East Wind Fest, Campus Rock Idols et al. And a film too! What began as director Abhishek Kapoor's attempt to make a boy-bonding, coming-of-age film turned into a full-fledged movie on rock music. "I was listening to rock on my iPod and thought why not make a film on an Indian music band," says Kapoor, who recalls friends in college who used to jam but left it all to pursue careers. "It has always been my fantasy to be a rock star. It was a surreal experience getting to play the part on screen. What helped was the fact that I have been a fan of rock music for 12 years," chips in Farhan Akhtar, whose favourite band is the Beatles.

For Luke Kenny, whose formed the Jim Morrison Tribute band, the sustainability comes from the non-conformism, no to consumerism and the amazing energy it has. Agreeing with energy and attitude, Nirdosh and Jaspal Singh Saib of De Innovatives call it a cult. "Some time back, being cool was in, today, the world rocks. Also, it's grown because of the exposure, experimentation and acceptance." Jaspal adds that because rock gives a raw kind of feel, it attracts the animal instinct in man. "It thrives on this." But not everything is rocking. "It's more of a fashion statement, shoshabaazi than serious rock music. Most of the bands break up, hardly rehearse and carry half-baked knowledge," Dr Rupak Das feels that everybody wants to be a rock star, no one wants to be a musician. "Noise is what they are making." And noise is the new music. As we root for rock, crowd surf, stage dive and mosh, we can only say; Jai Mata Di, let's rock!

Heading: Govt proposes power training institutes for technical manpower pool - Indian Express
Content:
The MCM College campus has three brand-new hot spots — podiums where students can explore their creative instincts. Here's where much music is made, new authors discussed and read, brain-storming sessions conducted... it's the students' personal space, where they can breathe easy. "We wanted to give them a place where they can learn and interact at the same time, far from the madding crowd,'' smiles Puneet Bedi, the principal. It's here that BA-I students Parul Khera, Shivani Sharma and Prasanahit Johar are strumming the guitar. "I am finally getting to learn the basics of the instrument and here we find both space and silence to enjoy the music," says Khera. Taran Guron, a BA-II student, found her love for anchoring on one of these stages. "During the one-hour novel reading sessions I discovered I could talk really well.''

SGGS College, Sector 26, is all set to dedicate a floor in the all-new Students' Centre, where students can do their own thing, without any intrusion from the faculty. "The space will give them much-needed break from studies and prove to be relaxing as well,'' Navjot, a faculty member takes us to the floor which has been designed aesthetically as well. "We now don't have to spend time on roads or restaurants. Here's where we jam now," Ritesh's happy that they're also saving pocket money in the process. At DAV College, Sector 10, students can use the manicured lawns for chilling out in-between classes, while Government College, Sector 11, has created a sculpture garden for them. "This one's a writers' paradise," agrees Aparna Kaushal. To more creative beginnings!

Heading: Bedazzled! - Indian Express
Content:
In a move aimed at preparing a technical manpower pool for the hydro-power sector, the Himachal Pradesh government proposes to set up power training institutes (PTIs) on the pattern of polytechnics and ITIs.

The government has asked leading power sector companies, including Satluj Jal Vidyut Nigam (SJVN), to join hands to set up such institutes for imparting quality education to youth seeking employment in the hydel sector. Replying to a discussion on hydro-power generation, initiated by BJP MLA Mohinder Singh, Chief Minister Prem Kumar Dhumal said the power sector has emerged as one of the biggest areas capable of making Himachal a self-reliant state. Half of the state's revenue comes from hydel power alone and with targets of harnessing the entire 21,000 MW potential power in the next over a decade, Himachal would rank number one in the country, he said.

By 2012, Himachal would produce 12,000 MW of power going by the current pace of work. Together with revenue, which will come in the form of free power as royalty from the project and also sale of surplus power, the BJP government is also focusing on providing employment to Himachalis in power projects coming up in the state and also outside, said Dhumal.

He said a a proposal is already under serious consideration to create a skilled human resource through power training institutes. Dhumal, focusing on the government's plans on hydro-power generation, came down heavily against the Congress for "corruption in the allotment of projects to private sector companies". He said no transparent policy or merit was followed in making allotments, alleging that a lot of cash exchanged hands illegally in the process and the state suffered as most companies either failed to set up projects or faced litigation in the High Court. "Notices for cancellation of 30 projects have been served on the companies and four new MoUs and five implementation agreements (IA) have been signed in the past eight months," he said.

Heading: Stadium, Physical Education College in Patti hang fire - Indian Express
Content:
This one is every girl's dream. To buy a piece of jewellery and wear it in different forms. Tanshiq's all-new range 'Dvaita', brings multi-functional jewellery which not only looks good but is pretty practical too. One piece of jewellery can be worn as a necklace and can also become a bracelet, loop or pendant!

With love...
Amid shouts of Hip, Hip, Hurrah for SJOBA, over 100 teachers of St Johns School laughed, joked and let their hair down at Sip 'N Dine as well as the Park outside the restaurant as they enjoyed a special lunch hosted exclusively for them by the St. Johns Old Boys Association (SJOBA). "Our teachers have done so much for us, given us a solid foundation and education. So, for Teachers' Day, all of us former students decided that we will also help them relax and enjoy themselves," smiles Navpreet Singh Aujla, President, SJOBA. Absolutely overwhelmed with the love and affection shown by the former students, Principal of St Johns, Kavita Das said, "We are truly blessed that they are so deeply involved with the school and giving so much back to us whether it is in the form of this Teachers' Day celebration. We are proud of our school, our students and of SJOBA." AT Taj Chandigarh, chefs designed a special menu for teachers at all the outlets. While Café17, had an elaborate lunch buffet, Black Lotus, the Chinese specialty restaurant, and Dera, the Indian restaurant, offered regional specialities and all-time favourites. Teachers were treated to a complimentary drink and a 50 per cent discount at all the restaurants.

Getting creative
A two-day workshop in creative writing held by Chandigarh Sahitya Akademi in collaboration with Dev Samaj College for women, had as many as 90 students from ten colleges participated in poetry writing, prose, short story, play-writing, competitions. According the Vice-Chairman of the Akademi, Dr DS Gupt, Prof Neelkamal Puri guided the students in short story writing and Prof Phool Chand Manav in article/essay writing.

Cool it!
Coca-Cola India, announced the launch of its latest consumer initiative Jodi BanaoLakhon Kamao' across Punjab, Haryana and Himachal Pradesh. The under-the-crown initiative will give a chance to consumers to win grand prizes ranging from cars, bikes to LCD TVs, refrigerators, mobile phones, DVD players and special Coke wrist watches. Besides, there are handsome cash prizes worth lakhs to be won.

Heading: Foreign trip row: FM defends his secretary - Indian Express
Content:
When an Indian comes home from Olympics armed with laurels, state and Central governments announce a slew of schemes to promote sports, especially in rural areas. But as the time passes, promises fade away and announcements die in a whimper.

One such example of government's lack of sportsman spirit can be seen in Patti, where two ambitious projects— a sports stadium and College of Physical Education, have been hanging fire for the past many years.

This neglect has exposed the face of the state government that boasts of promoting sports in border villages. The foundation stone of College of Physical Education was laid by former chief minister Captain Amarinder Singh, while that of the stadium was laid by SAD MLA from Patti Adesh Pratap Singh Kairon eight years ago during the previous tenure of the SAD-BJP government.

All that the stadium boasts of is a foundation stone bearing Kairon's name and a boundary wall broken at various places. Sources said the project was mooted to promote sports and wean youths from drugs.

In a complete anti-climax, the place now serves as a haven for addicts, who can be seen lolling in various corners filled with stench and dotted by puddles of dirty water.

"It has been like this ever since it was inaugurated. Only God knows when will it be completed," said Balkar Singh, a resident of the area. Khushwinder Singh, an aide of Kairon, said Rs 10 lakh had been sanctioned for the stadium when the foundation stone was laid. "Thereafter, no money was sent," he said, adding that nothing was done to push the work even during the Congress regime.

College of Physical Education, the foundation stone of which was laid in 2006 by Amarinder Singh, at present, functions from the building of Government College, Patti.

"The present government had stopped admission as soon as it came to power and now the institution is struggling for survival," said Sukhwinder Singh Sidhu, a Congress leader from the area. He charged the SAD-BJP government with stopping all ambitious projects started during the Congress regime.

Vijay Sharma, a lecturer in the college, said the tedious official procedures have delayed the project. When contacted, Sports Minister Gulzar Singh Ranike said the government was doing its best to spread sports education in the border villages. However, when asked about the status of these projects, he said he was not aware of them.

Heading: Two special trains to Nanded - Indian Express
Content:
Punjab Finance Minister Manpreet Badal, who is known for speaking his mind, today strongly defended his Finance Secretary D S Kahla on the floor of the House when certain members of the assembly raked up the issue of delay in grant of permission to Punjab Speaker Nirmal Singh Kahlon for going abroad.

Notably, Speaker had to cancel his tour to Malaysia due to delay by the Finance Department. Taking strong note of the "laxity", the Speaker had served notice on the FS, asking him to appear in person to explain the conduct.

The Finance Minister stood up in the assembly and told the Speaker, "It will be cowardice on my part if I do not defend him. The delay was at my end, it was not the fault of the Finance Secretary. I cannot compromise with my conscious, that's why I have to say this."

The FM urged the Speaker to allow him to meet in his chamber before he took a final decision on the issue.

Interestingly, the treasury bench of SAD-BJP MLAs, who were expected to support the Speaker, preferred not to do so. Instead, it was Congress MLA Makhan Singh who raised the matter before the House. He said it was a serious issue, as it involved a bureaucrat "dishonoring" the Speaker. The Speaker was quick to intervene. He said, "The proceedings in the issue are on and the official is suppose to file a written reply."

The Speaker said there was a lapse and if he was not convinced with the FS reply, he would pass the matter to the Privilege Committee of the House. All through there was no reaction from the treasury bench even as a few other Congress MLAs joined the debate and condemned the act. Congress MLA Balbir Sidhu told the Speaker how he had to undergo humiliation at the hands of a DC who allegedly came to his house and abused him in a drunken state. The Speaker asked Sidhu to represent the case to him. The House passed two resolutions, one hailing the victory of Abhinav Bindra in Olympics and the other lauding the role of teachers on Teachers' Day.

Instead of the Sports Minister, Information Technology Minister Bikram Singh Majithia moved the resolution to hail Bindra. When it came to the resolution on lauding teachers, it was Mohan Lal, Transport Minister and not the Education Minister, who moved the resolution. Achievements of wrestler Sushil Kumar and boxer Vijender Kumar were also hailed in the resolution.

Heading: Musicology - Indian Express
Content:
To ease the rush of passengers during Guruta-Gaddi Diwas, Northern Railway will run two special trains between Amritsar and Nanded and a fully air-conditioned one between Chandigarh and Nanded.

As per the Railways, 2716A Amritsar to Nanded super-fast special train will depart from the Holy City on September 20, 24 and 28 at 1.40 pm and arrive at Nanded at 4 am on the third day. The 2715A Nanded to Amritsar super-fast special train will depart from Nanded on September 22, 26 and 30 at 10.50 am and arrive at 11 pm the next day.

Consisting of one AC two-tier, three AC three-tier, 14 second class sleeper coaches and two general second class coaches, the 2715A/2716A train will stop at Jalandhar Cantonment, Ludhiana, Sirhind, Ambala, Kurukshetra, Karnal, Panipat, Delhi Safdarjang, Agra, Jhansi, Bina, Bhopal, Itarsi, Khandwa and Manmar stations. The AC special train between Chandigarh and Nanded train 2716B will depart from Chandigarh on September 21 and 26 at 9.25 am and arrive at Nanded at 5.40 pm the next day. The return service train (2715B) will depart from Nanded on September 23 and 28 at 7.45 am and arrive at Chandigarh at 4 pm the next day.

Heading: Alliance between INSO, SOI: will ABVP join? - Indian Express
Content:
Here's a quick lowdown on albums on the anvil by major metal bandsMetallica - Death Magnetic:The bay thrash metal titans, Metallica teams up with super producer Rick Rubin to follow its 2003 release, St Anger which left many fans in anger for its canny drum sounds and lack of guitar solos. But this time, Metallica, one of the most commercially successful thrash metal bands, promises to return back to its Kill 'em All, Master of Puppet glory days and give a mother of an offering to the fans with new recruit Rob Trujillo on the bass guitar.

Release date: September 12
AC/DC- Black Ice:One of the greatest hard rock act and perhaps one of the finest from Australia, AC/DC (Anti Christ Devil's Child or After Christ Devil Comes as fans put it) returns after an eight year hiatus since the release of Stiff Upper Lip in 2008. Ranked 72 in the Rolling Stone magazine list of the 100 Greatest Artists of All Time, AC/DC hopes to dominate the music world once again as it did when it released Back in Black after the death of Bon Scott with Brian Johnson on the vocals.

Release date: October 20
Queen - The Cosmos Rock:Left in disarray after the death of singer/song writer Freddy Mercury, Queen-the 80's glam rock heroes jammed with ex-Bad Company, Free singer Paul Rodgers and toured all over the world under the name Queen+Paul Rodgers to pay respect to its original vocalist, Freddy. This will be the first album that Queen will release after it released Made in Heaven in 1995.

Release date: October 14
Cradle of Filth- Godspeed On the Devil's Thunder:

The black metal band famous for its make-up as much for its musical abilities, England's most nefarious metal band will release Godspeed on the Devil'-a concept album that traces the life of Gilles de Rais, one of Joan of Arc's brothers-in-arms but a prolific serial killer who mixed prayers with his murders. Cradle of Filth us credited with bringing black metal music into the mainstream when it was signed on by Sony music for Damnation and a Day.

Release date: October 28

Heading: Governor honours 12 teachers with cash prizes - Indian Express
Content:
It was yet another hectic day for students contesting the forthcoming elections at Panjab University as they went around department-to-department rallying votes for themselves.

Rumours of the PUSU splitting into two, with one group to go under Simranjot Saini General Secretary and the other to be formed under Tejpal Singh Cheema, President PUSU, was doing the rounds.

PUSU president Cheema, however denied the rumours, stating that nothing of that sort had happened.

Sukhdev Kundu, President INSO, meanwhile laid to rest the rumour of the INSO aligning with SOI when he said, "There is a positive response by both the parties regarding an alliance. A formal announcement, however, is yet to be made".

Sources, meanwhile, maintain that all the three —ABVP, INSO and SOI — are expected to announce their alliance.

The various bodies, on Friday were engaged in helping the Science students.

While students were busy protesting outside the V-C office, student leaders were engaged in a tug-of-war to prove that they came to the aid first.

With the intervention of Prof R C Sobti, the issue was resolved.

With the exception of the ABVP, most bodies are yet to announce their candidates. The student leaders could be seen campaigning with all the recommendations and the dress code in mind.

Heading: Haryana soldiers can watch movies in civvies, still avail tax exemption - Indian Express
Content:

The Governor also honoured Prem Chand Aggarwal, a teacher at Government Primary School, Barwas (Sirmour); Yudhistra Mehta, teacher a GCPS (Girls), Solan; Roshan Lal Sharma, lecturer in economics, Government Senior Secondary School (Boys), Una, who had won the National Award in 2006, with a cash prize of Rs 50,000 each.
